rows.title: Untamed
rows.cast: Ray Milland, Patricia Morison, Akim Tamiroff
rows.extract: Untamed is a 1940 American Technicolor adventure film directed by George Archainbaud and starring Ray Milland, Patricia Morison and Akim Tamiroff. It is based on the 1926 Sinclair Lewis novel Mantrap.

rows.title: Up in the Air
rows.cast: Marjorie Reynolds, Frankie Darrow, Lorna Gray
rows.extract: Up in the Air is a 1940 American comedy mystery film directed by Howard Bretherton and starring Frankie Darro, Marjorie Reynolds and Mantan Moreland. It was produced and released by Monogram Pictures. It was remade in 1945 as There Goes Kelly.

rows.title: Victory
rows.cast: Fredric March, Cedric Hardwicke, Betty Field
rows.extract: Victory is a 1940 American adventure film directed by John Cromwell and starring Fredric March, Cedric Hardwicke and Betty Field. It was based on the popular 1915 novel by Joseph Conrad. On the eve of the American entry into World War II, Conrad's story of a hermit on an island invaded by thugs was

rows.title: Vigil in the Night
rows.cast: Carole Lombard, Brian Aherne, Anne Shirley
rows.extract: Vigil in the Night is a 1940 RKO Pictures drama film based on the 1939 serialized novel Vigil in the Night by A. J. Cronin. The film was produced and directed by George Stevens and stars Carole Lombard, Brian Aherne and Anne Shirley.

rows.title: Village Barn Dance
rows.cast: Richard Cromwell, George Barbier, Esther Dale
rows.extract: Village Barn Dance is a 1940 American comedy film directed by Frank McDonald, written by Dorrell McGowan and Stuart E. McGowan, and starring Richard Cromwell, Doris Day, George Barbier, Esther Dale, Robert Baldwin and Andrew Tombes. It was released on January 30, 1940, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Villain Still Pursued Her
rows.cast: Hugh Herbert, Anita Louise, Buster Keaton
rows.extract: The Villain Still Pursued Her is a 1940 American comedy film directed by Edward F. Cline and starring Billy Gilbert and Buster Keaton. It is a parody of old stage melodramas but is based primarily on The Drunkard, a 19th-century prohibitionist play by William H. Smith that had also been lampooned in

rows.title: Virginia City
rows.cast: Errol Flynn, Miriam Hopkins, Randolph Scott, Humphrey Bogart
rows.extract: Virginia City is a 1940 American Western film directed by Michael Curtiz and starring Errol Flynn, Miriam Hopkins, Randolph Scott, and a mustachioed Humphrey Bogart in the role of the real-life outlaw John Murrell. Based on a screenplay by Robert Buckner, the film is about a Union officer who escape

rows.title: Viva Cisco Kid
rows.cast: Cesar Romero, Jean Rogers, Stanley Fields
rows.extract: Viva Cisco Kid is a 1940 American Western film directed by Norman Foster, written by Samuel G. Engel and Hal Long, and starring Cesar Romero, Jean Rogers, Chris-Pin Martin, Minor Watson, Stanley Fields and Nigel De Brulier. It was released on April 12, 1940 by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Wagon Train
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Martha O'Driscoll, Ray Whitley
rows.extract: Wagon Train is a 1940 American Western film directed by Edward Killy and starring Tim Holt. It was this film that really started Holt's series of B Westerns for RKO, replacing those made by George O'Brien.

rows.title: Wagons Westward
rows.cast: Anita Louise, Chester Morris, Ona Munson
rows.extract: Wagons Westward is a 1940 American Western film directed by Lew Landers, written by Joseph Moncure March and Harrison Jacobs and starring Chester Morris, Anita Louise, Buck Jones, Ona Munson, George "Gabby" Hayes and Guinn "Big Boy" Williams. It was released on June 19, 1940 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Waterloo Bridge
rows.cast: Vivien Leigh, Robert Taylor, Lucile Watson
rows.extract: Waterloo Bridge is a 1940 American drama film and the remake of the 1931 film also called Waterloo Bridge, adapted from the 1930 play Waterloo Bridge. In an extended flashback narration, it recounts the story of a dancer and an army captain who meet by chance on Waterloo Bridge. The film was made by

rows.title: The Way of All Flesh
rows.cast: Akim Tamiroff, Gladys George, Muriel Angelus
rows.extract: The Way of All Flesh is a 1940 American drama film directed by Louis King and written by Lenore J. Coffee. The film stars Akim Tamiroff, Gladys George, William "Bill" Henry, Muriel Angelus, Berton Churchill and Roger Imhof. It was released on July 5, 1940 by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: The Westerner
rows.cast: Gary Cooper, Walter Brennan, Doris Davenport
rows.extract: The Westerner is a 1940 American Western film directed by William Wyler and starring Gary Cooper, Walter Brennan and Doris Davenport. Written by Niven Busch, Stuart N. Lake and Jo Swerling, the film concerns a self-appointed hanging judge in Vinegaroon, Texas, who befriends a saddle tramp who oppose

rows.title: We Who Are Young
rows.cast: Lana Turner, Gene Lockhart, Grant Mitchell
rows.extract: We Who Are Young is a 1940 American drama film directed by Harold S. Bucquet, written by Dalton Trumbo and starring Lana Turner, John Shelton and Gene Lockhart.

rows.title: West of Abilene
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Bruce Bennett, George Cleveland
rows.extract: West of Abilene is a 1940 American Western film directed by Ralph Ceder and written by Paul Franklin. The film stars Charles Starrett, Marjorie Cooley, Bruce Bennett, William Pawley, Don Beddoe and George Cleveland. The film was released on October 21, 1940, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: West of Carson City
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Peggy Moran, Bob Baker
rows.extract: West of Carson City is a 1940 American Western film directed by Ray Taylor and written by Milton Raison, Sherman L. Lowe and Jack Bernhard. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Bob Baker, Fuzzy Knight, Peggy Moran, Harry Woods and Robert Homans. The film was released on January 19, 1940, by Universal P

rows.title: West of Pinto Basin
rows.cast: Ray "Crash" Corrigan, Max Terhune, Gwen Gaze
rows.extract: West of Pinto Basin is a 1940 American Western film directed by S. Roy Luby and written by Earle Snell. The film is the third in Monogram Pictures' "Range Busters" series, and it stars Ray "Crash" Corrigan as Crash, John "Dusty" King as Dusty and Max "Alibi" Terhune as Alibi, with Gwen Gaze, Tris Co

rows.title: When the Daltons Rode
rows.cast: Randolph Scott, Kay Francis, Brian Donlevy
rows.extract: When the Daltons Rode is a 1940 American Western film directed by George Marshall and starring Randolph Scott, Kay Francis and Brian Donlevy. Based on the 1931 book of the same name by Emmett Dalton, a member of the Dalton Gang, and Jack Jungmeyer Sr., the film also includes a fictional family frien

rows.title: While Thousands Cheer
rows.cast: Kenny Washington, Mantan Moreland, Jeni Le Gon
rows.extract: While Thousands Cheer is a lost American film released in 1940. Leo C. Popkin directed. It was the only football-themed film with an African American lead character for decades. It starred Kenny Washington, a football star from UCLA who went on to become the first African American in the NFL after i

rows.title: Who Killed Aunt Maggie?
rows.cast: Wendy Barrie, Mona Barrie, John Hubbard
rows.extract: Who Killed Aunt Maggie? is a 1940 American mystery film directed by Arthur Lubin and starring John Hubbard, Wendy Barrie and Mona Barrie. It was produced and distributed by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Wild Horse Range
rows.cast: Jack Randall, Frank Yaconelli, Marin Sais
rows.extract: Wild Horse Range is a 1940 American Western film written by Carl Krusada from a story by Tom Gibson. It was directed by Raymond K. Johnson, and stars Jack Randall.

rows.title: Wild Horse Valley
rows.cast: Bob Steele, Lafe McKee, Ted Adams
rows.extract: Wild Horse Valley is a 1940 American Western film directed by Ira Webb and starring Bob Steele, Phyllis Adair and Lafe McKee.

rows.title: Wildcat Bus
rows.cast: Fay Wray, Paul Guilfoyle, Don Costello
rows.extract: Wildcat Bus is a 1940 American action film directed by Frank Woodruff and written by Lou Lusty. The film stars Fay Wray, Charles Lang, Paul Guilfoyle, Don Costello and Paul McGrath. The film was released on August 23, 1940, by RKO Pictures.

rows.title: The Wildcat of Tucson
rows.cast: Wild Bill Elliott, Evelyn Young, Kenneth MacDonald
rows.extract: The Wildcat of Tucson is a 1940 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and starring Bill Elliott as "Wild Bill" Hickok and Evelyn Young as Vivian Barlow.

rows.title: Wolf of New York
rows.cast: Edmund Lowe, Rose Hobart, James Stephenson
rows.extract: Wolf of New York is a 1940 American crime film directed by William C. McGann and written by Gordon Kahn and Lionel Houser. The film stars Edmund Lowe, Rose Hobart, James Stephenson, Jerome Cowan, William Demarest and Maurice Murphy. The film was released on January 23, 1940, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Women in War
rows.cast: Elsie Janis, Wendy Barrie, Patric Knowles
rows.extract: Women in War is a 1940 American war film about the nurses of the British Voluntary Aid Detachment during the Battle of France. Directed by John H. Auer and starring Wendy Barrie, Elsie Janis and Patric Knowles, it was nominated for an Oscar for Best Visual Effects.

rows.title: Women Without Names
rows.cast: Ellen Drew, Fay Helm, Judith Barrett
rows.extract: Women Without Names is a 1940 American drama film directed by Robert Florey.

rows.title: Wyoming
rows.cast: Wallace Beery, Leo Carrillo, Ann Rutherford
rows.extract: Wyoming is a 1940 Western film directed by Richard Thorpe and starring Wallace Beery. It was the first of seven films pairing Beery and character actress Marjorie Main.

rows.title: Yesterday's Heroes
rows.cast: Jean Rogers, Robert Sterling, Kay Aldridge
rows.extract: Yesterday's Heroes is a 1940 American drama film directed by Herbert I. Leeds and written by Irving Cummings Jr. and William Conselman Jr.. The film stars Jean Rogers, Robert Sterling, Ted North, Kay Aldridge, Russell Gleason and Richard "Dick" Lane. The film was released on September 20, 1940, by 2

rows.title: You Can't Fool Your Wife
rows.cast: Lucille Ball, James Ellison, Virginia Vale
rows.extract: You Can't Fool Your Wife is a 1940 American comedy film directed by Ray McCarey and written by Jerome Cady. The film stars Lucille Ball, James Ellison, Robert Coote, Virginia Vale, Emma Dunn and Elaine Shepard. The film was released on May 21, 1940, by RKO Pictures.

rows.title: You'll Find Out
rows.cast: Kay Kyser, Helen Parrish, Ginny Simms, Peter Lorre, Boris Karloff
rows.extract: You'll Find Out is a 1940 American comedy film directed by David Butler and starring Kay Kyser. In 1940, the film was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Original Song at the 13th Academy Awards. In the film, members of an orchestra hired to play at a young heiress's birthday party uncover a plo

rows.title: Young Bill Hickok
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Sally Payne, Julie Bishop
rows.extract: Young Bill Hickok is a 1940 American Western film directed by Joseph Kane and starring Roy Rogers.

rows.title: Young Buffalo Bill
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Pauline Moore, George "Gabby" Hayes
rows.extract: Young Buffalo Bill is a 1940 American Western film directed by Joseph Kane and starring Roy Rogers and George "Gabby" Hayes.

rows.title: Young People
rows.cast: Shirley Temple, Jack Oakie, Charlotte Greenwood
rows.extract: Young People is a 1940 American musical drama film directed by Allan Dwan and starring Shirley Temple and Jack Oakie. This would be Shirley's final film as a child actress.

rows.title: Young Tom Edison
rows.cast: Mickey Rooney, Fay Bainter, George Bancroft
rows.extract: Young Tom Edison is a 1940 biographical film about the early life of inventor Thomas Edison directed by Norman Taurog and starring Mickey Rooney. The film was the first of a complementary pair of Edison biopics that Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer released in 1940. Edison, the Man, starring Spencer Tracy, follo

rows.title: Young as You Feel
rows.cast: Jed Prouty, Spring Byington, Joan Valerie
rows.extract: Young as You Feel is a 1940 American comedy film directed by Malcolm St. Clair and starring Jed Prouty, Spring Byington and Joan Valerie. It was part of Twentieth Century Fox's Jones Family series of films. The film's plot was similar to that of the 1931 film Young as You Feel.

rows.title: You're Not So Tough
rows.cast: Billy Halop, Huntz Hall, Bobby Jordan, Nan Grey
rows.extract: You're Not So Tough is a 1940 Universal Studios drama film directed by Joe May and starring Dead End Kids and the Little Tough Guys and was the first in the series where Billy Halop and Huntz Hall weren't billed in the opening credits before the Dead End Kids name.

rows.title: Youth Will Be Served
rows.cast: Jane Withers, Kent Taylor, Kay Aldridge
rows.extract: Youth Will Be Served is a 1940 American musical film directed by Otto Brower and starring Jane Withers and Jane Darwell.

rows.title: Yukon Flight
rows.cast: Louise Stanley, James Newill, Warren Hull
rows.extract: Yukon Flight  is a 1940 American Western film directed by Ralph Staub and starring James Newill, Louise Stanley, Dave O'Brien and William Pawley. Released by Monogram Pictures, the film uses a musical/action formula, similar to the format of the "singing cowboy" films of the era.

rows.title: Zanzibar
rows.cast: Lola Lane, James Craig, Eduardo Ciannelli
rows.extract: Zanzibar is a 1940 American adventure film directed by Harold Schuster and starring James Craig, Lola Lane and Eduardo Ciannelli.

rows.title: Adventures of Red Ryder
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Noah Beery, Tommy Cook
rows.extract: The Adventures of Red Ryder is a 1940 12-chapter Republic movie serial directed by William Witney and John English and starring Don "Red" Barry and Noah Beery, Sr., based on the Western comic strip Red Ryder. This serial is the 18th of the 66 serials produced by Republic.

rows.title: City of Lost Men
rows.cast: William "Stage" Boyd, Kane Richmond, Claudia Dell

rows.title: Deadwood Dick
rows.cast: Don Douglas, Lorna Gray, Harry Harvey, Marin Sais
rows.extract: Deadwood Dick is a 1940 American Western Serial film directed by James W. Horne and starring Don Douglas and Lorna Gray. The character of Deadwood Dick was for the most part another version of "Zorro".

rows.title: The Green Archer
rows.cast: Victor Jory, Iris Meredith
rows.extract: The Green Archer is the 12th serial released by Columbia Pictures. It was based on Edgar Wallace's 1923 novel The Green Archer, which had previously been adapted into the silent serial of the same name in 1925 by Pathé Exchange.

rows.title: The Green Hornet
rows.cast: Gordon Jones, Wade Boteler, Anne Nagel
rows.extract: The Green Hornet is a 1940 black-and-white 13-chapter movie serial from Universal Pictures, produced by Henry MacRae, directed by Ford Beebe and Ray Taylor, starring Gordon Jones, Wade Boteler, Keye Luke, and Anne Nagel. The serial is based on The Green Hornet radio series by George W. Trendle and F

rows.title: Junior G-Men
rows.cast: Dead End Kids
rows.extract: Junior G-Men is a 1940 Universal film serial. It was Universal's 116th serial of their total of output of 137. The serial is one of the three serials starring "The Dead End Kids and Little Tough Guys" who were under contract to Universal at the time. The plot of Junior G-Men is a pre-World War II G-

rows.title: King of the Royal Mounted
rows.cast: Allan Lane
rows.extract: King of the Royal Mounted (1940) is a Republic Pictures northern serial based on the King of the Royal Mounted comic strip directed by William Witney and John English.

rows.title: The Lone Ranger
rows.cast: Lee Powell, Chief Thundercloud, Stanley Andrews
rows.extract: The Lone Ranger is a 1938 American Republic Movie serial based on the radio program of the same name. It was the ninth of the sixty-six serials produced by Republic, the fourth Western and the first Republic serial release of 1938. The following year a sequel serial The Lone Ranger Rides Again was r

rows.title: Mysterious Doctor Satan
rows.cast: Eduardo Ciannelli
rows.extract: Mysterious Doctor Satan is a 1940 American film serial directed by William Witney and John English. Produced by Republic Pictures, the serial stars Edward Ciannelli, Robert Wilcox, William Newell, C. Montague Shaw, Ella Neal, and Dorothy Herbert. The title of the serial is derived from that of its c

rows.title: Terry and the Pirates
rows.cast: William Tracy, Sheila Darcy
rows.extract: Terry and the Pirates (1940) is the 10th film serial released by Columbia. It is based on the comic strip Terry and the Pirates created by Milton Caniff. In his biography, Meanwhile..., Caniff stated that he hated the serial for changing so much of his comic strip, and that "I saw the first chapter

rows.title: Winners of the West
rows.cast: Dick Foran, Anne Nagel
rows.extract: Winners of the West is a 1940 American Western film serial from Universal Pictures directed by Ford Beebe and Ray Taylor. It stars Dick Foran and Anne Nagel in a plot about the construction of a railroad and a local ganglord who opposes it. It was Universal's 115th serial release.

rows.title: Americaner Shadchen
rows.cast: Leo Fuchs, Judith Abarbanel, Judel Dubinsky
rows.extract: American Matchmaker, or אמעריקאנער שדכן  is a 1940 Yiddish-language American comedy film directed by Edgar G. Ulmer and starring Leo Fuchs, Judith Abarbanel, Judel Dubinsky and Anna Guskin. The film has music composed by Sam Morgenstern.

rows.title: Elmer's Candid Camera
rows.cast: Mel Blanc, Arthur Q. Bryan
rows.extract: Elmer's Candid Camera is a 1940 Warner Bros. Merrie Melodies cartoon short directed by Chuck Jones. The short was released on March 2, 1940, and features Elmer Fudd and an early Bugs Bunny prototype.

rows.title: Eyes of the Navy
rows.cast: Charles B. Middleton
rows.extract: Eyes of the Navy is a 1940 American short documentary film. It was nominated for an Academy Award at the 13th Academy Awards for Best Short Subject (Two-Reel).

rows.title: From Nurse to Worse
rows.cast: The Three Stooges
rows.extract: From Nurse To Worse is a 1940 short subject directed by Jules White starring American slapstick comedy team The Three Stooges. It is the 49th entry in the series released by Columbia Pictures starring the comedians, who released 190 shorts for the studio between 1934 and 1959.

rows.title: Hired!
rows.extract: Henry Jamison "Jam" Handy was an American Olympic breaststroke swimmer, water polo player, and founder of the Jam Handy Organization (JHO), a producer of commercially sponsored motion pictures, slidefilms, trade shows, industrial theater and multimedia training aids. Credited as the first person to

rows.title: How High Is Up?
rows.cast: The Three Stooges
rows.extract: How High is Up? is a 1940 short subject directed by Del Lord starring American slapstick comedy team The Three Stooges. It is the 48th entry in the series released by Columbia Pictures starring the comedians, who released 190 shorts for the studio between 1934 and 1959.

rows.title: Knock Knock
rows.extract: Knock Knock is a 1940 animated short subject, part of the Andy Panda series, produced by Walter Lantz. The cartoon is noted for being the first appearance of Woody Woodpecker, and was released by Universal Pictures on November 25, 1940.

rows.title: The Milky Way
rows.cast: Bernice Hansen
rows.extract: The Milky Way is a one-reel animated cartoon short subject, produced in Technicolor and released to theatres with the film The Captain Is a Lady in 1940 by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. The short explores the adventures of the "three little kittens who lost their mittens", as they explore a dreamland where s

rows.title: Mr. Duck Steps Out
rows.extract: Mr. Duck Steps Out is a Donald Duck cartoon produced by Walt Disney Productions, which is released on June 7, 1940, and featured the debut of Daisy Duck. The short was directed by Jack King and written by Carl Barks, Chuck Couch, Jack Hannah, Harry Reeves, Milt Schaffer, and Frank Tashlin.

rows.title: No Census, No Feeling
rows.cast: The Three Stooges
rows.extract: No Census, No Feeling is a 1940 short subject directed by Del Lord starring American slapstick comedy team The Three Stooges. It is the 50th entry in the series released by Columbia Pictures starring the comedians, who released 190 shorts for the studio between 1934 and 1959.

rows.title: Nutty But Nice
rows.cast: The Three Stooges
rows.extract: Nutty but Nice is a 1940 short subject directed by Jules White starring American slapstick comedy team The Three Stooges. It is the 47th entry in the series released by Columbia Pictures starring the comedians, who released 190 shorts for the studio between 1934 and 1959.

rows.title: Of Fox and Hounds
rows.cast: Willoughby
rows.extract: Of Fox and Hounds is a 1940 Warner Bros. Merrie Melodies directed by Tex Avery. The short was released on December 7, 1940, and introduces Willoughby the Dog. Avery performed the voice of Willoughby, and Mel Blanc voiced George the Fox and the bear's yells. The short is an attempt to duplicate the s

rows.title: Patient Porky
rows.cast: Porky Pig
rows.extract: Patient Porky is a 1940 Warner Bros. Looney Tunes cartoon directed by Bob Clampett, written by Warren Foster, and scored by Carl W. Stalling. rows.title: Puss Gets the Boot
rows.cast: Lillian Randolph
rows.extract: Puss Gets the Boot is a 1940 American animated short film and is the first short in what would become the Tom and Jerry cartoon series, though neither were yet referred to by these names. It was directed by William Hanna, Joseph Barbera, and produced by Rudolf Ising. It was based on the Aesop's Fabl

rows.title: Quicker'n a Wink
rows.cast: Harold E. Edgerton
rows.extract: Quicker'n a Wink is a 1940 American short documentary film in the Pete Smith Specialities series about stroboscopic photography, written by Buddy Adler and directed by George Sidney. In 1941, it won an Oscar for Best Short Subject (One-Reel) at the 13th Academy Awards.

rows.title: Rockin' Thru the Rockies
rows.cast: The Three Stooges
rows.extract: Rockin' thru the Rockies is a 1940 short subject directed by Jules White starring American slapstick comedy team The Three Stooges. It is the 45th entry in the series released by Columbia Pictures starring the comedians, who released 190 shorts for the studio between 1934 and 1959.

rows.title: Accent on Love
rows.cast: George Montgomery, Osa Massen, J. Carrol Naish
rows.extract: Accent on Love is a 1941 American drama film directed and filmed by Ray McCarey and written by John Larkin. The film stars George Montgomery, Osa Massen, J. Carrol Naish, Cobina Wright, Stanley Clements and Minerva Urecal. It was released on July 11, 1941 by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Across the Sierras
rows.cast: Bill Elliott
rows.extract: Across the Sierras is a 1941 American Western film directed by D. Ross Lederman and starring Bill Elliott.

rows.title: Adam Had Four Sons
rows.cast: Ingrid Bergman, Warner Baxter, Susan Hayward
rows.extract: Adam Had Four Sons is a 1941 American romantic drama film directed by Gregory Ratoff and starring Ingrid Bergman, Warner Baxter, Susan Hayward, and Fay Wray,

rows.title: Adventure in Washington
rows.cast: Herbert Marshall, Virginia Bruce, Gene Reynolds
rows.extract: Adventure in Washington is a 1941 American drama film directed by Alfred E. Green and starring Herbert Marshall, Virginia Bruce and Gene Reynolds. The plot is about an unlikely U.S. Senate page boy whose misadventures in Washington, D.C., cause a Congressional scandal.

rows.title: Affectionately Yours
rows.cast: Merle Oberon, Rita Hayworth, Dennis Morgan
rows.extract: Affectionately Yours is a 1941 American romantic comedy film directed by Lloyd Bacon and starring Merle Oberon, Dennis Morgan, and Rita Hayworth.

rows.title: All-American Co-Ed
rows.cast: Frances Langford, Johnny Downs, Marjorie Woodworth
rows.extract: All-American Co-ed is a 1941 American musical film produced and directed by Leroy Prinz as a Hal Roach Streamliner for release by United Artists. It stars Frances Langford, Johnny Downs, Marjorie Woodworth, Noah Beery Jr., Esther Dale, Harry Langdon, and The Tanner Sisters.

rows.title: All Through the Night
rows.cast: Humphrey Bogart, Kaaren Verne, Conrad Veidt, Jane Darwell
rows.extract: All Through the Night is a 1942 American comedy-gangster-spy thriller film directed by Vincent Sherman and starring Humphrey Bogart, Conrad Veidt and Kaaren Verne, and featuring many of the Warner Bros. company of character actors. It was released by Warner Brothers. The supporting cast features Pet

rows.title: Aloma of the South Seas
rows.cast: Dorothy Lamour, Jon Hall, Katherine DeMille
rows.extract: Aloma of the South Seas is a 1941 American romantic adventure drama film directed by Alfred Santell and starring Dorothy Lamour and Jon Hall. The film was shot in Technicolor and distributed by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: Along the Rio Grande
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Betty Jane Rhodes, Ruth Clifford
rows.extract: Along the Rio Grande is a 1941 American Western film directed by Edward Killy and starring Tim Holt. The female lead was Betty Jane Rhodes.

rows.title: Among the Living
rows.cast: Albert Dekker, Susan Hayward, Harry Carey, Frances Farmer
rows.extract: Among the Living is a 1941 American film noir directed by Stuart Heisler and starring Albert Dekker, Susan Hayward, Harry Carey and Frances Farmer. The film is a mix of social drama, horror film, and suspense thriller.

rows.title: Andy Hardy's Private Secretary
rows.cast: Lewis Stone, Mickey Rooney, Kathryn Grayson
rows.extract: Andy Hardy's Private Secretary is a 1941 American comedy film directed by George B. Seitz and starring Lewis Stone, Mickey Rooney, Kathryn Grayson, Ann Rutherford and Fay Holden. It was the tenth of the 16-film Andy Hardy series. Marian Hardy does not appear in this film.

rows.title: Angels with Broken Wings
rows.cast: Jane Frazee, Mary Lee, Binnie Barnes
rows.extract: Angels with Broken Wings is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Bernard Vorhaus and starring Jane Frazee and Binnie Barnes. The screenplay was written by George Carleton Brown and Bradford Ropes. It was released by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Apache Kid
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Lynn Merrick, LeRoy Mason
rows.extract:
Haskay-bay-nay-ntayl, better known as the Apache Kid, was born in Aravaipa Canyon into one of the three local groups of the Aravaipa/Arivaipa Apache Band of San Carlos Apache, one subgroup of the Western Apache people.

rows.title: Appointment for Love
rows.cast: Charles Boyer, Margaret Sullavan, Rita Johnson
rows.extract: Appointment for Love is a 1941 romantic comedy film directed by William A. Seiter and starring Charles Boyer and Margaret Sullavan. It was made by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Arizona Bound
rows.cast: Buck Jones, Tim McCoy, Luana Walters
rows.extract: Arizona Bound is a 1941 American Western film directed by Spencer Gordon Bennet. rows.title: Arizona Cyclone
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Fuzzy Knight, Nell O'Day
rows.extract: Arizona Cyclone is a 1941 American Western film directed by Joseph H. Lewis and written by Sherman L. Lowe. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Fuzzy Knight, Nell O'Day, Kathryn Adams Doty, Herbert Rawlinson and Dick Curtis. The film was released on November 14, 1941, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Arkansas Judge
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Veda Ann Borg, Pauline Moore
rows.extract: Arkansas Judge  is a 1941 American Western film directed by Frank McDonald and starring Roy Rogers, Spring Byington, and Veda Ann Borg.

rows.title: Babes on Broadway
rows.cast: Judy Garland, Mickey Rooney, Fay Bainter
rows.extract: Babes on Broadway is a 1941 American musical film starring Mickey Rooney and Judy Garland and directed by Busby Berkeley, with Vincente Minnelli directing Garland's big solo numbers. The film, which features Fay Bainter and Virginia Weidler, was the third in the "Backyard Musical" series about kids

rows.title: Bachelor Daddy
rows.cast: Edward Everett Horton, Donald Woods, Evelyn Ankers
rows.extract: Bachelor Daddy is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Harold Young and written by Robert Lees and Frederic I. Rinaldo. The film stars Baby Sandy, Edward Everett Horton, Donald Woods, Raymond Walburn, Evelyn Ankers, Kathryn Adams Doty, Franklin Pangborn and Jed Prouty. The film was released on Ju

rows.title: Back in the Saddle
rows.cast: Gene Autry, Smiley Burnette, Mary Lee
rows.extract: Back in the Saddle is a 1941 American Western film directed by Lew Landers and starring Gene Autry, Smiley Burnette, and Mary Lee. rows.title: Back Street
rows.cast: Charles Boyer, Margaret Sullavan, Richard Carlson
rows.extract: Back Street is a 1941 American drama film directed by Robert Stevenson and starring Charles Boyer and Margaret Sullavan. It is a remake of the 1932 film of the same name, also from Universal. The film is adapted from the 1931 Fannie Hurst novel and the 1932 film version which it follows very closely

rows.title: Badlands of Dakota
rows.cast: Robert Stack, Frances Farmer, Richard Dix
rows.extract: Badlands of Dakota is a 1941 American Western film directed by Alfred E. Green and starring Robert Stack, Ann Rutherford, Richard Dix and Frances Farmer. Its plot follows a sheriff and his girlfriend who cross paths with Wild Bill Hickok and Calamity Jane.

rows.title: The Bad Man
rows.cast: Wallace Beery, Lionel Barrymore, Laraine Day, Ronald Reagan
rows.extract: The Bad Man is a 1941 American Western film starring Wallace Beery and featuring Lionel Barrymore, Laraine Day, and Ronald Reagan. rows.title: Bad Man of Deadwood
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Carol Adams, Sally Blane
rows.extract: Bad Man of Deadwood is a 1941 American Western film directed by Joseph Kane and starring Roy Rogers.

rows.title: Bad Men of Missouri
rows.cast: Jane Wyman, Dennis Morgan, Wayne Morris
rows.extract: Bad Men of Missouri is a 1941 American Western film directed by Ray Enright and written by Charles Grayson. The film stars Dennis Morgan, Jane Wyman, Wayne Morris and Arthur Kennedy. The film was released by Warner Bros. on July 26, 1941.

rows.title: Bahama Passage
rows.cast: Sterling Hayden, Madeleine Carroll, Flora Robson
rows.extract: Bahama Passage is a 1941 American drama film directed by Edward H. Griffith, starring Madeleine Carroll and Sterling Hayden. The film was primarily shot on Salt Cay, Turks Islands in Technicolor.

rows.title: Ball of Fire
rows.cast: Gary Cooper, Barbara Stanwyck, Oskar Homolka
rows.extract: Ball of Fire is a 1941 American screwball comedy film directed by Howard Hawks and starring Gary Cooper and Barbara Stanwyck. rows.title: The Bandit Trail
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Ray Whitley, Janet Waldo
rows.extract: The Bandit Trail is a 1941 Western film.

rows.title: Barnacle Bill
rows.cast: Wallace Beery, Marjorie Main, Leo Carrillo
rows.extract: Barnacle Bill is a 1941 feature film starring Wallace Beery. The screen comedy was directed by Richard Thorpe. Barnacle Bill was the second of seven MGM films pairing Beery and character actress Marjorie Main.

rows.title: Bedtime Story
rows.cast: Loretta Young, Fredric March
rows.extract: Bedtime Story is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Alexander Hall and starring Fredric March, Loretta Young, and Robert Benchley. The supporting cast includes Eve Arden and Joyce Compton.

rows.title: The Big Boss
rows.cast: Otto Kruger, Gloria Dickson, John Litel
rows.extract: The Big Boss is a 1941 American drama film directed by Charles Barton and starring Otto Kruger.

rows.title: The Big Store
rows.cast: Marx Brothers, Tony Martin, Virginia Grey
rows.extract: The Big Store is a 1941 American comedy film starring the Marx Brothers that takes place in a large department store. Groucho appears as private detective Wolf J. Flywheel.

rows.title: Billy the Kid
rows.cast: Robert Taylor, Brian Donlevy, Ian Hunter
rows.extract: Billy the Kid is a 1941 American Western film, a color remake of the 1930 film of the same name. The film features Robert Taylor as Billy and Brian Donlevy as a fictionalized version of Pat Garrett renamed "Jim Sherwood" in the film. Directed by David Miller and based on the book by Walter Noble Bur

rows.title: Billy the Kid's Fighting Pals
rows.cast: Bob Steele, Carleton Young
rows.extract: Billy the Kid's Fighting Pals is a 1941 American Western directed by Sam Newfield for Producers Releasing Corporation (PRC), and the fifth in PRC's Billy the Kid film series.

rows.title: Billy the Kid in Santa Fe
rows.cast: Bob Steele, Marin Sais
rows.extract: Billy the Kid in Santa Fe is a 1941 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield. This film is the sixth in the "Billy the Kid" film series, produced by PRC from 1940 to 1946, and the last to star Bob Steele. In the next film, Billy the Kid Wanted, Steele was replaced by Buster Crabbe.

rows.title: Billy the Kid's Range War
rows.cast: Bob Steele, Joan Barclay
rows.extract: Billy the Kid's Range War is a 1941 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield that was the fourth of Producers Releasing Corporation's Billy the Kid film series. Despite the film's title and mention of Lincoln County, there is neither a range war nor even a range seen in the film.

rows.title: Billy the Kid's Round-Up
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Carleton Young, Joan Barclay
rows.extract: Billy the Kid's Round-Up is a 1941 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Fred Myton. The film stars Buster Crabbe, Al St. John, Carleton Young, Joan Barclay, Glenn Strange and Charles King. The film was released on December 12, 1941, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: Billy the Kid Wanted
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Dave O'Brien, Glenn Strange
rows.extract: Billy the Kid Wanted is a 1941 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield. This film is the seventh in the "Billy the Kid" film series produced by PRC from 1940 to 1946, and the first starring Buster Crabbe as Billy the Kid, replacing Bob Steele. The film also features Sam Newfield's son Joel.

rows.title: Birth of the Blues
rows.cast: Bing Crosby, Mary Martin, Brian Donlevy
rows.extract: Birth of the Blues is a 1941 American musical film directed by Victor Schertzinger and starring Bing Crosby, Mary Martin and Brian Donlevy.

rows.title: The Black Cat
rows.cast: Basil Rathbone, Broderick Crawford, Bela Lugosi
rows.extract: The Black Cat is a 1941 American comedy horror and mystery film directed by Albert S. Rogell and starring Basil Rathbone. rows.title: Blonde Comet
rows.cast: Virginia Vale, Robert Kent, Vince Barnett
rows.extract: Blonde Comet is a 1941 racing movie directed by William Beaudine and starring Virginia Vale as a female racing driver who competes all over Europe then returns to America where she finds romance with a male driver against whom she races. Race driver Barney Oldfield plays himself in a large role bill

rows.title: The Blonde from Singapore
rows.cast: Florence Rice, Leif Erickson, Alexander D'Arcy
rows.extract: The Blonde from Singapore is a 1941 American adventure film directed by Edward Dmytryk and starring Florence Rice.

rows.title: Blonde Inspiration
rows.cast: John Shelton, Virginia Grey, Albert Dekker
rows.extract: Blonde Inspiration is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Busby Berkeley and written by Marion Parsonnet. The film stars John Shelton, Virginia Grey, Albert Dekker, Charles Butterworth, and Donald Meek. The film was released on February 7, 1941, by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer.

rows.title: Blondie Goes Latin
rows.cast: Penny Singleton, Arthur Lake, Tito Guízar
rows.extract: Blondie Goes Latin, also known as Conga Swing, is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Frank R. Strayer and Robert Sparks and starring Penny Singleton, Arthur Lake, and Larry Simms. It is the eighth of the Blondie films. The film showcases musical numbers of Kirby Grant, Ruth Terry, Tito Guizar,

rows.title: Blondie in Society
rows.cast: Penny Singleton, Arthur Lake, Jonathan Hale
rows.extract: Blondie in Society is a 1941 black-and-white comedy film directed by Frank R. Strayer and starring Penny Singleton, Arthur Lake, and Larry Simms. It is the ninth of the 28 features in the Blondie film series.

rows.title: Blood and Sand
rows.cast: Tyrone Power, Linda Darnell, Rita Hayworth, Alla Nazimova
rows.extract: Blood and Sand is a 1941 American romantic Technicolor film starring Tyrone Power, Linda Darnell, Rita Hayworth, and Nazimova. rows.cast: Greer Garson, Walter Pidgeon, Felix Bressart
rows.extract: Blossoms in the Dust is a 1941 American biographical film directed by Mervyn LeRoy and starring Greer Garson, Walter Pidgeon, Felix Bressart, Marsha Hunt, Fay Holden and Samuel S. Hinds. It tells the true story of Edna Gladney, who helped orphaned children find homes and began a campaign to remove t

rows.title: Blues in the Night
rows.cast: Priscilla Lane, Betty Field, Lloyd Nolan
rows.extract: Blues in the Night is a 1941 American musical in the film noir style directed by Anatole Litvak and starring Priscilla Lane, Richard Whorf, Betty Field, Lloyd Nolan, Elia Kazan, and Jack Carson. rows.title: The Body Disappears
rows.cast: Jeffrey Lynn, Jane Wyman, Edward Everett Horton
rows.extract: The Body Disappears is a 1941 American comedy film directed by D. Ross Lederman and starring Jeffrey Lynn and Jane Wyman.

rows.title: Border Vigilantes
rows.cast: William Boyd, Russell Hayden, Frances Gifford
rows.extract: Border Vigilantes is a 1941 American Western film directed by Derwin Abrahams and written by J. Benton Cheney. The film stars William Boyd, Russell Hayden, Andy Clyde, Frances Gifford, Victor Jory, Ethel Wales and Morris Ankrum. The film was released on April 18, 1941, by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: Borrowed Hero
rows.cast: Florence Rice, Alan Baxter, Constance Worth
rows.extract: Borrowed Hero is a 1941 American film directed by Lewis D. Collins.

rows.title: Bowery Blitzkrieg
rows.cast: The, East Side Kids, Keye Luke, Warren Hull
rows.extract: Bowery Blitzkrieg is a 1941 film and the sixth installment of the East Side Kids series. The film "introduced" Huntz Hall in his first of the East Side Kids film series.

rows.title: The Bride Came C.O.D.
rows.cast: James Cagney, Bette Davis, Eugene Pallette
rows.extract: The Bride Came C.O.D. is a 1941 American screwball romantic comedy starring James Cagney as an airplane pilot and Bette Davis as a runaway heiress, and directed by William Keighley. rows.title: The Bride Wore Crutches
rows.cast: Lynne Roberts, Robert Armstrong
rows.extract: The Bride Wore Crutches is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Shepard Traube and written by Edward Verdier. The film stars Lynne Roberts, Ted North, Edgar Kennedy, Robert Armstrong, Lionel Stander and Richard Lane. The film was released on May 25, 1941, by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Broadway Limited
rows.cast: Victor McLaglen, Patsy Kelly, ZaSu Pitts
rows.extract: Broadway Limited is a 1941 American film directed by Gordon Douglas and starring Victor McLaglen, Dennis O'Keefe and ZaSu Pitts. The film takes its name from the Broadway Limited train that the Pennsylvania Railroad used to run between New York and Chicago.

rows.title: Buck Privates
rows.cast: Abbott and Costello, Lee Bowman, Jane Frazee
rows.extract: Buck Privates is a 1941 musical military comedy film that turned Bud Abbott and Lou Costello into bona fide movie stars. rows.title: Burma Convoy
rows.cast: Charles Bickford, Evelyn Ankers, Cecil Kellaway
rows.extract: Burma Convoy is a 1941 film about a truck convoy on the Burma Road directed by Noel M. Smith and starring Charles Bickford and Evelyn Ankers.

rows.extract: Charley's Aunt is a 1941 American historical comedy film directed by Archie Mayo. It stars Jack Benny and Kay Francis. It was the third filmed version of the 1892 stage farce of the same name by Brandon Thomas. It remained one of Benny's personal favourites among his own films.

rows.title: Charlie Chan in Rio
rows.cast: Sidney Toler, Victor Sen Yung, Kay Linaker
rows.extract: Charlie Chan in Rio is a 1941 film featuring the Asian detective Charlie Chan. It was the tenth film to feature Sidney Toler as the title character, who is called upon to investigate the death of a suspected murderer in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

rows.cast: Martha Scott, William Gargan, Edmund Gwenn
rows.extract: Cheers for Miss Bishop is a 1941 American drama film based on the novel Miss Bishop by Bess Streeter Aldrich. It was directed by Tay Garnett and stars Martha Scott in the title role. rows.extract: A Dangerous Game is a 1941 American mystery film directed by John Rawlins and starring Richard Arlen, Andy Devine and Jean Brooks. It is part of Universal Pictures's Aces of Action series. The New York Times called the film "a crack-brained murder mystery."

rows.title: Dangerous Lady
rows.cast: Neil Hamilton, June Storey, Evelyn Brent
rows.extract: Dangerous Lady is a 1941 American crime film directed by Bernard B. Ray and written by Jack Natteford. rows.cast: John Garfield, Nancy Coleman, Raymond Massey
rows.extract: Dangerously They Live is a 1941 American World War II spy film directed by Robert Florey and starring John Garfield, Nancy Coleman and Raymond Massey. The plot concerns Nazi spies who try to pry information out of a British agent.

rows.cast: Sidney Toler, Sheila Ryan, Kay Aldridge

rows.title: Death Valley Outlaws

rows.extract: The Devil Pays Off is a 1941 American spy film directed by John H. Auer. The film was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Sound Recording.

rows.extract: Dive Bomber is a 1941 American aviation film from Warner Bros. Pictures, directed by Michael Curtiz, and starring Errol Flynn and Fred MacMurray. The film is notable for both its Technicolor photography of pre-World War II United States Navy aircraft and as a historical document of the U.S. in 1941.

rows.extract: Doctors Don't Tell is a 1941 American drama film directed by Jacques Tourneur and written by Theodore Reeves and Isabel Dawn. The film stars John Beal, Florence Rice, Edward Norris, Ward Bond, Douglas Fowley and Grady Sutton.

rows.cast: William Boyd, Andy Clyde, Russell Hayden
rows.extract: Doomed Caravan is a 1941 American Western film directed by Lesley Selander and starring William Boyd. The film is a serial Western and part of the Hopalong Cassidy series. It is the 32nd entry in a series of 66 films.

rows.title: Double Cross

rows.extract: Double Cross is a 1941 American Producers Releasing Corporation crime film directed by Albert H. Kelley and starring serial star Kane Richmond. The film is also known as Motorcycle Squad.

rows.title: The Face Behind the Mask
rows.cast: Peter Lorre, Evelyn Keyes
rows.extract: The Face Behind the Mask is a 1941 American film noir crime film directed by Robert Florey and starring Peter Lorre. The screenplay was adapted by Paul Jarrico, Arthur Levinson, and Allen Vincent from the play Interim, written by Thomas Edward O'Connell.

rows.title: Father Takes a Wife
rows.cast: Adolphe Menjou, Gloria Swanson, Desi Arnaz
rows.extract: Father Takes a Wife is a 1941 American comedy film starring Gloria Swanson and Adolphe Menjou. Silent screen queen Gloria Swanson returned to films after a seven-year absence. Eight years later, Swanson staged another comeback in the classic Sunset Boulevard (1950).

rows.title: Father's Son
rows.cast: John Litel, Frieda Inescort
rows.extract: Father's Son is a 1941 American drama film directed by D. Ross Lederman and written by Fred Niblo Jr. and Booth Tarkington. The film stars John Litel, Frieda Inescort, Billy Dawson and Christian Rub. The film was released by Warner Bros. on February 12, 1941.

rows.title: Father Steps Out
rows.cast: Frank Albertson, Lorna Gray
rows.extract: Father Steps Out is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Jean Yarbrough and starring Frank Albertson, Jed Prouty, Lorna Gray and Frank Faylen. It is a remake of the 1934 film City Limits.

rows.title: Federal Fugitives
rows.cast: Neil Hamilton, Victor Varconi
rows.extract: Federal Fugitives is a 1941 American film noir directed by William Beaudine. The film stars Neil Hamilton, Doris Day, Victor Varconi, and Charles C. Wilson.

rows.title: The Feminine Touch
rows.cast: Rosalind Russell, Don Ameche, Kay Francis
rows.extract: The Feminine Touch is a 1941 American comedy film directed by W.S. Van Dyke, and starring Rosalind Russell and Don Ameche.

rows.title: Fiesta
rows.cast: Ann Ayars, Armida, Antonio Moreno
rows.extract: Fiesta is a 1941 American Technicolor film directed by LeRoy Prinz that was one of Hal Roach's Streamliners. The film was the motion picture debut of the Los Angeles Civic Light Opera star Anne Ayars.

rows.title: Fighting Bill Fargo
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Fuzzy Knight, Jean Brooks
rows.extract: Fighting Bill Fargo is a 1941 American Western film directed by Ray Taylor and written by Paul Franklin, Arthur V. Jones and Dorcas Cochran. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Fuzzy Knight, Jean Brooks, Kenneth Harlan, Nell O'Day and Ted Adams. The film was released on December 9, 1941, by Universal

rows.title: The Flame of New Orleans
rows.cast: Marlene Dietrich, Mischa Auer, Roland Young
rows.extract: The Flame of New Orleans is a 1941 comedy film directed by René Clair and starring Marlene Dietrich and Bruce Cabot in his first comedy role. The supporting cast features Roland Young, Andy Devine and Franklin Pangborn.

rows.title: Flight from Destiny
rows.cast: Geraldine Fitzgerald, Jeffrey Lynn
rows.extract: Flight from Destiny is a 1941 American drama film directed by Vincent Sherman and written by Barry Trivers. The film stars Geraldine Fitzgerald, Thomas Mitchell, Jeffrey Lynn, James Stephenson, Mona Maris and Jonathan Hale. The film was released by Warner Bros. on February 8, 1941.

rows.title: Flying Blind
rows.cast: Jean Parker, Richard Arlen, Nils Asther
rows.extract: Flying Blind is a 1941 American action and comedy film directed by Frank McDonald and distributed by Paramount Pictures. The film was the second movie from Pine-Thomas Productions. That company's first three films formed an unofficial "aviation trilogy"; all starred Richard Arlen.

rows.title: Flying Cadets
rows.cast: William Gargan, Edmund Lowe, Peggy Moran
rows.extract: Flying Cadets is a 1941 American adventure film directed by Erle C. Kenton and written by George Waggner, Roy Chanslor and Stanley Rubin. The film stars William Gargan, Edmund Lowe, Peggy Moran, Frank Albertson, Frankie Thomas and Riley Hill. Flying Cadets was released on October 24, 1941, by Univer

rows.title: Flying Wild
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, David Gorcey
rows.extract: Flying Wild is a 1941 film directed by William Beaudine under the pseudonym "William West" as the fifth installment of the East Side Kids series which eventually totaled 22 films. The film is the team's first one in the spy film genre.

rows.title: Footlight Fever
rows.cast: Alan Mowbray, Donald MacBride, Elyse Knox
rows.extract: Footlight Fever is a 1941 sequel to the 1940 comedy Curtain Call, with Alan Mowbray and Donald MacBride.

rows.title: Footsteps in the Dark
rows.cast: Errol Flynn, Brenda Marshall, Ralph Bellamy
rows.extract: Footsteps in the Dark is a light-hearted 1941 mystery film, starring Errol Flynn as an amateur detective investigating a murder.

rows.title: For Beauty's Sake
rows.cast: Marjorie Weaver, Ned Sparks, Joan Davis
rows.extract: For Beauty's Sake is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Shepard Traube and written by Walter Bullock, Ethel Hill and Wanda Tuchock. The film stars Ned Sparks, Marjorie Weaver, Ted North, Joan Davis, Pierre Watkin and Lenita Lane. The film was released on June 6, 1941, by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Forbidden Trails
rows.cast: Buck Jones, Tim McCoy, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: Forbidden Trails is a 1941 American Western film directed by Robert N. Bradbury and written by Adele Buffington. This is the third film in Monogram Pictures' Rough Riders series, and stars Buck Jones as Marshal Buck Roberts, Tim McCoy as Marshal Tim McCall and Raymond Hatton as Marshal Sandy Hopkins

rows.title: Forced Landing
rows.cast: Richard Arlen, Eva Gabor, J. Carrol Naish, Nils Asther, Evelyn Brent
rows.extract: Forced Landing is a 1941 American action film directed by Gordon Wiles and distributed by Paramount Pictures. The film recounts the exploits of a pilot in Mosaque, an imaginary country in the midst of turmoil. Forced Landing stars Richard Arlen, Eva Gabor, J. Carrol Naish, Nils Asther and Evelyn Bre

rows.title: Four Mothers
rows.cast: Priscilla Lane, Rosemary Lane, Lola Lane
rows.extract: Four Mothers is a 1941 American drama film and sequel to Four Daughters (1938) and Four Wives (1939). The film stars Claude Rains, Jeffrey Lynn, May Robson and featuring the Lane Sisters: Priscilla Lane, Rosemary Lane and Lola Lane. It was directed by William Keighley and is based on the story "Sist

rows.title: Free and Easy
rows.cast: Robert Cummings, Ruth Hussey
rows.extract: Free and Easy is a 1941 film directed by George Sidney, and starring Robert Cummings and Ruth Hussey. The film is a remake of MGM's But the Flesh Is Weak (1932) with Robert Montgomery and C. Aubrey Smith as the son-and-father team.

rows.title: Fugitive Valley
rows.cast: Ray Corrigan, Max Terhune, Julie Duncan
rows.extract: Fugitive Valley is a 1941 American Western film directed by S. Roy Luby. The film is the eighth in Monogram Pictures' "Range Busters" series, and it stars Ray "Crash" Corrigan as Crash, John "Dusty" King as Dusty and Max "Alibi" Terhune as Alibi, with Julie Duncan, Glenn Strange and Bob Kortman.

rows.title: Gambling Daughters
rows.cast: Cecilia Parker, Gale Storm
rows.extract: Gambling Daughters is a 1941 American mystery film directed by Max Nosseck and starring Cecilia Parker, Roger Pryor and Robert Baldwin.

rows.title: Gangs of Sonora
rows.cast: Robert Livingston, Bob Steele, Rufe Davis
rows.extract: Gangs of Sonora is a 1941 American Western "Three Mesquiteers" B-movie directed by John English.

rows.title: The Gang's All Here
rows.cast: Frankie Darro, Mantan Moreland, Robert Homans
rows.extract: The Gang's All Here (1941) is an American black-and-white feature film starring Frankie Darro, Mantan Moreland, Marcia Mae Jones, and Jackie Moran in a story about a trucking company targeted by saboteurs. The film was directed by Jean Yarbrough, produced by Lindsley Parsons, and is one of several t

rows.title: Gauchos of El Dorado
rows.cast: Bob Steele, Tom Tyler, Rufe Davis
rows.extract: Gauchos of Eldorado is a 1941 American Western "Three Mesquiteers" B-movie directed by Lester Orlebeck.

rows.title: The Gay Falcon
rows.cast: George Sanders, Wendy Barrie, Allen Jenkins
rows.extract: The Gay Falcon is a 1941 B film, the first in a series of 16 films about a suave detective nicknamed The Falcon. Intended to replace the earlier The Saint detective series, the first film took its title from the lead character, Gay Laurence. George Sanders was cast in the title role; he had played T

rows.title: The Gay Vagabond
rows.cast: Roscoe Karns, Ruth Donnelly, Margaret Hamilton
rows.extract: The Gay Vagabond is a 1941 American comedy film directed by William Morgan and written by Ewart Adamson and Taylor Caven. The film stars Roscoe Karns, Ruth Donnelly, Ernest Truex, Margaret Hamilton, Abner Biberman and Bernadene Hayes. The film was released on May 12, 1941, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Gentleman from Dixie
rows.cast: Jack La Rue, Marian Marsh, Clarence Muse
rows.extract: Gentleman from Dixie is a 1941 American drama film directed by Albert Herman and starring Jack La Rue, Marian Marsh and Clarence Muse.

rows.title: The Get-Away
rows.cast: Robert Sterling, Donna Reed, Charles Winninger
rows.extract: The Get-Away is a 1941 film directed by Edward Buzzell. It stars Robert Sterling, Charles Winninger and Donna Reed. It is a remake of Public Hero No. 1.

rows.title: A Girl, a Guy and a Gob
rows.cast: Lucille Ball, George Murphy, Edmond O'Brien
rows.extract: A Girl, a Guy and a Gob is a 1941 film produced by Harold Lloyd and starring George Murphy, Lucille Ball, and Edmond O'Brien.

rows.title: The Girl in the News
rows.cast: Margaret Lockwood, Barry K. Barnes, Emlyn Williams
rows.extract: The Girl in the News is a 1940 British thriller film directed by Carol Reed and starring Margaret Lockwood, Barry K. Barnes and Emlyn Williams. It was based on the eponymous novel by Roy Vickers, released the same year.

rows.title: Glamour Boy
rows.cast: Jackie Cooper, Susanna Foster
rows.extract: Glamour Boy is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Ralph Murphy and written by Val Burton, F. Hugh Herbert and Bradford Ropes. rows.title: Golden Hoofs
rows.cast: Jane Withers, Buddy Rogers, Kay Aldridge
rows.extract: Golden Hoofs is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Lynn Shores and written by Ben Grauman Kohn. The film stars Jane Withers, Charles "Buddy" Rogers, Kay Aldridge, George Irving, Buddy Pepper and Cliff Clark. The film was released on February 14, 1941, by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Go West, Young Lady
rows.cast: Ann Miller, Glenn Ford, Ann Miller
rows.extract: Go West, Young Lady is a 1941 American comedy Western film directed by Frank R. Strayer and starring Penny Singleton, Glenn Ford and Ann Miller.

rows.title: Great Guns
rows.cast: Laurel and Hardy, Sheila Ryan, Mae Marsh
rows.extract: Great Guns is a 1941 film directed by Monty Banks, and produced by Sol M. Wurtzel for 20th Century Fox starring Laurel and Hardy. It is also known as Forward March.

rows.title: The Great American Broadcast
rows.cast: Alice Faye, John Payne, Jack Oakie
rows.extract: The Great American Broadcast is a 1941 comedy film directed by Archie Mayo. It stars Jack Oakie, Alice Faye and John Payne.

rows.title: The Great Awakening
rows.cast: Ilona Massey, Alan Curtis
rows.extract: The Great Awakening is a 1941 American historical musical drama film starring Alan Curtis, Ilona Massey, and Billy Gilbert. Directed by Reinhold Schünzel, the film was produced by Gloria Pictures Corporation, and released by United Artists. Miklós Rózsa was responsible for the musical direction, tho

rows.title: The Great Lie
rows.cast: Mary Astor, Bette Davis, George Brent
rows.extract: The Great Lie is a 1941 American drama film directed by Edmund Goulding, and starring Bette Davis, George Brent and Mary Astor. The screenplay by Lenore J. Coffee is based on the novel January Heights by Polan Banks.

rows.title: The Great Mr. Nobody
rows.cast: Eddie Albert, Joan Leslie, John Litel
rows.extract: The Great Mr. Nobody is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Benjamin Stoloff and written by Ben Markson and Kenneth Gamet. The film stars Eddie Albert, Joan Leslie, Alan Hale, Sr., William Lundigan, John Litel, Charles Trowbridge and Paul Hurst. The film was released by Warner Bros. on February

rows.title: The Great Swindle
rows.cast: Jack Holt, Marjorie Reynolds, Henry Kolker
rows.extract: The Great Swindle is a 1941 American mystery film directed by Lewis D. Collins and starring Jack Holt, Jonathan Hale and Henry Kolker.

rows.title: The Great Train Robbery
rows.cast: Bob Steele, Claire Carleton, Milburn Stone
rows.extract: The Great Train Robbery is a 1941 American low-budget B-western film. It was directed by Joseph Kane and starred Bob Steele and Claire Carleton. It was remade in 1949 as The Last Bandit and again in 1952 as South Pacific Trail.

rows.title: The Gunman from Bodie
rows.cast: Buck Jones, Tim McCoy, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: The Gunman from Bodie is a 1941 American Western film directed by Spencer Gordon Bennet and written by Adele Buffington. This is the second film in Monogram Pictures' Rough Riders series, and stars Buck Jones as Marshal Buck Roberts, Tim McCoy as Marshal Tim McCall and Raymond Hatton as Marshal Sand

rows.title: H. M. Pulham, Esq.
rows.cast: Robert Young, Hedy Lamarr, Ruth Hussey
rows.extract: H. M. Pulham, Esq. is a 1941 American drama film directed by King Vidor and starring Hedy Lamarr, Robert Young, and Ruth Hussey. Based on the novel H. M. Pulham, Esq. by John P. Marquand, the film is about a middle-aged businessman who has lived a conservative life according to the routine conventio

rows.title: Hands Across the Rockies
rows.cast: Bill Elliott
rows.extract: Hands Across the Rockies is a 1941 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and starring Bill Elliott.

rows.title: The Hard-Boiled Canary
rows.cast: Susanna Foster, Allan Jones, Margaret Lindsay
rows.extract: The Hard-Boiled Canary is a 1941 American musical comedy film directed by Andrew L. Stone and written by Robert Lively and Andrew L. Stone. It was later reissued as There's Magic in Music.

rows.title: Hard Guy
rows.cast: Jack LaRue, Mary Healy, Iris Adrian
rows.extract: Hard Guy is a 1941 American film directed by Elmer Clifton.

rows.title: Harmon of Michigan
rows.cast: Tom Harmon, Anita Louise, Larry Parks
rows.extract: Harmon of Michigan is a 1941 American film starring Anita Louise and Larry Parks. Ostensibly a biopic about University of Michigan football player Tom Harmon's post-collegiate career as a coach, it was actually filmed immediately upon his graduation and is thus entirely fictional. Harmon, who was an

rows.title: Harvard, Here I Come
rows.cast: Maxie Rosenbloom, Arline Judge
rows.extract: Harvard, Here I Come! is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Lew Landers and stars Max 'Slapsie Maxie' Rosenbloom, Arline Judge, Stanley Brown, Don Beddoe, Marie Wilson, and Virginia Sale. The film is also known as Here I Come in the United Kingdom.

rows.title: Hello, Sucker
rows.cast: Hugh Herbert, Peggy Moran, June Storey
rows.extract: Hello, Sucker is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Edward F. Cline and written by Maurice Leo and Paul Gerard Smith. The film stars Hugh Herbert, Tom Brown, Peggy Moran, Lewis Howard, June Storey, Walter Catlett and Robert Emmett Keane. The film was released on July 11, 1941, by Universal Pict

rows.title: Hellzapoppin'
rows.cast: Ole Olsen, Chic Johnson, Martha Raye
rows.extract: Hellzapoppin' is a 1941 American musical comedy film, and an adaptation of the stage musical of the same name that ran on Broadway from 1938 to 1941. The film is directed by H. C. Potter and distributed by Universal Pictures. Although the entire Broadway cast was initially slated to feature in the f

rows.title: Henry Aldrich for President
rows.cast: Jimmy Lydon, Mary Anderson
rows.extract: Henry Aldrich for President is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Hugh Bennett and written by Val Burton. The film stars Jimmy Lydon, June Preisser, Mary Anderson, Charles Smith, John Litel, Dorothy Peterson and Martha O'Driscoll. The film was released on October 24, 1941, by Paramount Pictures

rows.title: Here Comes Happiness
rows.cast: Mildred Coles, Edward Norris, Richard Ainley
rows.extract: Here Comes Happiness is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Noel M. Smith and written by Charles L. Tedford. The film stars Mildred Coles, Edward Norris, Richard Ainley, Russell Hicks, Marjorie Gateson and John Ridgely. The film was released by Warner Bros. on March 15, 1941.

rows.title: Here Comes Mr. Jordan
rows.cast: Robert Montgomery, Evelyn Keyes, Claude Rains
rows.extract: Here Comes Mr. Jordan is a 1941 American fantasy romantic comedy film directed by Alexander Hall, in which a boxer, mistakenly taken to Heaven before his time, is given a second chance back on Earth. It stars Robert Montgomery, Claude Rains and Evelyn Keyes.

rows.title: Her First Beau
rows.cast: Jane Withers, Jackie Cooper, Josephine Hutchinson
rows.extract: Her First Beau is a 1941 comedy-drama directed by Theodore Reed and starring Jane Withers and Jackie Cooper. The film was produced by Columbia Pictures, and the screenplay was written by Gladys Lehman and Karen DeWolf based on the 1939 play June Mad by Florence Ryerson and Colin Clements, which was

rows.title: High Sierra
rows.cast: Ida Lupino, Humphrey Bogart, Joan Leslie, Arthur Kennedy, Cornel Wilde
rows.extract: High Sierra is a 1941 American film noir directed by Raoul Walsh, written by William R. Burnett and John Huston from the novel by Burnett, and starring Ida Lupino and Humphrey Bogart. Its plot follows a career criminal who becomes involved in a jewel heist in a resort town in California's Sierra Nev

rows.title: Highway West
rows.cast: Brenda Marshall, Arthur Kennedy, William Lundigan
rows.extract: Highway West is a 1941 American crime film directed by William C. McGann and starring Brenda Marshall, Arthur Kennedy and William Lundigan. It is a remake of the 1934 film Heat Lightning.

rows.title: Hit the Road
rows.cast: Gladys George, Barton MacLane, Dead End Kids
rows.extract: Hit the Road is a 1941 crime comedy film featuring the Dead End Kids and Little Tough Guys.

rows.title: Hold Back the Dawn
rows.cast: Charles Boyer, Olivia de Havilland, Paulette Goddard
rows.extract: Hold Back the Dawn is a 1941 American romantic drama film in which a Romanian gigolo marries an American woman in Mexico in order to gain entry to the United States, but winds up falling in love with her. It stars Charles Boyer, Olivia de Havilland, Paulette Goddard, Victor Francen, Walter Abel, Cur

rows.title: Hold That Ghost
rows.cast: Abbott and Costello, Richard Carlson, Joan Davis
rows.extract: Hold That Ghost is a 1941 horror comedy film starring the comedy team of Abbott and Costello and featuring Joan Davis, Evelyn Ankers and Richard Carlson.

rows.title: Honeymoon for Three
rows.cast: Ann Sheridan, George Brent, Jane Wyman
rows.extract: Honeymoon for Three is a 1941 romantic comedy film directed by Lloyd Bacon. It is a remake of the 1933 film Goodbye Again.

rows.title: Honky Tonk
rows.cast: Clark Gable, Lana Turner, Claire Trevor, Frank Morgan, Chill Wills
rows.extract: Honky Tonk is a 1941 black-and-white Western film directed by Jack Conway, produced by Pandro S. Berman, and starring Clark Gable and Lana Turner. The supporting cast features Claire Trevor, Frank Morgan, Marjorie Main, Albert Dekker and Chill Wills.

rows.title: Honolulu Lu
rows.cast: Lupe Vélez, Bruce Bennett, Leo Carrillo
rows.extract: Honolulu Lu is a 1941 American musical film directed by Charles Barton and written by Eliot Gibbons. The film stars Lupe Vélez, Bruce Bennett, Leo Carrillo, Marjorie Gateson, Don Beddoe and Forrest Tucker. The film was released December 11, 1941, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Horror Island
rows.cast: Dick Foran, Peggy Moran, Leo Carrillo
rows.extract: Horror Island is a 1941 American mystery and horror film directed by George Waggner. It was based on the short story "Terror of the South Seas" by Alex Gottlieb. It stars Dick Foran, Peggy Moran, Leo Carrillo, Eddie Parker, Dale Van Sickle, John Eldredge, Lewis Howard, Hobart Cavanaugh, Iris Adrian

rows.title: How Green Was My Valley
rows.cast: Walter Pidgeon, Maureen O'Hara, Roddy McDowall, Donald Crisp
rows.extract: How Green Was My Valley is a 1941 American drama film set in Wales, directed by John Ford. The film, based on the bestselling 1939 novel of the same name by Richard Llewellyn, was produced by Darryl F. Zanuck and scripted by Philip Dunne. It stars Walter Pidgeon, Maureen O'Hara, Anna Lee, Donald Cri

rows.title: Hudson's Bay
rows.cast: Paul Muni, Gene Tierney, Virginia Field
rows.extract: Hudson's Bay is a 1941 American adventure historical western film directed by Irving Pichel and starring Paul Muni and Gene Tierney. Produced by 20th Century Fox, the film is about a pair of French-Canadian explorers whose findings lead to the formation of the Hudson's Bay Company.

rows.title: Hurricane Smith
rows.cast: Ray Middleton, Jane Wyatt, Harry Davenport
rows.extract: Hurricane Smith is a 1941 American action film directed by Bernard Vorhaus and written by Robert Presnell Sr.. The film stars Ray Middleton, Jane Wyatt, Harry Davenport, J. Edward Bromberg, Henry Brandon and Casey Johnson. The film was released on July 20, 1941, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Hurry, Charlie, Hurry
rows.cast: Leon Errol, Mildred Coles
rows.extract: Hurry, Charlie, Hurry is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Charles E. Roberts and written by Paul Gerard Smith. The film stars Leon Errol, Mildred Coles, Kenneth Howell, Cecil Cunningham and George Watts. The film was released on June 13, 1941, by RKO Pictures.

rows.title: I Killed That Man
rows.cast: Ricardo Cortez, Joan Woodbury, Iris Adrian
rows.extract: I Killed That Man is a 1941 American film directed by Phil Rosen that was a remake of his 1933 film The Devil's Mate. It starred Ricardo Cortez and was produced by the King Brothers.

rows.title: I Wake Up Screaming
rows.cast: Betty Grable, Victor Mature, Carole Landis
rows.extract: I Wake Up Screaming is a 1941 film noir. It is based on the novel of the same name by Steve Fisher, adapted by Dwight Taylor. The film stars Betty Grable, Victor Mature and Carole Landis, and features one of Grable's few dramatic roles.

rows.title: I Wanted Wings
rows.cast: Ray Milland, William Holden, Brian Donlevy
rows.extract:
I Wanted Wings is a 1941 American drama film directed by Mitchell Leisen and based on a book by Lieutenant Beirne Lay Jr. The film stars Ray Milland and William Holden. The supporting cast includes Wayne Morris, Brian Donlevy, Constance Moore and Veronica Lake. 

I Wanted Wings features Lake's first

rows.title: I Was a Prisoner on Devil's Island
rows.cast: Sally Eilers, Donald Woods, Eduardo Ciannelli
rows.extract: I Was a Prisoner on Devil's Island is a 1941 American crime film directed by Lew Landers and written by Karl Brown. The film stars Sally Eilers, Donald Woods, Eduardo Ciannelli, Victor Kilian, Charles Halton and Dick Curtis. The film was released on August 4, 1941, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Ice-Capades
rows.cast: James Ellison, Phil Silvers, Barbara Jo Allen
rows.extract: Ice-Capades is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Joseph Santley and starring James Ellison, Phil Silvers, and Barbara Jo Allen. rows.title: I'll Sell My Life
rows.cast: Rose Hobart, Michael Whalen, Joan Woodbury
rows.extract: I'll Sell My Life is a 1941 American crime film directed by Elmer Clifton and starring Rose Hobart, Michael Whalen and Joan Woodbury.

rows.title: I'll Wait for You
rows.cast: Robert Sterling, Marsha Hunt, Carol Hughes
rows.extract: I'll Wait for You is a 1941 American drama film directed by Robert B. Sinclair and written by Guy Trosper. rows.title: In Old Cheyenne
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Joan Woodbury
rows.extract: In Old Cheyenne is a 1941 American Western film directed by Joseph Kane and starring Roy Rogers.

rows.title: In Old Colorado
rows.cast: William Boyd, Russell Hayden, Margaret Hayes
rows.extract: In Old Colorado is a 1941 American Western film directed by Howard Bretherton and written by J. Benton Cheney, Russell Hayden and Norton S. Parker. rows.title: In the Navy
rows.cast: Abbott and Costello, Dick Powell, Claire Dodd
rows.extract: In the Navy is a 1941 film starring the comedy team of Abbott and Costello. It was the second service comedy based on the peacetime draft of 1940. rows.title: International Lady
rows.cast: George Brent, Ilona Massey, Basil Rathbone
rows.extract: International Lady is a 1941 American spy-drama film directed by Tim Whelan and starring George Brent, Ilona Massey and Basil Rathbone.

rows.title: International Squadron
rows.cast: Ronald Reagan, Olympe Bradna, James Stephenson
rows.extract: International Squadron is a 1941 American war film directed by Lewis Seiler and Lothar Mendes that starred Ronald Reagan, Olympe Bradna and in his final film, James Stephenson. The film is based on the Eagle Squadrons, American pilots who volunteered to fly for the Royal Air Force during World War I

rows.title: Invisible Ghost
rows.cast: Bela Lugosi, Polly Ann Young
rows.extract: Invisible Ghost is a 1941 American horror film directed by Joseph H. Lewis, produced by Sam Katzman and starring Bela Lugosi.

rows.title: It Started with Eve
rows.cast: Deanna Durbin, Charles Laughton, Robert Cummings
rows.extract: It Started with Eve is a 1941 American musical romantic comedy film directed by Henry Koster and starring Deanna Durbin, Robert Cummings, and Charles Laughton. rows.title: Jesse James at Bay
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Sally Payne
rows.extract: Jesse James at Bay is a 1941 American Western film directed by Joseph Kane starring Roy Rogers and George "Gabby" Hayes.

rows.title: Johnny Eager
rows.cast: Robert Taylor, Lana Turner, Edward Arnold
rows.extract: Johnny Eager is a 1941 film noir directed by Mervyn LeRoy and starring Robert Taylor, Lana Turner and Van Heflin. Heflin won an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor. The film was one of many spoofed in Dead Men Don't Wear Plaid (1982).

rows.title: Jungle Man
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Sheila Darcy
rows.extract:
Jungle Man is a 1941 American film directed by Harry L. Fraser and starring Buster Crabbe in his first of many films for Producers Releasing Corporation. He is reunited with Charles B. Middleton from the Flash Gordon serials. Cinematographer and associate producer Mervyn Freeman (1890–1965) 
was an

rows.title: Kansas Cyclone
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Lynn Merrick, Dorothy Sebastian
rows.extract: Kansas Cyclone is a 1941 American Western film directed by George Sherman and written by Oliver Drake and Doris Schroeder. The film stars Don "Red" Barry, Lynn Merrick, William Haade, Milton Kibbee, Harry Worth and Dorothy Sebastian. The film was released on June 24, 1941, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Kathleen
rows.cast: Shirley Temple, Gail Patrick, Laraine Day
rows.extract: Kathleen is a 1941 American comedy-drama film starring Shirley Temple in her first comeback role since "retiring" from the screen a year earlier. It was the only movie she made for Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer.

rows.title: Keep 'Em Flying
rows.cast: Abbott and Costello, Martha Raye, Carol Bruce
rows.extract: Keep 'Em Flying is a 1941 film starring the comedy team of Abbott and Costello. The film was their third service comedy based on the peacetime draft of 1940. The comedy team had appeared in two previous service comedies in 1941, before the United States entered the war: Buck Privates, released in Ja

rows.title: The Kid from Kansas
rows.cast: Leo Carillo, Andy Devine, Ann Doran
rows.extract: The Kid from Kansas  is a 1941 American drama set on a fictional island banana plantation owned by Juan Garcia Pancho. rows.title: The Kid's Last Ride
rows.cast: Ray Corrigan, Max Terhune, Luana Walters
rows.extract: The Kid's Last Ride is a 1941 American Western film directed by S. Roy Luby and written by Earle Snell. rows.title: King of Dodge City
rows.cast: Wild Bill Elliott, Tex Ritter
rows.extract: King of Dodge City is a 1941 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by Gerald Geraghty. The film stars Wild Bill Elliott, Tex Ritter, Judith Linden, Dub Taylor, Guy Usher and Rick Anderson. The film was released on August 14, 1941, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: King of the Zombies
rows.cast: Dick Purcell, Joan Woodbury, Henry Victor
rows.extract: King of the Zombies is a 1941 American zombie comedy film directed by Jean Yarbrough and starring Dick Purcell, Joan Woodbury, and Mantan Moreland. rows.title: Kiss the Boys Goodbye
rows.cast: Mary Martin, Don Ameche, Virginia Dale

rows.extract: The Nurse's Secret is a 1941 murder mystery film directed by Noel M. Smith and starring Lee Patrick as a crime-solving nurse. The supporting cast features Regis Toomey and Julie Bishop.

rows.title: The Officer and the Lady
rows.cast: Rochelle Hudson, Bruce Bennett, Roger Pryor
rows.extract: The Officer and the Lady is a 1941 American crime film directed by Sam White and written by Lambert Hillyer and Joseph Hoffman. The film stars Rochelle Hudson, Bruce Bennett, Roger Pryor, Richard Fiske, Sidney Blackmer and Tom Kennedy. The film was released on October 12, 1941, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: One Foot in Heaven
rows.cast: Fredric March, Martha Scott, Beulah Bondi, Gene Lockhart
rows.extract: One Foot in Heaven is a 1941 American biographical film starring Fredric March, Martha Scott, Beulah Bondi, Gene Lockhart and Elisabeth Fraser. The film was adapted by Casey Robinson from the autobiography by Hartzell Spence. It was directed by Irving Rapper.

rows.title: One Night in Lisbon
rows.cast: Fred MacMurray, Madeleine Carroll, Patricia Morison
rows.extract: One Night in Lisbon is a 1941 American thriller film directed by Edward H. Griffith and starring Fred MacMurray, Madeleine Carroll and Patricia Morison.
