rows.title: Our Wife
rows.cast: Melvyn Douglas, Ruth Hussey, Ellen Drew
rows.extract: Our Wife is a 1941 American romantic comedy film directed by John M. Stahl and starring Melvyn Douglas, Ruth Hussey and Ellen Drew. When a composer comes up with a hit, his ex-wife sets out to break up his romance with another woman and get him back.

rows.title: Out of the Fog
rows.cast: Ida Lupino, John Garfield, Eddie Albert
rows.extract: Out of the Fog is a 1941 American film noir crime drama directed by Anatole Litvak, starring John Garfield, Ida Lupino and Thomas Mitchell. The film was based on the play The Gentle People by Irwin Shaw.

rows.title: Outlaws of Cherokee Trail
rows.cast: Robert Livingston, Bob Steele, Rufe Davis
rows.extract: Outlaws of Cherokee Trail is a 1941 American Western "Three Mesquiteers" B-movie directed by Lester Orlebeck.

rows.title: Outlaws of the Desert
rows.cast: William Boyd, Andy Clyde, Duncan Renaldo
rows.extract: Outlaws of the Desert is a 1941 American Western film directed by Howard Bretherton and written by J. Benton Cheney and Bernard McConville. The film stars William Boyd, Andy Clyde, Brad King, Duncan Renaldo, Luli Deste, Jean Phillips, Forrest Stanley and Nina Guilbert. The film was released on Novem

rows.title: Outlaws of the Panhandle
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Frances Robinson
rows.extract: Outlaws of the Panhandle is a 1941 American Western film directed by Sam Nelson and written by Paul Franklin. The film stars Charles Starrett, Frances Robinson, Stanley Brown, Norman Willis, Ray Teal and Lee Prather. The film was released on February 27, 1941, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Outlaws of the Rio Grande
rows.cast: Tim McCoy, Rex Lease, Charles King
rows.extract: Outlaws of the Rio Grande is a 1941 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and written by George H. Plympton. The film stars Tim McCoy, Virginia Carpenter, Charles King, Ralph Peters, Karl Hackett and Rex Lease. The film was released on February 26, 1941, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: Pacific Blackout
rows.cast: Robert Preston, Martha O'Driscoll, Eva Gabor
rows.extract: Pacific Blackout is a 1941 American mystery thriller film directed by Ralph Murphy and starring Robert Preston, Eva Gabor and Martha O'Driscoll. It was produced and distributed by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: Pals of the Pecos
rows.cast: Robert Livingston, Bob Steele, Rufe Davis
rows.extract: Pals of the Pecos is a 1941 American Western "Three Mesquiteers" B-movie directed by Lester Orlebeck.

rows.title: Paper Bullets
rows.cast: Joan Woodbury, Jack La Rue, Alan Ladd
rows.extract: Paper Bullets is a 1941 American film directed by Phil Rosen and starring Joan Woodbury. It was the first film produced by the King Brothers, launching their career.

rows.title: Parachute Battalion
rows.cast: Robert Preston, Nancy Kelly, Edmond O'Brien, Harry Carey
rows.extract: Parachute Battalion is a 1941 war film directed by Leslie Goodwins and stars Robert Preston and Nancy Kelly. The supporting cast includes Edmond O'Brien, Harry Carey, and Buddy Ebsen.

rows.title: Paris Calling
rows.cast: Elisabeth Bergner, Randolph Scott, Basil Rathbone
rows.extract: Paris Calling is a 1941 war film noir directed by Edwin L. Marin and starring Randolph Scott, Elisabeth Bergner, and Basil Rathbone.

rows.title: The Parson of Panamint
rows.cast: Charlie Ruggles, Ellen Drew, Phillip Terry
rows.extract: The Parson of Panamint is a 1941 American Western film directed by William C. McGann and written by Adrian Scott and Harold Shumate. The film stars Charlie Ruggles, Ellen Drew, Phillip Terry, Joseph Schildkraut, Porter Hall and Henry Kolker. The film was released on July 25, 1941, by Paramount Pictu

rows.title: Passage from Hong Kong
rows.cast: Lucile Fairbanks, Paul Cavanagh, Richard Ainley
rows.extract: Passage from Hong Kong is a 1941 American comedy film directed by D. Ross Lederman and written by Fred Niblo Jr. and Earl Derr Biggers. The film stars Lucile Fairbanks, Douglas Kennedy, Paul Cavanagh, Richard Ainley, Marjorie Gateson and Gloria Holden. The film was released by Warner Bros. in Septem

rows.title: The Penalty
rows.cast: Lionel Barrymore, Edward Arnold, Marsha Hunt
rows.extract: The Penalty is a 1941 American crime film directed by Harold S. Bucquet and written by Harry Ruskin and John C. Higgins. The film stars Edward Arnold, Lionel Barrymore, Marsha Hunt, Robert Sterling, Gene Reynolds and Emma Dunn. The film was released on March 14, 1941, by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer.

rows.title: Penny Serenade
rows.cast: Irene Dunne, Cary Grant, Beulah Bondi, Edgar Buchanan
rows.extract: Penny Serenade is a 1941 American melodrama film directed by George Stevens starring Irene Dunne and Cary Grant as a loving couple who must overcome adversity to keep their marriage and raise a child. Grant was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actor for his performance.

rows.title: The People vs. Dr. Kildare
rows.cast: Lew Ayres, Laraine Day, Bonita Granville
rows.extract: The People vs. Dr. Kildare is a 1941 drama directed by Harold S. Bucquet, starring Lew Ayres, Lionel Barrymore, Bonita Granville, and Laraine Day. Dr. Kildare performs an emergency operation on a crash victim.

rows.title: The Perfect Snob
rows.cast: Lynn Bari, Cornel Wilde, Charles Ruggles
rows.extract: The Perfect Snob is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Ray McCarey and written by Lee Loeb and Harold Buchman. The film stars Charlie Ruggles, Charlotte Greenwood, Lynn Bari, Cornel Wilde, Anthony Quinn and Alan Mowbray. The film was released on December 19, 1941, by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Petticoat Politics
rows.cast: Ruth Donnelly, Roscoe Karns, Polly Moran
rows.extract: Petticoat Politics is a 1941 film, the ninth and final of Republic's Higgins Family series.

rows.title: The Phantom Cowboy
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Virginia Carroll, Milburn Stone
rows.extract: The Phantom Cowboy is a 1941 American Western film directed by George Sherman and written by Doris Schroeder. The film stars Don "Red" Barry, Virginia Carroll, Milburn Stone, Neyle Morrow, Rex Lease and Nick Thompson. The film was released on February 14, 1941, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Pinto Kid
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Louise Currie, Bob Nolan
rows.extract: The Pinto Kid is a 1941 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and starring Charles Starrett, Louise Currie and Bob Nolan.

rows.title: The Pioneers
rows.cast: Tex Ritter, Wanda McKay
rows.extract: The Pioneers is a 1941 American Western film directed by Albert Herman and starring Tex Ritter, Karl Hackett and Wanda McKay.

rows.title: Pirates on Horseback
rows.cast: William Boyd, Russell Hayden, Eleanor Stewart
rows.extract: Pirates on Horseback is a 1941 American Western film directed by Lesley Selander and written by Ethel La Blanche and J. Benton Cheney. The film stars William Boyd, Russell Hayden, Andy Clyde, Eleanor Stewart, Morris Ankrum and William Haade. The film was released on May 23, 1941, by Paramount Pictur

rows.title: The Pittsburgh Kid
rows.cast: Billy Conn, Jean Parker, Veda Ann Borg
rows.extract: The Pittsburgh Kid is a 1941 American sports film directed by Jack Townley and starring Billy Conn, Jean Parker and Dick Purcell.

rows.title: Play Girl
rows.cast: Kay Francis, Mildred Coles
rows.extract: Play Girl is a 1941 romantic comedy film, starring Kay Francis as an aging gold digger who decides to pass on her skills to a young protégée, and featuring James Ellison, Mildred Coles, Nigel Bruce, Margaret Hamilton and Katherine Alexander.

rows.title: Playmates
rows.cast: John Barrymore, Kay Kyser, Lupe Vélez
rows.extract: Playmates is a 1941 American comedy film directed by David Butler and written by James V. Kern. The film stars Kay Kyser, John Barrymore, Lupe Vélez, Ginny Simms, May Robson and Patsy Kelly. It was released on December 26, 1941 by RKO Radio Pictures.

rows.title: Pot o' Gold
rows.cast: James Stewart, Paulette Goddard, Charles Winninger
rows.extract: Pot o' Gold is a 1941 American romantic musical comedy film starring James Stewart and Paulette Goddard, directed by George Marshall, and based on the radio series Pot o' Gold. rows.title: Power Dive
rows.cast: Richard Arlen, Jean Parker, Helen Mack
rows.extract: Power Dive is a 1941 American film directed by James P. Hogan. The film stars Richard Arlen, Jean Parker and Helen Mack.

rows.title: Prairie Pioneers
rows.cast: Robert Livingston, Bob Steele, Rufe Davis
rows.extract: Prairie Pioneers is a 1941 American Western "Three Mesquiteers" B-movie directed by Lester Orlebeck.

rows.title: Prairie Stranger
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Cliff Edwards
rows.extract: Prairie Stranger is a 1941 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by Winston Miller. It is based on the 1936 novel The Medico Rides the Trail by James L. Rubel. rows.title: Public Enemies
rows.cast: Wendy Barrie, Phillip Terry, Edgar Kennedy
rows.extract: Public Enemies is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Albert S. Rogell and written by Edward T. Lowe Jr. and Lawrence Kimble. rows.cast: Robert Montgomery, Ingrid Bergman, Oskar Homolka, George Sanders
rows.extract: Rage in Heaven is a 1941 American psychological thriller film noir about the destructive power of jealousy. It was directed by W.S. Van Dyke and based on the 1932 novel by James Hilton. It features Robert Montgomery, Ingrid Bergman, and George Sanders.

rows.title: Rags to Riches
rows.cast: Alan Baxter, Mary Carlisle, Jerome Cowan
rows.extract: Rags to Riches is a 1941 American crime film directed by Joseph Kane and written by James R. Webb. The film stars Alan Baxter, Mary Carlisle, Jerome Cowan, Adrian Morris, Ralf Harolde and Paul Porcasi. The film was released on July 31, 1941, by Republic Pictures.

rows.cast: Andy Devine, Richard Arlen, Maria Montez
rows.extract: Raiders of the Desert is a 1941 American comedy adventure film directed by John Rawlins and starring Andy Devine, Richard Arlen and Linda Hayes. rows.cast: Joel McCrea, Ellen Drew, Eddie Bracken

The film stars Joel McCrea, Ellen Drew, Eddie Bracken, Albert Dekker, Billy Gilbert, George Chandler and Bodil Ann Rosing. The film was released on May 2, 1941, by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: Red River Valley
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Gabby Hayes, Sally Payne
rows.extract: Red River Valley is a 1941 American Western film about ranchers struggling to build a reservoir. It stars Roy Rogers, Gabby Hayes, and Gale Storm, and the director was Joseph Kane.

rows.title: Redhead
rows.cast: Johnny Downs, June Lang, Eric Blore
rows.extract: Redhead is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Edward L. Cahn and starring Johnny Downs, June Lang, and Eric Blore.

rows.title: Reg'lar Fellers
rows.cast: Billy Lee, Sarah Padden
rows.extract: Reg'lar Fellers is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Arthur Dreifuss and starring Billy Lee, Carl 'Alfalfa' Switzer and Sarah Padden. It was based on the comic strip of the same name. Former silent film star Marguerite De La Motte appears in a supporting role.

rows.title: The Reluctant Dragon
rows.cast: Robert Benchley, Frances Gifford
rows.extract: The Reluctant Dragon is a 1941 American comedy film produced by Walt Disney, directed by Alfred Werker, and released by RKO Radio Pictures on June 27, 1941. rows.title: Remember the Day
rows.cast: Claudette Colbert, John Payne, Shepperd Strudwick
rows.extract: Remember the Day is a 1941 film released by 20th Century Fox, directed by Henry King, and starring Claudette Colbert and John Payne.

rows.cast: Kent Taylor, Wendy Barrie, Thurston Hall

rows.extract: The Richest Man in Town is a 1941 comedy film directed by Charles Barton, which stars Frank Craven, Edgar Buchanan, and Eileen O'Hearn.

rows.title: Ride on Vaquero
rows.cast: Cesar Romero, Mary Beth Hughes, Lynne Roberts
rows.extract: Ride on Vaquero is a 1941 American Western film directed by Herbert I. Leeds and written by Samuel G. Engel. The film stars Cesar Romero, Mary Beth Hughes, Lynne Roberts, Chris-Pin Martin, Robert Lowery and Ben Carter. The film was released on April 18, 1941, by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Riders of the Badlands
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Russell Hayden
rows.extract: Riders of the Badlands is a 1941 American Western film directed by Howard Bretherton and written by Betty Burbridge. The film stars Charles Starrett, Russell Hayden, Cliff Edwards, Ilene Brewer, Kay Hughes and Roy Barcroft. The film was released on December 18, 1941, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Riders of the Purple Sage
rows.cast: George Montgomery, Mary Howard, Lynne Roberts

rows.cast: Tom Keene, Betty Miles
rows.extract: Riding the Sunset Trail is a 1941 American Western film directed by Robert Emmett Tansey and written by Robert Emmett Tansey and Frances Kavanaugh. rows.title: Ringside Maisie
rows.cast: Ann Sothern, George Murphy, Robert Sterling
rows.extract: Ringside Maisie is a 1941 film directed by Edwin L. Marin. It stars Ann Sothern, Robert Sterling and George Murphy. It is the fifth of ten pictures in the Maisie series. This was Sothern and future husband Sterling's only film together.

rows.title: Riot Squad
rows.cast: Richard Cromwell, Rita Quigley, John Miljan

rows.title: Road Show
rows.cast: Carole Landis, Adolphe Menjou, John Hubbard
rows.extract: Road Show is a 1941 American film directed by Hal Roach.

rows.cast: Bob Hope, Bing Crosby, Dorothy Lamour
rows.extract: Road to Zanzibar is a 1941 Paramount Pictures semi-musical comedy film starring Bing Crosby, Bob Hope, and Dorothy Lamour, and marked the second of seven pictures in the popular "Road to …" series made by the trio. It takes place in the Sultanate of Zanzibar.

rows.title: Roar of the Press
rows.cast: Jean Parker, Wallace Ford, Suzanne Kaaren

The Army technical advisor was Captain Jack Voglin who performed the same duty on the 1941 films You're in the Army Now, You'll Never Get Rich, and Buck Privates.

rows.cast: Richard Dix, Patricia Morison, Preston Foster
rows.extract: The Round Up is a 1941 American Western film directed by Lesley Selander and written by Harold Shumate. rows.title: Shining Victory

rows.extract: Shining Victory is a 1941 American drama film based on the 1940 play Jupiter Laughs, by A. J. Cronin. It stars James Stephenson, Geraldine Fitzgerald, Donald Crisp, and Barbara O'Neil. It is the first film directed by Irving Rapper. Bette Davis makes a brief cameo appearance as a nurse.

rows.extract: A Shot in the Dark is a 1941 American drama film directed by William C. McGann and written by M. Coates Webster, starring William Lundigan, Nan Wynn, and Ricardo Cortez. rows.cast: Gene Autry, Fay McKenzie
rows.extract: Sierra Sue is a 1941 American Western film directed by William Morgan and starring Gene Autry, Smiley Burnette, and Fay McKenzie. rows.title: Sign of the Wolf
rows.cast: Michael Whalen, Grace Bradley, Mantan Moreland
rows.extract: Sign of the Wolf is a 1941 American adventure film directed by Howard Bretherton and written by Elizabeth Sutphin and Edmond Kelso. The film stars Michael Whalen, Grace Bradley, Darryl Hickman, Mantan Moreland, Louise Beavers and Wade Crosby. The film was released on March 25, 1941, by Monogram Pict

rows.title: Silver Stallion
rows.cast: David Sharpe, LeRoy Mason

rows.extract: Sing for Your Supper is a 1941 American musical comedy film directed by Charles Barton and starring Jinx Falkenburg.

rows.extract: Singapore Woman is a 1941 American drama film directed by Jean Negulesco and starring Brenda Marshall and David Bruce.

rows.title: The Singing Hill
rows.cast: Gene Autry, Mary Lee, Virginia Dale
rows.extract: The Singing Hill is a 1941 American Western film directed by Lew Landers and starring Gene Autry, Smiley Burnette, and Virginia Dale. rows.cast: Judy Canova, Bob Crosby, Susan Hayward
rows.extract: Sis Hopkins is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Joseph Santley and written by Jack Townley, Milt Gross and Edward Eliscu. rows.extract: Six Gun Gold is a 1941 Western film directed by David Howard and starring Tim Holt.

rows.cast: Lupe Vélez, Leon Errol, Helen Parrish
rows.extract: Six Lessons from Madame La Zonga is a 1941 American comedy film directed by John Rawlins and starring Lupe Vélez. The film was inspired by the same-name song interpreted by Helen O'Connell and Jimmy Dorsey Orchestra.

rows.cast: Claudette Colbert, Ray Milland, Brian Aherne
rows.extract: Skylark is a 1941 American comedy film starring Claudette Colbert, Ray Milland and Brian Aherne and directed by Mark Sandrich. Film historian James H. rows.title: Sleepers West
rows.cast: Lloyd Nolan, Lynn Bari, Mary Beth Hughes
rows.extract: Sleepers West is a 1941 American mystery drama film directed by Eugene Forde and starring Lloyd Nolan, Lynn Bari and Mary Beth Hughes.

rows.title: The Smiling Ghost
rows.cast: Alexis Smith, Wayne Morris, Brenda Marshall
rows.extract: The Smiling Ghost is a 1941 American film directed by Lewis Seiler and starring Wayne Morris, Alexis Smith, and Alan Hale. The film is in the horror comedy genre, which was popular in the 1940s.

rows.title: Smilin' Through
rows.cast: Jeanette MacDonald, Brian Aherne, Ian Hunter
rows.extract: Smilin' Through is a 1941 Technicolor MGM musical film based on the 1919 play of the same name by Jane Cowl and Jane Murfin.

rows.title: So Ends Our Night
rows.cast: Fredric March, Margaret Sullavan, Glenn Ford
rows.extract: So Ends Our Night is a 1941 drama directed by John Cromwell and starring Fredric March, Margaret Sullavan and Glenn Ford. rows.title: The Son of Davy Crockett
rows.cast: Wild Bill Elliott, Iris Meredith, Dub Taylor
rows.extract: The Son of Davy Crockett is a 1941 American Western film written and directed by Lambert Hillyer. The film stars Wild Bill Elliott, Iris Meredith, Dub Taylor, Kenneth MacDonald, Richard Fiske and Eddy Waller. The film was released on July 15, 1941, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: South of Panama
rows.cast: Roger Pryor, Virginia Vale, Lionel Royce
rows.extract: South of Panama is a 1941 American action film directed by Jean Yarbrough and written by Ben Roberts and Sidney Sheldon. The film stars Roger Pryor, Virginia Vale, Lionel Royce, Lucien Prival, Duncan Renaldo and Lester Dorr. The film was released on May 2, 1941, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: South of Tahiti
rows.cast: Maria Montez, Brian Donlevy, Broderick Crawford
rows.extract: South of Tahiti is a 1941 American south seas adventure film directed by George Waggner and starring Brian Donlevy. It helped launch Maria Montez as a pin-up star. She played a leading role; response was such that Universal then cast her in Arabian Nights.

rows.title: Spooks Run Wild
rows.cast: Bela Lugosi, Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall, Bobby Jordan
rows.extract: Spooks Run Wild is a 1941 American horror comedy film and the seventh film in the East Side Kids series. It stars Bela Lugosi with Leo Gorcey, Bobby Jordan and Huntz Hall. rows.title: Steel Against the Sky
rows.cast: Alexis Smith, Lloyd Nolan, Gene Lockhart
rows.extract: Steel Against the Sky is a 1941 American comedy film directed by A. Edward Sutherland, written by Paul Gerard Smith, and starring Lloyd Nolan, Alexis Smith, Craig Stevens, Gene Lockhart, Edward Ellis and Walter Catlett. It was released by Warner Bros. on December 13, 1941.

rows.title: Strange Alibi
rows.cast: Arthur Kennedy, Joan Perry
rows.extract: Strange Alibi is a 1941 American crime film directed by D. Ross Lederman, written by Kenneth Gamet, Leslie T. White and Fred Niblo Jr., and starring Arthur Kennedy, Joan Perry, Jonathan Hale, John Ridgely, Florence Bates and Charles Trowbridge. It was released by Warner Bros. on April 19, 1941.

rows.title: The Strawberry Blonde
rows.cast: James Cagney, Olivia de Havilland, Rita Hayworth
rows.extract: The Strawberry Blonde is a 1941 American romantic comedy film directed by Raoul Walsh, starring James Cagney and Olivia de Havilland, and featuring Rita Hayworth, Alan Hale, Jack Carson, and George Tobias. rows.title: Stick to Your Guns
rows.cast: William Boyd, Jennifer Holt
rows.extract: Stick to Your Guns is a 1941 American Western film directed by Lesley Selander, written by J. Benton Cheney, and starring William Boyd, Andy Clyde, Brad King, Jennifer Holt, Dick Curtis, Weldon Heyburn, and Henry Hall. It was released on September 17, 1941, by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: The Stork Pays Off
rows.cast: Victor Jory, Rochelle Hudson, Maxie Rosenbloom
rows.extract: The Stork Pays Off is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Lew Landers and written by Fanya Foss and Aleen Leslie. The film stars Victor Jory, Rochelle Hudson, Maxie Rosenbloom, Horace McMahon, George McKay and Ralf Harolde. The film was released on October 6, 1941, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.cast: Joel McCrea, Veronica Lake, Robert Warwick
rows.extract: Sullivan's Travels is a 1941 American comedy film written and directed by Preston Sturges. rows.cast: Anna Neagle, Ray Bolger, Edward Everett Horton
rows.extract: Sunny is a 1941 American musical film directed by Herbert Wilcox and starring Anna Neagle, Ray Bolger, John Carroll, Edward Everett Horton, Grace Hartman, Paul Hartman, Frieda Inescort, and Helen Westley. It was adapted by Sig Herzig from the Jerome Kern-Oscar Hammerstein II musical play Sunny.

rows.extract: Sunset in Wyoming is a 1941 American Western film directed by William Morgan and starring Gene Autry, Smiley Burnette, George Cleveland, and Maris Wrixon. rows.cast: William Holden, Glenn Ford, Claire Trevor
rows.extract: Texas is a 1941 American Western film directed by George Marshall and starring William Holden, Glenn Ford and Claire Trevor. Texas was an early picture for both Holden and Ford. rows.cast: Jean Hersholt, Dorothy Lovett, Neil Hamilton

rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Al St. John, Joan Barclay
rows.extract: Billy the Kid's Smoking Guns is a 1942 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Milton Raison and George Wallace Sayre. rows.title: Billy the Kid Trapped
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Anne Jeffreys
rows.extract: Billy the Kid Trapped is a 1942 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield.

rows.title: Black Dragons
rows.cast: Bela Lugosi, Joan Barclay, Robert Frazer
rows.extract: Black Dragons is a 1942 American film directed by William Nigh and starring Bela Lugosi, Joan Barclay, and George Pembroke. rows.title: The Black Swan
rows.cast: Tyrone Power, Maureen O'Hara, Laird Cregar
rows.extract: The Black Swan is a 1942 American swashbuckler Technicolor film directed by Henry King and starring Tyrone Power and Maureen O'Hara. It was based on the 1932 novel of the same title by Rafael Sabatini.

rows.title: Blondie's Blessed Event
rows.cast: Penny Singleton, Arthur Lake, Jonathan Hale
rows.extract: Blondie's Blessed Event is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Frank R. Strayer and starring Penny Singleton, Arthur Lake, and Larry Simms. It is the 11th of the Blondie films. It was the first to feature the character of Cookie.

rows.title: Blondie Goes to College
rows.cast: Penny Singleton, Arthur Lake, Janet Blair
rows.extract: Blondie Goes to College is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Frank R. Strayer. The film is a part of the Blondie series, starring Penny Singleton in the title role. It is the tenth of twenty-eight Blondie movies starring Penny Singleton and Arthur Lake.

rows.title: Blondie for Victory
rows.cast: Penny Singleton, Arthur Lake, Stuart Erwin
rows.extract: Blondie for Victory is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Frank R. Strayer and starring Penny Singleton and Arthur Lake. It is the 12th entry in the Blondie series.

rows.title: Blue, White and Perfect
rows.cast: Lloyd Nolan, Mary Beth Hughes, Helene Reynolds
rows.extract: Blue, White and Perfect is a 1942 American mystery film directed by Herbert I. Leeds and starring Lloyd Nolan, Mary Beth Hughes, and Helene Reynolds. It is part of Twentieth Century Fox's Michael Shayne film series.

rows.title: Bombay Clipper
rows.cast: William Gargan, Maria Montez, Irene Hervey
rows.extract: Bombay Clipper is a 1942 aviation drama film directed by John Rawlins and starring William Gargan and Irene Hervey. The film features Maria Montez in an early role. Turhan Bey also appears.

rows.title: Bombs Over Burma
rows.cast: Anna May Wong, Noel Madison
rows.extract: Bombs Over Burma, based on a story by Milton Raison, is a 1942 American war film directed by Joseph H. Lewis. To depict the Chinese character faithfully, the star, Anna May Wong, and other characters speak Mandarin in the first few minutes of the film.

rows.title: The Boogie Man Will Get You
rows.cast: Boris Karloff
rows.extract: The Boogie Man Will Get You is a 1942 American comedy horror film directed by Lew Landers and starring Boris Karloff and Peter Lorre. It was the final film Karloff made under his contract with Columbia Pictures, and it was filmed in the wake of his success in the 1941 Broadway production Arsenic and

rows.title: Boot Hill Bandits
rows.cast: Ray Corrigan, Max Terhune, Jean Brooks
rows.extract: Boot Hill Bandits is a 1942 American Western film directed by S. Roy Luby. The film is the fourteenth in Monogram Pictures' "Range Busters" series, and it stars Ray "Crash" Corrigan as Crash, John "Dusty" King as Dusty and Max "Alibi" Terhune as Alibi, with Jean Brooks, John Merton and Glenn Strange

rows.title: Border Roundup
rows.cast: George F. Houston, Dennis Moore
rows.extract: Border Roundup is a 1942 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Joseph O'Donnell. The film stars George F. rows.title: Born to Sing
rows.cast: Virginia Weidler, Douglas McPhail
rows.extract: Born to Sing is a 1942 American feature film directed by Edward Ludwig starring Virginia Weidler and Ray McDonald.

rows.title: The Boss of Big Town
rows.cast: Florence Rice, John Litel, H. B. Warner
rows.extract: The Boss of Big Town is a 1942 American film directed by Arthur Dreifuss.

rows.title: Boss of Hangtown Mesa
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Fuzzy Knight, William Farnum
rows.extract: Boss of Hangtown Mesa is a 1942 American Western film directed by Joseph H. Lewis and written by Oliver Drake. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Fuzzy Knight, William Farnum, Rex Lease, Helen Deverell and Hugh Prosser. The film was released on August 21, 1942, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Boston Blackie Goes Hollywood
rows.cast: Chester Morris, Constance Worth
rows.extract: Boston Blackie Goes Hollywood is a 1942 American crime film, fourth of the fourteen Boston Blackie films of the 1940s Columbia's series of B pictures based on Jack Boyle's pulp-fiction character.

rows.title: Bowery at Midnight
rows.cast: Bela Lugosi, John Archer, Wanda McKay
rows.extract: Bowery at Midnight is a 1942 American Monogram Pictures horror film directed by Wallace Fox and starring Bela Lugosi and John Archer. The film was re-released by Astor Pictures in 1949.

rows.title: Broadway
rows.cast: George Raft, Pat O'Brien, Janet Blair
rows.extract: Broadway is a 1942 crime drama musical film directed by William A. Seiter and starring George Raft as himself and Pat O'Brien as a detective. The supporting cast features Janet Blair and Broderick Crawford.

rows.title: Broadway Big Shot
rows.cast: Ralph Byrd, Virginia Vale, Herbert Rawlinson
rows.extract: Broadway Big Shot is a 1942 American drama film directed by William Beaudine.

rows.title: Brooklyn Orchid
rows.cast: William Bendix, Grace Bradley
rows.extract: Brooklyn Orchid is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Kurt Neumann and written by Earle Snell and Clarence Marks that was one of Hal Roach's Streamliners. The film stars William Bendix, Joe Sawyer, Marjorie Woodworth, Grace Bradley, Richard "Skeets" Gallagher, Florine McKinney and Leonid Kinske

rows.title: The Bugle Sounds
rows.cast: Wallace Beery, Marjorie Main, Donna Reed
rows.extract: The Bugle Sounds is a 1942 American World War II movie starring Wallace Beery as a cavalry sergeant resistant to replacing horses with tanks. The supporting cast includes Marjorie Main, Lewis Stone, George Bancroft, Donna Reed, and Chill Wills, and the film was directed by S. Sylvan Simon.

rows.title: Bullet Scars
rows.cast: Regis Toomey, Howard Da Silva, Adele Longmire
rows.extract: Bullet Scars is a 1942 American film produced and distributed by Warner Bros. It was directed by D. Ross Lederman with top-billed stars Regis Toomey, Adele Longmire and Howard da Silva.

rows.title: Bullets for Bandits
rows.cast: Tex Ritter, Wild Bill Elliott
rows.extract: Bullets for Bandits is a 1942 American Western film directed by Wallace W. Fox, starring Wild Bill Elliott, Tex Ritter, and Frank Mitchell.

rows.title: Busses Roar
rows.cast: Richard Travis, Julie Bishop, Eleanor Parker
rows.extract: Busses Roar is a 1942 film directed by D. Ross Lederman and starring Richard Travis and Julie Bishop.

rows.title: Butch Minds the Baby
rows.cast: Virginia Bruce, Broderick Crawford, Dick Foran
rows.extract: Butch Minds the Baby is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Albert S. Rogell and written by Leonard Spigelgass, based on the short story of the same name by Damon Runyon. rows.title: Cadets on Parade
rows.cast: Freddie Bartholomew, Jimmy Lydon, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: Cadets on Parade is a 1942 American drama film directed by Lew Landers and written by Howard J. Green. The film stars Freddie Bartholomew, Jimmy Lydon, Joseph Crehan, Raymond Hatton, Minna Gombell and Robert Warwick. The film was released on January 22, 1942, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Cairo
rows.cast: Jeanette MacDonald, Robert Young, Lionel Atwill
rows.extract: Cairo is a 1942 musical comedy film made by MGM and Loew's, and directed by W. S. Van Dyke. The

rows.cast: Gene Autry, Ruth Terry
rows.extract: Call of the Canyon is a 1942 American Western film directed by Joseph Santley and starring Gene Autry, Smiley Burnette, the Sons of the Pioneers, and Ruth Terry. rows.cast: Victor McLaglen, Edmund Lowe, Binnie Barnes

rows.title: Canal Zone
rows.cast: Chester Morris, Harriet Nelson, Larry Parks
rows.extract: Canal Zone is a 1942 American aviation adventure film starring Chester Morris and Forrest Tucker. The action takes place in the Panama Canal Zone and revolves around aviators in an out-of-the-way air base flying U.S. Army bombers.

rows.title: Captains of the Clouds
rows.cast: James Cagney, Dennis Morgan, Brenda Marshall
rows.extract: Captains of the Clouds is a 1942 American war film in Technicolor, directed by Michael Curtiz and starring James Cagney. It was produced by William Cagney, with Hal B. rows.extract: Casablanca is a 1942 American romantic drama film directed by Michael Curtiz, and starring Humphrey Bogart, Ingrid Bergman, and Paul Henreid. rows.cast: Sidney Toler, Arleen Whelan
rows.extract: Castle in the Desert is a 1942 film featuring the Chinese detective Charlie Chan. rows.extract: Counter-Espionage is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Edward Dmytryk. Counter-Espionage was the ninth film in Columbia's Lone Wolf series, based on characters created by Louis Joseph Vance. It is also known as The Lone Wolf in Scotland Yard.

rows.cast: Lewis Stone, Mickey Rooney, Cecilia Parker, Donna Reed
rows.extract: The Courtship of Andy Hardy is a 1942 film, part of the Andy Hardy series. It gave an early role to Donna Reed although Mickey Rooney had lobbied for his then-wife Ava Gardner to have her part. Within a few months of the film's release, she filed for divorce.

rows.title: Cowboy Serenade

rows.extract: Cowboy Serenade is a 1942 American Western film directed by William Morgan and starring Gene Autry, Smiley Burnette, and Fay McKenzie. rows.cast: William Powell, Hedy Lamarr, Claire Trevor
rows.extract: Crossroads is a 1942 mystery film noir directed by Jack Conway, starring William Powell, Hedy Lamarr, Claire Trevor and Basil Rathbone. rows.title: The Cyclone Kid
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Lynn Merrick
rows.extract: The Cyclone Kid is a 1942 American Western film directed by George Sherman and written by Richard Murphy. The film stars Don "Red" Barry, John James, Lynn Merrick, Alex Callam, Joel Friedkin and Slim Andrews. The film was released on May 31, 1942, by Republic Pictures.

rows.cast: Don Terry, Louise Allbritton
rows.extract: Danger in the Pacific  is a 1942 espionage thriller set on a fictional island during World War II.

rows.title: A Date with the Falcon
rows.cast: George Sanders, Wendy Barrie, Allen Jenkins
rows.extract: A Date with the Falcon is the second in a series of 16 films about the suave detective nicknamed The Falcon. The 1942 sequel features many of the same characters as the first film, The Gay Falcon (1941).

rows.title: The Dawn Express
rows.cast: Michael Whalen, Anne Nagel, Constance Worth
rows.extract: The Dawn Express (aka Dawn Express and Nazi Spy Ring is a 1942 American film directed by Albert Herman. The film stars Michael Whalen, Anne Nagel, William Bakewell and Constance Worth.

rows.title: Destination Unknown
rows.cast: William Gargan, Irene Hervey, Turhan Bey
rows.extract: Destination Unknown is a 1942 American thriller film directed by Ray Taylor and starring William Gargan, Irene Hervey and Sam Levene. It was made as a second feature film by Universal Pictures set in China in World War II.

rows.extract: Down Texas Way is a 1942 American Western film directed by Howard Bretherton and written by Adele Buffington. rows.extract: Dr. Gillespie's New Assistant is a 1942 feature film from MGM in their long-running Dr. Kildare series. Directed by Willis Goldbeck, it introduced two new doctors, Dr. Randall Adams and Dr. Lee Wong How.

rows.cast: J. Carrol Naish, George Zucco, Lynne Roberts
rows.extract: Dr. Renault's Secret is a 1942 American horror mystery film. The story was written by William Bruckner and Robert Metzler. It is loosely based on the 1911 novel Balaoo by Gaston Leroux. rows.title: Drums of the Congo
rows.cast: Ona Munson, Stuart Erwin, Peggy Moran
rows.extract: Drums of the Congo is a 1942 American drama film, directed by Christy Cabanne. It stars Ona Munson, Stuart Erwin, and Peggy Moran, and was released on July 17, 1942.

rows.cast: Ralph Byrd, Stubby Kruger, Veda Ann Borg

rows.title: Enemy Agents Meet Ellery Queen

rows.extract: Enemy Agents Meet Ellery Queen is a 1942 black-and-white thriller film, directed by James P. Hogan and written by Ellery Queen, the duo of Manfred Lee and Frederic Dannay.

rows.title: Escape from Crime
rows.cast: Richard Travis, Jackie Gleason, Julie Bishop
rows.extract: Escape from Crime is a 1942 American crime film directed by D. Ross Lederman. It has essentially the same plot as the earlier Picture Snatcher (1933).

rows.extract: The Falcon's Brother is a 1942 American crime drama film in which George Sanders, who had been portraying "The Falcon" in a series of films, appears with his real-life brother Tom Conway; with Sanders handing off the series to Conway, who would play the new Falcon in nine subsequent films. rows.title: The Gay Sisters
rows.cast: Barbara Stanwyck, George Brent, Geraldine Fitzgerald
rows.extract: The Gay Sisters is a 1942 American drama film directed by Irving Rapper, and starring Barbara Stanwyck, George Brent, Geraldine Fitzgerald, Donald Crisp, Gig Young and Nancy Coleman. The Warner Bros. motion picture was based on a novel by Stephen Longstreet.

rows.title: A Gentleman After Dark
rows.cast: Miriam Hopkins, Brian Donlevy, Preston Foster
rows.extract: A Gentleman After Dark is a 1942 crime/drama film starring Brian Donlevy and Miriam Hopkins.

rows.title: A Gentleman at Heart
rows.cast: Cesar Romero, Carole Landis, Milton Berle
rows.extract: A Gentleman at Heart is a 1942 romantic comedy film starring Cesar Romero, Carole Landis, and Milton Berle. A bookie acquires an interest in an art gallery.

rows.title: Gentleman Jim
rows.cast: Errol Flynn, Alexis Smith, Alan Hale
rows.extract: Gentleman Jim is a 1942 film directed by Raoul Walsh and starring Errol Flynn as heavyweight boxing champion James J. Corbett (1866–1933). The supporting cast includes Alexis Smith, Jack Carson, Alan Hale, William Frawley, and Ward Bond as John L. Sullivan. The movie was based upon Corbett's 1894 au

rows.title: George Washington Slept Here
rows.cast: Jack Benny, Ann Sheridan, Charles Coburn
rows.extract: George Washington Slept Here is a 1942 comedy film starring Jack Benny, Ann Sheridan, Charles Coburn, Percy Kilbride, and Hattie McDaniel. It was based on the 1940 play of the same name by Moss Hart and George S. Kaufman, adapted by Everett Freeman, and was directed by William Keighley.

rows.title: Get Hep to Love
rows.cast: Gloria Jean, Donald O'Connor, Jane Frazee, Peggy Ryan
rows.extract: Get Hep to Love is a 1942 musical film starring Gloria Jean, Donald O'Connor, Jane Frazee, Robert Paige and Peggy Ryan. The film was directed by Charles Lamont.

rows.title: The Ghost of Frankenstein
rows.cast: Lon Chaney Jr., Cedric Hardwicke, Ralph Bellamy
rows.extract: The Ghost of Frankenstein is a 1942 American horror film directed by Erle C. Kenton and starring Cedric Hardwicke, Lon Chaney Jr. and Bela Lugosi. It is the fourth film in the Frankenstein series by Universal Pictures, and the follow-up to Son of Frankenstein (1939). The film's plot follows the prev

rows.title: Ghost Town Law
rows.cast: Buck Jones, Tim McCoy, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: Ghost Town Law is a 1942 American Western film directed by Howard Bretherton and written by Adele Buffington. This is the fifth film in Monogram Pictures' Rough Riders series, and stars Buck Jones as Marshal Buck Roberts, Tim McCoy as Marshal Tim McCall and Raymond Hatton as Marshal Sandy Hopkins, w

rows.title: The Girl from Alaska
rows.cast: Jean Parker, Ray Middleton, Jerome Cowan
rows.extract: The Girl from Alaska is a 1942 American Western film directed by Nick Grinde and William Witney and starring Ray Middleton, Jean Parker and Jerome Cowan.

rows.title: Girl Trouble
rows.cast: Don Ameche, Joan Bennett
rows.extract: Girl Trouble is a 1942 comedy film made by 20th Century Fox, directed by Harold D. Schuster, and starring Don Ameche and Joan Bennett. It is also known as Between You and Me and Man from Brazil.

rows.title: Girls' Town
rows.cast: Edith Fellows, June Storey, Alice White, Anna Q. Nilsson
rows.extract: Girls' Town is a 1942 American drama film directed by Victor Halperin and starring Edith Fellows, June Storey and Alice White.

rows.title: Give Out, Sisters
rows.cast: The Andrews Sisters, Dan Dailey, Donald O'Connor
rows.extract: Give Out, Sisters is a 1942 American film starring The Andrews Sisters. The film co-stars Dan Dailey and the teenage couple of the time, Donald O'Connor and Peggy Ryan. Dailey and O'Connor went on to be in the 1954 film There's No Business Like Show Business. The song "Pennsylvania Polka" was introd

rows.title: The Glass Key
rows.cast: Alan Ladd, Veronica Lake, Brian Donlevy, William Bendix
rows.extract: The Glass Key is a 1942 American crime drama based on the 1931 novel of the same name by Dashiell Hammett. The picture was directed by Stuart Heisler starring Brian Donlevy, Veronica Lake and Alan Ladd. A successful earlier film version starring George Raft in Ladd's role had been released in 1935.

rows.title: Grand Central Murder
rows.cast: Van Heflin, Cecilia Parker, Virginia Grey
rows.extract: Grand Central Murder is a comedy/mystery film released in 1942. It was based on Sue MacVeigh's 1939 novel of the same name, and stars Van Heflin as a private investigator who is one of the suspects in a murder on a private train car in Grand Central Terminal. The film was directed by S. Sylvan Simon

rows.title: The Great Gildersleeve
rows.cast: Harold Peary, Jane Darwell
rows.extract: The Great Gildersleeve is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Gordon Douglas. Based on the popular NBC radio series The Great Gildersleeve created by Leonard L. Levinson, which ran from 1941 to 1950, this is the first of four films in the Gildersleeve series produced and distributed by RKO Radio

rows.title: The Great Man's Lady
rows.cast: Barbara Stanwyck, Joel McCrea, Brian Donlevy
rows.extract: The Great Man's Lady is a 1942 American Western film directed by William A. Wellman and starring Barbara Stanwyck and Joel McCrea. It is based on the short story "The Human Side" by Viña Delmar.

rows.title: The Great Impersonation
rows.cast: Ralph Bellamy, Evelyn Ankers, Kaaren Verne
rows.extract: The Great Impersonation is a 1942 American thriller film directed by John Rawlins and starring Ralph Bellamy, Evelyn Ankers and Aubrey Mather. It is an adaptation of the 1920 novel The Great Impersonation by Edward Phillips Oppenheim with the setting moved from the early 1910s of the novel to the Se

rows.title: Halfway to Shanghai
rows.cast: Kent Taylor, Irene Hervey, Henry Stephenson
rows.extract: Halfway to Shanghai is a 1942 American adventure film directed by John Rawlins and written by Stuart Palmer. The film stars Kent Taylor, Irene Hervey, Henry Stephenson, J. Edward Bromberg, George Zucco and Charles Wagenheim. The film was released on September 18, 1942, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Hay Foot
rows.cast: William Tracy, Joe Sawyer, Elyse Knox
rows.extract: Hay Foot is a 1942 American military comedy, a sequel to Tanks a Million which brings back most of the characters from that film. The two leading characters, sergeant Doubleday and his rival Sergeant Ames, would go on to feature in six more films.

rows.title: Heart of the Golden West
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Ruth Terry, Smiley Burnette
rows.extract: Heart of the Golden West  is a 1942 American Western film starring Roy Rogers.

rows.title: Heart of the Rio Grande
rows.cast: Gene Autry, Fay McKenzie, Edith Fellows
rows.extract: Heart of the Rio Grande is a 1942 American Western film directed by William Morgan and starring Gene Autry, Smiley Burnette, Fay McKenzie, and Edith Fellows. Based on a story by Newlin B. Wildes, the film is about a singing cowboy and dude ranch foreman who helps a spoiled teenager and her business

rows.title: Hello, Annapolis
rows.cast: Tom Brown, Jean Parker, Larry Parks
rows.extract: Hello, Annapolis is a 1942 American film. Filming started January 1942.

rows.title: Henry Aldrich, Editor
rows.cast: Jimmy Lydon, Olive Blakeney, Rita Quigley
rows.extract: Henry Aldrich, Editor is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Hugh Bennett and written by Muriel Roy Bolton and Val Burton. The film stars Jimmy Lydon, Charles Smith, John Litel, Olive Blakeney, Rita Quigley and Vaughan Glaser. The film was released in September 1942, by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: Henry and Dizzy
rows.cast: Jimmy Lydon, Mary Anderson, John Litel
rows.extract: Henry and Dizzy is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Hugh Bennett and written by Val Burton. The film stars Jimmy Lydon, Mary Anderson, Charles Smith, John Litel, Olive Blakeney and Maude Eburne. The film was released on June 5, 1942, by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: Her Cardboard Lover
rows.cast: Norma Shearer, Robert Taylor, George Sanders
rows.extract: Her Cardboard Lover is a 1942 American comedy film directed by George Cukor, starring Norma Shearer, Robert Taylor, and George Sanders. The screenplay by Jacques Deval, John Collier, Anthony Veiller, and William H. Wright is based on the English translation of Deval's 1926 play Dans sa candeur naïve

rows.title: Here We Go Again
rows.cast: Jim Jordan, Marian Jordan, Edgar Bergen
rows.extract: Here We Go Again is a 1942 American film, a sequel to Look Who's Laughing. With RKO in financial trouble, with the success of the earlier zany comedy starring a bevy of radio stars, Here We Go Again put Fibber McGee and Molly in a search for where to celebrate the couple's 20th anniversary. They wan

rows.title: The Hidden Hand
rows.cast: Craig Stevens, Elisabeth Fraser, Julie Bishop
rows.extract: The Hidden Hand is a 1942 comedy horror film directed by Benjamin Stoloff, starring Craig Stevens, Elisabeth Fraser and Julie Bishop.

rows.title: Highways by Night
rows.cast: Richard Carlson, Jane Randolph, Barton MacLane
rows.extract: Highways by Night is a 1942 American crime drama film directed by Peter Godfrey from a screenplay by Lynn Root and Frank Fenton, based on the story Silver Spoon, by Clarence Budington Kelland. The film stars Richard Carlson and Jane Randolph.

rows.title: Hi, Neighbor
rows.cast: Jean Parker, John Archer, Janet Beecher
rows.extract: Hi, Neighbor is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Charles Lamont and written by Dorrell McGowan and Stuart E. McGowan. The film stars Jean Parker, John Archer, Janet Beecher, Marilyn Hare, Bill Shirley and Pauline Drake. The film was released on July 27, 1942, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Hillbilly Blitzkrieg
rows.cast: Bud Duncan, Edgar Kennedy, Cliff Nazarro
rows.extract: Hillbilly Blitzkrieg is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Roy Mack that was a sequel to Private Snuffy Smith. The film is also known as Enemy Round-Up.

rows.title: Hitler – Dead or Alive
rows.cast: Ward Bond, Dorothy Tree, Warren Hymer
rows.extract: Hitler – Dead or Alive is a 1942 American propaganda war film directed by Nick Grinde. The plot of Hitler – Dead or Alive was inspired by true events but takes a quasi-comic tone.

rows.title: Holiday Inn
rows.cast: Bing Crosby, Fred Astaire, Marjorie Reynolds, Virginia Dale
rows.extract: Holiday Inn is a 1942 American musical film starring Bing Crosby and Fred Astaire, with Marjorie Reynolds, Virginia Dale, and Walter Abel. It was directed by Mark Sandrich with music by Irving Berlin. The composer wrote twelve songs specifically for the film, the best known being "White Christmas".

rows.title: Home in Wyomin'
rows.cast: Gene Autry, Fay McKenzie
rows.extract: Home in Wyomin' is a 1942 American Western film directed by William Morgan and starring Gene Autry, Smiley Burnette, and Fay McKenzie. Based on a story by Stuart Palmer, the film is about a singing cowboy who helps out a former employer in trouble with his failing rodeo while romancing a woman repor

rows.title: House of Errors
rows.cast: Harry Langdon, Marian Marsh, Betty Blythe
rows.extract: House of Errors is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Bernard B. Ray and written by Ewart Adamson and Eddie Davis. The film stars Harry Langdon, Charley Rogers, Marian Marsh, Ray Walker, Betty Blythe and John Holland. The film was released on April 10, 1942, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: I Live on Danger
rows.cast: Chester Morris, Jean Parker
rows.extract: I Live on Danger is a 1942 film noir thriller film directed by Sam White and starring Chester Morris and Jean Parker.

rows.title: I Married a Witch
rows.cast: Veronica Lake, Fredric March, Susan Hayward
rows.extract: I Married a Witch is a 1942 American fantasy romantic comedy film, directed by René Clair, and starring Veronica Lake as a witch whose plan for revenge goes comically awry, with Fredric March as her foil. The film also features Robert Benchley, Susan Hayward and Cecil Kellaway. The screenplay by Rob

rows.title: I Married an Angel
rows.cast: Jeanette MacDonald, Nelson Eddy
rows.extract: I Married an Angel is a 1942 American musical film based on the 1938 musical comedy of the same name by Rodgers and Hart. The film was directed by W. S. Van Dyke and starred Jeanette MacDonald and Nelson Eddy, who were then a popular onscreen couple. Supporting cast members included Edward Everett H

rows.title: I Was Framed
rows.cast: Julie Bishop, Tod Andrews
rows.extract: I Was Framed is a 1942 American crime film directed by D. Ross Lederman. According to Warner Bros records the film earned $159,000 domestically and $90,000 foreign.

rows.title: Ice-Capades Revue
rows.cast: Ellen Drew, Richard Denning, Jerry Colonna
rows.extract: Ice-Capades Revue is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Bernard Vorhaus, and written by Bradford Ropes and Gertrude Purcell. The film stars Ellen Drew, Richard Denning, Jerry Colonna, Barbara Jo Allen, Harold Huber and Marilyn Hare. The film was released on December 24, 1942, by Republic Pictur

rows.title: Iceland
rows.cast: Sonja Henie, John Payne, Jack Oakie
rows.extract: Iceland (1942) is a 20th Century Fox musical film directed by H. Bruce Humberstone set in Iceland, starring skater Sonja Henie and John Payne as a U.S. Marine posted in Iceland during World War II. The film was titled Katina in Great Britain and Marriage on Ice in Australia.

rows.title: In Old California
rows.cast: John Wayne, Binnie Barnes, Albert Dekker
rows.extract: In Old California is a 1942 American Western film directed by William C. McGann starring John Wayne, Binnie Barnes and Albert Dekker. Wayne plays Tom Craig, a Boston pharmacist who relocates to Sacramento during the Gold Rush.

rows.title: In This Our Life
rows.cast: Bette Davis, Olivia de Havilland, George Brent
rows.extract: In This Our Life is a 1942 American drama film, the second to be directed by John Huston. The screenplay by Howard Koch is based on the 1941 Pulitzer Prize-winning novel of the same title by Ellen Glasgow. The cast included the established stars Bette Davis and Olivia de Havilland as sisters and riv

rows.title: Invisible Agent
rows.cast: Ilona Massey, Jon Hall, Peter Lorre
rows.extract: Invisible Agent is a 1942 American action and spy film directed by Edwin L. Marin with a screenplay written by Curt Siodmak. The invisible agent is played by Jon Hall, with Peter Lorre and Sir Cedric Hardwicke as members of the Axis, and Ilona Massey and Albert Basserman as Allied spies.

rows.title: Inside the Law
rows.cast: Wallace Ford, Luana Walters
rows.extract: Inside the Law is a 1942 American film directed by Hamilton MacFadden. It is also known as Rogues in Clover.

rows.title: Isle of Missing Men
rows.cast: John Howard, Helen Gilbert, Gilbert Roland
rows.extract: Isle of Missing Men is a 1942 American drama film directed by Richard Oswald and starring John Howard, Helen Gilbert and Gilbert Roland. In the film, a young woman receives an invitation from the governor of an island prison to spend a week with him. She does so, but conceals the fact that her husba

rows.title: It Happened in Flatbush
rows.cast: Lloyd Nolan, Carole Landis, Sara Allgood
rows.extract: It Happened in Flatbush is a 1942 American sports film directed by Ray McCarey and starring Lloyd Nolan, Carole Landis and Sara Allgood. The film is a baseball comedy inspired by the 1941 Brooklyn Dodgers' pennant win.

rows.title: It's All True
rows.extract: It's All True is an unfinished Orson Welles feature film comprising three stories about Latin America. "My Friend Bonito" was supervised by Welles and directed by Norman Foster in Mexico in 1941. "Carnaval" and "Jangadeiros" were directed by Welles in Brazil in 1942. It was to have been Welles's thi

rows.title: Jackass Mail
rows.cast: Wallace Beery, Marjorie Main, J. Carrol Naish
rows.extract: Jackass Mail is a 1942 Western comedy film directed by Norman Z. McLeod and starring Wallace Beery and Marjorie Main.

rows.title: Jail House Blues
rows.cast: Nat Pendleton, Anne Gwynne, Robert Paige
rows.extract: Jail House Blues is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Albert S. Rogell and written by Paul Gerard Smith and Harold Tarshis. The film stars Nat Pendleton, Anne Gwynne, Robert Paige, Horace McMahon, Elisabeth Risdon, Warren Hymer, and Samuel S. Hinds. It was released on February 1, 1942, by Univ

rows.title: Jesse James, Jr.
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Lynn Merrick
rows.extract: Jesse James, Jr. is a 1942 American Western film directed by George Sherman and written by Richard Murphy, Doris Schroeder and Taylor Caven. The film stars Don "Red" Barry, Lynn Merrick, Al St. John, Douglas Walton, Karl Hackett and Lee Shumway. The film was released on March 25, 1942, by Republic P

rows.title: Joan of Ozark
rows.cast: Judy Canova, Joe E. Brown, Jerome Cowan
rows.extract: Joan of Ozark is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Joseph Santley and starring Judy Canova, Joe E. Brown and Eddie Foy Jr. It was one of thirteen films Canova made with Republic Studios. It is also known by the alternative title The Queen of Spies.

rows.title: Joan of Paris
rows.cast: Michèle Morgan, Paul Henreid, Laird Cregar
rows.extract: Joan of Paris is a 1942 war film about five Royal Air Force pilots shot down over Nazi-occupied France during World War II and their attempt to escape to England. It stars Michèle Morgan and Paul Henreid, with Thomas Mitchell, Laird Cregar and May Robson in her last role.

rows.title: Joe Smith, American
rows.cast: Robert Young, Marsha Hunt
rows.extract: Joe Smith, American is a 1942 American spy film directed by Richard Thorpe and stars Robert Young and Marsha Hunt. The film, loosely based on the story of Herman W. Lang, and the theft of plans of a top-secret bombsight, is the account of a worker at an aviation factory who is kidnapped by enemy spi

rows.title: Johnny Doughboy
rows.cast: Jane Withers, Ruth Donnelly, Henry Wilcoxon
rows.extract: Johnny Doughboy is a 1942 American black-and-white musical comedy film directed by John H. Auer for Republic Pictures. It stars Jane Withers in a dual role as a 16-year-old actress who is sick of playing juvenile roles, and her lookalike fan who is persuaded by a group of "has-been" child stars to p

rows.title: Johnny Eager
rows.cast: Robert Taylor, Lana Turner
rows.extract: Johnny Eager is a 1941 film noir directed by Mervyn LeRoy and starring Robert Taylor, Lana Turner and Van Heflin. Heflin won an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor. The film was one of many spoofed in Dead Men Don't Wear Plaid (1982).

rows.title: Journey for Margaret
rows.cast: Robert Young, Laraine Day, Fay Bainter, Nigel Bruce
rows.extract: Journey for Margaret is a 1942 American drama film set in London in World War II. It stars Robert Young and Laraine Day as a couple who have to deal with the loss of their unborn child due to a bombing raid. It is an adaptation of the book of the same name in which William Lindsay White and his wife

rows.title: Juke Box Jenny
rows.cast: Ken Murray, Harriet Hilliard, Iris Adrian
rows.extract: Juke Box Jenny is a 1942 film directed by Harold Young and starring Ken Murray, Harriet Hilliard, Iris Adrian, and Donald Douglas. The film is a musical comedy with songs performed by Charlie Barnet and his Orchestra, The King's Men, Wingy Manone and his Orchestra, The Milt Herth Trio, and The Eddie

rows.title: Juke Girl
rows.cast: Ann Sheridan, Ronald Reagan, Gene Lockhart
rows.extract: Juke Girl is a 1942 American drama film directed by Curtis Bernhardt, written by A. I. Bezzerides, and starring Ann Sheridan and Ronald Reagan. The supporting cast includes Richard Whorf, George Tobias, Gene Lockhart, Alan Hale Sr., Howard Da Silva, Donald MacBride, Faye Emerson, Willie Best, and Fu

rows.title: Jungle Book
rows.cast: Sabu, Joseph Calleia
rows.extract: Jungle Book is a 1942 independent Technicolor action-adventure film by the Korda brothers, loosely adapted from Rudyard Kipling's The Jungle Book (1894). The story centers on Mowgli, a feral young man who is kidnapped by villagers who are cruel to the jungle animals as they attempt to steal a dead k

rows.title: Jungle Siren
rows.cast: Ann Corio, Buster Crabbe, Arno Frey
rows.extract: Jungle Siren is a 1942 American film directed by Sam Newfield.

rows.title: Junior Army
rows.cast: Freddie Bartholomew, Billy Halop, Huntz Hall
rows.extract: Junior Army is a 1942 American film directed by Lew Landers, starring Freddie Bartholomew, Billy Halop, and Huntz Hall, and released by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Just Off Broadway
rows.cast: Lloyd Nolan, Marjorie Weaver, Phil Silvers
rows.extract: Just Off Broadway is a 1942 Drama directed by Herbert I. Leeds, starring Lloyd Nolan and Marjorie Weaver. This is the sixth of a series of seven that Lloyd Nolan played Michael Shayne for Twentieth Century Fox films. Hugh Beaumont portrayed Shayne in five more films from Producers Releasing Corporat

rows.title: Kid Glove Killer
rows.cast: Van Heflin, Marsha Hunt
rows.extract: Kid Glove Killer is a 1942 American crime film, starring Van Heflin as a forensic scientist investigating the murder of a mayor. The B film, the feature-length directorial debut of Fred Zinnemann, was an expanded version of the 1938 Crime Does Not Pay short subject "They're Always Caught".

rows.title: King of the Mounties
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Peggy Drake
rows.extract: King of the Mounties is a 1942 Republic 12-chapter film serial, directed by William Witney. Allan Lane played Sgt. Dave King of the Mounties, with Peggy Drake as heroine Carol Brent, and Abner Biberman played the villainous Japanese admiral Yamata.

rows.title: King of the Stallions
rows.cast: Dave O'Brien, Rick Vallin, Chief Thundercloud
rows.extract: King of the Stallions is a 1942 American Western film directed by Edward Finney and written by Arthur St. Claire and Sherman L. Lowe. The film stars Chief Thundercloud, Rick Vallin, Barbara Felker, Dave O'Brien, Chief Yowlachie and Sally Cairns. The film was released on September 18, 1942, by Monogr

rows.title: Kings Row
rows.cast: Ann Sheridan, Ronald Reagan, Robert Cummings
rows.extract: Kings Row is a 1942 film starring Ann Sheridan, Robert Cummings, Ronald Reagan and Betty Field that tells a story of young people growing up in a small American town at the turn of the twentieth century. The picture was directed by Sam Wood. The film was adapted by Casey Robinson from a best-selling

rows.title: Klondike Fury
rows.cast: Edmund Lowe, Lucile Fairbanks, Ralph Morgan
rows.extract: Klondike Fury is a 1942 American drama film directed by William K. Howard, produced by the King Brothers, and released through Monogram. It stars Edmund Lowe.

rows.title: Lady for a Night
rows.cast: John Wayne, Joan Blondell, Ray Middleton
rows.extract: Lady for a Night is a 1942 American drama film starring Joan Blondell and John Wayne. The World War II B-17 bomber the Memphis Belle is named after a steamboat in this film. It is also known as The Lady from New Orleans, Memphis Belle and Lady of New Orleans.

rows.title: Lady from Chungking
rows.cast: Anna May Wong, Harold Huber, Mae Clarke
rows.extract: Lady from Chungking is a 1942 American war film.

rows.title: Lady Gangster
rows.cast: Faye Emerson, Julie Bishop
rows.extract: Lady Gangster is a 1942 Warner Bros. B picture crime film directed by Robert Florey, credited as "Florian Roberts". It is based on the play Gangstress, or Women in Prison by Dorothy Mackaye, who in 1928, as #440960, served less than ten months of a one- to three-year sentence in San Quentin State Pr

rows.title: The Lady Has Plans
rows.cast: Paulette Goddard, Ray Milland, Roland Young
rows.extract: The Lady Has Plans is a 1942 American comedy film spy thriller film directed by Sidney Lanfield and starring Ray Milland, Paulette Goddard and Roland Young. It was produced ad distributed by Paramount Pictures as a World War II espionage film set in neutral Portugal.

rows.title: Lady in a Jam
rows.cast: Irene Dunne, Ralph Bellamy, Patric Knowles
rows.extract: Lady in a Jam is a 1942 film comedy directed by Gregory La Cava and starring Irene Dunne, Patric Knowles, Ralph Bellamy, and Eugene Pallette. It was made and distributed by Universal Pictures. The film's sets were designed by the art director Jack Otterson.

rows.title: The Lady Is Willing
rows.cast: Marlene Dietrich, Fred MacMurray
rows.extract: The Lady is Willing is a 1942 Columbia Pictures screwball comedy film starring Marlene Dietrich and Fred MacMurray, directed by Mitchell Leisen.

rows.title: Land of the Open Range
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Janet Waldo
rows.extract: Land of the Open Range is a 1942 Western film. It uses out takes from Cimarron (1931).

rows.title: Larceny, Inc.
rows.cast: Edward G. Robinson, Jane Wyman, Broderick Crawford
rows.extract: Larceny, Inc. is a 1942 American film. Originally released on May 2, 1942, by Warner Bros., the film is a cross between comedy and gangster genres. Directed by Lloyd Bacon, the film stars Edward G. Robinson, Jane Wyman, Broderick Crawford, and Jack Carson, and features Anthony Quinn, and Edward Brop

rows.title: Laugh Your Blues Away
rows.cast: Jinx Falkenburg, Bert Gordon, Isobel Elsom
rows.extract: Laugh Your Blues Away is a 1942 American comedy film directed by Charles Barton and written by Harry Sauber and Ned Dandy. The film stars Jinx Falkenburg, Bert Gordon, Johnny Mitchell, Isobel Elsom, Roger Clark and George Lessey. The film was released on November 12, 1942, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Law and Order
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Al St. John, Wanda McKay
rows.extract: Law and Order is a 1942 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Sam Robins. The film stars Buster Crabbe, Al St. John, Dave O'Brien, Sarah Padden, Wanda McKay and Charles King. The film was released on August 21, 1942, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: Law of the Jungle
rows.cast: Arline Judge, John King
rows.extract: Law of the Jungle is a 1942 American adventure film directed by Jean Yarbrough.

rows.title: Lawless Plainsmen
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Russell Hayden, Luana Walters
rows.extract: Lawless Plainsmen is a 1942 American Western film directed by William Berke and written by Luci Ward. The film stars Charles Starrett, Russell Hayden, Cliff Edwards, Luana Walters, Ray Bennett and Gwen Kenyon. The film was released on March 17, 1942, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Let's Get Tough!
rows.cast: East Side Kids, Florence Rice
rows.extract: Let's Get Tough! is a 1942 film and the ninth film in the East Side Kids series, starring Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall, Bobby Jordan, and Robert Armstrong. Released in early 1942, it was directed by Wallace Fox, and features the gang caught up in World War II and fighting the Black Dragon Society, an enem

rows.title: Life Begins at Eight-Thirty
rows.cast: Ida Lupino, Monty Woolley, Cornel Wilde
rows.extract: Life Begins at Eight-Thirty is a 1942 comedy-drama romance film starring Monty Woolley as a washed-up, alcoholic actor, Ida Lupino as his daughter, and Cornel Wilde as her boyfriend. It is based on the West End play The Light of Heart by Emlyn Williams.

rows.title: Little Joe, the Wrangler
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Tex Ritter, Jennifer Holt
rows.extract: Little Joe, the Wrangler is a 1942 American Western film directed by Lewis D. Collins and written by Sherman L. Lowe and Elizabeth Beecher. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Tex Ritter, Fuzzy Knight, Jennifer Holt, Florine McKinney and James Craven. The film was released on November 13, 1942, by Uni

rows.title: Little Tokyo, U.S.A.
rows.cast: Preston Foster, Brenda Joyce, June Duprez
rows.extract: Little Tokyo, U.S.A. is a 1942 American film. Produced in the period just after the United States entered World War II, it was meant to alert Americans to the dangers of foreign agents. It is now controversial for its largely negative portrayal of Japanese-Americans.

rows.title: The Living Ghost
rows.cast: James Dunn, Joan Woodbury
rows.extract: The Living Ghost is a 1942 American mystery-drama film directed by William Beaudine and produced by Monogram Pictures. Starring James Dunn and Joan Woodbury, the film incorporates elements of the horror genre as it follows an ex-private detective who is called in to investigate why a banker has turn

rows.title: The Lone Prairie
rows.cast: Russell Hayden, Dub Taylor
rows.extract: The Lone Prairie is a 1942 American Western film directed by William Berke. It is one of a series of Westerns that Berke directed with the trio of Russell Hayden, Dub Taylor, and Bob Wills. It was produced and distributed by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: The Lone Rider in Cheyenne
rows.cast: George Houston, Al St. John, Dennis Moore
rows.extract: The Lone Rider in Cheyenne is a 1942 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Oliver Drake and Elizabeth Beecher. The film stars George Houston as the Lone Rider, Al St. John as his sidekick "Fuzzy" Jones, and Dennis Moore as Sheriff Smoky Moore, with Ella Neal, Roy Barcroft and

rows.title: Lone Star Ranger
rows.cast: John Kimbrough, Sheila Ryan
rows.extract: Lone Star Ranger is a 1942 American Western film directed by James Tinling and written by William Conselman Jr., Irving Cummings Jr. and George Kane. The film stars John Kimbrough, Sheila Ryan, Jonathan Hale, William Farnum, Truman Bradley and George E. Stone. The film was released on March 20, 1942

rows.title: The Lone Star Vigilantes
rows.cast: Wild Bill Elliott, Tex Ritter, Luana Walters
rows.extract: The Lone Star Vigilantes is a 1942 American Western film directed by Wallace Fox and written by Luci Ward. The film stars Wild Bill Elliott, Tex Ritter, Frank Mitchell, Virginia Carpenter, Luana Walters and Budd Buster. The film was released on January 1, 1942, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Lost Canyon
rows.cast: William Boyd, Lola Lane
rows.extract: Lost Canyon is a 1942 American Western film directed by Lesley Selander and written by Harry O. Hoyt. The film stars William Boyd, Andy Clyde, Jay Kirby, Lola Lane, Douglas Fowley and Herbert Rawlinson, is a remake of Rustlers' Valley (1937). The film was released on December 18, 1942, by United Art

rows.title: The Loves of Edgar Allan Poe
rows.cast: Linda Darnell, Shepperd Strudwick, Virginia Gilmore
rows.extract: The Loves of Edgar Allan Poe is a 1942 drama film directed by Harry Lachman, starring Linda Darnell and Shepperd Strudwick. The film is a cinematic biography of Edgar Allan Poe that examines his romantic relationships with Sarah Elmira Royster and Virginia Clemm.

rows.title: Lucky Ghost

rows.extract: Colt Comrades is a 1943 American Western film directed by Lesley Selander and written by Michael Wilson. The film stars William Boyd, Andy Clyde, Jay Kirby, Teddi Sherman, Victor Jory, George Reeves and Douglas Fowley. The film was released on June 18, 1943, by United Artists.

rows.title: Coney Island
rows.cast: Betty Grable, George Montgomery, Cesar Romero, Phil Silvers
rows.extract: Coney Island is a 1943 American Technicolor musical film released by Twentieth Century Fox and starring Betty Grable in one of her biggest hits. rows.title: The Constant Nymph
rows.cast: Charles Boyer, Joan Fontaine, Peter Lorre
rows.extract: The Constant Nymph is a 1943 romantic drama film starring Charles Boyer, Joan Fontaine, Alexis Smith, Brenda Marshall, Charles Coburn, May Whitty, and Peter Lorre with a famous score by Erich Wolfgang Korngold. It was adapted by Kathryn Scola from the 1924 novel of the same name by Margaret Kennedy

rows.title: Corregidor
rows.cast: Otto Kruger, Elissa Landi, Donald Woods
rows.extract: Corregidor is a 1943 American war film directed by William Nigh and starring Otto Kruger, Elissa Landi and Donald Woods. rows.title: Corvette K-225
rows.cast: Randolph Scott, Ella Raines
rows.extract: Corvette K-225 is a 1943 American war film starring Randolph Scott and James Brown, with Ella Raines making her feature film debut. rows.title: Cowboy Commandos
rows.cast: Ray Corrigan, Max Terhune, Evelyn Finley
rows.extract: Cowboy Commandos is a 1943 American Western film directed by S. Roy Luby and written by Elizabeth Beecher. rows.title: Cowboy in Manhattan
rows.cast: Frances Langford, Robert Paige, Leon Errol
rows.extract: Cowboy in Manhattan is a 1943 American comedy film directed by Frank Woodruff and written by Warren Wilson. The film stars Robert Paige, Frances Langford, Leon Errol, Walter Catlett, Joe Sawyer and Jennifer Holt. The film was released on May 21, 1943, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Cowboy in the Clouds
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Dub Taylor
rows.extract: Cowboy in the Clouds is a 1943 American Western film directed by Benjamin H. Kline and written by Elizabeth Beecher. The film stars Charles Starrett, Dub Taylor, Julie Duncan, Jimmy Wakely, Davison Clark and Wally Wales. The film was released on December 23, 1943, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Crash Dive
rows.cast: Tyrone Power, Dana Andrews, Anne Baxter
rows.extract: Crash Dive is a World War II film in Technicolor released in 1943. It was directed by Archie Mayo, written by Jo Swerling, and starred Tyrone Power, Dana Andrews and Anne Baxter. rows.title: Crazy House
rows.cast: Olsen and Johnson, Cass Daley
rows.extract: Crazy House is a 1943 comedy film starring Ole Olsen and Chic Johnson.

rows.title: Crime Doctor
rows.cast: Warner Baxter, Ray Collins
rows.extract: Crime Doctor (1943) is a crime film adapted from the radio series of the same name. The film stars Warner Baxter as a man with amnesia determined to remember his past. rows.title: The Crime Doctor's Strangest Case
rows.cast: Warner Baxter, Gloria Dickson
rows.extract: The Crime Doctor's Strangest Case is a 1943 American mystery film directed by Eugene Forde and starring Warner Baxter, Lynn Merrick and Gloria Dickson. It is the second in a series of Crime Doctor films made by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: The Crime Smasher
rows.cast: Richard Cromwell, Gale Storm
rows.extract: The Crime Smasher is a 1943 American crime comedy film directed by James Tinling and starring Edgar Kennedy, Richard Cromwell and Gale Storm. It is based on the Radio program Cosmo Jones featuring Frank Graham. The film's sets were designed by the art director Dave Milton. It is sometimes alternativ

rows.title: The Cross of Lorraine
rows.cast: Jean-Pierre Aumont, Gene Kelly, Cedric Hardwicke
rows.extract: The Cross of Lorraine is a 1943 Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer war film about French prisoners of war escaping a German prison camp and joining the French Resistance. Directed by Tay Garnett, starring Jean-Pierre Aumont and Gene Kelly, was partly based on Hans Habe's 1941 novel A Thousand Shall Fall. The title

rows.title: Cry "Havoc"
rows.cast: Margaret Sullavan, Ann Sothern, Joan Blondell, Fay Bainter
rows.extract: Cry 'Havoc' is a 1943 American war drama film, produced by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer and directed by Richard Thorpe. It stars Margaret Sullavan, Ann Sothern and Joan Blondell, and features Fay Bainter, Marsha Hunt, Ella Raines, Frances Gifford, Diana Lewis, Heather Angel, Dorothy Morris and Connie Gilchri

rows.title: The Crystal Ball
rows.cast: Paulette Goddard, Ray Milland
rows.extract: The Crystal Ball is a 1943 film directed by Elliott Nugent and starring Ray Milland and Paulette Goddard.

rows.title: The Dancing Masters
rows.cast: Laurel and Hardy, Trudy Marshall
rows.extract: The Dancing Masters is a 1943 black and white American comedy film directed by Malcolm St. Clair, produced by 20th Century-Fox, and featuring Laurel and Hardy. A young Robert Mitchum has a small, uncredited role as a gangster posing as an insurance salesman.

rows.title: Danger! Women at Work
rows.cast: Patsy Kelly, Mary Brian, Isabel Jewell
rows.extract: Danger! Women at Work is a 1943 American comedy film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Martin Mooney. The film stars Patsy Kelly, Mary Brian, Isabel Jewell, Wanda McKay, Betty Compson and Cobina Wright Sr.. The film was released on August 23, 1943, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: Dangerous Blondes
rows.cast: Evelyn Keyes, Anita Louise
rows.extract: Dangerous Blondes is a 1943 American comedy film directed by Leigh Jason and written by Richard Flournoy and Jack Henley, from the story If the Shroud Fits by Kelley Roos.The film stars Allyn Joslyn and Evelyn Keyes, and was released by Columbia Pictures in September 1943. Alternate titles for this

rows.title: Days of Old Cheyenne
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Lynn Merrick
rows.extract: Days of Old Cheyenne is a 1943 American Western film directed by Elmer Clifton and starring Don 'Red' Barry, Lynn Merrick and William Haade.

rows.title: Dead Man's Gulch
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Lynn Merrick
rows.extract: Dead Man's Gulch is a 1943 American Western film directed by John English and written by Norman S. Hall and Robert Creighton Williams. The film stars Don "Red" Barry, Lynn Merrick, Clancy Cooper, Emmett Lynn, Malcolm 'Bud' McTaggart and John Vosper. The film was released on February 12, 1943, by Rep

rows.title: Dead Men Walk
rows.cast: George Zucco, Mary Carlisle
rows.extract: Dead Men Walk is a 1943 American horror film produced by Sigmund Neufeld for Producers Releasing Corporation (PRC). It is an original story and screenplay by Fred Myton, starring George Zucco, Mary Carlisle, Nedrick Young, and Dwight Frye, directed by Sam Newfield. It was originally distributed by P

rows.title: Death Rides the Plains
rows.cast: Robert Livingston, Al St. John
rows.extract: Death Rides the Plains is a 1943 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Joseph O'Donnell. The film stars Robert Livingston as the Lone Rider and Al St. John as his sidekick "Fuzzy Jones", with Patti McCarty, Ray Bennett, I. Stanford Jolley and George Chesebro. The film was rel

rows.title: Death Valley Manhunt
rows.cast: Wild Bill Elliott, Anne Jeffreys
rows.extract: Death Valley Manhunt is a 1943 American Western film directed by John English and written by Norman S. Hall and Anthony Coldeway. The film stars Wild Bill Elliott, George "Gabby" Hayes, Anne Jeffreys, Weldon Heyburn, Herbert Heyes and Davison Clark. The film was released on November 24, 1943, by Rep

rows.title: Death Valley Rangers
rows.cast: Ken Maynard, Hoot Gibson, Bob Steele
rows.extract: Death Valley Rangers is a 1943 American Western film directed by Robert Emmett Tansey and starring Ken Maynard, Hoot Gibson and Bob Steele.

rows.title: Deerslayer
rows.cast: Jean Parker, Larry Parks, Yvonne DeCarlo
rows.extract: Deerslayer is a 1943 American Western film. It is based on the 1841 novel The Deerslayer by James Fenimore Cooper. It stars Bruce Kellogg and Jean Parker, and was directed by Lew Landers.

rows.title: The Desert Song
rows.cast: Dennis Morgan, Irene Manning
rows.extract: The Desert Song is a 1943 American musical film. It was directed by Robert Florey and starred Dennis Morgan, Irene Manning and Bruce Cabot. It is based on the 1926 operetta with music by Sigmund Romberg. It was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Art Direction.

rows.title: The Desperadoes
rows.cast: Randolph Scott, Claire Trevor, Glenn Ford
rows.extract: The Desperadoes is a 1943 American Western film directed by Charles Vidor and starring Randolph Scott, Claire Trevor, Glenn Ford, Evelyn Keyes and Edgar Buchanan. Based on a story by Max Brand, the film is about a wanted outlaw who arrives in town to rob a bank that has already been held up. His pas

rows.title: Destination Tokyo
rows.cast: Cary Grant, John Garfield
rows.extract: Destination Tokyo is a 1943 black and white American submarine war film. The film was directed by Delmer Daves in his directorial debut, and the screenplay was written by Daves and Albert Maltz, based on an original story by former submariner Steve Fisher. The film stars Cary Grant and John Garfield

rows.title: Destroyer
rows.cast: Glenn Ford, Edward G. Robinson
rows.extract: Destroyer is a 1943 American war film directed by William A. Seiter and starring Edward G. Robinson.

rows.title: Devil Riders
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Patti McCarty
rows.extract: Devil Riders is a 1943 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield. It was the first film in Producers Releasing Corporation's Billy the Kid film series where Crabbe changed his name to "Billy Carson".

rows.title: Dixie
rows.cast: Bing Crosby, Dorothy Lamour
rows.extract: Dixie is a 1943 American biographical film of songwriter Daniel Decatur Emmett directed by A. Edward Sutherland and starring Bing Crosby and Dorothy Lamour. Filming in Technicolor, Dixie was only a moderate success and received mixed reviews. Contrary to rumor, it has not been withdrawn from circula

rows.title: Dixie Dugan
rows.cast: Lois Andrews, James Ellison, Charlotte Greenwood
rows.extract: Dixie Dugan is a 1943 American comedy film, directed by Otto Brower. It stars Lois Andrews, James Ellison, and Charlotte Greenwood. Intended as the first of a series, the film was not a success and the plans for sequels were scrapped.

rows.title: Doughboys in Ireland
rows.cast: Kenny Baker, Jeff Donnell, Lynn Merrick
rows.extract: Doughboys in Ireland is a 1943 American musical war film directed by Lew Landers and starring Kenny Baker, Jeff Donnell and Lynn Merrick. The film offered an early role for future star Robert Mitchum, who appeared in many films that year. A group of American troops are stationed in Ireland, where th

rows.title: Dr. Gillespie's Criminal Case
rows.cast: Lionel Barrymore, Van Johnson, Margaret O'Brien
rows.extract: Dr. Gillespie's Criminal Case is a 1943 film in the Dr. Kildare series. Based on characters created by Max Brand. The third of MGM's Dr. Gillespie series to dispense with the services of Dr. Kildare after Dr. Kildare's Victory (1942).

rows.title: DuBarry Was a Lady
rows.cast: Red Skelton, Lucille Ball, Gene Kelly
rows.extract: Du Barry Was a Lady is a 1943 American musical comedy film directed by Roy Del Ruth, starring Red Skelton, Lucille Ball, Gene Kelly, and Tommy Dorsey and His Orchestra. It is based on the 1939 stage musical of the same name. Shot in Technicolor, the film was produced and distributed by Metro-Goldwyn

rows.title: Edge of Darkness
rows.cast: Errol Flynn, Ann Sheridan, Walter Huston
rows.extract: Edge of Darkness is a 1943 World War II film directed by Lewis Milestone that features Errol Flynn, Ann Sheridan, and Walter Huston. The feature is based on a script written by Robert Rossen which was adapted from the 1942 novel The Edge of Darkness by William Woods.

rows.title: The Falcon and the Co-eds
rows.cast: Tom Conway, Amelita Ward
rows.extract: The Falcon and the Co-eds is a 1943 film under the direction of William Clemens, and produced by Maurice Geraghty, the same team that had worked on The Falcon in Danger (1943) and would stay together for the next film in the Falcon series. The Falcon and the Co-eds was the seventh of 16 in the Falco

rows.title: The Falcon in Danger
rows.cast: Tom Conway, Jean Brooks
rows.extract: The Falcon in Danger is a 1943 American mystery film directed by William Clemens and starring Tom Conway, Jean Brooks, Amelita Ward and Elaine Shepard. The film was the sixth of thirteen The Falcon detective films produced by RKO, all starring Conway.

rows.title: The Falcon Strikes Back
rows.cast: Tom Conway, Harriet Hilliard
rows.extract: The Falcon Strikes Back is a 1943 American crime film directed by Edward Dmytryk and stars Tom Conway as the title character, the amateur sleuth, the Falcon. Supporting roles are filled by Harriet Hilliard, Jane Randolph, Edgar Kennedy, with Cliff Edwards filling in for Allen Jenkins as the Falcon's

rows.title: The Fallen Sparrow
rows.cast: Maureen O'Hara, John Garfield, Walter Slezak, Patricia Morison
rows.extract: The Fallen Sparrow is a 1943 American spy film starring John Garfield, Maureen O'Hara, Patricia Morison, and Walter Slezak. It is based on the novel of the same name by Dorothy B. Hughes. Nazi spies pursue an American, John "Kit" McKittrick, a Spanish Civil War veteran in possession of a priceless k

rows.title: False Colors
rows.cast: William Boyd, Andy Clyde
rows.extract: False Colors is a 1943 American Western film directed by George Archainbaud and written by Morton Grant, Michael Wilson and Norman Houston.
