rows.extract: Lost in a Harem is a 1944 American comedy film directed by Charles Reisner and starring the team of Abbott and Costello alongside Marilyn Maxwell.

rows.cast: Judy Canova, Ross Hunter
rows.extract: Louisiana Hayride is a 1944 American comedy film directed by Charles Barton and starring Judy Canova, Ross Hunter and Richard Lane. rows.cast: William Boyd, Andy Clyde, Ellen Hall

rows.cast: Chester Morris, Janis Carter
rows.extract: One Mysterious Night is a 1944 crime film, the seventh in a Columbia Pictures series of fourteen starring Chester Morris as reformed crook Boston Blackie. rows.cast: Elsa Lanchester, Gordon Oliver

rows.cast: Basil Rathbone, Nigel Bruce, Evelyn Ankers
rows.extract: The Pearl of Death is a 1944 Sherlock Holmes film starring Basil Rathbone as Holmes and Nigel Bruce as Dr. Watson, the ninth of fourteen such films the pair made. rows.title: Phantom Lady
rows.cast: Franchot Tone, Ella Raines
rows.extract: Phantom Lady is a 1944 American film noir directed by Robert Siodmak and starring Franchot Tone, Ella Raines, and Alan Curtis. Based on the novel of the same name by Cornell Woolrich, it follows a young Manhattan secretary and her endeavors to prove that her boss did not murder his wife.

rows.title: Pin Up Girl
rows.cast: Betty Grable, Martha Raye
rows.extract: Pin Up Girl is a 1944 American Technicolor musical romantic comedy motion picture starring Betty Grable, John Harvey, Martha Raye, and Joe E. Brown.

rows.title: The Pinto Bandit
rows.cast: Dave (Tex) O'Brien, Jim Newill, Guy Wilkerson

rows.cast: Stephanie Bachelor, Tom Keene
rows.extract: The Port of 40 Thieves is a 1944 American crime film directed by John English, written by Dane Lussier, and starring Stephanie Bachelor, Tom Keene, Lynne Roberts, Olive Blakeney, Russell Hicks and George Meeker. The film was released on August 13, 1944, by Republic Pictures.

rows.cast: Claudette Colbert, Fred MacMurray
rows.extract: Practically Yours is a 1944 comedic film made by Paramount Pictures, directed by Mitchell Leisen, written by Norman Krasna and starring Claudette Colbert and Fred MacMurray.

rows.cast: Robert Livingston, Smiley Burnette
rows.extract: Pride of the Plains is a 1944 American Western film directed by Wallace Fox and written by John K. Butler and Robert Creighton Williams. rows.extract: The Purple Heart is a 1944 American black-and-white war film, produced by Darryl F. Zanuck, directed by Lewis Milestone, and starring Dana Andrews, Richard Conte, Don "Red" Barry, Sam Levene and Trudy Marshall. Eighteen-year-old Farley Granger had a supporting role.

rows.title: The Racket Man
rows.cast: Hugh Beaumont, Tom Neal, Jeanne Bates
rows.extract: The Racket Man is a 1944 American crime film directed by D. Ross Lederman.

rows.extract: Raiders of the Border is a 1944 American Western film directed by John P. McCarthy and written by Adele Buffington. rows.title: Rainbow Island
rows.cast: Dorothy Lamour, Eddie Bracken
rows.extract: Rainbow Island is a 1944 American musical comedy film directed by Ralph Murphy and written by Arthur Phillips and Walter DeLeon. rows.title: Range Law
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: Range Law is a 1944 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer. This is the ninth film in the "Marshal Nevada Jack McKenzie" series, and stars Johnny Mack Brown as Jack McKenzie and Raymond Hatton as his sidekick Sandy Hopkins, with Sarah Padden, Ellen Hall and Lloyd Ingraham.

rows.title: Rationing
rows.cast: Wallace Beery, Marjorie Main
rows.extract: Rationing is a 1944 American comedy film about governmental restrictions on the sale of food, fuel, and other consumer items and services in the United States during World War II. rows.title: Reckless Age
rows.cast: Gloria Jean, Henry Stephenson
rows.extract: Reckless Age is a 1944 American comedy film directed by Felix E. Feist and written by Gertrude Purcell and Henry Blankfort. rows.title: Return of the Ape Man
rows.cast: Bela Lugosi, John Carradine, Frank Moran
rows.extract: Return of the Ape Man is a 1944 American film distributed by Monogram Pictures. It was directed by Philip Rosen with top-billed star Bela Lugosi and supporting actors John Carradine, George Zucco, Frank Moran, Judith Gibson and Michael Ames.

rows.title: The Return of the Vampire
rows.cast: Bela Lugosi, Nina Foch
rows.extract: The Return of the Vampire is a 1943 American horror film directed by Lew Landers and starring Bela Lugosi, Frieda Inescort, Nina Foch, Miles Mander, Roland Varno, and Matt Willis. rows.title: Riders of the Santa Fe
rows.cast: Rod Cameron, Jennifer Holt
rows.extract: Riders of the Santa Fe is a 1944 American Western film directed by Wallace Fox and written by Ande Lamb. The film stars Rod Cameron, Fuzzy Knight, Eddie Dew, Jennifer Holt, Ray Whitley and Lane Chandler. The film was released on November 10, 1944, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Riding West
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Shirley Patterson
rows.extract: Riding West is a 1944 American Western film directed by William Berke and starring Charles Starrett.

rows.title: Roger Touhy, Gangster
rows.cast: Preston Foster, Victor McLaglen, Lois Andrews
rows.extract: Roger Touhy, Gangster is a 1944 American gangster film based on the life of Chicago mob figure Roger Touhy, directed by film noir specialist Robert Florey.

rows.title: Rogues' Gallery
rows.cast: Robin Raymond, Frank Jenks
rows.extract: Rogues' Gallery is a 1944 American mystery film directed by Albert Herman and starring Frank Jenks, Robin Raymond and H.B. Warner. It was produced by the Poverty Row studio Producers Releasing Corporation. The film's sets were designed by the art director Paul Palmentola.

rows.title: Rosie the Riveter
rows.cast: Frank Albertson, Jane Frazee
rows.extract: Rosie the Riveter is a 1944 American musical film directed by Joseph Santley and starring Jane Frazee, Frank Albertson and Barbara Jo Allen. It is inspired by the iconic character of the same name.

rows.title: Saddle Leather Law
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Dub Taylor
rows.extract: Saddle Leather Law is a 1944 American Western film directed by Benjamin H. Kline and written by Elizabeth Beecher. The film stars Charles Starrett, Dub Taylor, Vi Athens, Lloyd Bridges, Jimmy Wakely and Salty Holmes. The film was released on December 21, 1944, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Sailor's Holiday
rows.cast: Arthur Lake, Shelley Winters
rows.extract: Sailor's Holiday is a 1944 American comedy film directed by William Berke and starring Arthur Lake, Jane Lawrence and Bob Haymes.

rows.extract: The San Antonio Kid is a 1944 American Western film directed by Howard Bretherton starring Wild Bill Elliott in the role of Red Ryder. rows.title: San Diego, I Love You
rows.cast: Jon Hall, Louise Allbritton

rows.title: San Fernando Valley
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Dale Evans
rows.extract: San Fernando Valley is a 1944 American Western film directed by John English and starring Roy Rogers, Dale Evans and Jean Porter. The film was part of the long-running series of Roy Rogers films produced by Republic Pictures.

rows.cast: Basil Rathbone, Nigel Bruce, Paul Cavanagh
rows.extract: The Scarlet Claw is a 1944 American mystery thriller film based on Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes detective stories. rows.title: Secret Command
rows.cast: Pat O'Brien, Carole Landis, Chester Morris
rows.extract: Secret Command is a 1944 American drama war film directed by A. Edward Sutherland and starring Pat O'Brien and Carole Landis. It was nominated for the Oscar for Best Effects in 1945.

rows.title: Secrets of Scotland Yard
rows.cast: Edgar Barrier, Stephanie Bachelor, C. Aubrey Smith
rows.extract: Secrets of Scotland Yard is a 1944 American thriller film directed by George Blair and starring Edgar Barrier, Stephanie Bachelor and C. Aubrey Smith. rows.title: See Here, Private Hargrove
rows.cast: Robert Walker, Donna Reed, Keenan Wynn
rows.extract: See Here, Private Hargrove is a 1944 black-and-white comedy film from MGM, produced by George Haight, directed by Wesley Ruggles, and starring Robert Walker, Donna Reed, and Keenan Wynn. The film was adapted from the 1942 memoir of the same name by Marion Hargrove.

rows.title: Sensations of 1945
rows.cast: Eleanor Powell, Dennis O'Keefe, W. C. Fields, Sophie Tucker, Cab Callaway
rows.extract: Sensations of 1945 is a 1944 American musical-comedy film directed by Andrew Stone and starring Eleanor Powell. rows.title: The Seventh Cross
rows.cast: Spencer Tracy, Hume Cronyn
rows.extract: The Seventh Cross is a 1944 American drama film, set in Nazi Germany, starring Spencer Tracy as a prisoner who escaped from a concentration camp. The story chronicles how he interacts with ordinary Germans, and gradually sheds his cynical view of humanity.

rows.title: Shadow of Suspicion

rows.title: Shake Hands with Murder
rows.cast: Iris Adrian, Frank Jenks

rows.title: Song of the Range
rows.cast: Jimmy Wakely, Dennis Moore
rows.extract: Song of the Range is a 1944 American musical Western film directed by Wallace Fox and starring Jimmy Wakely, Dennis Moore and Lee 'Lasses' White.

rows.title: Sonora Stagecoach
rows.cast: Bob Steele, Hoot Gibson
rows.extract: Sonora Stagecoach is a 1944 American black-and-white Western film starring Bob Steele, Hoot Gibson and Chief Thundercloud. Directed, produced and written by Robert Emett Tansey for Monogram Pictures, the film was released in the United States on June 10, 1944.

rows.title: The Spider Woman

rows.title: Strange Affair

rows.title: Sunday Dinner for a Soldier

rows.title: Sundown Valley

rows.extract: Sundown Valley is a 1944 American Western film directed by Benjamin H. Kline and written by Luci Ward. The film stars Charles Starrett, Dub Taylor, Jeanne Bates and Jimmy Wakely. The film was released on March 23, 1944, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: The Suspect

rows.title: Sweet and Low-Down
rows.cast: Linda Darnell, Benny Goodman

The film was a fictionalized version of life with Goodman, his band, and their manager while entertaining at military camps. The song "I'm Making Believe" was nominated for an Academy Award.

rows.title: Sweethearts of the U.S.A.

rows.extract: Tahiti Nights is a 1944 American comedy film directed by Will Jason and written by Lillie Hayward. The film stars Jinx Falkenburg, Dave O'Brien, Mary Treen, Florence Bates, Cy Kendall and Eddie Bruce. The film was released on December 28, 1944, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Take It Big

rows.extract: Tampico is a 1944 drama/war film directed by Lothar Mendes and starring Edward G. Robinson, Lynn Bari, Victor McLaglen, Marc Lawrence, and Mona Maris. It was released by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Texas Masquerade

rows.extract: Texas Masquerade is a 1944 American Western film directed by George Archainbaud, written by Jack Lait Jr. and Norman Houston, and starring William Boyd, Andy Clyde, Jimmy Rogers, Don Costello, Mady Correll and Francis McDonald. It was released on February 8, 1944, by United Artists.

rows.cast: Tom Neal, Adele Mara

rows.extract: Three Little Sisters is a 1944 American comedy directed by Joseph Santley, written by Olive Cooper, and starring Mary Lee, Ruth Terry, Cheryl Walker, William Terry, Jackie Moran and Charles Arnt. It was released on July 31, 1944, by Republic Pictures.

rows.cast: Lionel Barrymore, Van Johnson, Marilyn Maxwell
rows.extract: Three Men in White is a 1944 American comedy-drama film in the Dr Kildare series directed by Willis Goldbeck. It stars Lionel Barrymore, Van Johnson, and Marilyn Maxwell. Ava Gardner has a supporting role.

rows.title: Three of a Kind
rows.cast: Billy Gilbert, June Lang
rows.extract: Three of a Kind is a 1944 American comedy film directed by D. Ross Lederman and starring Billy Gilbert.

rows.title: Thundering Gun Slingers
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Al St. John

Coffee, and starring Ray Milland, Barbara Britton, Walter Slezak, Lucile Watson, Konstantin Shayne, Vladimir Sokoloff and Mona Freeman. It was released on August 30, 1944, by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: Timber Queen
rows.cast: Mary Beth Hughes, Richard Arlen
rows.extract: Timber Queen is a 1944 American lumberjack drama film directed by Frank McDonald.

rows.title: Together Again
rows.cast: Irene Dunne, Charles Boyer

Hugh Herbert and Virginia Van Upp, based on story by Herbert J. Biberman and Stanley Russell. The supporting cast features Charles Coburn and Mona Freeman.

rows.title: Tomorrow, the World!
rows.cast: Fredric March, Betty Field, Agnes Moorehead
rows.extract: Tomorrow, the World! is a 1944 black-and-white film directed by Leslie Fenton and starring Fredric March, Betty Field, and Agnes Moorehead, about a young German boy who had been active in the Hitler Youth who comes to live with his uncle in the United States, who tries to teach him to reject Nazism.

rows.title: The Town Went Wild
rows.cast: Freddie Bartholomew, Jimmy Lydon
rows.extract: The Town Went Wild is a 1944 American comedy film directed by Ralph Murphy and starring Freddie Bartholomew and Edward Everett Horton.

rows.title: Trigger Law

rows.extract: Trigger Law is a 1944 American Western film directed by Vernon Keays and starring Hoot Gibson, Bob Steele and Beatrice Gray.

rows.extract: Trigger Trail is a 1944 American Western film directed by Lewis D. Collins and starring Rod Cameron.

The film stars Johnny Downs, Vivian Austin, Leon Errol, Connie Haines, Eddie Quillan, Milburn Stone and Jimmie Dodd. The film was released on July 14, 1944, by Universal Pictures.

Williams, Abner Biberman and George Lynn. The film was released on March 16, 1944, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.extract: U-Boat Prisoner, also known as Dangerous Mists, is a 1944 American film. Direction was credited to Lew Landers. The script was written by Aubrey Wisberg.

rows.extract: Uncertain Glory is a 1944 war crime drama film, directed by Raoul Walsh and starring Errol Flynn and Paul Lukas.

rows.title: No Dough Boys
rows.cast: The Three Stooges
rows.extract: No Dough Boys is a 1944 short subject directed by Jules White starring American slapstick comedy team The Three Stooges. It is the 82nd entry in the series released by Columbia Pictures starring the comedians, who released 190 shorts for the studio between 1934 and 1959.

rows.title: The Old Grey Hare
rows.extract: The Old Grey Hare is a 1944 Merrie Melodies cartoon directed by Bob Clampett. The short was released on October 28, 1944, and features Bugs Bunny and Elmer Fudd.

rows.title: The Price of Rendova
rows.extract: The Price of Rendova is a 1944 propaganda film created by the US Army Signal Corps. It documents the Landings on Rendova and Munda in the Solomon Islands.

rows.title: Puttin' on the Dog
rows.extract: This is a complete list of the 164 shorts in the Tom and Jerry series produced and released between 1940 and 2014. Of these, 162 are theatrical shorts, one is a made-for-TV short, and one is a 2-minute sketch shown as part of a telethon.

rows.title: Return to Guam
rows.extract: Return to Guam is a 1944 short propaganda film produced by the US Navy about the taking and recapture of the island of Guam.

rows.title: Russian Rhapsody
rows.cast: Looney Tunes
rows.extract: Russian Rhapsody is a 1944 Warner Bros. Merrie Melodies cartoon directed by Bob Clampett. The short was released on May 20, 1944.

rows.title: Safety Sleuth
rows.cast: Pete Smith Specialty, with, Dave O'Brien

rows.title: Sportsman's Memories
rows.cast: Pete Smith Specialty, with, Dave O'Brien

rows.title: Stage Door Cartoon
rows.extract: Stage Door Cartoon is a 1944 Merrie Melodies cartoon directed by Friz Freleng. The short was released on December 30, 1944, and features Bugs Bunny and Elmer Fudd.

rows.title: Tick Tock Tuckered
rows.extract: Tick Tock Tuckered is a 1944 Warner Bros. Looney Tunes cartoon directed by Bob Clampett. The cartoon was released on April 8, 1944, and stars Porky Pig and Daffy Duck. This is a color remake of the cartoon Porky's Badtime Story (1937), with Daffy filling the role that was previously played by Gabby

rows.title: What Makes a Battle
rows.extract: What Makes a Battle was a propaganda short produced by the US Army Pictorial Service in 1944. It documents the taking of the Marshall Islands while also encouraging increased war production.

rows.title: What's Cookin' Doc?
rows.cast: Bugs Bunny
rows.extract: What's Cookin' Doc? is a 1943-produced, 1944 Warner Bros. cartoon in the Merrie Melodies series, directed by Bob Clampett, and stars Bugs Bunny. The short was also written by Michael Sasanoff, and was animated by Robert McKimson, along with uncredited work by Rod Scribner, Phil Monroe and Virgil Ros

rows.title: With the Marines at Tarawa
rows.extract: With the Marines at Tarawa is a 1944 short documentary film directed by Louis Hayward. It uses authentic footage taken at the Battle of Tarawa to tell the story of the American servicemen from the time they get the news that they are to participate in the invasion to the final taking of the island a

rows.title: The Yoke's on Me
rows.cast: The Three Stooges
rows.extract: The Yoke's on Me is a 1944 short subject directed by Jules White starring American slapstick comedy team The Three Stooges. It is the 79th entry in the series released by Columbia Pictures starring the comedians, who appeared in 190 shorts at the studio between 1934 and 1959.

rows.title: The Zoot Cat
rows.cast: Tom and Jerry
rows.extract: The Zoot Cat  is a 1944 American Technicolor one-reel animated short and is the 13th Tom and Jerry short. It was released to theatres on February 26, 1944 by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. The cartoon features much 1940s slang, a parody of the popular zoot suit, and some features of 1930s popular culture.

rows.title: Abbott and Costello in Hollywood
rows.cast: Abbott and Costello, Lucille Ball, Rags Ragland
rows.extract: Abbott and Costello in Hollywood is a 1945 American black-and-white comedy film directed by S. Sylvan Simon and starring the comedy team of Abbott and Costello alongside Frances Rafferty. Made by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, it was produced by Martin A. Gosch.

rows.title: Adventure
rows.cast: Clark Gable, Greer Garson, Joan Blondell
rows.extract: Adventure is a 1946 American romantic drama film directed by Victor Fleming and starring Clark Gable and Greer Garson. Based on the 1937 novel The Anointed by Clyde Brion Davis, the film is about a sailor who falls in love with a librarian. Adventure was Gable's first postwar film and the tagline re

rows.title: Adventures of Kitty O'Day
rows.cast: Jean Parker, Peter Cookson
rows.extract: Adventures of Kitty O'Day is a 1945 American comedy mystery film directed by William Beaudine and starring Jean Parker, Peter Cookson and Tim Ryan. It was a sequel to the 1944 film Detective Kitty O'Day. The two films were an attempt to create a new detective series but no further films were made. A

rows.title: Adventures of Rusty
rows.cast: Margaret Lindsay, Conrad Nagel
rows.extract: Adventures of Rusty is a 1945 drama film, the first in the "Rusty" series of children's films. The series of eight films were made in the 1940s by Columbia Pictures with stories centered on Rusty, a German Shepherd dog. The film is notable for featuring the famous Ace the Wonder Dog as Rusty, the on

rows.title: The Affairs of Susan
rows.cast: Joan Fontaine, George Brent, Dennis O'Keefe
rows.extract: The Affairs of Susan is a 1945 American romantic comedy drama film directed by William A. Seiter and starring Joan Fontaine, Walter Abel, George Brent, Dennis O'Keefe and Don DeFore. It is also known as Chameleon.

rows.title: Allotment Wives
rows.cast: Kay Francis, Otto Kruger, Gertrude Michael
rows.extract: Allotment Wives is a 1945 American film noir directed by William Nigh and starring Kay Francis. Its plot is about an army investigator who tries to shut down a scam that preys on soldiers, and unknowingly falls in love with the woman behind it.

rows.title: Along Came Jones
rows.cast: Gary Cooper, Loretta Young, William Demarest, Dan Duryea
rows.extract: Along Came Jones is a 1945 American Western comedy film directed by Stuart Heisler and starring Gary Cooper, Loretta Young, William Demarest, and Dan Duryea. The film was adapted by Nunnally Johnson from the 1944 novel Useless Cowboy by Alan Le May. It was the only feature film produced by Cooper du

rows.title: Along the Navajo Trail
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Dale Evans, Estelita Rodriguez
rows.extract: Along the Navajo Trail is a 1945 American Western film directed by Frank McDonald and starring Roy Rogers, Gabby Hayes and Dale Evans. The film's story was based on a William Colt MacDonald novel. The film marked the debut of the Cuban actress Estelita Rodriguez, who Republic Pictures then began to

rows.title: An Angel Comes to Brooklyn
rows.cast: Barbara Perry, Charles Kemper
rows.extract: An Angel Comes to Brooklyn is a 1945 American comedy film directed by Leslie Goodwins and written by June Carroll and Stanley Paley. The film stars Kaye Dowd, Robert Duke, David Street, Barbara Perry, Charles Kemper and Marguerite d'Alvarez. The film was released on November 27, 1945, by Republic Pi

rows.title: Anchors Aweigh
rows.cast: Frank Sinatra, Kathryn Grayson, Gene Kelly
rows.extract: Anchors Aweigh is a 1945 American musical comedy film directed by George Sidney, starring Frank Sinatra, Kathryn Grayson, and Gene Kelly, with songs by Jule Styne and Sammy Cahn. The film also features José Iturbi, Pamela Britton, Dean Stockwell, and Sharon McManus.

rows.title: And Then There Were None
rows.cast: Barry Fitzgerald, Walter Huston, Louis Hayward, Roland Young
rows.extract: And Then There Were None is a 1945 film adaptation of Agatha Christie's 1939 mystery novel of the same name, directed by René Clair. It was released in the United Kingdom as Ten Little Indians, in keeping with the third United Kingdom title of Christie's novel.

rows.title: Apology for Murder
rows.cast: Ann Savage, Hugh Beaumont
rows.extract: Apology for Murder is a 1945 American film noir directed by Sam Newfield and starring Ann Savage, Hugh Beaumont, Russell Hicks and Charles D. Brown.

rows.title: Arson Squad
rows.cast: Frank Albertson, Robert Armstrong

rows.title: Back to Bataan
rows.cast: John Wayne, Anthony Quinn, Beulah Bondi
rows.extract: Back to Bataan is a 1945 American black-and-white World War II war film drama from RKO Radio Pictures, produced by Robert Fellows, directed by Edward Dmytryk, that stars John Wayne and Anthony Quinn. The film depicts events that took place after the Battle of Bataan (1941–42) on the island of Luzon

rows.title: Bad Men of the Border
rows.cast: Kirby Grant, Armida
rows.extract: Bad Men of the Border is a 1945 American Western film directed by Wallace Fox and written by Adele Buffington. The film stars Kirby Grant, Fuzzy Knight, Armida, John Eldredge, Barbara Sears and Edward Howard. The film was released on September 28, 1945, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Bandits of the Badlands
rows.cast: Sunset Carson, Peggy Stewart
rows.extract: Bandits of the Badlands is a 1945 American Western film directed by Thomas Carr and written by Doris Schroeder. The film stars Sunset Carson, Peggy Stewart, Si Jenks, John Merton, Forrest Taylor and Wade Crosby. The film was released on September 14, 1945, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Bedside Manner
rows.cast: John Carroll, Ruth Hussey, Ann Rutherford
rows.extract: Bedside Manner is a 1945 American film directed by Andrew L. Stone, based on a 1944 Saturday Evening Post story of the same name by Robert Carson. The film was re-released in 1950 under the title Her Favorite Patient.

rows.title: Behind City Lights
rows.cast: Lynne Roberts, Peter Cookson
rows.extract: Behind City Lights is a 1945 American crime film directed by John English and written by Richard Weil and Gertrude Walker. The film stars Lynne Roberts, Peter Cookson, Jerome Cowan, Esther Dale, William Terry and Victor Kilian. The film was released on September 10, 1945, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: A Bell for Adano
rows.cast: Gene Tierney, John Hodiak, William Bendix
rows.extract: A Bell for Adano is a 1945 American war film directed by Henry King and starring John Hodiak and Gene Tierney. rows.title: Bells of Rosarita
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Dale Evans
rows.extract: Bells of Rosarita  is a 1945 American musical Western film starring Roy Rogers and directed by Frank McDonald.

rows.title: The Bells of St. Mary's
rows.cast: Bing Crosby, Ingrid Bergman
rows.extract: The Bells of St. Mary's (1945) is an American musical comedy-drama film, produced and directed by Leo McCarey and starring Bing Crosby and Ingrid Bergman. Written by Dudley Nichols and based on a story by McCarey, the film is about a priest and a nun who, despite their good-natured rivalry, try to s

rows.title: Betrayal from the East
rows.cast: Lee Tracy, Nancy Kelly
rows.extract: Betrayal from the East is a 1945 American spy drama film starring Lee Tracy and Nancy Kelly. The film was directed by William A. Berke and based on the book Betrayal from the East: The Inside Story of Japanese Spies in America by Alan Hynd. The supporting cast features Richard Loo, Regis Toomey, Phi

rows.title: Between Two Women
rows.cast: Van Johnson, Gloria DeHaven, Marilyn Maxwell
rows.extract: Between Two Women, made in 1945, was the sixteenth film in the Dr Kildare series. This was the fourteenth of fifteen in which Lionel Barrymore starred as Dr. Leonard B. Gillespie. The film following was Dark Delusion (1947), which was the last in the Dr. Kildare series released by Metro-Goldwyn-Maye

rows.title: Bewitched
rows.cast: Phyllis Thaxter, Edmund Gwenn
rows.extract: Bewitched is a 1945 American film noir directed and written by Arch Oboler. The drama features Phyllis Thaxter and Edmund Gwenn.

rows.title: Beyond the Pecos
rows.cast: Rod Cameron, Jennifer Holt
rows.extract: Beyond the Pecos is a 1945 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by Bennett Cohen. The film stars Rod Cameron, Eddie Dew, Fuzzy Knight, Jennifer Holt, Ray Whitley, Gene Roth, Robert Homans and Jack Ingram. The film was released on April 27, 1945, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: The Big Show-Off
rows.cast: Arthur Lake, Dale Evans
rows.extract: The Big Show-Off is a 1945 American comedy film directed by Howard Bretherton and distributed by Republic Pictures. It teams Arthur Lake before his return to the Blondie film series and Dale Evans, most frequently seen with her husband Roy Rogers.

rows.title: Black Market Babies
rows.cast: Teala Loring, Kane Richmond
rows.extract: Black Market Babies is a 1945 American crime drama film directed by William Beaudine and released by Monogram Pictures. The film has been released on dvd.

rows.title: Blazing the Western Trail
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Dub Taylor, Carole Mathews
rows.extract: Blazing the Western Trail is a 1945 American Western film directed by Vernon Keays and written by J. Benton Cheney. The film stars Charles Starrett, Tex Harding, Dub Taylor, Carole Mathews and Bob Wills. The film was released on September 18, 1945, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Blonde from Brooklyn
rows.cast: Bob Haymes, Lynn Merrick
rows.extract: Blonde from Brooklyn is a 1945 American musical comedy film directed by Del Lord and starring Bob Haymes, Lynn Merrick, Thurston Hall, and Mary Treen. The film was released by Columbia Pictures on June 21, 1945.

rows.title: Blonde Ransom
rows.cast: Virginia Grey, Pinky Lee
rows.extract: Blonde Ransom is a 1945 American comedy film directed by William Beaudine and starring Donald Cook, Virginia Grey, and Pinky Lee.

rows.title: Blood on the Sun
rows.cast: James Cagney, Sylvia Sidney
rows.extract: Blood on the Sun is a 1945 American war film directed by Frank Lloyd and starring James Cagney and Sylvia Sidney. The film is based on a fictional history behind the Tanaka Memorial document.

rows.title: The Body Snatcher
rows.cast: Boris Karloff, Bela Lugosi
rows.extract: The Body Snatcher is a 1945 American horror film directed by Robert Wise, based on the 1884 short story of the same name by Robert Louis Stevenson. rows.title: Border Badmen
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Lorraine Miller
rows.extract: Border Badmen is a 1945 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Milton Raison. The film stars Buster Crabbe, Al St. John, Lorraine Miller, Charles King, Ray Bennett and Arch Hall Sr. The film was released on October 10, 1945, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: Boston Blackie Booked on Suspicion
rows.cast: Chester Morris, Lynn Merrick
rows.extract: Boston Blackie Booked on Suspicion is the eighth of 14 Columbia Pictures B movies starring Chester Morris as reformed thief Boston Blackie.

rows.title: Boston Blackie's Rendezvous
rows.cast: Chester Morris, Nina Foch
rows.extract: Boston Blackie's Rendezvous is a 1945 American crime film directed by Arthur Dreifuss. The working title of this film was Surprise in the Night.

rows.title: Both Barrels Blazing
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Dub Taylor
rows.extract: Both Barrels Blazing is a 1945 American Western film directed by Derwin Abrahams and starring Charles Starrett.

rows.title: Brewster's Millions
rows.cast: Dennis O'Keefe, Helen Walker, June Havoc
rows.extract: Brewster's Millions is a 1945 American comedy film, one of many film adaptations of the 1902 novel of the same name by George Barr McCutcheon and the subsequent smash-hit play adaptation by Byron Ongley and Winchell Smith. In the novel, Brewster is a stockbroker; in this version, he is portrayed as

rows.title: The Brighton Strangler
rows.cast: John Loder, June Duprez
rows.extract: The Brighton Strangler is a 1945 American crime film directed by Max Nosseck and starring John Loder, June Duprez and Michael St. Angel. During the blitz in wartime London, an actor suffers concussion and believes himself to be the character he has most recently been playing - a vicious strangler wi

rows.title: Bring on the Girls
rows.cast: Veronica Lake, Marjorie Reynolds
rows.extract: Bring on the Girls is a 1945 American musical comedy film starring Eddie Bracken, Sonny Tufts and Veronica Lake. It is loosely based on the 1940 French comedy The Man Who Seeks the Truth.

rows.title: The Bullfighters
rows.cast: Laurel and Hardy
rows.extract: The Bullfighters is the penultimate feature film starring Laurel and Hardy, the sixth and final film the duo made under 20th Century Fox as well as the last released in the United States.

rows.title: Captain Eddie
rows.cast: Fred MacMurray, Lynn Bari
rows.extract: Captain Eddie is a 1945 American drama film directed by Lloyd Bacon, based on Seven Were Saved by "Eddie" Rickenbacker and Lt. James Whittaker's We Thought We Heard the Angels Sing. The film stars Fred MacMurray, Lynn Bari and Charles Bickford. Captain Eddie is a "biopic" of Rickenbacker, from his e

rows.title: The Captain from Köpenick
rows.cast: Albert Bassermann, Mary Brian
rows.extract: The Captain from Köpenick, also known as I Was a Criminal and Passport to Heaven, is a 1945 American comedy film directed by Richard Oswald and based upon the 1931 play The Captain of Köpenick by Carl Zuckmayer and Albright Joseph. The play was based on the true story of Wilhelm Voigt, a German ex-c

rows.title: Captain Kidd
rows.cast: Charles Laughton, Randolph Scott, Barbara Britton
rows.extract: Captain Kidd is a 1945 American adventure film starring Charles Laughton, Randolph Scott and Barbara Britton. It was directed by Rowland V. rows.title: Captain Tugboat Annie
rows.cast: Jane Darwell, Edgar Kennedy
rows.extract: Captain Tugboat Annie is a 1945 second sequel to the classic Tugboat Annie (1933), this time starring Jane Darwell as Annie and Edgar Kennedy as Horatio Bullwinkle. The film was directed by Phil Rosen, and is also known as Tugboat Annie's Son.

rows.title: The Caribbean Mystery
rows.cast: James Dunn, Sheila Ryan
rows.extract: The Caribbean Mystery is a 1945 American film noir mystery film which marked the directorial debut of Robert D. Webb. rows.cast: Joseph Schildkraut, Billie Burke
rows.extract: The Cheaters (1945) [also known as MR. M. and the Pigeons, The Amazing MR. M., The Magnificent Mr. M. and The Magnificent Rogue) is a Christmas "screwball comedy" tale about a has-been actor invited to Christmas dinner by a rich family. The film was atypical of the Republic Pictures studio, directed

rows.title: The Cherokee Flash
rows.cast: Sunset Carson, Linda Stirling, Tom London
rows.extract: The Cherokee Flash is a 1945 American Western film directed by Thomas Carr. It is a Sunset Carson serial Western in which Carson works to free his father and clear the family name from a crime his father did not commit.

rows.title: The Chicago Kid
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Otto Kruger
rows.extract: The Chicago Kid is a 1945 American crime film directed by Frank McDonald and written by Jack Townley and Albert Beich. The film stars Don "Red" Barry, Otto Kruger, Tom Powers, Lynne Roberts, Henry H. Daniels Jr. and Chick Chandler. The film was released on June 29, 1945, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: China Sky
rows.cast: Randolph Scott, Ruth Warrick, Ellen Drew
rows.extract: China Sky is a 1945 RKO Pictures film based on the novel by Pearl S. Buck. It was directed by Ray Enright and featured movie idol Randolph Scott, teamed with Ruth Warrick, Ellen Drew and Anthony Quinn. Although set in wartime China, Quinn and other lead actors portrayed Chinese characters, in keepin

rows.title: China's Little Devils
rows.cast: Harry Carey, Paul Kelly
rows.extract: China's Little Devils is a 1945 war film, directed by Monta Bell and starring Harry Carey, Paul Kelly and "Ducky" Louie. It is one of a number of Hollywood films dealing with the exploits of the Flying Tigers that began with the Republic Pictures production Flying Tigers (1942).

rows.title: Christmas in Connecticut
rows.cast: Barbara Stanwyck, Dennis Morgan, Reginald Gardiner, Sydney Greenstreet
rows.extract: Christmas in Connecticut is a 1945 American Christmas romantic comedy film about an unmarried city magazine writer who pretends to be a farm wife and mother and then falls in love with a returning war hero. The film was directed by English director Peter Godfrey and stars Barbara Stanwyck, Dennis Mo

rows.title: Circumstantial Evidence
rows.cast: Lloyd Nolan, Michael O'Shea, Trudy Marshall
rows.extract: Circumstantial Evidence is a 1945 American film noir directed by John Larkin and starring Michael O'Shea, Lloyd Nolan, and Trudy Marshall.

rows.title: The Cisco Kid Returns
rows.cast: Duncan Renaldo, Martin Garralaga
rows.extract: The Cisco Kid Returns is a 1945 American Western film. Released on April 3, 1945, it was the first of three Cisco Kid films made that year with Duncan Renaldo as Cisco and Martin Garralaga as Pancho. In this release, Cisco's real name is Juan Francisco Hernandez. Cisco must clear himself of murder c

rows.title: The Clock
rows.cast: Judy Garland, Robert Walker
rows.extract: The Clock is a 1945 American romantic drama film starring Judy Garland and Robert Walker and directed by Garland's future husband, Vincente Minnelli. This was Garland's first dramatic role, as well as her first starring vehicle in which she did not sing.

rows.title: Club Havana
rows.cast: Margaret Lindsay, Tom Neal, Lita Baron
rows.extract: Club Havana is a 1945 American film drama directed by Edgar G. Ulmer. It was produced and released by independent film company Producers Releasing Corporation. It has been compared to the 1933 film Grand Hotel.

rows.title: Code of the Lawless
rows.cast: Kirby Grant, Jane Adams
rows.extract: Code of the Lawless is a 1945 American Western film directed by Wallace Fox and written by Patricia Harper. The film stars Kirby Grant, Fuzzy Knight, Poni Adams, Hugh Prosser, Barbara Sears and Edward Howard. The film was released on October 19, 1945, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Colorado Pioneers
rows.cast: Wild Bill Elliott, Alice Fleming

rows.title: Come Out Fighting
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall, Billy Benedict
rows.extract: Come Out Fighting is a 1945 American film directed by William Beaudine. It was the last in the Monogram Pictures series of "East Side Kids" films before the series was reinvented as "The Bowery Boys. Film critic Leonard Maltin described the film as "grating," giving it one and a half out of four sta

rows.title: Confidential Agent
rows.cast: Charles Boyer, Lauren Bacall
rows.extract: Confidential Agent is a 1945 American spy film starring Charles Boyer and Lauren Bacall which was a Warner Brothers production. The movie was directed by Herman Shumlin and produced by Robert Buckner with Jack L. Warner as executive producer. The screenplay was by Robert Buckner, based on the 1939 n

rows.title: Conflict
rows.cast: Humphrey Bogart, Alexis Smith, Sydney Greenstreet
rows.extract: Conflict is a 1945 American black-and-white suspense film noir made by Warner Brothers. It was directed by Curtis Bernhardt, produced by William Jacobs from a screenplay by Arthur T. Horman and Dwight Taylor, based on the story The Pentacle by Alfred Neumann and Robert Siodmak. It starred Humphrey B

rows.title: The Corn Is Green
rows.cast: Bette Davis, Joan Lorring, John Dall
rows.extract: The Corn Is Green is a 1945 American drama film starring Bette Davis as a schoolteacher determined to bring education to a Welsh coal mining town despite great opposition. It was adapted from the 1938 play of the same name by Emlyn Williams, which originally starred Ethel Barrymore.

rows.title: Cornered
rows.cast: Dick Powell, Walter Slezak
rows.extract: Cornered is a 1945 film noir starring Dick Powell and directed by Edward Dmytryk. This is the second teaming of Powell and Dmytryk. The screenplay was written by John Paxton with uncredited help from Ben Hecht.

rows.title: Corpus Christi Bandits
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Helen Talbot
rows.extract: Corpus Christi Bandits is a 1945 American Western film directed by Wallace Grissell and written by Norman S. Hall. The film stars Allan Lane, Helen Talbot, Jack Kirk, Twinkle Watts, Francis McDonald and Roy Barcroft. The film was released on April 20, 1945, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Counter-Attack
rows.cast: Paul Muni, Marguerite Chapman, Larry Parks
rows.extract: Counter-Attack is a 1945 American war film directed by Zoltan Korda and starring Paul Muni and Marguerite Chapman as two Russians trapped in a collapsed building with seven enemy German soldiers during World War II. It was adapted from the 1944 Broadway play Counterattack by Janet and Philip Stevens

rows.title: The Crime Doctor's Courage
rows.cast: Warner Baxter, Hillary Brooke
rows.extract: The Crime Doctor's Courage is a 1945 American mystery film directed by George Sherman and starring Warner Baxter, Hillary Brooke and Jerome Cowan. It is part of the Crime Doctor series of films made by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Crime Doctor's Warning
rows.cast: Warner Baxter, Dusty Anderson
rows.extract: Crime Doctor's Warning is a 1945 American mystery film directed by William Castle, and fourth in the Crime Doctor series of ten films produced between 1943 and 1949.

rows.title: Crime, Inc.
rows.cast: Leo Carrillo, Tom Neal, Martha Tilton, Lionel Atwill
rows.extract: Crime, Inc. is a 1945 American film noir crime film directed by Lew Landers starring Leo Carrillo, Tom Neal and Martha Tilton.

rows.title: The Crimson Canary
rows.cast: Noah Beery Jr., Lois Collier, Steven Geray
rows.extract: The Crimson Canary is a 1945 American mystery film directed by John Hoffman and written by Henry Blankfort and Peggy Phillips. The film stars Noah Beery Jr., Lois Collier, John Litel, Steven Geray, Claudia Drake and Danny Morton. The film was released on November 9, 1945, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Dakota
rows.cast: John Wayne, Vera Ralston
rows.extract: Dakota is a 1945 American Western film directed by Joseph Kane, and starring John Wayne. The supporting cast features Walter Brennan, Ward Bond, and Mike Mazurki.

rows.title: The Daltons Ride Again
rows.cast: Lon Chaney Jr., Alan Curtis, Martha O'Driscoll
rows.extract: The Daltons Ride Again is a 1945 American Western film directed by Ray Taylor starring Alan Curtis, Lon Chaney Jr., Kent Taylor and Noah Beery Jr. The movie was made by Universal Pictures and the supporting cast features Milburn Stone and Douglas Dumbrille.

rows.title: Dangerous Intruder
rows.cast: Veda Ann Borg, Charles Arnt
rows.extract: Dangerous Intruder is a 1945 American film noir directed by Vernon Keays, starring Charles Arnt, Veda Ann Borg and Richard Powers.

rows.title: Dangerous Partners
rows.cast: Signe Hasso, James Craig
rows.extract: Dangerous Partners is a 1945 American adventure film directed by Edward L. Cahn and written by Marion Parsonnet and Edmund L. rows.title: Danger Signal
rows.cast: Faye Emerson, Zachary Scott
rows.extract: Danger Signal is a 1945 film noir starring Faye Emerson and Zachary Scott. The screenplay was adapted from the 1939 novel of the same name by Phyllis Bottome.

rows.title: Delightfully Dangerous
rows.cast: Jane Powell, Ralph Bellamy, Constance Moore
rows.extract: Delightfully Dangerous is a 1945 American musical film directed by Arthur Lubin showcasing teenage singer Jane Powell—in her second film on loan out to United Artists from MGM—and orchestra leader Morton Gould. rows.title: Detour
rows.cast: Tom Neal, Ann Savage
rows.extract: Detour is a 1945 American independent film noir directed by Edgar G. Ulmer starring Tom Neal and Ann Savage. rows.cast: Betty Grable, Dick Haymes, Phil Silvers
rows.extract: Diamond Horseshoe is a 1945 Technicolor musical film starring Betty Grable and Dick Haymes, directed by George Seaton, and released by 20th Century Fox. rows.title: Dick Tracy
rows.cast: Morgan Conway, Anne Jeffreys, Mike Mazurki
rows.extract: Dick Tracy is a 1945 American action film based on the Dick Tracy comic strip created by Chester Gould. The film is the first of four installment of the Dick Tracy film series, released by RKO Radio Pictures.

rows.title: Dillinger
rows.cast: Lawrence Tierney, Anne Jeffreys
rows.extract: Dillinger is a 1945 gangster film telling the story of John Dillinger.

rows.title: Divorce
rows.cast: Kay Francis, Bruce Cabot, Helen Mack
rows.extract: Divorce is a 1945 drama film about a much-divorced woman who sets her sights on her married childhood friend. It stars Kay Francis, Bruce Cabot, and Helen Mack.

rows.title: Docks of New York
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall
rows.extract: Docks of New York is a 1945 film directed by Wallace Fox and starring the East Side Kids.

rows.title: Doll Face
rows.cast: Vivian Blaine, Carmen Miranda, Dennis O'Keefe
rows.extract: Doll Face is a 1945 American film released by 20th Century Fox and directed by Lewis Seiler starring Vivian Blaine as "Doll Face" Carroll. rows.cast: Betty Grable, June Haver, John Payne
rows.extract: The Dolly Sisters is a 1945 American Technicolor biographical film about the Dolly Sisters, identical twins who became famous as entertainers on Broadway and in Europe in the early years of the 20th century as Jennie and Rosie Dolly, Hungarian-born entertainers. rows.title: Don Juan Quilligan
rows.cast: William Bendix, Phil Silvers

rows.title: Earl Carroll Vanities

rows.cast: Gloria Jean, Kirby Grant, Eric Blore
rows.extract: Easy to Look At is a 1945 American comedy film directed by Ford Beebe and written by Henry Blankfort. The film stars Gloria Jean, Kirby Grant, J. Edward Bromberg, Eric Blore, George Dolenz, and Mildred Law. The film was released on August 10, 1945, by Universal Pictures.

rows.cast: Robert Young, Dorothy McGuire
rows.extract: The Enchanted Cottage is a 1945 American romantic fantasy starring Dorothy McGuire, Robert Young, and Herbert Marshall, with Mildred Natwick.

rows.title: The Enchanted Forest
rows.cast: Edmund Lowe, Brenda Joyce
rows.extract: The Enchanted Forest is a 1945 family film starring Edmund Lowe and Brenda Joyce, also featuring Harry Davenport as a hermit who finds and raises a young boy in a forest. rows.cast: Tex Ritter, Kay Hughes
rows.extract: Enemy of the Law is a 1945 American Western film written and directed by Harry L. Fraser. The film stars Tex Ritter, Dave O'Brien, Guy Wilkerson, Kay Hughes, Jack Ingram and Charles King. The film was released on May 7, 1945, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: Escape in the Desert
rows.cast: Jean Sullivan, Philip Dorn, Irene Manning
rows.extract: Escape in the Desert is a 1945 American drama film directed by Edward A. Blatt and written by Marvin Borowsky and Thomas Job. rows.cast: Otto Kruger, Nina Foch
rows.extract: Escape in the Fog is a 1945 American film noir crime film directed by Budd Boetticher and starring Otto Kruger, Nina Foch and William Wright.

rows.cast: Ann Miller, William Wright
rows.extract: Eve Knew Her Apples is a 1945 musical comedy remake of the 1934 film It Happened One Night directed by Will Jason and starring Ann Miller. rows.cast: Alice Faye, Dana Andrews, Linda Darnell

Stanford Jolley, Kermit Maynard and John Cason. The film was released on October 31, 1945, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.cast: Tom Neal, Barbara Hale
rows.extract: First Yank into Tokyo is a 1945 American war film directed by Gordon Douglas for RKO Radio Pictures, starring Tom Neal, Keye Luke, Barbara Hale, and Richard Loo. rows.title: Flame of Barbary Coast
rows.cast: John Wayne, Ann Dvorak, Joseph Schildkraut
rows.extract: Flame of Barbary Coast is a 1945 American musical-drama film starring John Wayne, Ann Dvorak, Joseph Schildkraut, William Frawley, and Virginia Grey. The movie was scripted by Borden Chase and directed by Joseph Kane.

rows.title: Flame of the West
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Joan Woodbury
rows.extract: Flame of the West is a 1945 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and starring Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton and Joan Woodbury.

rows.cast: Tex Ritter, Dave O'Brien
rows.extract: Flaming Bullets is a 1945 American Western film written and directed by Harry L. Fraser. rows.title: Fog Island
rows.cast: George Zucco, Lionel Atwill
rows.extract: Fog Island is a 1945 American mystery-suspense film directed by Terry O. Morse. The film stars B movie horror film regulars George Zucco and Lionel Atwill. It was based on the 1937 play Angel Island by Bernadine "Bernie" Angus.

rows.title: Follow That Woman
rows.cast: William Gargan, Nancy Kelly
rows.extract: Follow That Woman is a 1945 crime film starring William Gargan, Nancy Kelly, and Regis Toomey. The movie was directed by Lew Landers.

rows.cast: Gale Storm, C. Aubrey Smith, Conrad Nagel
rows.extract: Forever Yours is a 1945 American drama film directed by William Nigh and starring Gale Storm, C. Aubrey Smith and Johnny Mack Brown. It was made by Monogram Pictures. rows.title: Frisco Sal
rows.cast: Susanna Foster, Turhan Bey
rows.extract: Frisco Sal is a 1945 American Western film directed by George Waggner and starring Susanna Foster and Turhan Bey. It was co written by Curt Siodmak.

rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: Frontier Feud is a 1945 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by Adele Buffington. rows.cast: Tex Ritter, Lorraine Miller

Stanford Jolley and Jack Ingram. The film was released on September 1, 1945, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: Frontier Gal
rows.cast: Yvonne de Carlo, Rod Cameron
rows.extract: Frontier Gal is a 1945 American Western film directed by Charles Lamont and starring Yvonne De Carlo and Rod Cameron.

rows.title: The Frozen Ghost
rows.cast: Lon Chaney Jr., Elena Verdugo, Evelyn Ankers, Douglas Dumbrille
rows.extract: The Frozen Ghost is a 1945 American film noir mystery film starring Lon Chaney, Jr., Elena Verdugo, Evelyn Ankers, Tala Birell, and Martin Kosleck, and directed by Harold Young. It is the fourth of the six "Inner Sanctum" mystery films.

rows.title: A Game of Death
rows.cast: Audrey Long, John Loder
rows.extract: A Game of Death is a 1945 American adventure film directed by Robert Wise and starring John Loder and Audrey Long. rows.cast: Stephanie Bachelor, Robert Armstrong
rows.extract: Gangs of the Waterfront is a 1945 American crime drama film directed by George Blair, and based on an original story by Samuel Fuller. rows.title: Gangster's Den
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Al St. John
rows.extract: Gangster's Den is a 1945 American Producers Releasing Corporation Western film of the "Billy the Kid" series directed by Sam Newfield. The film is notable for having three comedy relief characters; Al St. John, Emmett Lynn, and Charles King, who usually plays the villain.

rows.title: The Gay Senorita
rows.cast: Jinx Falkenburg, Jim Bannon
rows.extract: The Gay Senorita is a 1945 American comedy-drama film directed by Arthur Dreifuss, which stars Jinx Falkenburg, Jim Bannon, and Steve Cochran.

rows.title: G. I. Honeymoon
rows.cast: Gale Storm, Arline Judge
rows.extract: G.I. Honeymoon is a 1945 film directed by Phil Karlson. It stars Gale Storm and Peter Cookson. Both play a couple who encounter problems as the husband wants to leave the army, but can't. It was nominated for an Academy Award in 1946 for its music.

rows.title: George White's Scandals
rows.cast: Joan Davis, Jack Haley
rows.extract: George White's Scandals  is a 1945 American film starring Joan Davis, Jack Haley, Phillip Terry, and Glenn Tryon. It features Haley's Wizard of Oz co-star Margaret Hamilton. This film included music by Edwin Finckel.

rows.title: Getting Gertie's Garter
rows.cast: Dennis O'Keefe, Marie McDonald, Barry Sullivan
rows.extract: Getting Gertie's Garter is a 1945 American slapstick comedy film written and directed by Allan Dwan, and starring Dennis O'Keefe, Marie McDonald, and Barry Sullivan. rows.title: The Girl of the Limberlost
rows.cast: Ruth Nelson, Gloria Holden
rows.extract: The Girl of the Limberlost is a 1945 American drama film starring Ruth Nelson, Dorinda Clifton, and Loren Tindall, and directed by Mel Ferrer. The film is based on a 1909 novel by Gene Stratton-Porter, which was previously filmed in 1909 as "A Girl of the Limeberlost".

rows.title: Girls of the Big House

rows.cast: Eric von Stroheim, Mary Beth Hughes
rows.extract: The Great Flamarion is a 1945 film noir mystery film directed by Anthony Mann starring Erich von Stroheim and Mary Beth Hughes. The film, like many films noir, is shot in flashback narrative. The film was produced by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Great John L.
rows.cast: Linda Darnell, Barbara Britton, Greg McClure

rows.title: Gun Smoke

rows.cast: Fred Allen, Jack Benny, Don Ameche

It was the eighth of twenty-three Red Ryder feature films that would be produced by Republic Pictures.

rows.cast: Pat O'Brien, Ellen Drew
rows.extract: Man Alive is a 1945 romantic comedy film directed by Ray Enright and starring Pat O'Brien, Adolphe Menjou, Ellen Drew and Rudy Vallée.

rows.extract: The Man in Half Moon Street is a 1945 science fiction romantic melodrama dealing with a man who retains his youth and cannot die, living throughout the ages. rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Dale Evans
rows.extract: The Man from Oklahoma  is a 1945 American western film directed by Frank McDonald and starring Roy Rogers, Dale Evans and George 'Gabby' Hayes. It was produced and distributed by Republic Pictures.

rows.cast: Kay Aldridge, Dave O'Brien
rows.extract: The Man Who Walked Alone is a 1945 American B film romantic comedy film produced by PRC Pictures, Inc., directed by Christy Cabanne, with top-billed Dave O'Brien and Kay Aldridge, along with Walter Catlett and Guinn Williams.

rows.title: Marked for Murder
rows.cast: Tex Ritter, Dave O'Brien
rows.extract: Marked for Murder is a 1945 American Western film written and directed by Elmer Clifton. The film stars Dave O'Brien, Tex Ritter and Guy Wilkerson, with Marilyn McConnell, Ed Cassidy and Henry Hall. The film was released on 8 February 1945, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.extract: Marshal of Laredo is a 1945 American Western film directed by R.G. rows.title: Masquerade in Mexico
rows.cast: Dorothy Lamour, Patric Knowles, Ann Dvorak
rows.extract: Masquerade in Mexico is a 1945 comedy film directed by Mitchell Leisen. It stars Dorothy Lamour and Arturo de Córdova.

rows.title: A Medal for Benny
rows.cast: Dorothy Lamour, Arturo de Córdova
rows.extract: A Medal for Benny is a 1945 American film directed by Irving Pichel. The story was conceived by writer Jack Wagner, who enlisted his long-time friend John Steinbeck to help him put it into script form. The film was released by Paramount Pictures. The film is also known as Benny's Medal.

rows.title: Men in Her Diary
rows.cast: Peggy Ryan, Jon Hall
rows.extract: Men in Her Diary is a 1945 American comedy film. It stars Peggy Ryan and Jon Hall and was written by Lester Cole and directed by Charles Barton. It followed from the success of San Diego, I Love You.

rows.title: Mexicana
rows.cast: Tito Guízar, Constance Moore
rows.extract: Mexicana is a 1945 American musical film directed by Alfred Santell and starring Tito Guízar, Constance Moore and Leo Carrillo. rows.title: Midnight Manhunt
rows.cast: William Gargan, Ann Savage
rows.extract: Midnight Manhunt is a 1945 film noir crime film mystery directed by William C. Thomas and written by David Lang. The film premiered on July 24, 1945 and is in the public domain.

rows.title: Mildred Pierce
rows.cast: Joan Crawford, Jack Carson, Ann Blyth, Zachary Scott, Eve Arden
rows.extract: Mildred Pierce is a 1945 American melodrama/film noir directed by Michael Curtiz and starring Joan Crawford, Jack Carson, and Zachary Scott, also featuring Eve Arden, Ann Blyth, and Bruce Bennett. rows.title: The Missing Corpse
rows.cast: J. Edward Bromberg, Isabel Randolph
rows.extract: The Missing Corpse is a 1945 American comedy mystery film directed by Albert Herman.

rows.title: Molly and Me
rows.cast: Gracie Fields, Monty Woolley, Roddy McDowall
rows.extract: Molly and Me is a 1945 American comedy film directed by Lewis Seiler and starring Monty Woolley, Gracie Fields, Reginald Gardiner and Roddy McDowall and released by 20th Century Fox. The screenplay was based on the novel written by Frances Marion and adapted by Roger Burford.

rows.title: Mr. Muggs Rides Again
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall
rows.extract: Mr. Muggs Rides Again is a 1945 film directed by Wallace Fox and starring The East Side Kids.

rows.title: Murder, He Says
rows.cast: Fred MacMurray, Helen Walker
rows.extract: Murder, He Says is a 1945 American black comedy film directed by George Marshall and starring Fred MacMurray about a murderous rural family and the hapless pollster who becomes entangled in their hunt for a cache of money.

rows.title: My Name Is Julia Ross
rows.cast: Nina Foch, Dame May Whitty
rows.extract: My Name Is Julia Ross is a 1945 American gothic film noir directed by Joseph H. Lewis, and starring Nina Foch, Dame May Whitty, and George Macready. rows.cast: Bob Steele, Caren Marsh
rows.extract: Navajo Kid is a 1945 American Western film directed by Harry L. Fraser for Alexander-Stern Productions and starring Bob Steele as the titular character, Syd Salor and Ed Cassidy. It was distributed by Producers Releasing Corporation (PRC) and commercially released in the United States on 21 November

rows.title: The Navajo Trail
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Jennifer Holt
rows.extract: The Navajo Trail is a 1945 American Western film directed by Howard Bretherton and written by Frank H. Young. rows.title: The Naughty Nineties
rows.cast: Abbott and Costello, Alan Curtis, Lois Collier
rows.extract: The Naughty Nineties is a 1945 American film starring the comedy team of Abbott and Costello. The film is noteworthy for containing a filmed version of the duo's famous "Who's on First?" routine. This version is shown at the National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum in Cooperstown, New York.

rows.title: Night Club Girl
rows.cast: Vivian Austin, Judy Clark
rows.extract: Night Club Girl is a 1945 American comedy film directed by Edward F. Cline and written by Henry Blankfort and Dick Irving Hyland. The film stars Vivian Austin, Edward Norris, Maxie Rosenbloom, Minna Gombell, Judy Clark and Bill Dunn. The film was released on January 5, 1945, by Universal Pictures.

rows.cast: George Raft, Joan Bennett, Vivian Blaine
rows.extract: Nob Hill is a 1945 Technicolor film about a Barbary Coast, San Francisco, United States saloon keeper, starring George Raft and Joan Bennett. rows.title: Northwest Trail
rows.cast: Bob Steele, Joan Woodbury
rows.extract: Northwest Trail is a 1945 American contemporary Western film directed by Derwin Abrahams shot in Cinecolor at Lake Hemet, California. It stars Bob Steele, Joan Woodbury, and Madge Bellamy making a comeback appearance in her final film.

rows.title: Objective, Burma!
rows.cast: Errol Flynn, William Prince
rows.extract: Objective, Burma! is a 1945 American war film that is loosely based on the six-month raid by Merrill's Marauders in the Burma Campaign during the Second World War. Directed by Raoul Walsh and starring Errol Flynn, the film was made by Warner Bros. immediately after the raid.

rows.title: On Stage Everybody
rows.cast: Jack Oakie, Peggy Ryan
rows.extract: On Stage Everybody is a 1945 film starring Jack Oakie, Peggy Ryan, and Johnny Coy. Also appearing are Otto Kruger, Esther Dale, Milburn Stone, Wallace Ford, Julie London, and The King Sisters, who sang "Stuff Like That There", written by Jay Livingston and Ray Evans.

rows.title: Oregon Trail
rows.cast: Sunset Carson, Peggy Stewart
rows.extract: Oregon Trail is a 1945 American Western film directed by Thomas Carr and written by Betty Burbridge. The film stars Sunset Carson, Peggy Stewart, Frank Jaquet, John Merton, Mary Carr and Si Jenks. The film was released on July 14, 1945, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Out of This World
rows.cast: Veronica Lake, Eddie Bracken, Diana Lynn, Cass Daley
rows.extract: Out of This World is a 1945 American romantic comedy film directed by Hal Walker and starring Eddie Bracken, Veronica Lake and Diana Lynn. The picture was a satire on the Frank Sinatra "bobby soxer" cult.

rows.title: Outlaws of the Rockies
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Carole Mathews, Dub Taylor
rows.extract: Outlaws of the Rockies is a 1945 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by J. Benton Cheney. rows.extract: Pan-Americana is a 1945 American romantic comedy film produced and directed by John H. Auer, from a screenplay by Lawrence Kimble, based on a story by Auer and Frederick Kohner. rows.title: Pardon My Past
rows.cast: Fred MacMurray, Marguerite Chapman

rows.title: Paris Underground
rows.cast: Constance Bennett, Gracie Fields, George Rigaud
rows.extract: Paris Underground, also known as Madame Pimpernel, is a 1945 film directed by Gregory Ratoff, and based on the memoir of the same title by Etta Shiber.

rows.title: Patrick the Great
rows.cast: Donald O'Connor, Peggy Ryan, Eve Arden
rows.extract: Patrick the Great is a 1945 American drama film starring Donald O'Connor, Peggy Ryan, and Frances Dee. This was the last film for O'Connor and Ryan together, who had been a teenage team for the past several years. This was also O'Connor's last film before he went to serve in World War II.

rows.cast: Kirby Grant, Lois Collier, Eric Blore

It was produced by the low-budget Poverty Row studio Producers Releasing Corporation. The film's sets were designed by the art director Paul Palmentola.

rows.title: Phantom of the Plains

rows.title: The Phantom Speaks

rows.extract: The Phantom Speaks is a 1945 American supernatural film noir directed by John English and written by John K. Butler. The film stars Richard Arlen, Stanley Ridges, Lynne Roberts, Tom Powers, Charlotte Wynters and Jonathan Hale. The film was released on May 10, 1945, by Republic Pictures.

rows.cast: George Sanders, Hurd Hatfield, Donna Reed, Peter Lawford
rows.extract: The Picture of Dorian Gray is a 1945 American horror-drama film based on Oscar Wilde's 1890 novel of the same name. rows.cast: Jack Haley, Ann Savage
rows.extract: Scared Stiff is a 1945 American comedic murder mystery directed by Frank McDonald for Pine-Thomas Productions and released by Paramount Pictures. The film stars Jack Haley, Ann Savage and Barton MacLane.
