rows.title: Earl Carroll Sketchbook
rows.cast: Constance Moore, Edward Everett Horton, Hillary Brooke
rows.extract: Earl Carroll Sketchbook is a 1946 American musical film directed by Albert S. Rogell and written by Frank Gill Jr. and Parke Levy. The film stars Constance Moore, William Marshall, Bill Goodwin, Johnny Coy, Barbara Jo Allen and Edward Everett Horton. It was released on August 22, 1946 by Republic Pi

rows.title: Easy to Wed
rows.cast: Lucille Ball, Esther Williams, Van Johnson
rows.extract: Easy to Wed is a 1946 Technicolor American musical comedy film directed by Edward Buzzell, and starring Van Johnson, Esther Williams, Lucille Ball, and Keenan Wynn. The screenplay by Dorothy Kingsley is an adaptation of the screenplay of the 1936 film Libeled Lady by Maurine Dallas Watkins, Howard E

rows.title: The El Paso Kid
rows.cast: Sunset Carson, Edmund Cobb
rows.extract: The El Paso Kid is a 1946 American Western film directed by Thomas Carr and written by Norman Sheldon. The film stars Sunset Carson, Marie Harmon, Hank Patterson, Edmund Cobb, Robert Filmer and Wheaton Chambers. The film was released on May 22, 1946, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Fabulous Suzanne
rows.cast: Barbara Britton, Rudy Vallée
rows.extract: The Fabulous Suzanne is a 1946 American romantic comedy film directed by Steve Sekely and starring Barbara Britton, Rudy Vallee and Otto Kruger. A waitress inherits a fortune from one of her customers.

rows.title: The Face of Marble
rows.cast: John Carradine, Claudia Drake
rows.extract: The Face of Marble is a 1946 American horror film directed by William Beaudine and starring John Carradine, Claudia Drake and Robert Shayne.

rows.title: Faithful in My Fashion
rows.cast: Donna Reed, Tom Drake
rows.extract: Faithful in My Fashion is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Sidney Salkow and starring Donna Reed, Tom Drake and Edward Everett Horton.

rows.title: The Falcon's Adventure
rows.cast: Tom Conway, Myrna Dell
rows.extract: The Falcon's Adventure is a 1946 film. It is the 13th of 16 films about the Falcon and the final film of RKO's Falcon series starring Tom Conway. It was directed by William Berke, who had served as producer for the previous entry in the series, 1946's The Falcon's Alibi.

rows.title: The Falcon's Alibi
rows.cast: Tom Conway, Rita Corday
rows.extract: The Falcon's Alibi is a 1946 American mystery film directed by Ray McCarey and starring Tom Conway, Rita Corday and Vince Barnett. It was the ninth film featuring Conway as The Falcon. After the following film, The Falcon's Adventure, the series was ended due to declining popularity.

rows.title: Fear
rows.cast: Peter Cookson, Warren William, Anne Gwynne
rows.extract: Fear is a 1946 low-budget film noir directed by Alfred Zeisler and produced by Monogram Pictures. The film loosely follows the main plot of Fyodor Dostoyevsky's 1866 novel Crime and Punishment, without attribution.

rows.title: The Fighting Frontiersman
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette
rows.extract: The Fighting Frontiersman is a 1946 American Western film directed by Derwin Abrahams and written by Ed Earl Repp. The film stars Charles Starrett, Helen Mowery, Hank Newman and Smiley Burnette. The film was released on December 10, 1946, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: The Fighting Guardsman
rows.cast: Willard Parker, Anita Louise, Janis Carter, John Loder
rows.extract: The Fighting Guardsman is a 1946 American adventure film directed by Henry Levin.

rows.title: Flight to Nowhere
rows.cast: Alan Curtis, Evelyn Ankers, Micheline Cheirel
rows.extract: Flight to Nowhere is a 1946 American film noir crime film directed by William Rowland and stars Alan Curtis and Evelyn Ankers. Flight to Nowhere was one of the first postwar productions to deal with the atom bomb secrets.

rows.title: The Flying Serpent
rows.cast: George Zucco, Eddie Acuff
rows.extract: The Flying Serpent is a 1946 American fantasy-horror film based on a story by John T Neville. It follows the deranged archaeologist, Dr Andrew Forbes, as he uses his discovery of a killer bird god, the mythical Quetzalcoatl, to murder his enemies. The film is directed by Sam Newfield and features Ge

rows.title: Freddie Steps Out
rows.cast: Freddie Stewart, June Preisser
rows.extract: Freddie Steps Out is a 1946 American film starring Freddie Stewart.

rows.title: The French Key
rows.cast: Albert Dekker, Mike Mazurki, Evelyn Ankers
rows.extract: The French Key is a 1946 American mystery film directed by Walter Colmes and written by Frank Gruber. The film stars Albert Dekker, Mike Mazurki, Evelyn Ankers, John Eldredge, Frank Fenton and Selmer Jackson. The film was released on May 18, 1946, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: From This Day Forward
rows.cast: Joan Fontaine, Mark Stevens
rows.extract: From This Day Forward is a 1946 American drama film directed by John Berry, starring Joan Fontaine and Mark Stevens.

rows.title: Frontier Gunlaw
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Jack Rockwell
rows.extract: Frontier Gunlaw is a 1946 American Western film directed by Derwin Abrahams and written by Bennett Cohen. The film stars Charles Starrett, Tex Harding, Dub Taylor, Jean Stevens, Weldon Heyburn and Jack Rockwell. The film was released on January 31, 1946, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: G. I. War Brides
rows.cast: Anna Lee, James Ellison

rows.title: Gallant Bess
rows.cast: Marshall Thompson, George Tobias
rows.extract: Gallant Bess is a 1947 dramatic film released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. It is loosely based on the true story of U.S. Navy warrant officer Arthur Parker, who rescued an injured filly during World War II. Portions of the film were shot on the coast of Santa Barbara, California in October 1945. This was

rows.title: Gallant Journey
rows.cast: Glenn Ford, Janet Blair, Charlie Ruggles
rows.extract: Gallant Journey is a 1946 American historical film written, produced and directed by William A. Wellman and starring Glenn Ford and Janet Blair. The film is a biopic of the early U.S. aviation pioneer John Joseph Montgomery. Gallant Journey depicts his efforts to build and fly gliders, from his chil

rows.title: Galloping Thunder
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette
rows.extract: Galloping Thunder is a 1946 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and starring Charles Starrett. It was part of the series of Durango Kid films.

rows.title: Gas House Kids
rows.cast: Robert Lowery, Billy Halop
rows.extract: Gas House Kids is a 1946 American comedy-drama film directed by Sam Newfield and starring Robert Lowery, Billy Halop and Teala Loring. It was followed by two sequels, Gas House Kids Go West and Gas House Kids in Hollywood, both released in 1947. In the film, a group of unruly New York City children

rows.title: Gay Blades
rows.cast: Jean Rogers, Allan Lane
rows.extract: Gay Blades is a 1946 American comedy film directed by George Blair and written by Albert Beich and Marcy Klauber. The film stars Allan Lane, Jean Rogers, Edward Ashley, Frank Albertson, Ann Gillis and Robert Armstrong. The film was released on January 25, 1946, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Gay Cavalier
rows.cast: Gilbert Roland, Martin Garralaga
rows.extract: The Gay Cavalier is a 1946 black and white Western adventure starring Gilbert Roland, Helen Gerald and Tristram Coffin. It is based on a story by the author O. Henry.

rows.title: Genius at Work
rows.cast: Anne Jeffreys, Wally Brown, Alan Carney
rows.extract: Genius at Work is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Leslie Goodwins and written by Monte Brice and Robert E. Kent. The film stars Wally Brown, Alan Carney, Anne Jeffreys, Lionel Atwill and Bela Lugosi. The film was released on October 20, 1946, by RKO Pictures.

rows.title: The Gentleman from Texas
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Claudia Drake, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: The Gentleman from Texas is a 1946 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by J. Benton Cheney. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Claudia Drake, Raymond Hatton, Reno Browne, Christine McIntyre and Tris Coffin. The film was released on June 8, 1946, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Gentleman Joe Palooka
rows.cast: Leon Errol, Joe Kirkwood, Elyse Knox
rows.extract: Gentleman Joe Palooka is a 1946 film directed by Cy Endfield. It was the second of the Joe Palooka series.

rows.title: The Gentleman Misbehaves
rows.cast: Osa Massen, Hillary Brooke
rows.extract: The Gentleman Misbehaves is a 1946 American musical film.

rows.title: Gentlemen with Guns
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Al St. John
rows.extract: Gentlemen with Guns is a 1946 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Fred Myton. The film stars Buster Crabbe, Al St. John, Patricia Knox, Steve Darrell, George Chesebro, Karl Hackett, Budd Buster and Frank Ellis. The film was released on March 27, 1946, by Producers Releasing

rows.title: Ghost of Hidden Valley
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Al St. John
rows.extract: Ghost of Hidden Valley is a 1946 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Ellen Coyle. The film stars Buster Crabbe, Al St. John, Jean Carlin, John Meredith, Charles King and Jimmy Aubrey. The film was released on June 5, 1946, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: Gilda
rows.cast: Glenn Ford, Rita Hayworth
rows.extract: Gilda is a 1946 American film noir directed by Charles Vidor and starring Rita Hayworth and Glenn Ford. The film is known for cinematographer Rudolph Maté's lush photography, costume designer Jean Louis's wardrobe for Hayworth, and choreographer Jack Cole's staging of "Put the Blame on Mame" and "Am

rows.title: Ginger
rows.cast: Frank Albertson, ., Barbara Read
rows.extract: Ginger is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Oliver Drake and starring Frank Albertson, Barbara Read and Janet Burston. It was produced and distributed by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Girl on the Spot
rows.cast: Lois Collier, Jess Barker
rows.extract: Girl on the Spot is a 1946 musical crime film directed by William Beaudine and starring Lois Collier, Jess Barker and George Dolenz.

rows.title: The Glass Alibi
rows.cast: Maris Wrixon, Anne Gwynne
rows.extract: The Glass Alibi is a 1946 crime drama film noir directed by W. Lee Wilder starring Paul Kelly, Douglas Fowley, Anne Gwynne and Maris Wrixon.

rows.title: God's Country
rows.cast: Robert Lowery, Helen Gilbert, Buster Keaton
rows.extract: God's Country is a 1946 comedy Western film directed by Robert Emmett Tansey and starring Robert Lowery, Helen Gilbert and Buster Keaton. It is a low-budget color B Western set in the contemporary American West.

rows.title: The Great Morgan
rows.cast: Frank Morgan, Tommy Dorsey
rows.extract: The Great Morgan is a 1945 American musical-comedy film released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. The film is considered one of the more unusual in the MGM canon in that it is a compilation film built around a slight plot line, with a running time of less than 60 minutes.

rows.title: The Green Years
rows.cast: Charles Coburn, Tom Drake, Beverly Tyler
rows.extract: The Green Years is a 1946 American drama film featuring Charles Coburn, Tom Drake, Beverly Tyler and Hume Cronyn. It was adapted by Robert Ardrey and Sonya Levien from A. J. Cronin's 1944 novel of the same name. It tells the story of the coming-of-age of an Irish orphan in Scotland and was directed

rows.title: Gun Town
rows.cast: Kirby Grant, Claire Carleton, Lyle Talbot
rows.extract: Gun Town is a 1946 American Western film directed by Wallace Fox and starring Kirby Grant, Claire Carleton and Lyle Talbot.

rows.title: Gunman's Code
rows.cast: Kirby Grant, Jane Adams
rows.extract: Gunman's Code is a 1946 American Western film directed by Wallace Fox and starring Kirby Grant, Fuzzy Knight and Jane Adams.

rows.title: Gunning for Vengeance
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette
rows.extract: Gunning for Vengeance is a 1946 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro, which stars Charles Starrett, Marjean Neville, and The Trailsmen.

rows.title: A Guy Could Change
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Jane Frazee
rows.extract: A Guy Could Change is a 1946 American drama film starring Allan Lane and Jane Frazee. The supporting cast features 13-year-old Robert Blake, Wallace Ford, Adele Mara and Gerald Mohr. A Guy Could Change was the final film of director William K. Howard.

rows.title: The Haunted Mine
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Linda Leighton
rows.extract: The Haunted Mine is a 1946 American Western film directed by Derwin Abrahams and written by Frank H. Young. This is the twentieth and final film in the "Marshal Nevada Jack McKenzie" series, and stars Johnny Mack Brown as Jack McKenzie and Raymond Hatton as his sidekick Sandy Hopkins, with Linda Lei

rows.title: The Harvey Girls
rows.cast: Judy Garland, Ray Bolger, Angela Lansbury
rows.extract: The Harvey Girls is a 1946 Technicolor American musical film produced by Arthur Freed for Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. It is based on the 1942 novel of the same name by Samuel Hopkins Adams, about Fred Harvey's Harvey House waitresses. Directed by George Sidney, the film stars Judy Garland and features John

rows.title: Heading West
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette
rows.extract: Heading West is a 1946 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Ed Earl Repp. The film stars Charles Starrett, Doris Houck, Hank Penny and Smiley Burnette. The film was released on August 15, 1946, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Heartbeat
rows.cast: Ginger Rogers, Jean-Pierre Aumont
rows.extract: Heartbeat is a 1946 American romantic drama film directed by Sam Wood and starring Ginger Rogers. It is a direct remake of the French romantic drama Battement de cœur, released in 1940.

rows.title: Heldorado
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, George "Gabby" Hayes
rows.extract: Heldorado  is a 1946 American Western film starring Roy Rogers set during the annual Helldorado Days celebrations in Las Vegas. It was the last teaming of Roy and comedy relief sidekick Gabby Hayes. Hayes shares a scene with Pat Brady who later became Rogers' comedy relief sidekick.

rows.title: Her Adventurous Night
rows.cast: Dennis O'Keefe, Helen Walker
rows.extract: Her Adventurous Night is a 1946 American comedy film directed by John Rawlins and written by Jerry Warner. The film stars Dennis O'Keefe, Helen Walker, Scotty Beckett, Fuzzy Knight, Milburn Stone and Tom Powers. The film was released on June 5, 1946, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Her Kind of Man
rows.cast: Janis Paige, Zachary Scott, Dane Clark
rows.extract: Her Kind of Man is a 1946 American crime film noir directed by Frederick De Cordova, and starring Dane Clark, Janis Paige and Zachary Scott. The film is not to be confused with His Kind of Woman (1951) starring Robert Mitchum and Jane Russell.

rows.title: Her Sister's Secret
rows.cast: Nancy Coleman, Margaret Lindsay
rows.extract: Her Sister's Secret is a 1946 drama film directed by Edgar G. Ulmer and starring Nancy Coleman, Margaret Lindsay, Phillip Reed, and Regis Toomey. It centers around a woman who falls in love with a soldier. Believing she has been abandoned, she gives her baby to her married sister. The picture was pr

rows.title: High School Hero
rows.cast: Freddie Stewart, June Preisser, Noel Neill
rows.extract: High School Hero is a 1946 American film directed by Arthur Dreifuss and starring Freddie Stewart.

rows.title: Holiday in Mexico
rows.cast: Jane Powell, Walter Pidgeon
rows.extract: Holiday in Mexico is a 1946 Technicolor musical directed by George Sidney and starring Walter Pidgeon, Jane Powell, and Ilona Massey.

rows.title: Home in Oklahoma
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Dale Evans, Carol Hughes
rows.extract: Home in Oklahoma  is a 1946 American Western film starring Roy Rogers.

rows.title: Home on the Range
rows.cast: Monte Hale, Lorna Gray
rows.extract: Home on the Range is a 1946 American Western film directed by R. G. Springsteen and written by Betty Burbridge. The film stars Monte Hale, Lorna Gray, Bob Nolan, Tom Chatterton, Robert Blake and LeRoy Mason. The film was released on April 18, 1946, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Home Sweet Homicide
rows.cast: Peggy Ann Garner, Randolph Scott
rows.extract: Home Sweet Homicide is an American mystery film directed by Lloyd Bacon and released in 1946. It stars Peggy Ann Garner, Randolph Scott and Lynn Bari, and was based on the eponymous mystery novel by Craig Rice.

rows.title: The Hoodlum Saint
rows.cast: William Powell, Esther Williams, Lewis Stone
rows.extract: The Hoodlum Saint is a 1946 American drama film starring William Powell and Esther Williams.

rows.title: Hot Cargo
rows.cast: Jean Rogers, William Gargan
rows.extract: Hot Cargo is a 1946 American drama film directed by Lew Landers and written by Daniel Mainwaring. The film stars William Gargan, Jean Rogers, Phillip Reed, Larry Young, Harry Cording and Will Wright. The film was released on June 28, 1946, by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: House of Horrors
rows.cast: Rondo Hatton, Robert Lowery, Virginia Grey
rows.extract: House of Horrors is a 1946 American horror film released by Universal Pictures, starring Rondo Hatton as a madman named "the Creeper".

rows.title: Humoresque
rows.cast: John Garfield, Joan Crawford
rows.extract: Humoresque is a 1946 American melodrama film by Warner Bros. starring Joan Crawford and John Garfield in an older woman/younger man tale about a violinist and his patroness. The screenplay by Clifford Odets and Zachary Gold was based upon the 1919 short story "Humoresque" by Fannie Hurst, which prev

rows.title: I Ring Doorbells
rows.cast: Anne Gwynne, Robert Shayne, Roscoe Karns
rows.extract: I Ring Doorbells is a 1946 American comedy-drama film directed by Frank Strayer, which stars Anne Gwynne, Robert Shayne, and Roscoe Karns. The story was adapted by Dick Irving Hyland and Raymond L. Schrock from the book of the same name by Russell Birdwell, and Hyland wrote the screenplay. The pictu

rows.title: Idea Girl
rows.cast: Jess Barker, Julie Bishop, Alan Mowbray
rows.extract: Idea Girl is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Will Jason and written by Charles R. Marion and Elwood Ullman. The film stars Jess Barker, Julie Bishop, Alan Mowbray, George Dolenz, Joan Shawlee and Laura Deane Dutton. The film was released on February 8, 1946, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: If I'm Lucky
rows.cast: Vivian Blaine, Perry Como
rows.extract: If I'm Lucky is a 1946 American musical comedy film directed by Lewis Seiler and starring Vivian Blaine, Perry Como, Phil Silvers and Carmen Miranda in the leading roles. The film also featured bandleader Harry James.

rows.title: In Fast Company
rows.cast: The Bowery Boys, Jane Randolph
rows.extract: In Fast Company is a 1946 film starring the comedy team of The Bowery Boys. It is the second film in the series.

rows.title: In Old Sacramento
rows.cast: Bill Elliott, Constance Moore
rows.extract: In Old Sacramento is a 1946 American Western film directed by Joseph Kane and written by Frances Hyland and Frank Gruber. The film stars Wild Bill Elliott, Constance Moore, Henry H. Daniels Jr., Ruth Donnelly, Eugene Pallette and Jack La Rue.

rows.title: The Inner Circle
rows.cast: Adele Mara, Warren Douglas, Ricardo Cortez
rows.extract: The Inner Circle is a 1946 film noir mystery film directed by Philip Ford starring Adele Mara, Warren Douglas, William Frawley and Ricardo Cortez.

rows.title: Inside Job
rows.cast: Preston Foster, Ann Rutherford
rows.extract: Inside Job is a 1946 American crime film noir directed by Jean Yarbrough starring Preston Foster, Ann Rutherford, Alan Curtis and Milburn Stone.

rows.title: The Invisible Informer
rows.cast: Linda Stirling, Adele Mara
rows.extract: The Invisible Informer is a 1946 action film starring Linda Stirling, William Henry, and Adele Mara. Produced by Republic Pictures, it was directed by Philip Ford and written by Gerald Adams and Sherman Lowe.

rows.title: It's Great to Be Young
rows.cast: Leslie Brooks, Jeff Donnell
rows.extract: It's Great to Be Young is a 1946 film comedy directed by Del Lord, starring Leslie Brooks, Jimmy Lloyd, Jeff Donnell, Bob Haymes, Jack Williams, Jack Fina, Frank Orth, Ann Codee, Pat Yankee, Frank Sully and Milton Delugg. It was released by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: It's a Wonderful Life
rows.cast: James Stewart, Donna Reed, Lionel Barrymore
rows.extract: It's a Wonderful Life is a 1946 American Christmas fantasy drama film produced and directed by Frank Capra. It is based on the short story and booklet The Greatest Gift self-published by Philip Van Doren Stern in 1943, which itself is loosely based on the 1843 Charles Dickens novella A Christmas Car

rows.title: It Shouldn't Happen to a Dog
rows.cast: Carole Landis, Allyn Joslyn, Margo Woode
rows.extract: It Shouldn't Happen to a Dog is a 1946 American comedy crime film starring Carole Landis, Allyn Joslyn and Margo Woode, and directed by Herbert I. Leeds.

rows.title: I've Always Loved You
rows.cast: Catherine McLeod, Philip Dorn
rows.extract: I've Always Loved You is a 1946 American drama musical film produced and directed by Frank Borzage and written by Borden Chase. The film stars Philip Dorn, Catherine McLeod, William Carter, Maria Ouspenskaya, Felix Bressart and Elizabeth Patterson. Rare for a film produced by Republic Pictures, I've

rows.title: The James Brothers of Missouri
rows.cast: Keith Richards, Noel Neill
rows.extract: The James Brothers of Missouri is a 1949 American Republic Western film serial.

rows.title: Janie Gets Married
rows.cast: Joan Leslie, Ann Harding, Edward Arnold
rows.extract: Janie Gets Married is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Vincent Sherman, and written by Agnes Christine Johnston. The film stars Joan Leslie, Robert Hutton, Edward Arnold, Ann Harding, Robert Benchley, and Dorothy Malone. The film was released by Warner Bros. on June 22, 1946.

rows.title: Joe Palooka, Champ
rows.cast: Leon Errol, Joe Kirkwood, Elyse Knox
rows.extract:
Joe Palooka, Champ is a 1946 American film featuring the comic-strip boxer Joe Palooka. This film from Monogram Pictures is the beginning of a series with eleven sequels:Gentleman Joe Palooka (1946)
Joe Palooka in the Knockout (1947)
Joe Palooka in Fighting Mad (1948)
Joe Palooka in Winner Take All

rows.title: Johnny Comes Flying Home
rows.cast: Faye Marlowe, Martha Stewart
rows.extract: Johnny Comes Flying Home is a 1946 American adventure film directed by Benjamin Stoloff and starring Richard Crane and Faye Marlowe; the supporting cast features Harry Morgan. The plot involves postwar pilots starting a small aviation company.

rows.title: The Jolson Story
rows.cast: Larry Parks, William Demarest
rows.extract: The Jolson Story is a 1946 American biographical musical film, a fictionalized account of the life of singer Al Jolson. It stars Larry Parks as Jolson, Evelyn Keyes as Julie Benson, William Demarest as his manager, Ludwig Donath and Tamara Shayne as his parents, and Scotty Beckett as the young Jolso

rows.title: Junior Prom
rows.cast: Judy Clark, Noel Neill
rows.extract: Junior Prom is a 1946 American musical comedy, directed by Arthur Dreifuss and produced by Sam Katzman and Maurice Duke. It was released by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Just Before Dawn
rows.cast: Warner Baxter, Adele Roberts
rows.extract: Just Before Dawn (1946) is the sixth Crime Doctor film produced by Columbia Pictures. It was directed by William Castle and written by Eric Taylor and Aubrey Wisberg. The film stars Warner Baxter, Adele Roberts, Mona Barrie and Martin Kosleck. It is also known as Exposed by the Crime Doctor.

rows.title: The Kid from Brooklyn
rows.cast: Danny Kaye, Virginia Mayo, Vera-Ellen
rows.extract: The Kid from Brooklyn is a 1946 American musical comedy film directed by Norman Z. McLeod and starring Danny Kaye, Virginia Mayo, Vera-Ellen, Steve Cochran, Walter Abel, Eve Arden, and Fay Bainter. Virginia Mayo's and Vera-Ellen's singing voices were dubbed by Betty Russell and Dorothy Ellers, respe

rows.title: The Killers
rows.cast: Ava Gardner, Burt Lancaster, Edmond O'Brien
rows.extract: The Killers is a 1946 American film noir starring Burt Lancaster, Ava Gardner, Edmond O'Brien and Sam Levene. Based in part on the 1927 short story of the same name by Ernest Hemingway, it focuses on an insurance detective's investigation into the execution by two professional killers of a former bo

rows.title: Lady Chaser
rows.cast: Robert Lowery, Ann Savage
rows.extract: Lady Chaser is a 1946 American mystery film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Fred Myton. The film stars Robert Lowery, Ann Savage, Inez Cooper, Frank Ferguson, William Haade and Ralph Dunn. The film was released on November 25, 1946, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: Lady Luck
rows.cast: Robert Young, Barbara Hale
rows.extract: Lady Luck is a 1946 American comedy film starring Robert Young and Barbara Hale. The picture tells the story of a professional gambler who falls in love with a woman who hates gambling and tries to reform him.

rows.title: Landrush
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette
rows.extract: Landrush is a 1946 American Western film directed by Vernon Keays and starring Charles Starrett, Doris Houck, Smiley Burnette, Emmett Lynn, Bud Geary and Steve Barclay. The film was released on November 18, 1946, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Larceny in Her Heart
rows.cast: Hugh Beaumont, Cheryl Walker
rows.extract: Larceny in Her Heart is a 1946 American crime film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Raymond L. Schrock. The film stars Hugh Beaumont, Cheryl Walker, Ralph Dunn, Paul Bryar, Charles C. Wilson, Douglas Fowley and Gordon Richards. It was released on July 10, 1946 by Producers Releasing Corporati

rows.title: The Last Crooked Mile
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Ann Savage, Adele Mara
rows.extract: The Last Crooked Mile is a 1946 American crime film directed by Philip Ford and written by Jerry Sackheim and Jerome Gruskin. The film stars Don "Red" Barry, Ann Savage, Adele Mara, Tom Powers, Sheldon Leonard and Nestor Paiva. The film was released on August 9, 1946, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Lawless Breed
rows.cast: Kirby Grant, Jane Adams
rows.extract: Lawless Breed is a 1946 American Western film directed by Wallace Fox and written by Robert Creighton Williams. The film stars Kirby Grant, Fuzzy Knight, Poni Adams, Dick Curtis, Claudia Drake, Harry Brown, Charles King and Karl Hackett. The film was released on August 14, 1946, by Universal Picture

rows.title: A Letter for Evie
rows.cast: Marsha Hunt, Hume Cronyn
rows.extract: A Letter for Evie is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Jules Dassin.

rows.title: Little Giant
rows.cast: Abbott and Costello, Brenda Joyce, Elena Verdugo
rows.extract: Little Giant is a 1946 American comedy drama film directed by William A. Seiter and starring the comedy team of Abbott and Costello. The film was released in the UK with the title On the Carpet.

rows.title: Little Iodine
rows.cast: Jo Ann Marlowe, Irene Ryan
rows.extract: Little Iodine is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Reginald Le Borg and written by Richard H. Landau. The film is based on the comic strip Little Iodine by Jimmy Hatlo. The film stars Jo Ann Marlowe, Marc Cramer, Eve Whitney, Irene Ryan, and Hobart Cavanaugh. The film was released on October 2

rows.title: Little Miss Big
rows.cast: Fay Holden, Frank McHugh
rows.extract: Little Miss Big is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Erle C. Kenton and written by Erna Lazarus. The film stars Beverly Simmons, Frederick Brady, Fay Holden, Frank McHugh, Dorothy Morris and Milburn Stone. The film was released on August 30, 1946, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Little Mister Jim
rows.cast: James Craig, Butch Jenkins
rows.extract: Little Mister Jim is a 1946 American drama film directed by Fred Zinnemann and starring Butch Jenkins, James Craig and Frances Gifford.

rows.title: Live Wires
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall
rows.extract: Live Wires is a 1946 film starring the comedy team of The Bowery Boys. It is the first film in the series, which lasted until 1958 and included forty-eight films, after the comedy team of the East Side Kids was revamped and renamed The Bowery Boys.

rows.title: The Locket
rows.cast: Laraine Day, Brian Aherne, Robert Mitchum
rows.extract: The Locket is a 1946 American psychological thriller with noirish undertones directed by John Brahm, starring Laraine Day, Brian Aherne, Robert Mitchum, and Gene Raymond, and released by RKO Pictures. The film is based on a screenplay by Sheridan Gibney, adapted from "What Nancy Wanted" by Norma Bar

rows.title: Lone Star Moonlight
rows.cast: Ken Curtis, Joan Barton, Guy Kibbee
rows.extract: Lone Star Moonlight is a 1946 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Louise Rousseau. The film stars Ken Curtis, Joan Barton, Guy Kibbee, Robert Kellard, Claudia Drake and Arthur Loft. It was released on December 12, 1946 by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Love Laughs at Andy Hardy
rows.cast: Mickey Rooney, Lewis Stone, Bonita Granville
rows.extract: Love Laughs at Andy Hardy is a 1946 American film released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, directed by Willis Goldbeck and starring Mickey Rooney and Lewis Stone.

rows.title: Lover Come Back
rows.cast: George Brent, Lucille Ball
rows.extract: Lover Come Back is a 1946 romantic comedy film directed by William A. Seiter. The film stars George Brent, Lucille Ball and Vera Zorina in her last film role. Supporting actors include Raymond Walburn and Charles Winninger.

rows.title: The Madonna's Secret
rows.cast: Gail Patrick, Ann Rutherford
rows.extract: The Madonna's Secret is a 1946 American film noir crime film directed by Wilhelm Thiele and starring Francis Lederer, Gail Patrick, Ann Rutherford and Edward Ashley.

rows.title: Magnificent Doll
rows.cast: Ginger Rogers, David Niven
rows.extract: Magnificent Doll is a 1946 American drama film directed by Frank Borzage and starring Ginger Rogers as Dolley Madison and David Niven as Aaron Burr. The supporting cast features Burgess Meredith as James Madison and Grandon Rhodes as Thomas Jefferson. The screenplay was written by Irving Stone.

rows.title: The Magnificent Rogue
rows.cast: Lynne Roberts, Stephanie Bachelor
rows.extract: The Magnificent Rogue is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Albert S. Rogell and written by Dane Lussier and Sherman L. Lowe. The film stars Lynne Roberts, Warren Douglas, Gerald Mohr, Stephanie Bachelor, Adele Mara and Grady Sutton. The film was released on November 7, 1946, by Republic Pictur

rows.title: Make Mine Music
rows.cast: Dinah Shore, Benny Goodman, Nelson Eddy, Andrews Sisters
rows.extract: Make Mine Music is a 1946 American animated musical anthology film produced by Walt Disney and released by RKO Radio Pictures. It is the eighth Disney feature animated film, released on April 20, 1946.

rows.title: Man from Rainbow Valley
rows.cast: Monte Hale, Lorna Gray
rows.extract: Man from Rainbow Valley is a 1946 American Western Magnacolor film directed by R. G. Springsteen and written by Betty Burbridge. The film stars Monte Hale, Lorna Gray, Jo Ann Marlowe, Ferris Taylor, Emmett Lynn and Tom London. The film was released on June 15, 1946, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Man Who Dared
rows.cast: George Macready, Forrest Tucker
rows.extract: The Man Who Dared is a 1946 American film noir crime film directed by John Sturges, which serves as the first film he directed.

rows.title: Margie
rows.cast: Jeanne Crain, Glenn Langan, Lynn Bari
rows.extract: Margie is a 1946 American romantic comedy film directed by Henry King and starring Jeanne Crain, about a high school girl in the 1920s who develops a crush on her French teacher. Margie was a box-office hit, ranking in the top 15 highest-grossing films of the year, and established Crain as an import

rows.title: The Mask of Diijon
rows.cast: Erich von Stroheim, Jeanne Bates
rows.extract: The Mask of Diijon is a 1946 American black-and-white film noir suspense film released from PRC Studios, directed by Lew Landers and featuring Erich von Stroheim, Jeanne Bates and William Wright.

rows.title: Meet Me on Broadway
rows.cast: Marjorie Reynolds, Jinx Falkenburg
rows.extract: Meet Me on Broadway is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Leigh Jason and written by George Bricker and Jack Henley. The film stars Marjorie Reynolds, Frederick Brady, Jinx Falkenburg, Spring Byington, Allen Jenkins, Gene Lockhart and Loren Tindall. The film was released on January 26, 1946, by

rows.title: The Missing Lady
rows.cast: Kane Richmond, Barbara Read
rows.extract: The Missing Lady is a 1946 American mystery film directed by Phil Karlson and starring Kane Richmond and Barbara Read. It was the third and final in a series of three films released by Monogram in 1946 starring Richmond as The Shadow, the others being The Shadow Returns and Behind The Mask.

rows.title: Miss Susie Slagle's
rows.cast: Veronica Lake, Sonny Tufts, Joan Caulfield
rows.extract: Miss Susie Slagle's is a 1946 American drama film directed by John Berry. It was based on the popular novel by Augusta Tucker. The film was Berry's directorial debut and first starring role for Joan Caulfield.

rows.title: Monsieur Beaucaire
rows.cast: Bob Hope, Joan Caulfield
rows.extract: Monsieur Beaucaire is a 1946 comedy film starring Bob Hope as the title character, the barber of King Louis XV of France. It is loosely based on the novel of the same name by Booth Tarkington. It is a remake of the 1924 Rudolph Valentino silent film of the same name Monsieur Beaucaire.

rows.title: Moon Over Montana
rows.cast: Jimmy Wakely, Jennifer Holt
rows.extract: Moon Over Montana is a 1946 American Western film directed by Oliver Drake and written by Louise Rousseau. The film stars Jimmy Wakely, Lee "Lasses" White, Jennifer Holt, Jack Ingram, Louise Arthur and Stanley Blystone. The film was released on February 16, 1946, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Mr. Ace
rows.cast: George Raft, Sylvia Sidney, Jerome Cowan
rows.extract: Mr. Ace is a 1946 American film noir starring George Raft and Sylvia Sidney involving a society woman who taps a gangster for his political support as she runs for Congress. The movie was written by Fred F. Finkelhoffe, directed by Edwin L. Marin, and photographed by legendary cinematographer Karl S

rows.title: Mr. Hex
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall, Gale Robbins
rows.extract: Mr. Hex is a 1946 film directed by William Beaudine and starring the comedy team of The Bowery Boys. It is the fifth film in the series.

rows.title: Murder in the Music Hall
rows.cast: Nancy Kelly, Vera Ralston
rows.extract: Murder in the Music Hall is a 1946 American musical mystery film directed by John English and starring Vera Ralston, William Marshall and Helen Walker. The film involves a murder in Radio City Music Hall with The Rockettes as suspects.

rows.title: Murder Is My Business
rows.cast: Hugh Beaumont, Cheryl Walker, Lyle Talbot
rows.extract: Murder Is My Business is a 1946 American action film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Fred Myton. It is based on the 1940 novel The Uncomplaining Corpses by Brett Halliday. The film stars Hugh Beaumont, Cheryl Walker, Lyle Talbot, George Meeker, Pierre Watkin, and Richard Keene. The film was

rows.title: My Darling Clementine
rows.cast: Henry Fonda, Victor Mature, Walter Brennan, Linda Darnell, Cathy Downs
rows.extract: My Darling Clementine is a 1946 American Western film directed by John Ford and starring Henry Fonda as Wyatt Earp during the period leading up to the gunfight at the O.K. Corral. The ensemble cast also features Victor Mature, Linda Darnell, Walter Brennan, Tim Holt, Cathy Downs and Ward Bond.

rows.title: My Dog Shep
rows.cast: Tom Neal, William Farnum
rows.extract: My Dog Shep is a 1946 American drama film directed by Ford Beebe.

rows.title: My Pal Trigger
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Dale Evans, Jack Holt
rows.extract: My Pal Trigger is a 1946 American Western musical film directed by Frank McDonald. The screenplay by Jack Townley and John K. Butler was based upon a story by Paul Gangelin. The film stars Roy Rogers, Dale Evans, George “Gabby” Hayes, Jack Holt, and Trigger in a story about the origin of Rogers' mou

rows.title: My Reputation
rows.cast: Barbara Stanwyck, George Brent, Eve Arden
rows.extract: My Reputation is a 1946 American romantic drama film directed by Curtis Bernhardt. Barbara Stanwyck portrays an upper-class widow whose romance with an army officer causes trouble for her gossiping friends, domineering mother and young sons. Catherine Turney wrote the script, an adaptation of Clare

rows.title: Mysterious Intruder
rows.cast: Richard Dix, Barton MacLane, Nina Vale
rows.extract: Mysterious Intruder is a 1946 American mystery film noir based on the radio drama The Whistler. Directed by William Castle, the production features Richard Dix, Barton MacLane and Nina Vale. It is the fifth of Columbia Pictures' eight "Whistler" films produced in the 1940s, the first seven starring

rows.title: The Mysterious Mr. Valentine
rows.cast: William Henry, Linda Stirling, Virginia Christine
rows.extract: The Mysterious Mr. Valentine is a 1946 American film noir crime film directed by Philip Ford starring William Henry, Linda Stirling and Virginia Christine.

rows.title: Never Say Goodbye
rows.cast: Errol Flynn, Eleanor Parker
rows.extract: Never Say Goodbye is a 1946 American comedy-drama romance film about a divorced couple and the daughter who works to bring them back together. It was Errol Flynn's first purely comedic role since Footsteps in the Dark.

rows.title: Night and Day
rows.cast: Cary Grant, Alexis Smith, Jane Wyman
rows.extract: Night and Day is a 1946 American biographical and musical film starring Cary Grant, in a fictionalized account of the life of American composer and songwriter Cole Porter.

rows.title: Night Editor
rows.cast: William Gargan, Janis Carter
rows.extract: Night Editor is a 1946 B-movie film noir directed by Henry Levin and based on a popular radio program of the same name. The script for the film was based on a previous radio program episode "Inside Story."

rows.title: A Night in Casablanca
rows.cast: Marx Brothers, Sig Ruman, Lois Collier
rows.extract: A Night in Casablanca is a 1946 film starring the Marx Brothers:. The picture was directed by Archie Mayo, and written by Joseph Fields and Roland Kibbee.

rows.title: Night in Paradise
rows.cast: Merle Oberon, Turhan Bey, Gale Sondergaard
rows.extract: Night in Paradise is a 1946 American comedy-drama film produced by Walter Wanger and directed by Arthur Lubin.

rows.title: Night Train to Memphis
rows.cast: Roy Acuff, Allan Lane
rows.extract: Night Train to Memphis is a 1946 American action film directed by Lesley Selander and written by Dorrell McGowan and Stuart E. McGowan. The film stars Roy Acuff, Allan Lane, Adele Mara, Irving Bacon, Joseph Crehan and Emma Dunn. The film was released on July 12, 1946, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Nobody Lives Forever
rows.cast: John Garfield, Geraldine Fitzgerald
rows.extract: Nobody Lives Forever is a 1946 American crime film noir directed by Jean Negulesco and based on the novel I Wasn't Born Yesterday by W. R. Burnett. It stars John Garfield and Geraldine Fitzgerald and features Walter Brennan, Faye Emerson, George Coulouris and George Tobias.

rows.title: Nocturne
rows.cast: George Raft, Lynn Bari, Virginia Huston
rows.extract: Nocturne is a 1946 American film noir starring George Raft and Lynn Bari. The film was produced by longtime Alfred Hitchcock associate Joan Harrison, scripted by Jonathan Latimer, and directed by Edwin L. Marin. It was one of several medium budget thrillers Raft made in the late 1940s.

rows.title: No Leave, No Love
rows.cast: Van Johnson, Patricia Kirkwood
rows.extract: No Leave, No Love  is a 1946 American musical film directed by Charles Martin and starring Van Johnson, Keenan Wynn and Pat Kirkwood.

rows.title: Notorious
rows.cast: Cary Grant, Ingrid Bergman, Claude Rains, Louis Calhern
rows.extract: Notorious is a 1946 American spy film noir directed and produced by Alfred Hitchcock, starring Cary Grant, Ingrid Bergman, and Claude Rains as three people whose lives become intimately entangled during an espionage operation.

rows.title: The Notorious Lone Wolf
rows.cast: Gerald Mohr, Janis Carter, Eric Blore
rows.extract: The Notorious Lone Wolf (1946) is the twelfth Lone Wolf film produced by Columbia Pictures. The picture features Gerald Mohr in his inaugural performance as the protagonist detective Lone Wolf, Janis Carter, and Ian Wolfe as Adam Wainwright, the film's antagonist. The film was directed by D. Ross Le

rows.title: Of Human Bondage
rows.cast: Paul Henreid, Eleanor Parker, Janis Paige
rows.extract: Of Human Bondage is a 1946 American drama film directed by Edmund Goulding. The second screen adaptation of W. Somerset Maugham's 1915 novel, this Warner Bros. sanitized version was written by Catherine Turney. The central characters are Philip Carey, a clubfooted medical student, and Mildred Rogers

rows.title: One Exciting Week
rows.cast: Al Pearce, Jerome Cowan
rows.extract: One Exciting Week is a 1946 American comedy film directed by William Beaudine and written by Jack Townley and John K. Butler. The film stars Al Pearce, Pinky Lee, Jerome Cowan, Shemp Howard, Arlene Harris and Mary Treen. It was released on June 8, 1946 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: One More Tomorrow
rows.cast: Ann Sheridan, Jane Wyman
rows.extract: One More Tomorrow is a 1946 American film directed by Peter Godfrey and written by Charles Hoffman and Catherine Turney from the play The Animal Kingdom by Philip Barry. The film, starring Ann Sheridan, Dennis Morgan, Jack Carson, Alexis Smith, Jane Wyman and Reginald Gardiner, is a remake of the 19

rows.title: One Way to Love
rows.cast: Marguerite Chapman, Chester Morris, Janis Carter
rows.extract: One Way to Love is a 1946 American comedy film starring Willard Parker and Chester Morris. It was directed by Ray Enright.

rows.title: O.S.S.
rows.cast: Alan Ladd, Geraldine Fitzgerald, Patric Knowles
rows.extract: O.S.S. is a 1946 American war film starring Alan Ladd and Geraldine Fitzgerald about the Office of Strategic Services. It was directed by Irving Pichel, who would later be blacklisted by the House Un-American Activities Committee, and written by Richard Maibaum, a World War II veteran who would late

rows.title: Our Hearts Were Growing Up
rows.cast: Gail Russell, Diana Lynn
rows.extract: Our Hearts Were Growing Up is a 1946 American comedy film directed by William D. Russell and written by Melvin Frank, Norman Panama and Frank Waldman. It is the sequel to the 1944 film Our Hearts Were Young and Gay. The film stars Gail Russell, Diana Lynn, Brian Donlevy, Billy De Wolfe, James Brown

rows.title: Out California Way
rows.cast: Monte Hale, Lorna Gray, Roy Rogers
rows.extract: Out California Way is a 1946 American Western musical film directed by Lesley Selander for Republic Pictures. It starred Monte Hale, Lorna Gray and Robert Blake. Roy Rogers and Dale Evans made cameo appearances. The film was the first feature to be shot in Trucolor.

rows.title: Outlaws of the Plains
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Al St. John, Bud Osborne
rows.extract: Outlaws of the Plains is a 1946 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and starring Buster Crabbe, Al St. John and Patti McCarty.

rows.title: Overland Riders
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Al St. John
rows.extract: Overland Riders is a 1946 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Ellen Coyle. The film stars Buster Crabbe, Al St. John, Patti McCarty, Slim Whitaker, Bud Osborne and Jack O'Shea. The film was released on August 21, 1946, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: Partners in Time
rows.cast: Chester Lauck, Pamela Blake, Teala Loring
rows.extract: Partners in Time is a 1946 American comedy film directed by William Nigh and written by Charles E. Roberts. The film stars Chester Lauck, Norris Goff, Pamela Blake, John James, Teala Loring and Danny Duncan. The film was released on April 25, 1946, by RKO Pictures.

rows.title: Passkey to Danger
rows.cast: Stephanie Bachelor, Adele Mara
rows.extract: Passkey to Danger is a 1946 American film noir crime film directed by Lesley Selander and written by O'Leta Rhinehart and William Hagens. The film stars Kane Richmond, Stephanie Bachelor, Adele Mara, Gregory Gaye, Gerald Mohr and John Eldredge. It was released on May 11, 1946 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: People Are Funny
rows.cast: Jack Haley, Helen Walker, Rudy Vallée
rows.extract: People Are Funny is a 1946 American musical comedy film directed by Sam White based on the popular radio show of the same name.

rows.title: Perilous Holiday
rows.cast: Pat O'Brien, Ruth Warrick, Audrey Long
rows.extract: Perilous Holiday is a 1946 American film noir crime film directed by Edward H. Griffith and starring Pat O'Brien and Ruth Warrick. The screenplay concerns a woman newspaper reporter who is on the trail of a smuggling ring operating out of Mexico.

rows.title: Personality Kid
rows.cast: Anita Louise, Michael Duane
rows.extract: Personality Kid is a 1946 American adventure drama film directed by George Sherman and starring Anita Louise, Michael Duane and Ted Donaldson. It was produced and distributed by Columbia Pictures. The film's sets were designed by the art director Cary Odell.

rows.title: The Phantom Thief
rows.cast: Chester Morris, Jeff Donnell
rows.extract: The Phantom Thief is a 1946 American crime film directed by D. Ross Lederman. The film follows detective Boston Blackie as he tries to track down a blackmailer-murderer. As the investigation goes on, a supernatural element becomes clear.

rows.title: Plainsman and the Lady
rows.cast: Wild Bill Elliott, Gail Patrick
rows.extract: Plainsman and the Lady is a 1946 American Western film directed by Joseph Kane and written by Richard Wormser. The film stars Wild Bill Elliott, Vera Ralston, Gail Patrick, Joseph Schildkraut, Andy Clyde and Don "Red" Barry. It was released on November 11, 1946 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Postman Always Rings Twice
rows.cast: Lana Turner, John Garfield
rows.extract: The Postman Always Rings Twice is a 1946 American film noir based on the 1934 novel of the same name by James M. Cain. This adaptation of the novel features Lana Turner, John Garfield, Cecil Kellaway, Hume Cronyn, Leon Ames, and Audrey Totter. It was directed by Tay Garnett. The musical score was wr

rows.title: Prairie Badmen
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Al St. John
rows.extract: Prairie Badmen is a 1946 American Western film directed by Sam Newfield and written by Fred Myton. The film stars Buster Crabbe, Al St. John, Patricia Knox, Charles King, Ed Cassidy and Kermit Maynard. The film was released on July 17, 1946, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: Queen of Burlesque
rows.cast: Evelyn Ankers, Carleton G. Young, Marion Martin
rows.extract: Queen of Burlesque is a 1946 murder mystery film starring Evelyn Ankers and directed by Sam Newfield. rows.title: Rainbow Over Texas
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Dale Evans
rows.extract: Rainbow Over Texas is a 1946 American Western film in which Roy Rogers plays himself as a famous cowboy-singer returning to Texas. Directed by Frank McDonald from a story by Max Brand, it co-stars George "Gabby" Hayes and Dale Evans.

rows.title: The Razor's Edge
rows.cast: Tyrone Power, Gene Tierney
rows.extract: The Razor's Edge is a 1946 American drama film based on W. Somerset Maugham's 1944 novel of the same name. It stars Tyrone Power, Gene Tierney, John Payne, Anne Baxter, Clifton Webb, and Herbert Marshall, with a supporting cast including Lucile Watson, Frank Latimore, and Elsa Lanchester. Marshall p

rows.title: The Red Dragon
rows.cast: Sidney Toler, Benson Fong
rows.extract: The Red Dragon is a 1946 mystery film starring Sidney Toler as Charlie Chan, who has to sift through a host of suspects for three murders.

rows.title: Red River Renegades
rows.cast: Sunset Carson, Peggy Stewart
rows.extract: Red River Renegades is a 1946 American Western film directed by Thomas Carr and written by Norman S. Hall. The film stars Sunset Carson, Peggy Stewart, Tom London, Ted Adams, LeRoy Mason and Kenne Duncan. It was released on July 23, 1946 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Rendezvous with Annie
rows.cast: Eddie Albert, Faye Marlowe, Gail Patrick
rows.extract: Rendezvous with Annie is a 1946 comedy film directed by Allan Dwan and written by and Mary Loos and Richard Sale. The film stars Eddie Albert, Faye Marlowe and Gail Patrick. The supporting cast features C. Aubrey Smith and William Frawley. The plot involves a World War II serviceman who surreptitiou

rows.title: Rendezvous 24
rows.cast: William Gargan, Maria Palmer
rows.extract: Rendezvous 24 is a 1946 American drama film directed by James Tinling and written by Aubrey Wisberg. The film stars William Gargan, Maria Palmer, Patrick O'Moore, Herman Bing, Kay Connors and Kurt Katch. The film was released on May 6, 1946, by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Renegade Girl
rows.cast: Ann Savage, Alan Curtis, Jack Holt
rows.extract: Renegade Girl is a 1946 American western film directed by William Berke and starring Ann Savage, Alan Curtis and Edward Brophy. It was one of a few movies made by the short-lived Affiliated Productions, and was released through Robert L. Lippert's Screen Guild Productions.

rows.title: Renegades
rows.cast: Evelyn Keyes, Willard Parker, Larry Parks
rows.extract: Renegades is a 1946 American Western film directed by George Sherman and starring Evelyn Keyes, Willard Parker, Larry Parks and Edgar Buchanan.

rows.title: The Return of Monte Cristo
rows.cast: Louis Hayward, Barbara Britton
rows.extract: The Return of Monte Cristo is a 1946 swashbuckler film which is a sequel to The Count of Monte Cristo (1934) and The Son of Monte Cristo (1940).

rows.title: The Return of Rusty
rows.cast: John Litel, Barbara Woodell
rows.extract: The Return of Rusty is a 1946 American drama film directed by William Castle and starring Ted Donaldson, John Litel and Mark Dennis. It was the second in the eight part Rusty film series produced by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Rio Grande Raiders
rows.cast: Sunset Carson, Linda Stirling
rows.extract: Rio Grande Raiders is a 1946 American Western film directed by Thomas Carr and written by Norton S. Parker. The film stars Sunset Carson, Linda Stirling, Bob Steele, Tom London, Tristram Coffin and Edmund Cobb. It was released on September 9, 1946 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Riverboat Rhythm
rows.cast: Leon Errol, Glen Vernon
rows.extract: Riverboat Rhythm is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Leslie Goodwins and written by Charles E. Roberts. The film stars Leon Errol, Glenn Vernon, Walter Catlett, Joan Newton, Marc Cramer, and Jonathan Hale. The film was released on February 13, 1946, by RKO Radio Pictures.

rows.title: Road to Utopia
rows.cast: Bing Crosby, Bob Hope, Dorothy Lamour
rows.extract: Road to Utopia is a 1946 American semi-musical comedy film directed by Hal Walker and starring Bing Crosby, Bob Hope, and Dorothy Lamour. rows.title: Roaring Rangers
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette
rows.extract: Roaring Rangers is a 1946 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Barry Shipman. The film stars Charles Starrett, Adele Roberts, Merle Travis and Smiley Burnette. The film was released on February 14, 1946, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Roll on Texas Moon
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Dale Evans, Dennis Hoey
rows.extract: Roll on Texas Moon  is a 1946 American Western film directed by William Witney and starring Roy Rogers.

rows.title: Rolling Home
rows.cast: Jean Parker, Pamela Blake
rows.extract: Rolling Home is a 1946 American drama film directed by William Berke and starring Jean Parker, Russell Hayden, and Pamela Blake.

rows.title: Romance of the West
rows.cast: Eddie Dean, Emmett Lynn
rows.extract: Romance of the West is a 1946 American Western film directed by Robert Emmett Tansey and written by Frances Kavanaugh. The film stars Eddie Dean, Emmett Lynn, Joan Barton, Forrest Taylor, Robert McKenzie, Jerry Jerome, Stanley Price and Chief Thundercloud. The film was released on March 20, 1946, by

rows.title: The Runaround
rows.cast: Rod Cameron, Ella Raines, Broderick Crawford
rows.extract: The Runaround is a 1946 American black-and-white film directed by Charles Lamont and starring Rod Cameron, Ella Raines, Broderick Crawford, and Frank McHugh. The film is also known as Deadly Enemies.

rows.title: Rustler's Round-up
rows.cast: Kirby Grant, Jane Adams

rows.title: San Quentin
rows.cast: Lawrence Tierney, Barton MacLane, Carol Forman
rows.extract: San Quentin is a 1946 American romantic drama film directed by Gordon Douglas.

rows.title: Santa Fe Uprising
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Martha Wentworth
rows.extract: Santa Fe Uprising is a 1946 American Western film in the Red Ryder film series directed by R. G. Springsteen, written by Earle Snell, and starring Allan Lane, Robert Blake, Martha Wentworth, Barton MacLane, Jack La Rue and Tom London. It was released on November 15, 1946, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: A Scandal in Paris
rows.cast: George Sanders, Carole Landis, Signe Hasso
rows.extract: A Scandal in Paris is a 1946 American biographical film directed by Douglas Sirk and starring George Sanders, Signe Hasso and Carole Landis. It loosely depicts the life of Eugène François Vidocq, a French criminal who reformed and became a famous French Prefect of Police during the Napoleonic era.

rows.title: The Searching Wind
rows.cast: Robert Young, Sylvia Sidney
rows.extract: The Searching Wind is a 1946 American feature film directed by William Dieterle and starring Robert Young, Sylvia Sidney, and Ann Richards. It is based on the play of the same name by Lillian Hellman. It had originally been planned for producer Hal Wallis to make the film at Warner Bros., but after

rows.title: The Secret Heart
rows.cast: Claudette Colbert, Walter Pidgeon, June Allyson
rows.extract: The Secret Heart is a 1946 film directed by Robert Z. Leonard and starring Claudette Colbert, Walter Pidgeon and June Allyson.

rows.title: The Secret of the Whistler
rows.cast: Richard Dix, Leslie Brooks
rows.extract: The Secret of the Whistler is a 1946 American mystery film noir based on the radio drama The Whistler. rows.title: Sentimental Journey
rows.cast: Maureen O'Hara, John Payne
rows.extract: Sentimental Journey  is a 1946 American drama film directed by Walter Lang and starring John Payne and Maureen O'Hara.

rows.title: Shadow of a Woman
rows.cast: Helmut Dantine, Andrea King
rows.extract: Shadow of a Woman is a 1946 American drama film noir directed by Joseph Santley, featuring Helmut Dantine and Andrea King. The film is based on the novel He Fell Down Dead written by Virginia Perdue.

rows.title: Shadowed
rows.cast: Anita Louise, Lloyd Corrigan
rows.extract: Shadowed, also known as The Gloved Hand, is a 1946 American film noir crime film directed by John Sturges and starring Anita Louise, Lloyd Corrigan, and Robert Scott.

rows.title: The Shadow Returns
rows.cast: Kane Richmond, Barbara Read
rows.extract: The Shadow Returns is a 1946 American comedy crime film directed by Phil Rosen and starring Kane Richmond, Barbara Read and Tom Dugan. It features the pulp character The Shadow, already a popular hero of novels and a radio show. It was the first in a series of three films released by Monogram in 194

rows.title: Shadows on the Range
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: Shadows on the Range is a 1946 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by Adele Buffington. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Jan Bryant, Jack Perrin, John Merton and Marshall Reed. The film was released on October 16, 1946, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Shadows Over Chinatown
rows.cast: Sidney Toler, Mantan Moreland
rows.extract: Shadows Over Chinatown is a 1946 film directed by Terry O. Morse. It is the second to last film featuring Sidney Toler as Charlie Chan.

rows.title: She-Wolf of London
rows.cast: June Lockhart, Don Porter
rows.extract: She-Wolf of London is a 1946 American mystery and horror film directed by Jean Yarbrough. It stars June Lockhart and Don Porter. rows.title: She Wrote the Book
rows.cast: Joan Davis, Jack Oakie
rows.extract: She Wrote the Book is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Charles Lamont and starring Joan Davis, Jack Oakie, and Mischa Auer. The screenplay concerns a shy midwestern professor who travels to New York City to visit a publisher of her friend's book which turns out to be a racy bestseller.

rows.title: Sheriff of Redwood Valley
rows.cast: Wild Bill Elliott, Peggy Stewart
rows.extract: Sheriff of Redwood Valley is a 1946 American Western film in the Red Ryder film series directed by R. G. Springsteen and written by Earle Snell. rows.title: Shock
rows.cast: Vincent Price, Lynn Bari, Frank Latimore
rows.extract: Shock is a 1946 American film noir directed by Alfred L. Werker and starring Vincent Price, Lynn Bari and Frank Latimore.

rows.title: The Show-Off
rows.cast: Red Skelton, Marilyn Maxwell, Virginia O'Brien
rows.extract: The Show-Off is a 1946 film directed by Harry Beaumont based on the play of the same name by George Kelly. It stars Red Skelton and Marilyn Maxwell. rows.title: Silver Range
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: Silver Range is a 1946 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by J. Benton Cheney. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Jan Bryant, I. Stanford Jolley, Terry Frost and Eddie Parker. The film was released on November 16, 1946, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Sing While You Dance
rows.cast: Ellen Drew, Kirby Grant
rows.extract: Sing While You Dance is a 1946 American musical comedy film directed by D. Ross Lederman and starring Ellen Drew, Kirby Grant, and Andrew Tombes.

rows.title: Singing on the Trail
rows.cast: Ken Curtis, Jeff Donnell, Guy Kibbee
rows.extract: Singing on the Trail is a 1946 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by J. Benton Cheney. The film stars Ken Curtis, Jeff Donnell, Guy Kibbee, Dusty Anderson and Guinn "Big Boy" Williams. The film was released on September 2, 1946, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Singin' in the Corn
rows.cast: Judy Canova, Allen Jenkins
rows.extract: Singin' in the Corn is a 1946 American Comedy Western film directed by Del Lord and written by Isabel Dawn, Monte Brice, and Elwood Ullman. rows.title: Sioux City Sue
rows.cast: Gene Autry, Lynne Roberts
rows.extract: Sioux City Sue is a 1946 American Western film directed by Frank McDonald and written by Olive Cooper. Starring Gene Autry, Lynne Roberts, Sterling Holloway, Richard Lane, Ralph Sanford and Ken Lundy, it was released on November 21, 1946, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Sister Kenny
rows.cast: Rosalind Russell, Alexander Knox
rows.extract: Sister Kenny is a 1946 American biographical film about Sister Elizabeth Kenny, an Australian bush nurse, who fought to help people who suffered from polio, despite opposition from the medical establishment. The film stars Rosalind Russell, Alexander Knox, and Philip Merivale.

rows.title: Six Gun Man
rows.cast: Bob Steele, Syd Saylor
rows.extract: Six Gun Man is a 1946 American Western film written and directed by Harry L. Fraser. The film stars Bob Steele, Syd Saylor, Jimmy Martin, Jean Carlin, I. Stanford Jolley, Brooke Temple, Bud Osborne and Budd Buster. The film was released on February 1, 1946, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: Slightly Scandalous
rows.cast: Sheila Ryan, Lita Baron
rows.extract: Slightly Scandalous is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Will Jason and written by Erna Lazarus, David Mathews, Joel Malone and Jerry Warner. The film stars Frederick Brady, Sheila Ryan, Paula Drew, Walter Catlett, Lita Baron, Louis DaPron and Jack Marshall. It was released on August 2, 1946 b

rows.title: Smoky
rows.cast: Fred MacMurray, Anne Baxter
rows.extract: Smoky is a 1946 American Western film directed by Louis King and starring Fred MacMurray. It is the second of three film adaptations of the 1926 novel Smoky the Cowhorse by Will James; others were made in 1933 and 1966.

rows.title: Smooth as Silk
rows.cast: Kent Taylor, Virginia Grey
rows.extract: Smooth as Silk is a 1946 American noir film directed by Charles Barton and starring Kent Taylor, Virginia Grey, and Milburn Stone. rows.title: So Dark the Night
rows.cast: Steven Geray, Micheline Cheirel
rows.extract: So Dark the Night is a 1946 American crime film with film noir influences, featuring Steven Geray, Micheline Cheirel, and Eugene Borden. Based on a story written by Aubrey Wisberg, the screenplay was written by Dwight V. Babcock and Martin Berkeley, and directed by Joseph H. Lewis.

rows.title: So Goes My Love
rows.cast: Myrna Loy, Don Ameche, Molly Lamont
rows.extract: So Goes My Love is an American 1946 comedy-drama film, produced by Universal Pictures. It is based on a true story, A Genius in the Family, the memoir of Hiram Percy Maxim, which focuses on the relationship between Maxim and his father, Sir Hiram Stevens Maxim.

rows.title: Somewhere in the Night
rows.cast: John Hodiak, Lloyd Nolan, Nancy Guild
rows.extract: Somewhere in the Night is a 1946 American film noir psychological thriller film directed by Joseph L. rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Dale Evans, Lyle Talbot
rows.extract: Song of Arizona is a 1946 American Western film directed by Frank McDonald and starring Roy Rogers, Dale Evans and George "Gabby" Hayes. It was produced and distributed by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Song of the Sierras
rows.cast: Jimmy Wakely, Jack Baxley
rows.extract: Song of the Sierras is a 1946 American Western film directed by Oliver Drake and written by Elmer Clifton. The film stars Jimmy Wakely, Lee "Lasses" White, Jack Baxley, Jean Carlin, Iris Lancaster and Zon Murray. The film was released on December 28, 1946, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.cast: James Baskett, Bobby Driscoll, Luana Patten
rows.extract: Song of the South is a 1946 American live-action/animated musical drama film directed by Harve Foster and Wilfred Jackson; produced by Walt Disney and released by RKO Radio Pictures. rows.title: South of Monterey
rows.cast: Gilbert Roland, Martin Garralaga
rows.extract: South of Monterey is a 1946 American Western film directed by William Nigh and written by Charles S. Belden. The film stars Gilbert Roland, Martin Garralaga, Frank Yaconelli, Marjorie Riordan, Iris Flores and George J. Lewis. The film was released on June 15, 1946, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Specter of the Rose
rows.cast: Judith Anderson, Lionel Stander
rows.extract: Specter of the Rose is a 1946 film noir thriller film written and directed by Ben Hecht and starring Judith Anderson, Ivan Kirov, Viola Essen, Michael Chekhov, and Lionel Stander, with choreography by Tamara Geva, and music by George Antheil.

rows.title: The Spider Woman Strikes Back
rows.cast: Gale Sondergaard, Kirby Grant, Brenda Joyce
rows.extract: The Spider Woman Strikes Back is a 1946 horror film starring Gale Sondergaard, with a running time of 59 minutes. rows.title: Spook Busters
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall
rows.extract: Spook Busters is a 1946 film directed by William Beaudine and starring the comedy team of The Bowery Boys. It is the fourth film in the series of forty eight.

rows.title: The Spiral Staircase
rows.cast: Dorothy McGuire, George Brent, Rhonda Fleming
rows.extract: The Spiral Staircase is a 1946 American psychological horror film directed by Robert Siodmak and starring Dorothy McGuire, George Brent, and Ethel Barrymore. rows.title: Stagecoach to Denver
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Peggy Stewart
rows.extract: Stagecoach to Denver is a 1946 American Western film and one of the Republic Pictures Red Ryder film series directed by R. G. Springsteen.

rows.title: Stars Over Texas
rows.cast: Eddie Dean, Roscoe Ates, Shirley Patterson
rows.extract: Stars Over Texas is a 1946 American Western film directed by Robert Emmett Tansey and starring Eddie Dean, Roscoe Ates, and Shirley Patterson.

rows.title: A Stolen Life
rows.cast: Bette Davis, Glenn Ford
rows.extract: A Stolen Life is a 1946 American drama film starring Bette Davis, who also produced it. The film, based on the 1935 novel A Stolen Life by Karel Josef Benes, was directed by Curtis Bernhardt. rows.title: Strange Conquest
rows.cast: Jane Wyatt, Lowell Gilmore, Julie Bishop
rows.extract: Strange Conquest is a 1946 American drama film directed by John Rawlins and written by Roy Chanslor. The film stars Jane Wyatt, Lowell Gilmore, Julie Bishop, Peter Cookson, Milburn Stone, Samuel S. Hinds and Abner Biberman. The film was released on May 10, 1946, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Strange Impersonation
rows.cast: Brenda Marshall, William Gargan, Hillary Brooke
rows.extract: Strange Impersonation is a 1946 American film noir drama film directed by Anthony Mann and starring Brenda Marshall, William Gargan and Hillary Brooke.

rows.title: Strange Journey
rows.cast: Paul Kelly, Osa Massen, Hillary Brooke, Lee Patrick
rows.extract: Strange Journey is a 1946 American drama film directed by James Tinling and starring Paul Kelly, Osa Massen and Hillary Brooke. On an isolate island, a reformer gangster and his wife battle a group of Nazi agents attempting to get their hands of uranium deposits.

rows.title: The Strange Love of Martha Ivers
rows.cast: Barbara Stanwyck, Van Heflin, Lizabeth Scott
rows.extract: The Strange Love of Martha Ivers is a 1946 American film noir drama directed by Lewis Milestone from a screenplay written by Robert Rossen, based on the short story "Love Lies Bleeding" by playwright John Patrick. rows.extract: The Stranger is a 1946 American thriller film noir directed and co-written by Orson Welles, starring Edward G. Robinson, Loretta Young and Orson Welles. rows.title: Strange Triangle
rows.cast: Signe Hasso, Preston Foster
rows.extract: Strange Triangle is a 1946 American crime film noir directed by Ray McCarey and starring Signe Hasso, Preston Foster and Anabel Shaw.

rows.title: The Strange Woman

rows.extract: The Strange Woman is a 1946 American melodrama film directed by Edgar G. Ulmer and written by Ulmer and Hunt Stromberg, starring Hedy Lamarr, George Sanders and Louis Hayward. Originally released by United Artists, the film is now in the public domain.

rows.title: Strangler of the Swamp
rows.cast: Rosemary La Planche, Blake Edwards
rows.extract: Strangler of the Swamp is a 1946 American horror film, produced and distributed by Producers Releasing Corporation. It was written and directed by Frank Wisbar, and stars Rosemary LaPlanche, Robert Barrat and Blake Edwards. It is a remake of Wisbar's earlier German film Fährmann Maria (1936).

rows.title: Sun Valley Cyclone
rows.cast: Wild Bill Elliott, Alice Fleming
rows.extract: Sun Valley Cyclone is a 1946 American Western film in the Red Ryder film series directed by R. G. Springsteen, written by Earle Snell, and starring Wild Bill Elliott, Robert Blake, Alice Fleming, Roy Barcroft, Kenne Duncan and Eddy Waller. It was released on May 10, 1946, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Sunset Pass

The film stars James Warren, Nan Leslie, John Laurenz, Jane Greer, Robert Barrat, Harry Woods, Robert Clarke, Steve Brodie, and Harry Harvey.

rows.title: Susie Steps Out
rows.cast: David Bruce, Margaret Dumont
rows.extract: Susie Steps Out is a 1946 American comedy film directed by Reginald Le Borg, written by Elwood Ullman and Fred Freiberger, and starring David Bruce, Cleatus Caldwell, Nita Hunter, Howard Freeman, Grady Sutton and Margaret Dumont. It was released on December 13, 1946 by United Artists.

rows.title: Suspense

rows.title: Swamp Fire
rows.cast: Johnny Weissmuller

rows.title: Sweetheart of Sigma Chi

rows.extract: Sweetheart of Sigma Chi is a 1946 American film directed by Jack Bernhard and William Beaudine.

rows.title: Swell Guy

rows.title: Talk About a Lady

rows.title: Tangier
