rows.title: When a Girl's Beautiful
rows.cast: Adele Jergens, Marc Platt, Patricia Barry
rows.extract: When a Girl's Beautiful is a 1947 musical comedy directed by Frank McDonald from a script by Brenda Weisberg. Actress Joi Lansing made her film debut on this film.

rows.title: Where There's Life
rows.cast: Bob Hope, Signe Hasso, William Bendix, George Coulouris
rows.extract: Where There's Life is a 1947 American thriller comedy film directed by Sidney Lanfield. The film's title derives from a line in Don Quixote as a play on the name of its star, Bob Hope. Also in the cast are Signe Hasso, William Bendix, and George Coulouris.

rows.title: Whispering City
rows.cast: Paul Lukas, Helmut Dantine
rows.extract: Whispering City is a 1947 black-and-white film noir directed by Fedor Ozep and starring Paul Lukas, Mary Anderson, and Helmut Dantine. It was filmed on location in Quebec City and Montmorency Falls, Quebec, Canada in both English and French.

rows.title: Wild Country
rows.cast: Eddie Dean, Roscoe Ates
rows.extract: Wild Country is a 1947 American Western film directed by Ray Taylor.

rows.title: The Wild Frontier
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Jack Holt
rows.extract: The Wild Frontier is a 1947 American Western film directed by Philip Ford and written by Albert DeMond. The film stars Allan Lane, Jack Holt, Eddy Waller, Pierre Watkin, John James and Roy Barcroft. The film was released on October 1, 1947, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Wild Harvest
rows.cast: Alan Ladd, Dorothy Lamour, Robert Preston
rows.extract: Wild Harvest is a 1947 film directed by Tay Garnett and starring Alan Ladd and Dorothy Lamour.

rows.title: Wild Horse Mesa
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Nan Leslie
rows.extract: Wild Horse Mesa is a 1947 American Western film directed by Wallace Grissell and starring Tim Holt, Nan Leslie, and Richard Martin. It was written by Norman Houston, based on the novel of the same name by Zane Grey.

rows.title: The Wistful Widow of Wagon Gap
rows.cast: Bud Abbott, Lou Costello
rows.extract: The Wistful Widow of Wagon Gap is a 1947 black-and-white comedy Western film directed by Charles Barton and starring the comedy team of Abbott and Costello. It was released on October 8 and distributed by Universal-International.

rows.title: The Woman on the Beach
rows.cast: Joan Bennett, Robert Ryan, Charles Bickford
rows.extract: The Woman on the Beach is a 1947 film noir directed by Jean Renoir and starring Joan Bennett, Robert Ryan and Charles Bickford. It was released by RKO Radio Pictures. rows.title: Wyoming
rows.cast: Wild Bill Elliott, Vera Ralston
rows.extract: Wyoming is a 1947 American Western film directed by Joseph Kane and starring Wild Bill Elliott, Vera Ralston and John Carroll. It was produced by Republic Pictures. While Republic specialized in lower-budget second features, it also released more prestigious films such as this in an attempt to compe

rows.title: Yankee Fakir
rows.cast: Douglas Fowley, Joan Woodbury
rows.extract: Yankee Fakir is a 1947 American mystery film directed and produced by W. Lee Wilder and written by Richard S. Conway. The film stars Douglas Fowley, Joan Woodbury, Clem Bevans, Ransom M. Sherman, Frank Reicher and Marc Lawrence. The film was released on April 1, 1947, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Thunderbolt

rows.extract: The Creeper is a 1948 American horror film directed by Jean Yarbrough. The film stars Onslow Stevens who plays a mad doctor whose serum turns a man into a catlike killer.

rows.title: Crossed Trails
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Lynne Carver
rows.extract: Crossed Trails is a 1948 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by Adele Buffington. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Lynne Carver, Douglas Evans, Kathy Frye and Zon Murray. The film was released on April 11, 1948 by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Cry of the City
rows.cast: Victor Mature, Richard Conte
rows.extract: Cry of the City is a 1948 American film noir starring Victor Mature, Richard Conte, and Shelley Winters. Directed by Robert Siodmak, it is based on the novel by Henry Edward Helseth, The Chair for Martin Rome. The screenwriter Ben Hecht worked on the film's script, but is not credited. The film was

rows.title: Daredevils of the Clouds
rows.cast: Robert Livingston, Mae Clarke
rows.extract: Daredevils of the Clouds is a 1948 American drama film directed by George Blair and produced by Republic Pictures. The film stars Robert Livingston, Mae Clarke and James Cardwell. Daredevils of the Clouds depicts bush pilot flying in northern Canada.

rows.title: The Dark Past
rows.cast: William Holden, Nina Foch, Lee J. Cobb
rows.extract: The Dark Past is a 1948 American film noir psychological thriller film starring William Holden, Nina Foch, and Lee J. Cobb. Directed by Rudolph Maté, the Columbia Pictures release is a remake of Blind Alley (1939), also released by Columbia, and based on a play by American dramatist James Warwick.

rows.title: A Date with Judy
rows.cast: Wallace Beery, Jane Powell, Elizabeth Taylor
rows.extract: A Date with Judy is a 1948 American comedy musical film starring Wallace Beery, Jane Powell, and Elizabeth Taylor. Directed by Richard Thorpe, the film was based on the radio series of the same name.

rows.title: The Dead Don't Dream
rows.cast: William Boyd, Andy Clyde
rows.extract: The Dead Don't Dream is a 1948 American Western film directed by George Archainbaud and written by Francis Rosenwald. The picture stars William Boyd, Andy Clyde, Rand Brooks, Mary Ware, John Parrish and Leonard Penn, and was released in 1948 by United Artists.

rows.title: Dead Man's Gold
rows.cast: Lash La Rue, Al St. John, Peggy Stewart
rows.extract: Dead Man's Gold is a 1948 American Western film starring Lash LaRue and Al "Fuzzy" St. John, the first of his Westerns for producer Ron Ormond.

rows.title: Deadline
rows.cast: Sunset Carson, Lee Roberts
rows.extract: Deadline is a 1948 American Western film directed by Oliver Drake and starring Sunset Carson, Al Terry and Pat Starling.

rows.title: The Decision of Christopher Blake
rows.cast: Alexis Smith, Cecil Kellaway, John Hoyt, Robert Douglas
rows.extract: The Decision of Christopher Blake is a 1948 American drama film based upon the Moss Hart play. It was adapted by Ranald MacDougall and directed by Peter Godfrey. The film stars Alexis Smith, Robert Douglas, Cecil Kellaway, Ted Donaldson, John Hoyt and Harry Davenport and was released by Warner Bros.

rows.title: Deep Waters
rows.cast: Jean Peters, Dana Andrews
rows.extract: Deep Waters is a 1948 drama film directed by Henry King. The film is based on the 1946 novel Spoonhandle written by Ruth Moore and was nominated for a 1949 Oscar for Best Special Effects, but lost to Portrait of Jennie.

rows.title: The Denver Kid
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Eddy Waller
rows.extract: The Denver Kid is a 1948 American Western film directed by Philip Ford and written by Robert Creighton Williams. The film stars Allan Lane, Eddy Waller, William "Bill" Henry, Douglas Fowley, Rory Mallinson and George Lloyd. The film was released on October 1, 1948, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Desperadoes of Dodge City
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Mildred Coles
rows.extract: Desperadoes of Dodge City is a 1948 American Western film directed by Philip Ford and written by Robert Creighton Williams. The film stars Allan Lane, Eddy Waller, Mildred Coles, Roy Barcroft, Tristram Coffin and William Phipps. The film was released on September 15, 1948, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Devil's Cargo
rows.cast: John Calvert, Rochelle Hudson
rows.extract: Devil's Cargo is a 1948 American film directed by John F. Link Sr.

rows.title: Disaster
rows.cast: Richard Denning, Trudy Marshall
rows.extract: Disaster is a 1948 American drama film directed by William H. Pine and written by Thomas Ahearn. The film stars Richard Denning, Trudy Marshall, Damian O'Flynn, Will Wright, James Millican and Jack Lambert. The film was released on December 3, 1948, by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: Docks of New Orleans
rows.cast: Roland Winters, Virginia Dale
rows.extract: Docks of New Orleans is a 1948 American mystery film directed by Derwin Abrahams and starring Roland Winters, Virginia Dale and Mantan Moreland. It featured Winters in his second appearance as Charlie Chan, having replaced Sidney Toler in the role.

rows.title: Dream Girl
rows.cast: Betty Hutton, Patric Knowles, Virginia Field
rows.extract: Dream Girl is a 1948 comedy film directed by Mitchell Leisen, adapted from the 1945 play of the same name written by Elmer Rice. It stars Betty Hutton and Macdonald Carey.

rows.title: The Dude Goes West
rows.cast: Eddie Albert, Gale Storm
rows.extract: The Dude Goes West is a 1948 American comedy western film starring Eddie Albert and Gale Storm. It was directed by Kurt Neumann and released by Monogram Pictures. The film was originally known as Tombstone.

rows.title: Easter Parade
rows.cast: Fred Astaire, Judy Garland, Ann Miller, Peter Lawford
rows.extract: Easter Parade is a 1948 American Technicolor musical film starring Judy Garland, Fred Astaire, Peter Lawford, and Ann Miller. The film contains some of Astaire's and Garland's best-known songs, including "Easter Parade", "Steppin' Out with My Baby", and "We're a Couple of Swells", all by Irving Berl

rows.title: El Dorado Pass
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Elena Verdugo
rows.extract: El Dorado Pass is a 1948 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Earle Snell. The film stars Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette, Elena Verdugo, Steve Darrell, Rory Mallinson and Ted Mapes. The film was released on October 14, 1948, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Embraceable You
rows.cast: Dane Clark, Geraldine Brooks
rows.extract: Embraceable You is a 1948 romantic drama film starring Dane Clark and Geraldine Brooks, and directed by Felix Jacoves.

rows.title: The Emperor Waltz
rows.cast: Bing Crosby, Joan Fontaine
rows.extract: The Emperor Waltz is a 1948 American musical film directed by Billy Wilder, and starring Bing Crosby and Joan Fontaine. Written by Wilder and Charles Brackett, the film is about a brash American gramophone salesman in Austria at the turn of the twentieth century who tries to convince Emperor Franz J

rows.title: The Enchanted Valley
rows.cast: Alan Curtis, Anne Gwynne
rows.extract: The Enchanted Valley is a 1948 American drama film directed by Robert Emmett Tansey and written by Frances Kavanaugh. The film stars Alan Curtis, Anne Gwynne, Charley Grapewin, Donn Gift, Joseph Crehan, Lash LaRue and Joe Devlin. The film was released on March 24, 1948, by Eagle-Lion Films.

rows.title: Enchantment
rows.cast: David Niven, Teresa Wright
rows.extract: Enchantment is a 1948 romantic drama film starring David Niven and Teresa Wright, directed by Irving Reis, produced by Samuel Goldwyn, and based on the 1945 novel A Fugue in Time by Rumer Godden.

rows.title: Escape
rows.cast: Rex Harrison, Peggy Cummins
rows.extract: Escape is a 1948 British-American thriller film directed by Joseph L. Mankiewicz. It follows a Royal Air Force World War II veteran who goes to prison and then escapes and meets a woman who persuades him to surrender. The screenplay by Philip Dunne was based on the 1926 play Escape by John Galsworth

rows.title: Every Girl Should Be Married
rows.cast: Cary Grant, Betsy Drake
rows.extract: Every Girl Should Be Married is a 1948 American romantic comedy film directed by Don Hartman and starring Cary Grant, Betsy Drake and Franchot Tone. Grant and Drake married a year after the film's release.

rows.title: Eyes of Texas
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Lynne Roberts
rows.extract: Eyes of Texas is a 1948 American Western film shot in Trucolor directed by William Witney and starring Roy Rogers.

rows.title: False Paradise
rows.cast: William Boyd, Elaine Riley
rows.extract: False Paradise  is a 1948 American Western film starring William Boyd as western character Hopalong Cassidy. This fi;m was the sixty-fifth of sixty-six Hopalong Cassidy movies and was the 11th of 12 Hopalong Cassidy Westerns produced by William Boyd for United Artists release.

rows.title: The Far Frontier
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Clayton Moore, Gail Davis
rows.extract: The Far Frontier  is a 1948 American Western film starring Roy Rogers.

rows.title: The Feathered Serpent
rows.cast: Roland Winters, Keye Luke
rows.extract: The Feathered Serpent is a 1948 mystery film, the fifth of six in which Roland Winters portrayed Charlie Chan. It is the only Chan film which featured both Keye Luke and Victor Sen Yung together. Luke had been cast in the later Warner Oland Chan films while Yung appeared primarily in the Sidney Tole

rows.title: Feudin', Fussin' and A-Fightin'
rows.cast: Donald O'Connor, Penny Edwards
rows.extract: Feudin', Fussin' and A-Fightin' is a 1948 American musical comedy film directed by George Sherman and starring Donald O'Connor. Also featured are Marjorie Main and Percy Kilbride,, with Penny Edwards as the perky love interest. It was produced and distributed by Universal Studios.

rows.title: Fighter Squadron
rows.cast: Edmond O'Brien, Robert Stack
rows.extract: Fighter Squadron is a 1948 American World War II aviation war film in Technicolor from Warner Bros., produced by Seton I. Miller, directed by Raoul Walsh, that stars Edmond O'Brien, Robert Stack, and John Rodney.

rows.title: Fighting Back
rows.cast: Jean Rogers, Paul Langton
rows.extract: Fighting Back is a 1948 American drama film directed by Malcolm St. Clair and written by John Stone. The film stars Paul Langton, Jean Rogers, Gary Gray, Joe Sawyer, Morris Ankrum and John Kellogg. The film was released on July 30, 1948, by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Fighting Father Dunne
rows.cast: Pat O'Brien, Una O'Connor
rows.extract: Fighting Father Dunne is a 1948 American biographical film about the life of Father Peter Dunne, and the creation of his News Boys Home in St. Louis, Missouri. Directed by Ted Tetzlaff, the screenplay was written by Martin Rackin and Frank Davis, based on an original story by William Rankin. The fil

rows.title: Fighting Mustang
rows.cast: Sunset Carson, Lee Roberts
rows.extract: Fighting Mustang is a 1948 American Western film directed by Oliver Drake and written by Rita Ross. The film stars Sunset Carson, Al Terry, Pat Starling, Felice Richmond, Polly McKay and William Val. The film was released on February 20, 1948, by Astor Pictures.

rows.title: The Fighting Ranger
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: The Fighting Ranger is a 1948 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by Ronald Davidson. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Christine Larson, Marshall Reed, Eddie Parker and Charlie Hughes. The film was released on August 15, 1948 by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Force of Evil
rows.cast: John Garfield, Beatrice Pearson
rows.extract: Force of Evil is a 1948 American crime film noir starring John Garfield and directed by Abraham Polonsky. It was adapted by Polonsky and Ira Wolfert from Wolfert's novel Tucker's People. Polonsky had been a screenwriter for the boxing film Body and Soul (1947), in which Garfield had also played the

rows.title: A Foreign Affair
rows.cast: Jean Arthur, Marlene Dietrich
rows.extract: A Foreign Affair is a 1948 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Billy Wilder and starring Jean Arthur, Marlene Dietrich, and John Lund. The screenplay by Wilder, Charles Brackett, and Richard L. Breen is based on a story by David Shaw adapted by Robert Harari.

rows.title: For the Love of Mary
rows.cast: Deanna Durbin, Edmond O'Brien
rows.extract: For the Love of Mary is a 1948 American romantic comedy film directed by Frederick de Cordova and starring Deanna Durbin, Edmond O'Brien, Don Taylor, and Jeffrey Lynn. Written by Oscar Brodney, the film is about a young woman who takes a job at the White House as a switchboard operator and soon rece

rows.title: Fort Apache
rows.cast: John Wayne, Henry Fonda
rows.extract: Fort Apache is a 1948 American Western film directed by John Ford and starring John Wayne and Henry Fonda. The film was the first of the director's "Cavalry Trilogy" and was followed by She Wore a Yellow Ribbon (1949) and Rio Grande (1950), both also starring Wayne. The screenplay was inspired by Ja

rows.title: Four Faces West
rows.cast: Joel McCrea, Frances Dee, Charles Bickford
rows.extract: Four Faces West is a 1948 American Western film starring Joel McCrea, his real-life wife Frances Dee, and Charles Bickford. It is based on the novel Pasó por aquí by Eugene Manlove Rhodes. Its plot concerns a down-on-his-luck cowboy who robs a bank. For its genre the film is unusual in that not a si

rows.title: French Leave
rows.cast: Jackie Cooper, Renee Godfrey
rows.extract: French Leave is a 1948 American comedy film directed by Frank McDonald and starring Jackie Cooper, Jackie Coogan and Renee Godfrey. It is the sequel to the 1947 film Kilroy Was Here and is sometimes known by the alternative title of Kilroy on Deck.

rows.title: Frontier Agent
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Reno Browne
rows.extract: Frontier Agent is a 1948 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by J. Benton Cheney. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Reno Browne, Kenneth MacDonald, Dennis Moore and Riley Hill. The film was released on May 16, 1948 by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Frontier Revenge
rows.cast: Lash La Rue, Peggy Stewart
rows.extract: Frontier Revenge is a 1948 American Western film written and directed by Ray Taylor and starring Lash LaRue and Al "Fuzzy" St. John. The film is a remake of Ray Taylor's Panamint's Bad Man (1938). Filmed at the Corriganville Movie Ranch, the film is neither set on a frontier nor is any revenge depic

rows.title: The Fuller Brush Man
rows.cast: Red Skelton, Janet Blair, Hillary Brooke, Adele Jergens
rows.extract: The Fuller Brush Man is a 1948 American comedy film starring Red Skelton as a door-to-door salesman for the Fuller Brush Company who becomes a murder suspect.

rows.title: Fury at Furnace Creek
rows.cast: Victor Mature, Coleen Gray
rows.extract: Fury at Furnace Creek  is a 1948 American Western film directed by H. Bruce Humberstone and starring Victor Mature, Coleen Gray, Glenn Langan, and Reginald Gardiner.

rows.title: The Gallant Blade
rows.cast: Larry Parks, Marguerite Chapman
rows.extract: The Gallant Blade is a 1948 American Cinecolor adventure film directed by Henry Levin and starring Larry Parks as a peasant hero of France in the 17th century after the Thirty Years' War.

rows.title: The Gallant Legion
rows.cast: Wild Bill Elliott, Lorna Gray
rows.extract: The Gallant Legion is a 1948 American Western film directed by Joseph Kane and written by Gerald Drayson Adams. The film stars Wild Bill Elliott, Lorna Gray, Joseph Schildkraut, Bruce Cabot, Andy Devine and Jack Holt. The film was released on May 24, 1948, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Gay Intruders
rows.cast: John Emery, Tamara Geva
rows.extract: The Gay Intruders is a 1948 comedy film directed by Ray McCarey and released by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: The Gay Ranchero
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Jane Frazee
rows.extract: The Gay Ranchero  is a 1948 American Western film starring Roy Rogers. It was filmed in Wildwood Regional Park in Thousand Oaks, California.

rows.title: The Gentleman from Nowhere
rows.cast: Warner Baxter, Fay Baker
rows.extract: The Gentleman from Nowhere is a 1948 American crime-drama film directed by William Castle.

rows.title: The Girl from Manhattan
rows.cast: Dorothy Lamour, George Montgomery, Charles Laughton
rows.extract: The Girl from Manhattan is a 1948 American comedy drama film directed by Alfred E. Green, starring Dorothy Lamour, George Montgomery, and Charles Laughton.

rows.title: Give My Regards to Broadway
rows.cast: Dan Dailey, Fay Bainter
rows.extract: Give My Regards to Broadway is a 1948 American musical film starring Dan Dailey and directed by Lloyd Bacon.

rows.title: Glamour Girl
rows.cast: Gene Krupa, Virginia Grey
rows.extract: Glamour Girl is a 1948 musical film starring Gene Krupa.

rows.title: The Golden Eye
rows.cast: Roland Winters, Wanda McKay
rows.extract: The Golden Eye is a 1948 American film directed by William Beaudine and starring Roland Winters in his fourth appearance as Charlie Chan. The film is also known as Charlie Chan in Texas and Charlie Chan in the Golden Eye.

rows.title: Good Sam
rows.cast: Gary Cooper, Ann Sheridan, Edmund Lowe
rows.extract: Good Sam is a 1948 American romantic comedy-drama film starring Gary Cooper as a Good Samaritan who is helpful to others at the expense of his own family. The film was directed by Leo McCarey and produced by McCarey's production company, Rainbow Productions. It received mixed reviews, with critics a

rows.title: Grand Canyon Trail
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Jane Frazee
rows.extract: Grand Canyon Trail  is a 1948 American Western film starring Roy Rogers combining Western action with Three Stooges-style slapstick. Robert Livingston plays the head villain and James Finlayson plays the sheriff. The Republic Pictures film was shot in Trucolor, but only black and white prints survi

rows.title: Green Grass of Wyoming
rows.cast: Peggy Cummins, Charles Coburn
rows.extract: Green Grass of Wyoming is a 1948 American Western film directed by Louis King, and starring Peggy Cummins, Charles Coburn and Robert Arthur.

rows.title: The Green Promise
rows.cast: Marguerite Chapman, Walter Brennan
rows.extract: The Green Promise is a 1948 American film directed by William D. Russell. The film was co-produced by Houston oilman Glenn McCarthy and leading man Robert Paige to display the concept and meaning of the 4-H Club and highlight farming issues such as soil erosion, government programs, and individual e

rows.title: Gunning for Justice
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: Gunning for Justice is a 1948 American Western film directed by Ray Taylor and written by J. Benton Cheney. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Max Terhune, Evelyn Finley, I. Stanford Jolley and House Peters Jr. The film was released on November 7, 1948 by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Guns of Hate
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Nan Leslie
rows.extract: Guns of Hate is a 1948 Western film directed by Lesley Selander featuring RKO's Western stars Tim Holt, with Nan Leslie and Richard Martin.

rows.title: Gun Smugglers
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Martha Hyer
rows.extract: Gun Smugglers is a 1948 American Western directed by Frank McDonald. The film is a Tim Holt B Western wherein Holt serves as a scout for the army in search of some smuggled gattling guns.

rows.title: Half Past Midnight
rows.cast: Peggy Knudsen, Kent Taylor
rows.extract: Half Past Midnight is a 1948 American comedy murder mystery film. It was William F. Claxton's first directed feature after eight years as a film editor.

rows.title: Harpoon
rows.cast: John Bromfield, James Cardwell
rows.extract: Harpoon is a 1948 American adventure film directed and produced by Ewing Scott, and starring John Bromfield in his first film role. Although described by some sources as a "documentary," it is a fictional feature film shot on location in Alaska.

rows.title: The Hawk of Powder River
rows.cast: Eddie Dean, Jennifer Holt
rows.extract: The Hawk of Powder River is a 1948 American Western film directed by Ray Taylor.

rows.title: Hazard
rows.cast: Paulette Goddard
rows.extract: Hazard is a 1948 American comedy drama film starring Paulette Goddard and Macdonald Carey, and directed by George Marshall.

rows.title: Heart of Virginia
rows.cast: Janet Martin, Robert Lowery
rows.extract: Heart of Virginia is a 1948 American sports drama film directed by R. G. Springsteen and starring Janet Martin, Robert Lowery and Frankie Darro. Believing that he is responsible for the death of a fellow rider, a jockey develops a fear of the racetrack.

rows.title: Here Comes Trouble
rows.cast: Joe Sawyer, William Tracy, Joan Woodbury
rows.extract: Here Comes Trouble is a 1948 American comedy film in the Hal Roach's Streamliners series. It was produced and directed by Fred Guiol and written by George Carleton Brown and Edward E. Seabrook. The film stars William Tracy, Joe Sawyer, Emory Parnell, Betty Compson and Joan Woodbury. It was released

rows.title: He Walked by Night
rows.cast: Richard Basehart, Jack Webb
rows.extract: He Walked by Night is a 1948 American police procedural film noir directed by Alfred L. Werker and an uncredited Anthony Mann. The film, shot in semidocumentary tone, is loosely based on the real-life actions of Erwin "Machine-Gun" Walker, a former Glendale, California police department employee and

rows.title: Hidden Danger
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: Hidden Danger is a 1948 American western film directed by Ray Taylor and starring Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton and Max Terhune. It was a second feature, distributed by Monogram Pictures which specialized in low-budget westerns and crime films. It was partly shot on location in Santa Clarita, Ca

rows.title: Highway 13
rows.cast: Robert Lowery, Pamela Blake
rows.extract: Highway 13 is a 1948 American film directed by William Berke and starring Robert Lowery. Lowery had just made Shep Comes Home for financier Robert L. Lippert.

rows.title: Hills of Home
rows.cast: Edmund Gwenn, Janet Leigh
rows.extract: Hills of Home is a 1948 Technicolor drama film, the fourth in a series of seven MGM Lassie films. It starred Edmund Gwenn, Donald Crisp, and Tom Drake.

rows.title: Hollow Triumph
rows.cast: Paul Henreid, Joan Bennett
rows.extract: Hollow Triumph is a 1948 American film noir crime film directed by Steve Sekely starring Paul Henreid, Joan Bennett and Leslie Brooks. It was released by Eagle-Lion Films, based on the 1946 novel of the same title written by Murray Forbes. The film's sets designed by the art director Edward L. Ilou.

rows.title: Homecoming
rows.cast: Clark Gable, Lana Turner, Anne Baxter
rows.extract: Homecoming is a 1948 romantic drama starring Clark Gable and Lana Turner. It was the third of their four films together, and like two of the others, was about a couple caught up in World War II.

rows.title: Homicide for Three
rows.cast: Audrey Long, Grant Withers
rows.extract: Homicide for Three is a 1948 American crime film directed by George Blair and written by Bradbury Foote and Albert DeMond. The film stars Warren Douglas, Audrey Long, Grant Withers, Lloyd Corrigan, Stephanie Bachelor and George Lynn. The film was released on December 8, 1948 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Hunted
rows.cast: Preston Foster, Belita
rows.extract: The Hunted is a 1948 American film noir crime film starring Preston Foster, Belita, Pierre Watkin and Edna Holland. It was directed by Jack Bernhard.

rows.title: I, Jane Doe
rows.cast: Vera Ralston, Ruth Hussey
rows.extract: I, Jane Doe is a 1948 American drama war film directed by John H. Auer and written by Lawrence Kimble and Decla Dunning. The film stars Ruth Hussey, John Carroll, Vera Ralston, Gene Lockhart, John Howard and Benay Venuta.

rows.title: I Love Trouble
rows.cast: Franchot Tone, Janet Blair, Janis Carter, Adele Jergens, Glenda Farrell
rows.extract: I Love Trouble is a 1948 American film noir crime film written by Roy Huggins from his first novel The Double Take, directed by S. rows.title: I Remember Mama
rows.cast: Irene Dunne, Barbara Bel Geddes
rows.extract: I Remember Mama is a 1948 American drama film directed by George Stevens from a screenplay by DeWitt Bodeen, whose work was adapted from John Van Druten's stage play. Druten, in turn, had based his play on Kathryn Forbes' novel Mama's Bank Account, which was originally published by Harcourt Brace in

rows.title: I Surrender Dear
rows.cast: Gloria Jean, David Street
rows.extract: I Surrender Dear is a 1948 American musical film directed by Arthur Dreifuss and starring Gloria Jean.

rows.title: I Walk Alone
rows.cast: Burt Lancaster, Lizabeth Scott, Kirk Douglas
rows.extract: I Walk Alone is a 1947 film noir directed by Byron Haskin and starring Burt Lancaster and Lizabeth Scott, with a supporting cast featuring Wendell Corey and Kirk Douglas.

rows.title: I Wouldn't Be in Your Shoes
rows.cast: Don Castle, Elyse Knox
rows.extract: I Wouldn't Be in Your Shoes is a 1948 American film noir directed by William Nigh, starring Don Castle and Elyse Knox. It was based on a novel of the same name by Cornell Woolrich with a screenplay by fellow pulp writer Steve Fisher.

rows.title: If You Knew Susie
rows.cast: Eddie Cantor, Joan Davis
rows.extract: If You Knew Susie is a 1948 American comedy film directed by Gordon Douglas and written by Warren Wilson, Oscar Brodney, Bud Pearson and Lester A. White. rows.title: In This Corner
rows.cast: Scott Brady, Anabel Shaw
rows.extract: In This Corner is a 1948 American sports drama film directed by Charles Reisner and starring Scott Brady, Anabel Shaw and James Millican.

rows.title: Incident
rows.cast: Jane Frazee, Joyce Compton
rows.extract: Incident is a 1948 American film noir directed by William Beaudine and featuring Warren Douglas, Jane Frazee and Robert Osterloh.

rows.title: Indian Agent
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Richard Martin, Nan Leslie
rows.extract: Indian Agent is a 1948 Western film starring Tim Holt as a cowboy trying to convince Indians not to go on the warpath due to the activities of a corrupt Indian agent.

rows.title: Inner Sanctum
rows.cast: Charles Russell, Mary Beth Hughes
rows.extract: Inner Sanctum is a 1948 American film noir directed by Lew Landers based on the Simon & Schuster book series of the same name and the Inner Sanctum Mystery radio series. A previous film series of the show had been produced by Universal Pictures until 1945. It is the first and only film of M.R.S. pro

rows.title: An Innocent Affair
rows.cast: Fred MacMurray, Madeleine Carroll
rows.extract: An Innocent Affair is a 1948 American comedy film directed by Lloyd Bacon and written by Lou Breslow and Joseph Hoffman. The film stars Fred MacMurray, Madeleine Carroll, Charles "Buddy" Rogers, Rita Johnson, Louise Allbritton and Alan Mowbray. It was released on October 15, 1948 by United Artists.

rows.title: The Inside Story
rows.cast: Marsha Hunt, William Lundigan, Charles Winninger
rows.extract: The Inside Story is a 1948 American comedy film directed by Allan Dwan and written by Mary Loos and Richard Sale. The film stars Marsha Hunt, William Lundigan, Charles Winninger, Gail Patrick, Gene Lockhart and Florence Bates. The film was released on March 14, 1948 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Iron Curtain
rows.cast: Dana Andrews, Gene Tierney, June Havoc
rows.extract: The Iron Curtain is a 1948 American thriller film starring Dana Andrews and Gene Tierney, directed by William A. Wellman. The film was based on the memoirs of Igor Gouzenko. Principal photography was done on location in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada by Charles G. Clarke. The film was later re-released as

rows.title: Isn't It Romantic?
rows.cast: Veronica Lake, Billy De Wolfe, Pearl Bailey
rows.extract: Isn't It Romantic? is a 1948 American comedy musical film from Paramount Pictures, directed by Norman Z. McLeod and starring Veronica Lake and Billy De Wolfe. Supporting actors included Mona Freeman, Richard Webb and Pearl Bailey. Although it takes its title from a 1932 song by Richard Rodgers and L

rows.title: Jiggs and Maggie in Court
rows.cast: Joe Yule, Renie Riano
rows.extract: Jiggs and Maggie in Court is a 1948 American comedy film directed by William Beaudine and starring Joe Yule, Renie Riano and George McManus. It was the second of a series of four films featuring Yule and Riano as the title characters, in a spin-off from the 1946 film Bringing Up Father.

rows.title: Jinx Money
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall
rows.extract: Jinx Money is a 1948 film starring the comedy team of The Bowery Boys. It is the tenth film in the series and the first one to include Bennie Bartlett as part of the team.

rows.title: Joan of Arc
rows.cast: Ingrid Bergman, José Ferrer
rows.extract: Joan of Arc is a 1948 American hagiographic epic film directed by Victor Fleming, and starring Ingrid Bergman as the eponymous French religious icon and war heroine. rows.title: Joe Palooka in Fighting Mad
rows.cast: Joe Kirkwood Jr., Leon Errol, Elyse Knox
rows.extract: Joe Palooka in Fighting Mad is a 1948 American comedy film directed by Reginald Le Borg and starring Leon Errol, Joe Kirkwood, Jr. and Elyse Knox. It was part of the Joe Palooka series, produced and distributed by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Joe Palooka in Winner Take All
rows.cast: Joe Kirkwood Jr., Elyse Knox
rows.extract: Joe Palooka in Winner Take All is a 1948 American film in the Joe Palooka series. It was directed by Reginald Le Borg.

rows.title: Johnny Belinda
rows.cast: Jane Wyman, Lew Ayres, Agnes Moorehead
rows.extract: Johnny Belinda is a 1948 American drama film, directed by Jean Negulesco, based on the 1940 Broadway stage hit of the same name by Elmer Blaney Harris. The play was adapted for the screen by writers Allen Vincent and Irma von Cube.

rows.title: Julia Misbehaves
rows.cast: Greer Garson, Walter Pidgeon, Peter Lawford, Elizabeth Taylor
rows.extract: Julia Misbehaves is a 1948 American romantic comedy film starring Greer Garson and Walter Pidgeon as a married couple who are separated by the man's snobbish family. They meet again many years later, when the daughter whom the man has raised, played by Elizabeth Taylor, invites her mother to her wed

rows.title: June Bride

rows.cast: Ida Lupino, Cornel Wilde
rows.extract: Road House is a 1948 American film noir drama film directed by Jean Negulesco, with cinematography by Joseph LaShelle. The picture features Ida Lupino, Cornel Wilde, Celeste Holm and Richard Widmark.

rows.title: Rocky
rows.cast: Roddy McDowall, Gale Sherwood
rows.extract: Rocky is a 1948 American drama film directed by Phil Karlson and starring Roddy McDowall, Edgar Barrier and Gale Sherwood. It was produced and distributed by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Rogues' Regiment
rows.cast: Dick Powell, Märta Torén, Vincent Price
rows.extract: Rogues' Regiment is a 1948 film noir action film directed by Robert Florey and starring Dick Powell, Märta Torén, and Vincent Price. It is the first American feature film to be set in the First Indochina War.

rows.title: Romance on the High Seas
rows.cast: Jack Carson, Janis Paige, Doris Day
rows.extract: Romance on the High Seas is a 1948 American musical romantic comedy film directed by Michael Curtiz, and starred Jack Carson, Janis Paige, Don DeFore and Doris Day in her film debut. Busby Berkeley was the choreographer. The film was nominated for two Academy Awards, for Original Song for "It's Magi

rows.title: Rope
rows.cast: James Stewart, Farley Granger, John Dall
rows.extract: Rope is a 1948 American psychological crime thriller film directed by Alfred Hitchcock, based on the 1929 play of the same name by Patrick Hamilton. The film was adapted by Hume Cronyn with a screenplay by Arthur Laurents.

rows.title: Rusty Leads the Way
rows.cast: John Litel, Ann Doran
rows.extract: Rusty Leads the Way is a 1948 American drama film directed by Will Jason and starring Ted Donaldson, Sharyn Moffett and John Litel. It is part of the Rusty film series.

rows.title: Ruthless
rows.cast: Zachary Scott, Martha Vickers
rows.extract: Ruthless is a 1948 American drama film directed by Edgar G. Ulmer starring Zachary Scott, Sydney Greenstreet and Louis Hayward.

rows.title: Saigon
rows.cast: Alan Ladd, Veronica Lake
rows.extract: Saigon is a 1948 American crime film directed by Leslie Fenton starring Alan Ladd and Veronica Lake. In their fourth and final film together. It was distributed by Paramount Pictures and was one of the last films Veronica Lake made under her contract with the studio. Ladd and Lake made four films to

rows.title: The Sainted Sisters
rows.cast: Veronica Lake, Joan Caulfield, George Reeves
rows.extract: The Sainted Sisters is a 1948 American comedy film starring Veronica Lake and co-starring Joan Caulfield, Barry Fitzgerald, George Reeves, William Demarest and Beulah Bondi. The film was distributed by Paramount Pictures and is notable for being the last film Veronica Lake made under her contract wi

rows.title: The Saxon Charm
rows.cast: Robert Montgomery, Susan Hayward
rows.extract: The Saxon Charm is a 1948 American film noir drama film written and directed by Claude Binyon based on the novel of the same name by Frederic Wakeman Sr. and starring Robert Montgomery, Susan Hayward, John Payne and Audrey Totter.

rows.title: Scudda Hoo! Scudda Hay!
rows.cast: June Haver, Lon McCallister
rows.extract: Scudda Hoo! Scudda Hay! is a 1948 American romantic comedy-drama film written and directed by F. Hugh Herbert, based on the novel of the same name by George Agnew Chamberlain. Released by 20th Century Fox, the film stars June Haver, Lon McCallister, and Walter Brennan. Marilyn Monroe has a bit part

rows.title: Sealed Verdict
rows.cast: Ray Milland, Florence Marly, Broderick Crawford
rows.extract: Sealed Verdict is a 1948 American adventure drama war film directed by Lewis Allen and starring Ray Milland and Florence Marly.

rows.title: The Search
rows.cast: Montgomery Clift, Aline MacMahon
rows.extract: The Search is a 1948 American film directed by Fred Zinnemann that tells the story of a young Auschwitz survivor and his mother who search for each other across post-World War II Europe. It stars Montgomery Clift, Ivan Jandl, Jarmila Novotná and Aline MacMahon.

rows.title: Secret Beyond the Door
rows.cast: Joan Bennett, Michael Redgrave
rows.extract: Secret Beyond the Door is a 1947 American film noir psychological thriller and a modern updating of the Bluebeard fairytale, directed by Fritz Lang, produced by Lang's Diana Productions, and released by Universal Pictures. The film stars Joan Bennett and was produced by her husband Walter Wanger. Th

rows.title: Secret Service Investigator
rows.cast: Lloyd Bridges, Lynne Roberts
rows.extract: Secret Service Investigator is a 1948 American crime film directed by R. G. Springsteen and written by John K. Butler. The film stars Lynne Roberts, Lloyd Bridges, George Zucco, June Storey, Trevor Bardette and John Kellogg. The film was released on May 31, 1948 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Shaggy
rows.cast: Brenda Joyce, Robert Shayne
rows.extract: Shaggy is a 1948 American drama film directed by Robert Emmett Tansey, written by Maxwell Shane and filmed in Cinecolor. The film stars Brenda Joyce, Georgie Nokes, Robert Shayne, Jody Gilbert, Ralph Sanford and Alex Frazer. The film was released on June 11, 1948 by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: Shanghai Chest
rows.cast: Roland Winters, Mantan Moreland
rows.extract: Shanghai Chest is a 1948 American film directed by William Beaudine and featuring Roland Winters in his third appearance as Charlie Chan.

rows.title: Shed No Tears
rows.cast: June Vincent, Wallace Ford
rows.extract: Shed No Tears is a 1948 American film noir directed by Jean Yarbrough and starring Wallace Ford and June Vincent.

rows.title: Shep Comes Home
rows.cast: Robert Lowery, Margia Dean
rows.extract: Shep Comes Home is a 1948 American film written and directed by Ford Beebe for Lippert Pictures. It was a sequel to My Dog Shep (1946).

rows.title: The Sheriff of Medicine Bow
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton
rows.extract: The Sheriff of Medicine Bow is a 1948 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by J. Benton Cheney. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Max Terhune, Evelyn Finley, Bill Kennedy and George J. Lewis. The film was released on October 3, 1948, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: The Sign of the Ram
rows.cast: Susan Peters, Alexander Knox
rows.extract: The Sign of the Ram is a 1948 American film noir directed by John Sturges and screenplay by Charles Bennett, based on a novel written by Margaret Ferguson. The drama features Susan Peters, Alexander Knox and Phyllis Thaxter. It also featured Ron Randell. The film's title alludes to people born under

rows.title: Silent Conflict
rows.cast: William Boyd, Virginia Belmont
rows.extract: Silent Conflict is a 1948 American Western film directed by George Archainbaud and written by Charles Belden. The film stars William Boyd, Andy Clyde, Rand Brooks, Virginia Belmont, Earle Hodgins and James Harrison. It was released on March 19, 1948, by United Artists.

rows.title: Silver River
rows.cast: Errol Flynn, Ann Sheridan, Thomas Mitchell
rows.extract: Silver River is a 1948 Western film directed by Raoul Walsh and starring Errol Flynn and Ann Sheridan. The film is based on a Stephen Longstreet story that was turned into a novel.

rows.title: Silver Trails
rows.cast: Jimmy Wakely, Dub Taylor
rows.extract: Silver Trails is a 1948 American Western film, directed by Christy Cabanne. It stars Jimmy Wakely, Dub Taylor, and Christine Larson, and was released on August 28, 1948. The film starred Whip Wilson, who later went on to have a career as a famous Western film star.

rows.title: Singin' Spurs
rows.cast: Kirby Grant, Patricia Barry, Lee Patrick
rows.extract: Singin' Spurs is a 1948 American Western musical film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Barry Shipman. The film stars Kirby Grant, Patricia Barry, Lee Patrick, Jay Silverheels, Dick Elliott and William Wilkerson. The film was released on September 23, 1948, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Sinister Journey
rows.cast: William Boyd, Elaine Riley
rows.extract: Sinister Journey is a 1948 American Western film directed by George Archainbaud and written by Doris Schroeder. The film stars William Boyd, Andy Clyde, Rand Brooks, Elaine Riley, John Kellogg and Don Haggerty. The film was released on June 11, 1948, by United Artists.

rows.title: Sitting Pretty
rows.cast: Robert Young, Maureen O'Hara
rows.extract: Sitting Pretty is a 1948 American comedy film directed by Walter Lang from a screenplay by F. Hugh Herbert, adapted from the novel Belvedere by Gwen Davenport. The film stars Robert Young, Maureen O'Hara, and Clifton Webb, about a family who hires the mysterious Lynn Belvedere to babysit their rowdy

rows.title: Six-Gun Law
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Nancy Saunders
rows.extract: Six-Gun Law is a 1948 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Barry Shipman. The film stars Charles Starrett, Nancy Saunders, Paul Campbell, Hugh Prosser, Curly Clements and Smiley Burnette. The film was released on January 9, 1948, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Sixteen Fathoms Deep
rows.cast: Lloyd Bridges, Lon Chaney Jr.
rows.extract: Sixteen Fathoms Deep is a 1948 American adventure film directed by Irving Allen and starring Lloyd Bridges, Lon Chaney Jr. and Arthur Lake. It was a remake of the 1934 film of the same title in which Chaney had also starred.

rows.title: Sleep, My Love
rows.cast: Claudette Colbert, Don Ameche, Robert Cummings
rows.extract: Sleep, My Love is a 1948 American noir film directed by Douglas Sirk. It features Claudette Colbert, Robert Cummings and Don Ameche.

rows.title: Slippy McGee
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Dale Evans
rows.extract: Slippy McGee is a 1948 American crime film directed by Albert H. Kelley, written by Jerome Gruskin and Norman S. Hall, and starring Don "Red" Barry, Dale Evans, Tom Brown, Harry Cheshire, James Seay and Murray Alper. It was released on January 15, 1948 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Smart Girls Don't Talk
rows.cast: Virginia Mayo, Bruce Bennett
rows.extract: Smart Girls Don't Talk is a 1948 crime film directed by Richard L. Bare and starring Virginia Mayo and Bruce Bennett.

rows.title: Smart Politics
rows.cast: June Preisser, Frankie Darro, Noel Neill
rows.extract: Smart Politics is a 1948 American film directed by Will Jason and starring Freddie Stewart and June Preisser. It is part of The Teen Agers series made by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Smart Woman
rows.cast: Constance Bennett, Brian Aherne
rows.extract: Smart Woman is a 1948 romantic drama film directed by Edward A. Blatt and starring Brian Aherne, Constance Bennett, and Barry Sullivan.

rows.title: Smoky Mountain Melody
rows.cast: Roy Acuff, Russell Arms
rows.extract: Smoky Mountain Melody is a 1948 American musical Western film directed by Ray Nazarro, and starring Roy Acuff, Guinn 'Big Boy' Williams, Russell Arms, Sybil Merritt, Tommy Ivo, and Jason Robards Sr. The film was released by Columbia Pictures on December 16, 1948.

rows.title: Smugglers' Cove
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall, Amelita Ward
rows.extract: Smuggler's Cove is a 1948 comedy film starring The Bowery Boys. The film was released on October 10, 1948 by Monogram Pictures and is the eleventh film in the series.

rows.title: The Snake Pit
rows.cast: Olivia de Havilland, Leo Genn
rows.extract: The Snake Pit is a 1948 American psychological drama film directed by Anatole Litvak and starring Olivia de Havilland, Mark Stevens, Leo Genn, Celeste Holm, Beulah Bondi, and Lee Patrick. Based on Mary Jane Ward's 1946 semi-autobiographical novel of the same name, the film recounts the tale of a wom

rows.title: So Evil My Love
rows.cast: Ray Milland, Geraldine Fitzgerald
rows.extract: So Evil My Love is a 1948 British and American Gothic psychological thriller film directed by Lewis Allen and starring Ray Milland, Ann Todd and Geraldine Fitzgerald.

rows.title: So This Is New York
rows.cast: Henry Morgan, Rudy Vallee, Virginia Grey
rows.extract: So This Is New York is a 1948 satirical movie comedy starring acerbic radio and television comedian Henry Morgan and directed by Richard Fleischer. The cynically sophisticated screenplay was written by Carl Foreman and Herbert Baker from the 1920 novel The Big Town by Ring Lardner. Foreman was black

rows.title: Sofia
rows.cast: Patricia Morison, Sigrid Gurie
rows.extract: Sofia is a 1948 American thriller film directed by John Reinhardt and starring Gene Raymond, Sigrid Gurie and Patricia Morison. It is an early Cold War thriller set partly in the Bulgarian capital Sofia. The film was shot on location in Mexico and at the Estudios Churubusco in Mexico City Made in Ci

rows.title: Son of God's Country
rows.cast: Monte Hale, Pamela Blake
rows.extract: Son of God's Country is a 1948 American Western film directed by R. G. Springsteen and written by Paul Gangelin and Robert Creighton Williams. The film stars Monte Hale, Pamela Blake, Paul Hurst, James Nolan, Jay Kirby and Steve Darrell. The film was released on September 15, 1948, by Republic Pictu

rows.title: A Song Is Born
rows.cast: Danny Kaye, Virginia Mayo, Tommy Dorsey, Benny Goodman
rows.extract: A Song Is Born, starring Danny Kaye and Virginia Mayo, is a 1948 Technicolor musical film remake of Howard Hawks' 1941 movie Ball of Fire with Gary Cooper and Barbara Stanwyck. rows.title: Song of the Drifter
rows.cast: Jimmy Wakely, Dub Taylor, Mildred Coles
rows.extract: Song of the Drifter is a 1948 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by Frank H. Young. The film stars Jimmy Wakely, Dub Taylor, Mildred Coles, William Ruhl, Marshall Reed and Patsy Moran. The film was released on January 17, 1948, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Song of Idaho
rows.cast: Kirby Grant, June Vincent
rows.extract: Song of Idaho is a 1948 American Western musical film directed by Ray Nazarro. It was released by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Song of My Heart
rows.cast: Audrey Long, Cedric Hardwicke
rows.extract: Song of My Heart is a 1948 American historical drama film directed by Benjamin Glazer and starring Frank Sundström, Audrey Long and Cedric Hardwicke. It is a highly fictionalised biopic of the nineteenth century Russian composer Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky. It was distributed by Allied Artists.

rows.title: Sons of Adventure
rows.cast: Lynne Roberts, Russell Hayden
rows.extract: Sons of Adventure is a 1948 American Western film directed by Yakima Canutt, written by Franklin Adreon and Sol Shor, and starring Lynne Roberts, Russell Hayden, Gordon Jones, Grant Withers, George Chandler and Roy Barcroft. It was released on September 1, 1948 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Sorry, Wrong Number
rows.cast: Barbara Stanwyck, Burt Lancaster
rows.extract: Sorry, Wrong Number is a 1948 American thriller film noir directed by Anatole Litvak, from a screenplay by Lucille Fletcher, based on her 1943 radio play of the same name. The film stars Barbara Stanwyck and Burt Lancaster. It follows a bedridden woman, who overhears the plot of murder. While on the

rows.title: A Southern Yankee
rows.cast: Red Skelton, Arlene Dahl
rows.extract: A Southern Yankee is a 1948 American comedy western film directed by Edward Sedgwick and starring Red Skelton, Brian Donlevy and Arlene Dahl.

rows.title: Speed to Spare
rows.cast: Richard Arlen, Jean Rogers
rows.extract: Speed to Spare is a 1948 American drama film directed by William Berke, written by Milton Raison, and starring Richard Arlen, Jean Rogers, Richard Travis, Roscoe Karns, Nanette Parks and Pat Phelan. It was released on May 14, 1948, by Paramount Pictures. It is unrelated to the same-titled auto-racin

rows.title: Stage Struck
rows.cast: Conrad Nagel, Kane Richmond
rows.extract: Stage Struck is a 1948 American crime film directed by William Nigh and starring Kane Richmond, Audrey Long and Conrad Nagel.

rows.title: State of the Union
rows.cast: Spencer Tracy, Katharine Hepburn
rows.extract: State of the Union is a 1948 drama film directed by Frank Capra about a man’s desire to run for the nomination as the Republican candidate for President, and the machinations of those around him. The New York Times described it as "a slick piece of screen satire...sharper in its knife-edged slicing

rows.title: Station West
rows.cast: Dick Powell, Jane Greer
rows.extract: Station West is a 1948 American Western black-and-white film directed by Sidney Lanfield and based on a Western novel by Luke Short. Burl Ives plays a small role and sings the following songs on the soundtrack: "A Stranger in Town," "The Sun's Shining Warm," and "A Man Can't Grow Old."

rows.title: Strange Gamble
rows.cast: William Boyd, Elaine Riley
rows.extract: Strange Gamble is a 1948 American Western film directed by George Archainbaud, written by Doris Schroeder, Bennett Cohen and Ande Lamb, and starring William Boyd, Andy Clyde, Rand Brooks, Elaine Riley, James Craven and Robert Williams. It was released on October 8, 1948, by United Artists.

rows.title: The Strange Mrs. Crane
rows.cast: Marjorie Lord, Robert Shayne
rows.extract: The Strange Mrs. Crane is a 1948 American film noir directed by Sam Newfield for Eagle-Lion Films.

rows.title: The Strawberry Roan
rows.cast: Gene Autry, Gloria Henry
rows.extract: The Strawberry Roan is a 1948 American Western film directed by John English and starring Gene Autry.

rows.title: Street Corner
rows.cast: Johnny Duncan, Eddie Gribbon
rows.extract: Street Corner is a 1948 American exploitation film directed by Albert H. Kelley, produced by Wilshire Pictures, and featuring Johnny Duncan, Eddie Gribbon, and Marcia Mae Jones. It was released on DVD in 2003 by Something Weird Video.

rows.title: The Street with No Name
rows.cast: Mark Stevens, Richard Widmark, Lloyd Nolan
rows.extract: The Street with No Name is a 1948 film noir directed by William Keighley. A follow-up to The House on 92nd Street (1945), it tells the story of an undercover FBI agent, Gene Cordell, who infiltrates a deadly crime gang. Cordell's superior, FBI Inspector George A. Briggs, also appears in The House on

rows.title: Strike It Rich
rows.cast: Rod Cameron, Bonita Granville
rows.extract: Strike It Rich is a 1948 American comedy film directed by Lesley Selander and starring Rod Cameron, Bonita Granville and Don Castle.

rows.title: Summer Holiday
rows.cast: Mickey Rooney, Gloria DeHaven
rows.extract: Summer Holiday is a 1948 American musical-comedy film, directed by Rouben Mamoulian and starring Mickey Rooney and Gloria DeHaven. The picture is based on the play Ah, Wilderness! (1933) by Eugene O'Neill, which had been filmed under that name by MGM in 1935 with Rooney in a much smaller role, as th

rows.title: Sundown in Santa Fe
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Eddy Waller
rows.extract: Sundown in Santa Fe is a 1948 American Western film directed by R. G. Springsteen, written by Norman S. Hall, and starring Allan Lane, Eddy Waller, Roy Barcroft, Trevor Bardette, Jean Dean and Russell Simpson. It was released on November 5, 1948 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Sunset Carson Rides Again
rows.cast: Sunset Carson, Dan White
rows.extract: Sunset Carson Rides Again is a 1948 American Western film produced and directed by Oliver Drake and shot on his own ranch. rows.title: Sword of the Avenger
rows.cast: Sigrid Gurie
rows.extract: Sword of the Avenger is a 1948 American adventure film directed by Sidney Salkow and starring Ramon del Gado, Sigrid Gurie, and Ralph Morgan.

rows.title: The Swordsman
rows.cast: Larry Parks, Ellen Drew
rows.extract: The Swordsman is a 1948 American swashbuckler film directed by Joseph H. Lewis and starring Larry Parks, Ellen Drew and George Macready. It was produced and distributed by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Tap Roots
rows.cast: Van Heflin, Susan Hayward
rows.extract: Tap Roots is a 1948 Technicolor Western war film set during the American Civil War. It is very loosely based on the true life story of Newton Knight, a farm owner who attempted to secede Jones County from Mississippi.

rows.title: Tarzan and the Mermaids
rows.cast: Johnny Weissmuller, Brenda Joyce, Linda Christian, Andrea Palma
rows.extract: Tarzan and the Mermaids is a 1948 adventure film based on the Tarzan character created by Edgar Rice Burroughs. Directed by Robert Florey, it was the last of twelve Tarzan films to star Johnny Weissmuller in the title role. It was also the first Tarzan film since 1939 not to feature the character Bo

rows.title: The Tender Years
rows.cast: Joe E. Brown, Noreen Nash
rows.extract: The Tender Years is a 1948 American drama film directed by Harold D. Schuster, written by Arnold Belgard, Abem Finkel and Jack Jungmeyer, and starring Joe E. Brown, Richard Lyon, Noreen Nash, Charles Drake, Josephine Hutchinson and James Millican. It was released on January 3, 1948, by 20th Century

rows.title: Tenth Avenue Angel
rows.cast: Margaret O'Brien, Angela Lansbury
rows.extract: Tenth Avenue Angel is a 1948 American film directed by Roy Rowland and starring Margaret O'Brien, Angela Lansbury, and George Murphy. rows.title: Texas, Brooklyn & Heaven
rows.cast: Diana Lynn, Guy Madison
rows.extract: Texas, Brooklyn & Heaven is a 1948 American black-and-white romantic comedy film directed by William Castle and starring Guy Madison, Diana Lynn, James Dunn, and Florence Bates. A reporter in Dallas, Texas, goes to New York with the dream of becoming a playwright. En route, he picks up a hitchhiker

rows.title: That Lady in Ermine
rows.cast: Betty Grable, Douglas Fairbanks Jr.
rows.extract: That Lady in Ermine is a 1948 American Technicolor musical film directed by Ernst Lubitsch. The screenplay by Samson Raphaelson is based on the 1919 operetta Die Frau im Hermelin by Rudolph Schanzer and Ernst Welisch.

rows.title: That Wonderful Urge
rows.cast: Tyrone Power, Gene Tierney
rows.extract: That Wonderful Urge is a 1948 20th Century Fox screwball comedy film directed by Robert B. Sinclair and starring Tyrone Power and Gene Tierney. It is a remake of Love Is News (1937), which stars Power and Loretta Young.

rows.title: They Live by Night
rows.cast: Cathy O'Donnell, Farley Granger
rows.extract: They Live by Night is a 1948 American film noir directed by Nicholas Ray, in his directorial debut, and starring Cathy O'Donnell and Farley Granger. Based on Edward Anderson's Depression-era novel Thieves Like Us, the film follows a young convict on the run who falls in love with a woman and attempt

rows.title: Three Daring Daughters
rows.cast: Jeanette MacDonald, Jane Powell
rows.extract: Three Daring Daughters is a 1948 musical Technicolor film directed by Fred M. Wilcox and released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. The screenplay was written by Albert Mannheimer, Frederick Kohner, Sonya Levien and John Meehan.

rows.title: The Three Musketeers
rows.cast: Gene Kelly, Van Heflin, Lana Turner, June Allyson, Angela Lansbury
rows.extract: The Three Musketeers is a 1948 film directed by George Sidney, written by Robert Ardrey, and starring Gene Kelly and Lana Turner. It is a Technicolor adventure film adaptation of the classic 1844 novel The Three Musketeers by Alexandre Dumas.

rows.title: Thunder in the Pines
rows.cast: George Reeves, Ralph Byrd
rows.extract: Thunder in the Pines is a 1948 American Western film directed by Robert Edwards and starring George Reeves and Ralph Byrd. The film was shot in sepia tone. It was executive produced by Robert L. Lippert.

rows.title: Thunderhoof
rows.cast: Preston Foster, Mary Stuart
rows.extract: Thunderhoof is a 1948 American Western film directed by Phil Karlson and starring Preston Foster, Mary Stuart and William Bishop. The film's sets were designed by the art director Walter Holscher.

rows.title: The Tioga Kid
rows.cast: Eddie Dean, Roscoe Ates, Jennifer Holt
rows.extract: The Tioga Kid is a 1948 American Western film directed by Ray Taylor and written by Ed Earl Repp. The film stars Eddie Dean, Roscoe Ates, Jennifer Holt, Dennis Moore, Lee Bennett and William Fawcett. The film was released on June 17, 1948, by Eagle-Lion Films.

rows.title: The Timber Trail
rows.cast: Monte Hale, Lynne Roberts
rows.extract: The Timber Trail is a 1948 American Western film directed by Philip Ford, written by Robert Creighton Williams, and starring Monte Hale, Lynne Roberts, James Burke, Roy Barcroft, Francis Ford, and Robert Emmett Keane. It was released on June 15, 1948, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Time of Your Life
rows.cast: James Cagney, William Bendix, Wayne Morris, Jeanne Cagney
rows.extract: The Time of Your Life is a 1948 American comedy drama film directed by H. C. Potter and starring James Cagney, William Bendix, Wayne Morris and Jeanne Cagney. rows.title: To the Ends of the Earth
rows.cast: Dick Powell, Signe Hasso
rows.extract: To the Ends of the Earth is a 1948 American crime film directed by Robert Stevenson and starring Dick Powell and Signe Hasso.

rows.title: To the Victor
rows.cast: Dennis Morgan, Viveca Lindfors
rows.extract: To the Victor is a 1948 drama film directed by Delmer Daves and starring Dennis Morgan and Viveca Lindfors. The plot concerns an American black-marketeer who falls in love with a Nazi collaborator's wife in post-World War II Paris.

rows.title: Tornado Range
rows.cast: Eddie Dean, Roscoe Ates, Jennifer Holt
rows.extract: Tornado Range is a 1948 American Western film directed by Ray Taylor and written by William Lively. The film stars Eddie Dean, Roscoe Ates, Jennifer Holt, George Chesebro, Buster Slaven and Marshall Reed. The film was released on February 21, 1948, by Eagle-Lion Films.

rows.title: Trail to Laredo
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette
rows.extract: Trail to Laredo is a 1948 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Barry Shipman. The film stars Charles Starrett, Jim Bannon, Virginia Maxey, Tommy Ivo, Hugh Prosser and Smiley Burnette. The film was released on August 12, 1948, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Train to Alcatraz
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Janet Martin
rows.extract: Train to Alcatraz is a 1948 American prison film directed by Philip Ford and starring Don Barry, Janet Martin, William Phipps, Roy Barcroft, and June Storey.

rows.title: Trapped by Boston Blackie
rows.cast: Charles Marion, June Vincent
rows.extract: Trapped by Boston Blackie is a 1948 American crime drama directed by Seymour Friedman. It is the thirteenth of fourteen Columbia Pictures films starring Chester Morris as reformed crook Boston Blackie, and the final film with George E. Stone as "The Runt".

rows.title: The Treasure of the Sierra Madre
rows.cast: Humphrey Bogart, Walter Huston, Tim Holt, Bruce Bennett
rows.extract:
The Treasure of the Sierra Madre is a 1948 American Western film written and directed by John Huston. It is an adaptation of B. Traven's 1927 novel of the same name, set in 1925, and follows two downtrodden men who join forces with a grizzled old prospector
(Walter Huston, the director's father), in

rows.title: Triggerman
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton, Virginia Carroll
rows.extract: Triggerman is a 1948 American Western film written by Howard Bretherton, from a screenplay by Ronald Davidson. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown and Raymond Hatton.

rows.title: Triple Threat
rows.cast: Gloria Henry, Mary Stuart
rows.extract: Triple Threat is a 1948 American drama sport film directed by Jean Yarbrough, produced by Sam Katzman, and starring Gloria Henry.

rows.title: Trouble Makers
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall, Helen Parrish
rows.extract: Trouble Makers is a 1948 comedy film directed by Reginald LeBorg and starring The Bowery Boys. rows.title: Trouble Preferred
rows.cast: Peggy Knudsen, Lynne Roberts
rows.extract: Trouble Preferred is a 1948 American thriller film directed by James Tinling, written by Arnold Belgard, and starring Peggy Knudsen, Lynne Roberts, Charles Russell, Paul Langton, Marcia Mae Jones and Mary Bear. It was released on December 31, 1948, by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Two Guys from Texas
rows.cast: Dennis Morgan, Jack Carson
rows.extract: Two Guys from Texas is a 1948 American comedy musical western film directed by David Butler, and starring Dennis Morgan, Jack Carson and Dorothy Malone. The film was written by Allen Boretz and I.A.L. Diamond, produced by Alex Gottlieb, and released by Warner Bros. Pictures on September 4, 1948. Thi

rows.title: Under California Stars
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Jane Frazee
rows.extract: Under California Stars  is a 1948 American Trucolor Western film directed by William Witney and starring Roy Rogers, Jane Frazee and Andy Devine. The film was shot in Trucolor. After returning from Hollywood after his tenth anniversary in films to his ranch, Rogers tackles a gang who kidnap his hor

rows.title: Unfaithfully Yours
rows.cast: Rex Harrison, Linda Darnell, Rudy Vallée, Barbara Lawrence
rows.extract: Unfaithfully Yours is a 1948 American screwball black comedy film written and directed by Preston Sturges, and starring Rex Harrison, Linda Darnell, Rudy Vallée and Barbara Lawrence. The film is about a jealous symphony conductor who imagines three different ways to deal with the supposed infidelity

rows.title: Unknown Island
rows.cast: Virginia Grey, Richard Denning
rows.extract: Unknown Island is a 1948 American adventure film directed by Jack Bernhard and starring Virginia Grey, Phillip Reed and Richard Denning. Shot in Cinecolor it was released by Film Classics and in Britain by General Film Distributors.

rows.title: The Untamed Breed
rows.cast: Sonny Tufts, Barbara Britton
rows.extract: The Untamed Breed is a 1948 American Western film directed by Charles Lamont and starring Sonny Tufts, Barbara Britton and George 'Gabby' Hayes.

rows.title: Up in Central Park
rows.cast: Deanna Durbin, Dick Haymes, Vincent Price
rows.extract: Up in Central Park is a 1948 American musical comedy film directed by William A. Seiter and starring Deanna Durbin, Dick Haymes and Vincent Price. rows.title: The Velvet Touch
rows.cast: Rosalind Russell, Leo Genn, Claire Trevor
rows.extract: The Velvet Touch is a 1948 American film noir drama directed by Jack Gage and starring Rosalind Russell, Leon Ames, Leo Genn and Claire Trevor.

rows.title: The Vicious Circle
rows.cast: Conrad Nagel, Fritz Kortner
rows.extract: The Vicious Circle is a 1948 American drama film directed by W. Lee Wilder and based on the play The Burning Bush by Heinz Herald and Geza Herczeg. The film is also known as The Woman in Brown.

rows.title: Wake of the Red Witch
rows.cast: John Wayne, Gail Russell
rows.extract: Wake of the Red Witch is a 1948 American adventure film directed by Edward Ludwig, produced by Edmund Grainger and starring John Wayne, Gail Russell, Gig Young, Adele Mara and Luther Adler. rows.title: Walk a Crooked Mile
rows.cast: Dennis O'Keefe, Louis Hayward
rows.extract: Walk a Crooked Mile is a 1948 America anti-communist, Cold War film noir crime film, directed by Gordon Douglas, starring Dennis O'Keefe and Louis Hayward.

rows.title: Wallflower
rows.cast: Joyce Reynolds, Janis Paige
rows.extract: Wallflower is a 1948 American comedy film directed by Frederick de Cordova, written by Henry Ephron and Phoebe Ephron adapted from the play of the same name by Reginald Denham and Mary Orr, and starring Robert Hutton, Joyce Reynolds, Janis Paige, Edward Arnold, Barbara Brown and Jerome Cowan. rows.title: The Walls of Jericho

Stahl, written by Lamar Trotti, and starring Cornel Wilde, Linda Darnell, Anne Baxter, Kirk Douglas, Ann Dvorak, Colleen Townsend and Marjorie Rambeau. rows.title: Waterfront at Midnight
rows.cast: Mary Beth Hughes, William Gargan
rows.extract: Waterfront at Midnight is a 1948 American film noir crime film directed by William Berke, written by Bernard Girard and starring William Gargan, Mary Beth Hughes, Richard Travis, Richard Crane, Cheryl Walker and Horace McMahon. It was released on June 25, 1948 by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: West of Sonora
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette
rows.extract: West of Sonora is a 1948 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Barry Shipman. The film stars Charles Starrett, Steve Darrell, George Chesebro, Anita Castle and Smiley Burnette. The film was released on March 25, 1948, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Western Heritage
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Richard Martin, Lois Andrews
rows.extract: Western Heritage is a 1948 American Western film directed by Wallace Grissell. The film is a Tim Holt B Western about land robbers and forgers in the southwest.

rows.title: The Westward Trail
rows.cast: Eddie Dean, Roscoe Ates
rows.extract: The Westward Trail is a 1948 American Western film directed by Ray Taylor and written by Robert Alan Miller. The film stars Eddie Dean, Roscoe Ates, Phyllis Planchard, Eileene Hardin, Steve Drake and Bob Duncan. The film was released on March 13, 1948, by Producers Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: When My Baby Smiles at Me
rows.cast: Betty Grable, Dan Dailey, Jack Oakie, June Havoc
rows.extract: When My Baby Smiles at Me is a 1948 musical film directed by Walter Lang and starring Betty Grable and Dan Dailey. rows.title: Whiplash
rows.cast: Dane Clark, Zachary Scott, Eve Arden
rows.extract: Whiplash is a 1948 American film noir directed by Lewis Seiler and written by Kenneth Earl, Harriet Frank Jr., Maurice Geraghty and Gordon Kahn. The film stars Dane Clark, Alexis Smith, Zachary Scott and Eve Arden.

rows.title: Whirlwind Raiders
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Nancy Saunders
rows.extract: Whirlwind Raiders is a 1948 American Western film directed by Vernon Keays and written by Norman S. Hall. The film stars Charles Starrett, Don Reynolds, Nancy Saunders, Fred F. Sears, Doye O'Dell and Smiley Burnette. The film was released on May 13, 1948, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Whispering Smith
rows.cast: Alan Ladd, Robert Preston, Brenda Marshall
rows.extract: Whispering Smith is a 1948 American Western film directed by Leslie Fenton and starring Alan Ladd as a railroad detective assigned to stop a gang of train robbers. The supporting cast includes Robert Preston, Brenda Marshall and Donald Crisp.

rows.title: Who Killed Doc Robbin
rows.cast: Larry Casey, Virginia Grey
rows.extract: Who Killed Doc Robbin is a 1948 film directed by Bernard Carr and starring Larry Olsen, Billy Gray, and Renee Beard. It was produced by Hal Roach and Robert F. McGowan as a reimagining of their Our Gang series.

rows.title: The Winner's Circle
rows.cast: Jean Willes, Morgan Farley
rows.extract: The Winner's Circle is a 1948 American drama film directed by Felix E. Feist and written by Howard J. Green and Leonard Praskins. The film stars Jean Willes, Morgan Farley, Johnny Longden, Robert S. Howard, William Gould and John Beradino. It was released on June 8, 1948 by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Winter Meeting
rows.cast: Bette Davis, Janis Paige
rows.extract: Winter Meeting is a 1948 American drama film directed by Bretaigne Windust and starring Bette Davis and Jim Davis. The screenplay, based on the novel of the same name by Grace Zaring Stone, was written by Catherine Turney.

rows.title: A Woman's Vengeance
rows.cast: Charles Boyer, Ann Blyth, Jessica Tandy
rows.extract: A Woman's Vengeance is a 1948 American film noir drama mystery film directed by Zoltán Korda and starring Charles Boyer, Ann Blyth, Jessica Tandy, Cedric Hardwicke, Rachel Kempson, and Mildred Natwick. rows.title: The Woman from Tangier
rows.cast: Adele Jergens, Stephen Dunne
rows.extract: The Woman from Tangier is a 1948 American crime film directed by Harold Daniels and starring Adele Jergens, Stephen Dunne and Ian MacDonald. It was one of a number of Hollywood films set in Tangier during the International Zone era. The film's art direction was by Walter Holscher.

rows.title: The Woman in White
rows.cast: Alexis Smith, Eleanor Parker, Sydney Greenstreet
rows.extract: The Woman in White is a 1948 drama film directed by Peter Godfrey which stars Alexis Smith, Eleanor Parker, Sydney Greenstreet, and Gig Young. The screenplay is based on Wilkie Collins' 1860 novel The Woman in White.

rows.title: Women in the Night
rows.cast: Tala Birell, Bernadene Hayes
rows.extract: Women in the Night is a 1948 American film directed by William Rowland shot in Mexico. The film is also known as When Men Are Beasts. The film depicts activities of German and Japanese who wish revenge on the Allies with a cosmic ray weapon.

rows.title: Words and Music
rows.cast: Mickey Rooney, Janet Leigh, Betty Garrett, June Allyson, Gene Kelly
rows.extract: Words and Music is a 1948 American biographical musical film loosely based on the creative partnership of the composer Richard Rodgers and lyricist Lorenz Hart. rows.cast: Patricia Barry, Willard Parker

It was produced by silent film actor Wallace MacDonald in association with Columbia Pictures, which also distributed the film. It is preserved in the L

rows.title: Yellow Sky
rows.cast: Gregory Peck, Richard Widmark, Anne Baxter
rows.extract: Yellow Sky is a 1948 American Western film directed by William A. Wellman and starring Gregory Peck, Richard Widmark, and Anne Baxter. rows.title: You Gotta Stay Happy
rows.cast: Joan Fontaine, James Stewart, Eddie Albert
rows.extract: You Gotta Stay Happy is a 1948 American romantic comedy film directed by H.C. Potter and starring Joan Fontaine, James Stewart and Eddie Albert. rows.title: You Were Meant for Me
rows.cast: Dan Dailey, Jeanne Crain
rows.extract: You Were Meant for Me is a 1948 musical film directed by Lloyd Bacon and starring Dan Dailey and Jeanne Crain as a bandleader and his wife. It was released by 20th Century Fox. The film includes performances of "You Were Meant for Me", "I'll Get By ", and "Ain't Misbehavin'".

rows.extract: Louisiana Story is a 1948 American black-and-white drama film directed by Robert J. Flaherty. rows.cast: Clayton Moore, Noel Neill
rows.extract: Adventures of Frank and Jesse James is a 1948 Republic film serial directed by Fred C. Brannon and Yakima Canutt and starring Clayton Moore, Steve Darrell, Noel Neill, George J. Lewis, John Crawford, and Sam Flint.

rows.title: Congo Bill
rows.cast: Don McGuire, Cleo Moore
rows.extract: Congo Bill (1948) is a Columbia movie serial based on the DC Comics character Congo Bill, later named Congorilla.

rows.extract: Dangers of the Canadian Mounted is a 1948 Northern Republic film serial.

rows.title: G-Men Never Forget
rows.cast: Clayton Moore
rows.extract: G-Men Never Forget is a 1948 Republic movie serial. The serial was condensed into a feature film in 1966 and re-released under the title Code 645.

rows.cast: Kirk Alyn, Noel Neill
rows.extract: Superman is a 1948 15-part Columbia Pictures film serial based on the comic book character Superman. It stars an uncredited Kirk Alyn and Noel Neill as Lois Lane. rows.extract: Bill and Coo is a 1948 film directed by Dean Riesner, filmed in Trucolor, and conceived to showcase George Burton's trained birds.

rows.extract: Bob and Sally is 1948 American drama film produced by J. G. Sanford at Universal Studios and directed by Erle C. Kenton. Director of photography was Ellis Carter and the original screenplay was written by Mary C. Palmer.

rows.cast: Bugs Bunny

rows.extract: Bugs Bunny Rides Again is a 1948 Merrie Melodies animated short directed by Friz Freleng. The short was released on June 12, 1948, and stars Bugs Bunny and Yosemite Sam.

rows.title: The Chicken of Tomorrow
rows.cast: Lowell Thomas
rows.extract: The Chicken of Tomorrow is a 1948 documentary short film about advances in chicken farming. This mini-documentary was narrated by Lowell Thomas and is in the public domain. The film was sponsored by Texaco.

rows.title: A Feather in His Hare
rows.extract: A Feather in His Hare is a 1948 produced Warner Brothers Looney Tunes animated short, directed by Chuck Jones. It was originally released on February 7, 1948. The title is yet another pun on "hair".

rows.title: Fiddlers Three
rows.cast: The Three Stooges
rows.extract: Fiddlers Three is a 1948 short subject directed by Jules White starring American slapstick comedy team The Three Stooges. It is the 107th entry in the series released by Columbia Pictures starring the comedians, who released 190 shorts for the studio between 1934 and 1959.

rows.title: Gorilla My Dreams
rows.cast: Looney Tunes
rows.extract: Gorilla My Dreams is a Warner Bros. Looney Tunes theatrical animated short directed by Robert McKimson and written by Warren Foster. The short was released on January 3, 1948, and stars Bugs Bunny.

rows.title: Haredevil Hare
rows.cast: Looney Tunes
rows.extract: Haredevil Hare is a 1948 Looney Tunes cartoon directed by Chuck Jones. It stars Bugs Bunny and it is the debut for Marvin the Martian — although he is unnamed in this film—along with his Martian dog, K-9. Marvin's nasal voice for this first film is different from the later one he is most known for.

rows.cast: Looney Tunes
rows.extract: Hop, Look and Listen is a 1948 Warner Bros. Looney Tunes cartoon directed by Robert McKimson. The short was released on April 17, 1948, and stars Sylvester and Hippety Hopper, in the latter's first appearance.

rows.title: Hot Cross Bunny
rows.cast: Bugs Bunny
rows.extract: Hot Cross Bunny is a 1948 Warner Bros. Merrie Melodies theatrical animated short. The short was released on August 21, 1948, and features Bugs Bunny. The title is a play on the nursery rhyme Hot Cross Buns as well as a punny allusion to the basic plot premise.

rows.cast: Donald Duck
rows.extract: Three for Breakfast is a 1948 American animated short film directed by Jack Hannah. Part of the Donald Duck film series, the film was produced in Technicolor by Walt Disney Productions and released to theaters by RKO Radio Pictures on November 5, 1948.

rows.title: Any Number Can Play
rows.cast: Clark Gable, Alexis Smith, Wendell Corey, Mary Astor
rows.extract: Any Number Can Play is a 1949 drama film directed by Mervyn LeRoy. It is based on Edward Harris Heth's novel of the same name. It stars Clark Gable and Alexis Smith.

rows.title: Arctic Manhunt
rows.cast: Mikel Conrad, Carol Thurston
rows.extract: Arctic Manhunt is a 1949 American adventure film directed by Ewing Scott and starring Mikel Conrad, Carol Thurston and Wally Cassell.

rows.title: Arson, Inc.
rows.cast: Robert Lowery, Anne Gwynne
rows.extract: Arson, Inc. is a 1949 American film noir directed by William Berke. It is also known as Firebug Squad and Three Alarm Fire.

rows.title: Bad Boy
rows.cast: Audie Murphy, Jane Wyatt
rows.extract: Bad Boy is a 1949 American drama film directed by Kurt Neumann and starring Audie Murphy, Lloyd Nolan and Jane Wyatt. It was Murphy's first leading role. It was distributed by the independent studio Allied Artists.

rows.title: Bad Men of Tombstone

rows.extract: Bad Men of Tombstone is a 1949 American Western film from King Brothers Productions. It was co-written by Philip Yordan and stars Barry Sullivan and Broderick Crawford. King Brothers announced plans for a sequel, The Marshall of Tombstone but it was never made.

rows.cast: Allan Lane, Helene Stanley
rows.extract: Bandit King of Texas is a 1949 American Western film directed by Fred C. Brannon and written by Olive Cooper. The film stars Allan Lane, Eddy Waller, Helene Stanley, James Nolan, Harry Lauter and Robert Bice. The film was released on August 29, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Bandits of El Dorado
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Clayton Moore
rows.extract: Bandits of El Dorado is a 1949 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Barry Shipman. The film stars Charles Starrett, George J. Lewis, Fred F. Sears, John Dehner, Clayton Moore and Smiley Burnette. The film was released on October 20, 1949, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Barbary Pirate
rows.cast: Donald Woods, Trudy Marshall, Lenore Aubert
rows.extract: Barbary Pirate is a 1949 American adventure film directed by Lew Landers and starring Donald Woods and Trudy Marshall.

rows.title: The Barkleys of Broadway
rows.cast: Fred Astaire, Ginger Rogers, Billie Burke
rows.extract: The Barkleys of Broadway is a 1949 American Technicolor musical comedy film from the Arthur Freed unit at Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer that reunited Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers after ten years apart. rows.title: The Beautiful Blonde from Bashful Bend

rows.extract: Big Jack is a 1949 American Western film starring Wallace Beery, Richard Conte and Marjorie Main. rows.extract: The Big Sombrero is a 1949 American Western film directed by Frank McDonald and starring Gene Autry and Champion. rows.title: The Big Steal
