rows.cast: Roddy McDowall, Damian O'Flynn, Lyn Thomas
rows.extract: Black Midnight is a 1949 American Western film directed by Budd Boetticher and starring Roddy McDowall, Damian O'Flynn, and Lyn Thomas.

rows.title: The Blazing Trail
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Marjorie Stapp
rows.extract: The Blazing Trail, known in the United Kingdom as The Forged Will, is a 1949 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and starring Charles Starrett.

rows.title: The Blonde Bandit
rows.cast: Dorothy Patrick, Gerald Mohr
rows.extract: The Blonde Bandit is a 1949 American crime film directed by Harry Keller and written by John K. Butler. The film stars Gerald Mohr, Dorothy Patrick, Robert Rockwell, Charles Cane, Larry J. Blake and Argentina Brunetti. The film was released on December 22, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Blondie's Big Deal
rows.cast: Penny Singleton, Arthur Lake
rows.extract: Blondie's Big Deal is a 1949 American comedy film directed by Edward Bernds and starring Penny Singleton, Arthur Lake, Larry Simms, Marjorie Ann Mutchie. It is the twenty-fifth of the 28 Blondie films.

rows.title: Blondie Hits the Jackpot
rows.cast: Penny Singleton, Arthur Lake
rows.extract: Blondie Hits the Jackpot is a 1949 American comedy film directed by Edward Bernds and starring Penny Singleton, Arthur Lake, Larry Simms, and Marjorie Ann Mutchie. It is the 26th of the 28 Blondie films.

rows.title: Bodyhold
rows.cast: Willard Parker, Lola Albright, Hillary Brooke
rows.extract: Bodyhold is a 1949 American crime film noir sport film directed by Seymour Friedman and starring Willard Parker, Lola Albright, and Hillary Brooke.

rows.title: Bomba, the Jungle Boy
rows.cast: Johnny Sheffield, Peggy Ann Garner
rows.extract: Bomba, the Jungle Boy is a 1949 American adventure film directed by Ford Beebe. It was the first in a 12-film series featuring Bomba, a sort of teenage Tarzan, played by Johnny Sheffield, who as a child had played "Boy" in several previous Tarzan films.

rows.title: Bomba on Panther Island
rows.cast: Johnny Sheffield, Allene Roberts
rows.extract: Bomba on Panther Island is a 1949 American adventure film directed by Ford Beebe and starring Johnny Sheffield. It is the second in the 12-film Bomba series following Bomba the Jungle Boy (1949).

rows.title: Border Incident
rows.cast: Ricardo Montalbán, Howard Da Silva
rows.extract: Border Incident is a 1949 film noir featuring Ricardo Montalbán, George Murphy, Howard Da Silva. Directed by Anthony Mann, the MGM production was written by John C. Higgins and George Zuckerman. The film was shot by cinematographer John Alton, who used shadows and lighting effects to involve an audi

rows.title: Boston Blackie's Chinese Venture
rows.cast: Chester Morris, Maylia Fong
rows.extract: Boston Blackie's Chinese Venture is a 1949 mystery film directed by Seymour Friedman, starring Chester Morris. This was the last of Columbia's 14 Boston Blackie pictures (1941–49). Richard Lane, as long-suffering Inspector Farraday, was the only other character who appeared in all of the Boston Blac

rows.title: Brand of Fear
rows.cast: Jimmy Wakely, Gail Davis
rows.extract: Brand of Fear is a 1949 American Western film directed by Oliver Drake and written by Basil Dickey. The film stars Jimmy Wakely, Dub Taylor, Tom London, Gail Davis, Marshall Reed and William Ruhl. The film was released on July 10, 1949, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: The Bribe
rows.cast: Robert Taylor, Ava Gardner, Charles Laughton, Vincent Price
rows.extract: The Bribe is a 1949 American film noir directed by Robert Z. Leonard and written by Marguerite Roberts, based on a story written by Frederick Nebel. The drama features Robert Taylor, Ava Gardner, Charles Laughton, and Vincent Price.

rows.title: Bride for Sale
rows.cast: Claudette Colbert, Robert Young
rows.extract: Bride for Sale is a 1949 American romantic comedy film distributed by RKO Radio Pictures, directed by William D. Russell, and starring Claudette Colbert, Robert Young and George Brent. The music score is by Frederick Hollander.

rows.title: Bride of Vengeance
rows.cast: Paulette Goddard, John Lund
rows.extract: Bride of Vengeance is a 1949 adventure film set in the Italian Renaissance era, directed by Mitchell Leisen.

rows.title: Brimstone
rows.cast: Rod Cameron, Walter Brennan, Lorna Gray
rows.extract: Brimstone is a 1949 American Trucolor Western film directed by Joseph Kane and written by Thames Williamson. The film stars Rod Cameron, Lorna Gray, Walter Brennan, Forrest Tucker, Jack Holt and Jim Davis. The film was released on August 15, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Brothers in the Saddle
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Richard Martin
rows.extract: Brothers in the Saddle is a 1949 Western film directed by Lesley Selander. Virginia Cox makes her film debut.

rows.title: Calamity Jane and Sam Bass
rows.cast: Yvonne De Carlo, Howard Duff, Dorothy Hart
rows.extract: Calamity Jane and Sam Bass is a 1949 American Western film directed by George Sherman and starring Yvonne de Carlo, Howard Duff and Dorothy Hart.

rows.title: Canadian Pacific
rows.cast: Randolph Scott, Jane Wyatt, J. Carrol Naish
rows.extract: Canadian Pacific  is a 1949 American historical Western film, directed by Edwin L. Marin and starring Randolph Scott and Jane Wyatt. Filmed in Cinecolor on location in the Canadian Rockies in Banff National Park, Morley Indian Reserve in Alberta, and Yoho National Park in British Columbia, it is a s

rows.title: Caught
rows.cast: James Mason, Barbara Bel Geddes
rows.extract: Caught is a 1949 American film noir directed by Max Ophüls, and starring James Mason, Barbara Bel Geddes and Robert Ryan. Caught was based on a novel by Libbie Block.

rows.title: Challenge of the Range
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Paula Raymond
rows.extract: Challenge of the Range is a 1949 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Ed Earl Repp. The film stars Charles Starrett, Paula Raymond, Billy Halop, Steve Darrell, Henry Hall, Robert Filmer and Smiley Burnette. The film was released on February 3, 1949, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Challenge to Lassie
rows.cast: Donald Crisp, Edmund Gwenn, Geraldine Brook, Reginald Owen
rows.extract: Challenge to Lassie is an American drama directed by Richard Thorpe in Technicolor and released October 31, 1949, by MGM Studios. It was the fifth feature film starring the original Lassie, a collie named Pal, and the fourth and final Lassie film starring Donald Crisp.

rows.title: Champion
rows.cast: Kirk Douglas, Arthur Kennedy, Marilyn Maxwell
rows.extract: Champion is a 1949 American drama film noir sport film directed by Mark Robson with a screenplay written by Carl Foreman based on a short story by Ring Lardner, and starring Kirk Douglas, Marilyn Maxwell and Arthur Kennedy. The picture recounts the struggles of boxer "Midge" Kelly fighting his own d

rows.title: Chicago Deadline
rows.cast: Alan Ladd, Donna Reed, June Havoc
rows.extract: Chicago Deadline is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by Lewis Allen and starring Alan Ladd and Donna Reed.

rows.title: Chicken Every Sunday
rows.cast: Dan Dailey, Celeste Holm, Colleen Townsend
rows.extract: Chicken Every Sunday is a 1949 American comedy film directed by George Seaton. The screenplay by Seaton and Valentine Davies is based on the 1944 play of the same title by Julius J. Epstein and Philip G. Epstein, which was based on the memoir by Rosemary Taylor.

rows.title: Chinatown at Midnight
rows.cast: Hurd Hatfield, Jean Willes
rows.extract: Chinatown at Midnight is a 1949 film noir crime film directed by Seymour Friedman and starring Hurd Hatfield.

rows.title: City Across the River
rows.cast: Stephen McNally, Thelma Ritter, Sue England, Jeff Corey, Barbara Whiting
rows.extract: City Across the River is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by Maxwell Shane and starring Stephen McNally, Thelma Ritter, Sue England, Barbara Whiting, Luis Van Rooten and Jeff Corey. The screenplay is based on the novel The Amboy Dukes by Irving Shulman.

rows.title: The Clay Pigeon
rows.cast: Barbara Hale, Bill Williams
rows.extract: The Clay Pigeon is a 1949 American film noir directed by Richard Fleischer and written by Carl Foreman, based on a true story. The drama features Bill Williams and Barbara Hale, a real-life husband and wife.

rows.title: C-Man
rows.cast: Dean Jagger, John Carradine
rows.extract: C-Man is a 1949 American film noir directed by Joseph Lerner featuring Dean Jagger, John Carradine, Lottie Elwen and Rene Paul. Gail Kubik based his Pulitzer Prize winning Symphony Concertante on his score for C-Man.

rows.title: Colorado Territory
rows.cast: Joel McCrea, Virginia Mayo
rows.extract:
Colorado Territory is a 1949 American Western 
film noir directed by Raoul Walsh and starring Joel McCrea, Virginia Mayo, and Dorothy Malone. Written by Edmund H. North and John Twist, and based on the novel High Sierra by W.R. Burnett, the film is about an outlaw who is sprung from jail to help pul

rows.title: Come to the Stable
rows.cast: Loretta Young, Celeste Holm, Hugh Marlowe
rows.extract: Come to the Stable is a 1949 American comedy drama film that tells the story of two French religious sisters who come to a small New England town and involve the townsfolk in helping them to build a children's hospital. It stars Loretta Young, Celeste Holm, Hugh Marlowe, Elsa Lanchester, Thomas Gome

rows.title: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court
rows.cast: Bing Crosby, Rhonda Fleming, Cedric Hardwicke, William Bendix
rows.extract: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court is a 1949 American comedy musical film directed by Tay Garnett and starring Bing Crosby, Rhonda Fleming, Sir Cedric Hardwicke and William Bendix.

rows.title: Cover Up
rows.cast: William Bendix, Dennis O'Keefe
rows.extract: Cover Up is a 1949 American film noir mystery film directed by Alfred E. Green starring Dennis O'Keefe, William Bendix and Barbara Britton. O'Keefe also co-wrote the screenplay, credited as Jonathan Rix. The murder mystery takes place during the Christmas season.

rows.title: The Cowboy and the Indians
rows.cast: Gene Autry, Sheila Ryan
rows.extract: The Cowboy and the Indians is a 1949 American Western film directed by John English and written by Dwight Cummins and Dorothy Yost. The film stars Gene Autry, Sheila Ryan, Frank Richards, Hank Patterson, Jay Silverheels and Claudia Drake. The film was released on September 15, 1949, by Columbia Pict

rows.title: The Crime Doctor's Diary
rows.cast: Warner Baxter, Lois Maxwell
rows.extract: The Crime Doctor's Diary is a 1949 American mystery film directed by Seymour Friedman and starring Warner Baxter, Stephen Dunne and Lois Maxwell. It is the last of the Crime Doctor series of films made by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Criss Cross
rows.cast: Burt Lancaster, Yvonne De Carlo
rows.extract: Criss Cross is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by Robert Siodmak and starring Burt Lancaster, Yvonne De Carlo and Dan Duryea, from Don Tracy's novel of the same name. This black-and-white film was shot partly on location in the Bunker Hill section of Los Angeles. The film was written b

rows.title: The Crooked Way
rows.cast: John Payne, Ellen Drew, Sonny Tufts
rows.extract: The Crooked Way is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by Robert Florey and starring John Payne, Sonny Tufts and Ellen Drew. The film, with a similar plot to another film noir Somewhere in the Night, was shot by cameraman John Alton.

rows.title: Dancing in the Dark
rows.cast: William Powell, Betsy Drake
rows.extract: Dancing In the Dark is a 1949 Technicolor musical comedy film directed by Irving Reis, starring William Powell and Mark Stevens. Betsy Drake's singing voice was dubbed by Bonnie Lou Williams.

rows.title: A Dangerous Profession
rows.cast: George Raft, Ella Raines, Pat O'Brien
rows.extract: A Dangerous Profession is a 1949 American film noir directed by Ted Tetzlaff, written by Warren Duff and Martin Rackin, and starring George Raft, Ella Raines, and Pat O'Brien. The supporting cast features Jim Backus.

rows.title: The Daring Caballero
rows.cast: Duncan Renaldo, Leo Carrillo
rows.extract: The Valiant Hombre is a 1949 American Western film directed by Wallace Fox and written by Betty Burbridge. The film stars Duncan Renaldo, Leo Carrillo, Kippee Valez, Charles Halton, Pedro de Cordoba and Stephen Chase. The film was released on June 14, 1949, by United Artists.

rows.title: Daughter of the Jungle
rows.cast: Lois Hall, Sheldon Leonard
rows.extract: Daughter of the Jungle is a 1949 American adventure film directed by George Blair and written by William Lively. The film stars Lois Hall, James Cardwell, William Wright, and Sheldon Leonard, with James Nolan, and Jim Bannon. The film was released on February 8, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Daughter of the West
rows.cast: Martha Vickers, Phillip Reed, Donald Woods
rows.extract: Daughter of the West is a 1949 American Western film directed by Harold Daniels and starring Martha Vickers, Phillip Reed and Donald Woods.

rows.title: Dear Wife
rows.cast: William Holden, Joan Caulfield
rows.extract: Dear Wife is a 1949 comedy film starring Joan Caulfield and William Holden. It is the sequel to Dear Ruth, which was based on the Broadway play of the same name by Norman Krasna.

rows.title: Death Valley Gunfighter
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Gail Davis
rows.extract: Death Valley Gunfighter is a 1949 American Western film directed by R. G. Springsteen and written by Robert Creighton Williams. The film stars Allan Lane, Eddy Waller, James Nolan, Gail Davis, William "Bill" Henry, Harry Harvey, Sr. and Mauritz Hugo. The film was released on March 29, 1949, by Repub

rows.title: Desert Vigilante
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Peggy Stewart
rows.extract: Desert Vigilante is a 1949 American Western film directed by Fred F. Sears and written by Earle Snell. The film stars Charles Starrett, Peggy Stewart, Tris Coffin, Mary Newton, George Chesebro and Smiley Burnette. The film was released on April 9, 1949, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: The Devil's Henchman
rows.cast: Warner Baxter, Mary Beth Hughes
rows.extract: The Devil's Henchman is a 1949 movie featuring Warner Baxter, Mary Beth Hughes, Mike Mazurki, and Regis Toomey. The film was written by Eric Taylor and directed by Seymour Friedman.

rows.title: The Doctor and the Girl
rows.cast: Glenn Ford, Gloria DeHaven
rows.extract: The Doctor and the Girl is a 1949 American drama film directed by Curtis Bernhardt and starring Glenn Ford, Charles Coburn, Gloria DeHaven and Janet Leigh that was inspired by the French novel Corps et Âmes by Maxence van der Meersch.

rows.title: The Doolins of Oklahoma
rows.cast: Randolph Scott, George Macready, Louise Allbritton
rows.extract: The Doolins of Oklahoma is a 1949 American Western film directed by Gordon Douglas and starring Randolph Scott, George Macready and Louise Allbritton. It was distributed by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Down Dakota Way
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Dale Evans
rows.extract: Down Dakota Way  is a 1949 American Trucolor Western film directed by William Witney starring Roy Rogers.

rows.title: Down to the Sea in Ships
rows.cast: Richard Widmark, Lionel Barrymore
rows.extract: Down to the Sea in Ships is a 1949 American seafaring drama film directed by Henry Hathaway, starring Richard Widmark and Lionel Barrymore. The supporting cast includes Dean Stockwell, Cecil Kellaway, Gene Lockhart, and John McIntire. There is no connection between this picture and the silent film b

rows.title: Duke of Chicago
rows.cast: Audrey Long, Grant Withers
rows.extract: Duke of Chicago is a 1949 film released in the United States by Republic Pictures and starring Tom Brown, Audrey Long and DeForest Kelley. rows.title: Dynamite
rows.cast: William Gargan, Richard Crane
rows.extract: Dynamite is a 1949 American film noir drama film directed by William H. Pine and written by Milton Raison. The film stars William Gargan, Virginia Welles, Richard Crane, Irving Bacon, Mary Newton and Frank Ferguson. The film was released on January 18, 1949, by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: East Side, West Side
rows.cast: Barbara Stanwyck, James Mason, Van Heflin, Ava Gardner
rows.extract: East Side, West Side is a 1949 American melodrama crime film, starring Barbara Stanwyck, James Mason, Van Heflin, and Ava Gardner. Based on the 1947 novel of the same title, written by Marcia Davenport, screenplay by Isobel Lennart, produced by Voldemar Vetluguin, directed by Mervyn LeRoy, and distr

rows.title: Easy Living
rows.cast: Victor Mature, Lucille Ball, Lizabeth Scott
rows.extract: Easy Living is a 1949 American drama film directed by Jacques Tourneur, starring Victor Mature, Lucille Ball and Lizabeth Scott. The film features the real-life Los Angeles Rams football team.

rows.title: Edward, My Son
rows.cast: Spencer Tracy, Deborah Kerr, Ian Hunter
rows.extract: Edward, My Son is a 1949 British drama film directed by George Cukor for MGM-British Studios that stars Spencer Tracy and Deborah Kerr. The screenplay by Donald Ogden Stewart is based on the 1947 play of the same title by Noel Langley and Robert Morley.

rows.title: El Paso
rows.cast: John Payne, Gail Russell, Sterling Hayden
rows.extract: El Paso is a 1949 American Western film directed by Lewis R. Foster and starring John Payne, Gail Russell and Sterling Hayden.

rows.title: Everybody Does It
rows.cast: Paul Douglas, Linda Darnell, Celeste Holm
rows.extract:
Everybody Does It is a 1949 comedy film starring Paul Douglas, Linda Darnell and Celeste Holm.
In the film, a businessman's wife tries to become an opera star, failing miserably due to her lack of talent. When it turns out that her totally untrained husband is found to have a marvelous singing voice

rows.title: Family Honeymoon
rows.cast: Claudette Colbert, Fred MacMurray
rows.extract: Family Honeymoon is a 1949 domestic comedy film made by Universal International, directed by Claude Binyon, and written by Dane Lussier, based on the novel by Homer Croy. It was shot in Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona.

rows.title: The Fan
rows.cast: Madeleine Carroll, Jeanne Crain, Richard Greene, George Sanders
rows.extract: The Fan is a 1949 American drama film directed by Otto Preminger, starring Jeanne Crain, Madeleine Carroll, George Sanders, and Richard Greene. The screenplay by Dorothy Parker, Walter Reisch, and Ross Evans is based on the 1892 play Lady Windermere's Fan by Oscar Wilde. The play had been filmed sev

rows.title: Father Was a Fullback
rows.cast: Fred MacMurray, Maureen O'Hara, Rudy Vallée
rows.extract: Father Was a Fullback is a 1949 black-and-white film from 20th Century Fox based on a comedy by Clifford Goldsmith. The film is about a college American football star and his woes. The film stars Fred MacMurray, Maureen O'Hara, Natalie Wood, and Betty Lynn.

rows.title: Feudin' Rhythm
rows.cast: Eddy Arnold, Gloria Henry, Kirby Grant
rows.extract: Feudin' Rhythm is a 1949 American Western film directed by Edward Bernds and written by Barry Shipman. The film stars Eddy Arnold, Gloria Henry, Kirby Grant, Isabel Randolph, Tommy Ivo, Fuzzy Knight and Carolina Cotton. The film was released on November 3, 1949, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Fighting Fools
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall, Lyle Talbot
rows.extract: Fighting Fools is a 1949 comedy film starring The Bowery Boys. The film was released on April 17, 1949 by Monogram Pictures and is the thirteenth film in the series.

rows.title: The Fighting Kentuckian
rows.cast: John Wayne, Oliver Hardy, Vera Ralston
rows.extract: The Fighting Kentuckian is a 1949 American Adventure Western film written and directed by George Waggner and starring John Wayne, who also produced the film. The supporting cast featured Vera Ralston; Philip Dorn; Oliver Hardy portraying Wayne's portly sidekick; Marie Windsor; John Howard; Hugo Haas

rows.title: Fighting Man of the Plains
rows.cast: Randolph Scott, Jane Nigh
rows.extract: Fighting Man of the Plains is a 1949 American Western film directed by Edwin L. Marin. It stars Randolph Scott, Bill Williams, Victor Jory and Jane Nigh. Dale Robertson had his first credited role, playing Jesse James.

rows.title: The Fighting O'Flynn
rows.cast: Douglas Fairbanks Jr., Helena Carter
rows.extract: The Fighting O'Flynn is a 1949 American adventure film directed by Arthur Pierson. The film's screenplay by Douglas Fairbanks Jr. is based on the novel of the same name by Justin Huntly McCarthy. Fairbanks stars, along with Helena Carter.

rows.title: The Fighting Redhead
rows.cast: Jim Bannon
rows.extract: The Fighting Redhead  is a 1949 American Western film directed by Lewis D. Collins and starring Jim Bannon as Red Ryder in the final film of the series. The film was shot at the Iverson Movie Ranch.

rows.title: Flame of Youth
rows.cast: Barbra Fuller, Danny Sue Nolan
rows.extract: Flame of Youth is a 1949 American drama film directed by R. G. Springsteen and written by Robert Libott and Frank Burt. The film stars Barbra Fuller, Ray McDonald, Danny Sue Nolan, Tony Barrett, Carol Brannon and Anita Carrell. The film was released on September 22, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Flaming Fury
rows.cast: George Cooper, Roy Roberts
rows.extract: Flaming Fury is a 1949 American crime film directed by George Blair and written by John K. Butler. The film stars George Cooper, Roy Roberts, Billy Wayne, Peter Brocco, David Wolfe and Paul Marion. The film was released on July 28, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Flamingo Road
rows.cast: Joan Crawford, Zachary Scott, Sydney Greenstreet
rows.extract: Flamingo Road is a 1949 American film noir drama directed by Michael Curtiz and starring Joan Crawford, Zachary Scott, Sydney Greenstreet and David Brian. The screenplay by Robert Wilder was based on a 1946 play written by Wilder and his wife, Sally, which was based on Robert Wilder's 1942 novel of

rows.title: Flaxy Martin
rows.cast: Virginia Mayo, Dorothy Malone, Zachary Scott
rows.extract: Flaxy Martin is a 1949 film noir starring Zachary Scott and Virginia Mayo, and featuring Elisha Cook Jr., Dorothy Malone, and Douglas Kennedy. The crime thriller was directed by Richard L. Bare based on a story written by David Lang.

rows.title: Follow Me Quietly
rows.cast: William Lundigan, Dorothy Patrick
rows.extract: Follow Me Quietly is a 1949 semidocumentary film noir / police procedural film directed by Richard Fleischer. The drama features William Lundigan, Dorothy Patrick, Jeff Corey, and others.

rows.title: The Forbidden Street
rows.cast: Maureen O'Hara, Dana Andrews
rows.extract: The Forbidden Street is a 1949 British melodrama film directed by Jean Negulesco and starring Dana Andrews, Maureen O'Hara, Sybil Thorndike, Fay Compton and A. E. Matthews. Set in Victorian London, it tells the story of a wealthy young woman who marries a poor drunken artist and struggles to make en

rows.title: Forgotten Women
rows.cast: Elyse Knox, Edward Norris
rows.extract: Forgotten Women is a 1949 American drama film directed by William Beaudine and starring Elyse Knox, Edward Norris and Robert Shayne. The film follows the lives and romantic entanglements of three women who frequent a bar.

rows.title: The Fountainhead
rows.cast: Gary Cooper, Patricia Neal, Raymond Massey
rows.extract: The Fountainhead is a 1949 American black-and-white drama film produced by Henry Blanke, directed by King Vidor, and starring Gary Cooper, Patricia Neal, Raymond Massey, Robert Douglas and Kent Smith. The film is based on the bestselling 1943 novel of the same name by Ayn Rand, who also wrote the sc

rows.title: Free for All
rows.cast: Robert Cummings, Ann Blyth
rows.extract: Free for All is a 1949 American comedy film directed by Charles Barton and starring Robert Cummings, Ann Blyth and Percy Kilbride.

rows.title: Frontier Investigator
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Gail Davis
rows.extract: Frontier Investigator is a 1949 American Western film directed by Fred C. Brannon and written by Robert Creighton Williams. The film stars Allan Lane, Eddy Waller, Roy Barcroft, Gail Davis, Robert Emmett Keane and Clayton Moore. The film was released on May 2, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Gal Who Took the West
rows.cast: Yvonne De Carlo, Scott Brady
rows.extract: The Gal Who Took the West is a 1949 American Western film directed by Frederick de Cordova starring Yvonne De Carlo, Charles Coburn, Scott Brady and John Russell. It was nominated for an award by the Writers Guild of America 1950.

rows.title: The Gay Amigo
rows.cast: Duncan Renaldo, Armida
rows.extract: The Gay Amigo  is a 1949 American Western film starring Duncan Renaldo in the lead role of The Cisco Kid. This film was one entry in a series of Cisco Kid B Westerns produced by Philip N. Krasne. Ziv Television Programs later advanced money to Krasne in order to purchase the television rights for t

rows.title: The Girl from Jones Beach
rows.cast: Ronald Reagan, Virginia Mayo, Eddie Bracken
rows.extract: The Girl from Jones Beach is a 1949 American comedy film directed by Peter Godfrey and written by I. A. L. Diamond. It stars Ronald Reagan, Virginia Mayo, Eddie Bracken, Dona Drake, Henry Travers and Lois Wilson. The film was released by Warner Bros. on July 16, 1949.

rows.title: The Golden Stallion
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Dale Evans
rows.extract: The Golden Stallion is a 1949 American Western film directed by William Witney and starring Roy Rogers, Dale Evans and Estelita Rodriguez. The film was part of the long-running series of Roy Rogers films produced by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Great Dan Patch
rows.cast: Dennis O'Keefe, Gail Russell, Ruth Warrick
rows.extract: The Great Dan Patch is a 1949 American film directed by Joseph M. Newman about the pacing horse Dan Patch. The film is also known as Ride a Reckless Mile, and Dan Patch.

rows.title: The Great Gatsby
rows.cast: Alan Ladd, Ruth Hussey, Betty Field
rows.extract: The Great Gatsby is a 1949 American drama film directed by Elliott Nugent, and produced by Richard Maibaum, from a screenplay by Richard Maibaum and Cyril Hume. It is based on the 1925 novel The Great Gatsby by F. Scott Fitzgerald. The music score was by Robert Emmett Dolan, and the cinematography b

rows.title: The Great Lover
rows.cast: Bob Hope, Rhonda Fleming
rows.extract: The Great Lover is a 1949 comedy film starring Bob Hope, Rhonda Fleming, and Roland Young. In the film, a scout leader takes his troop on an ocean cruise, pursues a beautiful duchess and is stalked by a murderer. It is also known as Easy Does It and My Favourite Redhead.

rows.title: The Great Sinner
rows.cast: Gregory Peck, Ava Gardner, Melvyn Douglas
rows.extract: The Great Sinner is a 1949 American film noir drama film directed by Robert Siodmak. Based on the 1866 short novel The Gambler written by Fyodor Dostoyevsky, the film stars Gregory Peck, Ava Gardner, Frank Morgan, Ethel Barrymore, Walter Huston, Agnes Moorehead and Melvyn Douglas.

rows.title: Gun Law Justice
rows.cast: Jimmy Wakely, Jane Adams
rows.extract: Gun Law Justice is a 1949 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by Basil Dickey. The film stars Jimmy Wakely, Dub Taylor, Poni Adams, Lee Phelps, John James and I. Stanford Jolley. The film was released on March 13, 1949, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Gun Runner
rows.cast: Jimmy Wakely, Noel Neill
rows.extract: Gun Runner is a 1949 American Western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by J. Benton Cheney. The film stars Jimmy Wakely, Dub Taylor, Noel Neill, Mae Clarke, Kenne Duncan and Marshall Reed. The film was released on January 30, 1949, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: The Hasty Heart
rows.cast: Ronald Reagan, Patricia Neal, Richard Todd
rows.extract: The Hasty Heart is a 1949 war drama film, an Anglo-American co-production starring Ronald Reagan, Patricia Neal, and Richard Todd and directed by Vincent Sherman. The film is based on the 1945 play of the same name by John Patrick.

rows.title: The Heiress
rows.cast: Olivia de Havilland, Montgomery Clift, Ralph Richardson
rows.extract: The Heiress is a 1949 American romantic drama film directed and produced by William Wyler, from a screenplay written by Ruth and Augustus Goetz, adapted from their 1947 stage play of the same title, which was itself adapted from Henry James' 1880 novel Washington Square. The film stars Olivia de Hav

rows.title: Hellfire
rows.cast: Wild Bill Elliott, Marie Windsor, Forrest Tucker
rows.extract: Hellfire is a 1949 American Trucolor Western film directed by R. G. Springsteen starring Wild Bill Elliott, Marie Windsor, Forrest Tucker and Jim Davis

rows.title: Hideout
rows.cast: Lloyd Bridges, Lorna Gray
rows.extract: Hideout is a 1949 American thriller film directed by Philip Ford and written by John K. Butler. The film stars Lloyd Bridges, Lorna Gray, Ray Collins, Sheila Ryan, Chick Chandler and Jeff Corey. The film was released on March 8, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Hold That Baby!
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall
rows.extract: Hold That Baby! is a 1949 comedy film starring The Bowery Boys. The film was released on June 26, 1949 by Monogram Pictures and is the fourteenth film in the series.

rows.title: Holiday Affair
rows.cast: Robert Mitchum, Janet Leigh
rows.extract: Holiday Affair is a 1949 romantic comedy film directed and produced by Don Hartman and starring Robert Mitchum and Janet Leigh. It was based on the story Christmas Gift by John D. Weaver, which was also the film's working title. The film allowed Mitchum to briefly depart from his typical roles in fi

rows.title: Holiday in Havana
rows.cast: Desi Arnaz, Mary Hatcher, Ann Doran
rows.extract: Holiday in Havana is a 1949 American musical comedy directed by Jean Yarbrough, and starring Desi Arnaz, Mary Hatcher and Ann Doran. The film is about a Cuban hotel busboy (Arnaz) who dreams of becoming a composer. According to author Mary Beltrán, in his portrayal of Carlos Estrada, Arnaz "establis

rows.title: Home in San Antone
rows.cast: Roy Acuff, Lyn Thomas
rows.extract: Home in San Antone is a 1949 American Western musical film directed by Ray Nazarro, and starring Roy Acuff, The Smoky Mountain Boys, The Modernaires, Doye O'Dell, Lyn Thomas, and Bill Edwards. The film was released by Columbia Pictures on April 15, 1949.

rows.title: Home of the Brave
rows.cast: Jeff Corey, Lloyd Bridges
rows.extract: Home of the Brave is a 1949 war film based on a 1946 play by Arthur Laurents. It was directed by Mark Robson, and stars Douglas Dick, Jeff Corey, Lloyd Bridges, Frank Lovejoy, James Edwards, and Steve Brodie. The original play featured the protagonist being Jewish, rather than black. The National Bo

rows.title: Homicide
rows.cast: Robert Douglas, Helen Westcott
rows.extract: Homicide is a 1949 American crime drama film directed by Felix Jacoves and written by William Sackheim. The film stars Robert Douglas, Helen Westcott, Robert Alda, Monte Blue, Warren Douglas and John Harmon. The film was released by Warner Bros. on April 2, 1949.

rows.title: Horsemen of the Sierras
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette
rows.extract: Horsemen of the Sierras is a 1949 American Western film directed by Fred F. Sears and written by Barry Shipman. The film stars Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette, T. Texas Tyler, Lois Hall, Tommy Ivo and John Dehner. The film was released on November 22, 1949, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: The House Across the Street
rows.cast: Wayne Morris, Janis Paige
rows.extract: The House Across the Street is a 1949 American comedy/newspaper film directed by Richard L. Bare and written by Russell S. Hughes. rows.cast: Edward G. Robinson, Susan Hayward, Richard Conte, Efrem Zimbalist Jr.
rows.extract: House of Strangers is a 1949 American film noir directed by Joseph L. Mankiewicz and starring Edward G. Robinson, Susan Hayward, and Richard Conte. rows.title: I Cheated the Law
rows.cast: Tom Conway, Barbara Billingsley
rows.extract: I Cheated the Law is a 1949 American crime film directed by Edward L. Cahn and written by Richard G. Hubler. The film stars Tom Conway, Steve Brodie, Robert Osterloh, Barbara Billingsley, Russell Hicks and James Seay. The film was released on March 4, 1949, by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: I Married a Communist
rows.cast: Laraine Day, Robert Ryan, John Agar
rows.extract: The Woman on Pier 13 is a 1949 American film noir drama directed by Robert Stevenson and starring Laraine Day, Robert Ryan, and John Agar. rows.title: I Shot Jesse James
rows.cast: Preston Foster, John Ireland
rows.extract: I Shot Jesse James is a 1949 American Western film starring Reed Hadley as Jesse James and John Ireland as Bob Ford. rows.title: I Was a Male War Bride
rows.cast: Cary Grant, Ann Sheridan
rows.extract: I Was a Male War Bride is a 1949 comedy film directed by Howard Hawks and starring Cary Grant and Ann Sheridan.

rows.title: Illegal Entry
rows.cast: Märta Torén, Howard Duff
rows.extract: Illegal Entry is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by Frederick De Cordova and starring Howard Duff, Märta Torén and George Brent. The film and its treatment of illegal entry and unlawful residence in the United States is introduced by Watson B. Miller, the commissioner of the Immigratio

rows.title: Impact
rows.cast: Brian Donlevy, Ella Raines, Charles Coburn
rows.extract: Impact is a 1949 American film noir drama film directed by Arthur Lubin, starring Brian Donlevy and Ella Raines. rows.title: In the Good Old Summertime
rows.cast: Judy Garland, Van Johnson, Buster Keaton
rows.extract: In the Good Old Summertime is a 1949 American Technicolor musical film directed by Robert Z. Leonard. It stars Judy Garland, Van Johnson, S.Z. Sakall, Spring Byington, Clinton Sundberg, and Buster Keaton in his first featured film role at MGM since 1933.

rows.title: The Inspector General
rows.cast: Danny Kaye, Walter Slezak, Barbara Bates
rows.extract: The Inspector General is a 1949 American Technicolor musical comedy film, suggested by the play by Nikolai Gogol. It stars Danny Kaye and was directed by Henry Koster. The film also stars Walter Slezak, Barbara Bates, and Elsa Lanchester. Original music and lyrics are by the associate producer Sylvi

rows.title: Intruder in the Dust
rows.cast: David Brian, Claude Jarman Jr.
rows.extract: Intruder in the Dust is a 1949 crime drama film produced and directed by Clarence Brown and starring David Brian, Claude Jarman Jr. and Juano Hernandez. The film is based on the 1948 novel Intruder in the Dust by William Faulkner.

rows.title: It Happens Every Spring
rows.cast: Ray Milland, Jean Peters, Paul Douglas
rows.extract: It Happens Every Spring is a 1949 American comedy film directed by Lloyd Bacon and starring Ray Milland, Jean Peters and Paul Douglas.

rows.title: It's a Great Feeling
rows.cast: Doris Day, Jack Carson, Dennis Morgan
rows.extract: It's a Great Feeling is a 1949 American Technicolor musical comedy film starring Doris Day, Jack Carson and Dennis Morgan in a parody of what goes on behind the scenes in Hollywood movie making. The screenplay by Jack Rose and Mel Shavelson was based upon a story by I. A. L. Diamond. The film was di

rows.title: Jiggs and Maggie in Jackpot Jitters
rows.cast: Joe Yule, Renie Riano
rows.extract: Jiggs and Maggie in Jackpot Jitters is a 1949 American comedy film directed by William Beaudine and starring Joe Yule, Renie Riano and George McManus. rows.title: Jigsaw
rows.cast: Franchot Tone, Jean Wallace
rows.extract: Jigsaw is a 1949 American film noir crime drama directed by Fletcher Markle starring Franchot Tone, Jean Wallace and Marc Lawrence. The feature was produced by the Danziger Brothers, Edward J. Danziger and Harry Lee Danziger, from a screenplay by Vincent McConnor and Fletcher Markle, based on a stor

rows.title: Joe Palooka in the Big Fight
rows.cast: Leon Errol, Joe Kirkwood, Lina Romay
rows.extract: Joe Palooka in the Big Fight is a 1949 comedy film directed by Cy Endfield, based on the comic strip by Ham Fisher. It is an entry in Monogram's Joe Palooka series.

rows.title: Joe Palooka in the Counterpunch
rows.cast: Leon Errol, Joe Kirkwood, Elyse Knox
rows.extract: Joe Palooka in the Counterpunch is a 1949 American film directed by Reginald Le Borg. It was one in the series of Joe Palooka films for Monogram starring Leon Errol.

rows.title: John Loves Mary
rows.cast: Ronald Reagan, Jack Carson, Wayne Morris, Patricia Neal
rows.extract: John Loves Mary is a 1949 comedy film directed by David Butler and written by Henry Ephron and Phoebe Ephron. The film stars Ronald Reagan, Patricia Neal and Jack Carson. The film was released by Warner Bros. on February 19, 1949. It's based on a Broadway play of the same name written by Norman Kras

rows.title: Johnny Allegro
rows.cast: George Raft, George Macready, Nina Foch
rows.extract: Johnny Allegro is a 1949 American film noir directed by Ted Tetzlaff and starring George Raft. An ex-gangster (Raft), temporarily working as a federal agent, runs afoul of a counterfeiting crime lord (Macready) who enjoys hunting. It was one of several thrillers Raft made in the late 1940s.

rows.title: Johnny Holiday
rows.cast: William Bendix, Hoagy Carmichael
rows.extract: Johnny Holiday is a 1949 American crime film directed by Willis Goldbeck and written by Jack Andrews, Willis Goldbeck, and Frederick Stephani. The film stars William Bendix, Stanley Clements, Hoagy Carmichael, Allen Martin Jr., Greta Granstedt, and Herbert Newcomb. The film was released on November

rows.title: Johnny Stool Pigeon
rows.cast: Shelley Winters, Howard Duff, Dan Duryea
rows.extract: Johnny Stool Pigeon is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by William Castle and starring Howard Duff, Shelley Winters and Dan Duryea.

rows.title: Jolson Sings Again
rows.cast: Larry Parks, Barbara Hale
rows.extract: Jolson Sings Again is a 1949 American musical biographical film directed by Henry Levin, and the sequel to The Jolson Story (1946), both of which cover the life of singer Al Jolson. It was the highest-grossing film of 1949 and received three Oscar nominations at the 22nd Academy Awards.

rows.title: The Judge
rows.cast: Milburn Stone, Katherine DeMille
rows.extract: The Judge is a 1949 American crime film directed by Elmer Clifton and starring Milburn Stone, Katherine DeMille and Paul Guilfoyle.

rows.title: The Judge Steps Out
rows.cast: Ann Sothern, Alexander Knox
rows.extract: The Judge Steps Out is a 1948 American comedy film directed by Boris Ingster and written by Ingster and Alexander Knox. rows.title: Kazan
rows.cast: Stephen Dunne, Lois Maxwell
rows.extract: Kazan is a 1949 American drama western film directed by Will Jason and starring Stephen Dunne, Lois Maxwell and Joe Sawyer. It is based on a novel by James Oliver Curwood which had previously been made into a 1921 silent film of the same title.

rows.title: The Kid from Cleveland
rows.cast: George Brent, Lynn Bari
rows.extract: The Kid from Cleveland is a 1949 sports drama film starring George Brent, Lynn Bari and Russ Tamblyn, directed by Herbert Kline, and released by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: King of the Rocket Men
rows.cast: Tristram Coffin, Mae Clarke, Don Haggerty
rows.extract: King of the Rocket Men is a 1949 12-chapter movie serial from Republic Pictures, produced by Franklin Adreon, directed Fred C. Brannon, that stars Tristram Coffin, Mae Clarke, Don Haggerty, House Peters, Jr., James Craven, and I. Stanford Jolley.

rows.title: A Kiss for Corliss
rows.cast: Shirley Temple, David Niven
rows.extract: A Kiss for Corliss is a 1949 American comedy film directed by Richard Wallace, written by Howard Dimsdale, and starring David Niven and Shirley Temple. The film, which was the last for both Wallace and Temple, was released on November 25, 1949, by United Artists. It is a sequel to the 1945 film Kiss

rows.title: A Kiss in the Dark
rows.cast: Jane Wyman, David Niven
rows.extract: A Kiss in the Dark is a 1949 comedy film directed by Delmer Daves, starring David Niven and Jane Wyman, and featuring Wayne Morris, Victor Moore, Broderick Crawford, and Maria Ouspenskaya. The plot revolves around a pianist who purchases, solely as a hands-off investment, an apartment house full of

rows.title: Knock on Any Door
rows.cast: Humphrey Bogart, John Derek, George Macready
rows.extract: Knock on Any Door is a 1949 American courtroom trial film noir directed by Nicholas Ray and starring Humphrey Bogart. The picture gave actor John Derek his breakthrough role, and was based on the 1947 novel of the same name by Willard Motley.

rows.title: Ladies of the Chorus
rows.cast: Adele Jergens, Marilyn Monroe
rows.extract: Ladies of the Chorus is a 1948 American musical romance film directed by Phil Karlson and starring Adele Jergens, Marilyn Monroe and Rand Brooks. The screenplay, written by Harry Sauber and Joseph Carole, was based on a story by Sauber.

rows.title: The Lady Gambles
rows.cast: Barbara Stanwyck, Robert Preston
rows.extract: The Lady Gambles is a 1949 American film noir drama film directed by Michael Gordon and starring Barbara Stanwyck, Robert Preston and Stephen McNally.

rows.title: The Lady Takes a Sailor
rows.cast: Jane Wyman, Dennis Morgan
rows.extract: The Lady Takes a Sailor is a 1949 comedy film directed by Michael Curtiz, and starring Jane Wyman, Eve Arden and Dennis Morgan.

rows.title: Laramie
rows.cast: Charles Starrett
rows.extract: Laramie is a 1949 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Barry Shipman. The film stars Charles Starrett, Fred F. Sears, Tommy Ivo, Elton Britt and Smiley Burnette. The film was released on May 19, 1949, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: The Last Bandit
rows.cast: Bill Elliott, Lorna Gray
rows.extract: The Last Bandit is a 1949 American Western film directed by Joseph Kane and starring Bill Elliott, Lorna Gray and Forrest Tucker. rows.title: Law of the Barbary Coast
rows.cast: Gloria Henry, Adele Jergens
rows.extract: Law of the Barbary Coast is a 1949 American historical crime western film directed by Lew Landers and starring Gloria Henry, Stephen Dunne and Adele Jergens.

rows.title: Law of the Golden West
rows.cast: Monte Hale, Gail Davis
rows.extract: Law of the Golden West is a 1949 American Western film directed by Philip Ford and written by Norman S. Hall. The film stars Monte Hale, Paul Hurst, Gail Davis, Roy Barcroft, John Holland and Scott Elliott. The film was released on May 23, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Law of the West
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Max Terhune
rows.extract: Law of the West is a 1949 American Western film directed by Ray Taylor and written by J. Benton Cheney. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Max Terhune, Bill Kennedy, Jack Ingram, Riley Hill and Eddie Parker. The film was released on February 20, 1949, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Lawless Code
rows.cast: Jimmy Wakely, Dub Taylor, Ellen Hall
rows.extract: Lawless Code is a 1949 American Western film directed by Oliver Drake and written by Basil Dickey. The film stars Jimmy Wakely, Dub Taylor, Ellen Hall, Tris Coffin, Riley Hill and Kenne Duncan. The film was released on December 4, 1949, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: A Letter to Three Wives
rows.cast: Linda Darnell, Ann Sothern, Jeanne Crain, Paul Douglas, Kirk Douglas
rows.extract: A Letter to Three Wives is a 1949 American romantic comedy-drama which tells the story of a woman who mails a letter to three women, telling them she has left town with the husband of one of them, but not saying which one. It stars Jeanne Crain, Linda Darnell, Ann Sothern, Paul Douglas, Kirk Douglas

rows.title: The Life of Riley
rows.cast: William Bendix, Rosemary DeCamp
rows.extract: The Life of Riley is a 1949 American comedy film directed by Irving Brecher and starring William Bendix, Rosemary DeCamp and James Gleason. It was based on the popular radio show of the same title.

rows.title: Little Women
rows.cast: Elizabeth Taylor, Margaret O'Brien, June Allyson, Mary Astor, Janet Leigh
rows.extract: Little Women is a 1949 American comedy-drama film with script and music taken directly from the earlier 1933 Hepburn version. rows.title: The Lone Wolf and His Lady
rows.cast: Ron Randell, June Vincent
rows.extract: The Lone Wolf and His Lady (1949) is the 15th and final Lone Wolf film produced by Columbia Pictures, directed by John Hoffman and written by Edward Dein and Michael Stuart Boylan.

rows.title: Look for the Silver Lining
rows.cast: June Haver, Ray Bolger
rows.extract: Look for the Silver Lining is a 1949 American biographical musical film directed by David Butler and written by Phoebe Ephron, Henry Ephron and Marian Spitzer. rows.cast: Johnny Weissmuller, Elena Verdugo
rows.extract: The Lost Tribe (1949) is the second Jungle Jim film produced by Columbia Pictures. rows.cast: Charles Ruggles, Peggy Ann Garner, Richard Ney
rows.extract: The Lovable Cheat is a 1949 American historical comedy film directed by Richard Oswald and starring Charles Ruggles, Peggy Ann Garner and Richard Ney. rows.title: Love Happy
rows.cast: Marx Brothers, Vera-Ellen, Ilona Massey, Marion Hutton, Raymond Burr
rows.extract: Love Happy is a 1949 American musical comedy film, released by United Artists, directed by David Miller and starring the Marx Brothers in their 13th and final feature film, as well as a memorable walk-on by a relatively unknown Marilyn Monroe.

rows.title: The Lucky Stiff
rows.cast: Dorothy Lamour, Claire Trevor
rows.extract: The Lucky Stiff is a 1949 American comedy crime film directed by Lewis R. Foster, starring Dorothy Lamour, Brian Donlevy, and Claire Trevor. The film is based on the 1945 novel of the same name by Craig Rice.

rows.title: Lust for Gold

rows.cast: Marjorie Main, Percy Kilbride
rows.extract: Ma and Pa Kettle is a 1949 American comedy film directed by Charles Lamont. rows.title: Madame Bovary
rows.cast: Jennifer Jones, James Mason, Van Heflin
rows.extract: Madame Bovary is a 1949 American romantic drama, a film adaptation of the classic 1857 novel of the same name by Gustave Flaubert. It stars Jennifer Jones, James Mason, Van Heflin, Louis Jourdan, Alf Kjellin, Gene Lockhart, Frank Allenby and Gladys Cooper.

rows.title: Make Believe Ballroom
rows.cast: Ruth Warrick, Ron Randell
rows.extract: Make Believe Ballroom is a 1949 American musical romantic comedy directed by Joseph Santley and produced by Ted Richmond. It was loosely based on a radio program of the same name by Martin Block and Al Jarvis. The film starred Jerome Courtland, Ruth Warrick, Ron Randell, Virginia Welles, and Jarvis.

rows.title: Make Mine Laughs
rows.cast: Ray Bolger, Joan Davis, Dennis Day
rows.extract: Make Mine Laughs is a 1949 film directed by Richard Fleischer. The film was a compilation of comic scenes and musical numbers from older and newer RKO Studios films.

rows.cast: Spencer Tracy, James Stewart, Sydney Greenstreet

rows.title: Manhandled
rows.cast: Dorothy Lamour, Dan Duryea, Sterling Hayden

rows.cast: Gloria Jean, Patricia Barry

rows.extract: Masked Raiders is a 1949 American Western film.

rows.title: Massacre River

rows.extract: Massacre River is a 1949 American western film directed by John Rawlins and starring Rory Calhoun, Guy Madison and Carole Mathews. The film's sets were designed by Lucius O. Croxton. It was distributed by Allied Artists.

rows.title: Master Minds
rows.cast: Leo Gorcey, Huntz Hall

rows.title: Miss Grant Takes Richmond
rows.cast: Lucille Ball, William Holden
rows.extract: Miss Grant Takes Richmond is a 1949 comedy film starring Lucille Ball and William Holden, directed by Lloyd Bacon and released by Columbia Pictures. It was released under the title Innocence is Bliss in the UK.

rows.title: Miss Mink of 1949
rows.cast: Lois Collier, Barbara Brown
rows.extract: Miss Mink of 1949 is a 1949 American comedy film directed by Glenn Tryon and written by Arnold Belgard. It stars Jimmy Lydon, Lois Collier, Richard Lane, Barbara Brown, Paul Guilfoyle and June Storey. The film was released on February 11, 1949, by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Mother Is a Freshman

rows.cast: Glenn Ford, Evelyn Keyes
rows.extract: Mr. Soft Touch is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by Gordon Douglas and Henry Levin and starring Glenn Ford and Evelyn Keyes. The film is also known as House of Settlement.

rows.title: Mrs. Mike
rows.cast: Dick Powell, Evelyn Keyes

rows.title: The Mutineers
rows.cast: Jon Hall, George Reeves
rows.extract: The Mutineers is a 1949 American adventure film starring Adele Jergens, George Reeves and Jon Hall.

rows.title: My Dream Is Yours
rows.cast: Doris Day, Jack Carson, Eve Arden
rows.extract: My Dream Is Yours is a 1949 Technicolor musical romantic comedy film starring Jack Carson, Doris Day, and Lee Bowman.

rows.title: My Foolish Heart
rows.cast: Susan Hayward, Dana Andrews
rows.extract: My Foolish Heart is a 1949 American romantic drama film directed by Mark Robson, starring Dana Andrews and Susan Hayward. It relates the story of a woman's reflections on the bad turns her life has taken.

rows.title: My Friend Irma
rows.cast: Dean Martin, Jerry Lewis
rows.extract: My Friend Irma is a 1949 American comedy film directed by George Marshall. It was the motion picture debut of the comedy team Dean Martin and Jerry Lewis. The film was released on August 16, 1949, by Paramount, and is based upon the CBS radio series My Friend Irma that first aired in 1947.

rows.title: My Own True Love
rows.cast: Phyllis Calvert, Melvyn Douglas, Wanda Hendrix
rows.extract: My Own True Love is a 1949 American drama film directed by Compton Bennett and written by Arthur Kober, Josef Mischel and Theodore Strauss. rows.title: The Mysterious Desperado
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Richard Martin, Movita Castaneda
rows.extract: The Mysterious Desperado is a 1949 American Western film. The Los Angeles Times reported that "Tim Holt Westerns have attained a good standard which is adequately maintained" in the film.

rows.title: Navajo Trail Raiders
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Eddy Waller
rows.extract: Navajo Trail Raiders is a 1949 American Western film directed by R. G. Springsteen and written by M. Coates Webster. The film stars Allan Lane, Eddy Waller, Robert Emmett Keane, Barbara Bestar, Harold Landon and Dick Curtis. The film was released on October 15, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Neptune's Daughter
rows.cast: Esther Williams, Red Skelton, Ricardo Montalbán
rows.extract: Neptune's Daughter is a 1949 Technicolor musical romantic comedy film released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer starring Esther Williams, Red Skelton, Ricardo Montalbán, Betty Garrett, Keenan Wynn, Xavier Cugat and Mel Blanc. rows.cast: Sally Forrest, Hugh O'Brian

rows.title: Night Unto Night
rows.cast: Ronald Reagan, Viveca Lindfors, Broderick Crawford
rows.extract: Night unto Night is a 1949 American drama film directed by Don Siegel and written by Kathryn Scola. It is based on the 1944 novel by Philip Wylie. rows.title: Not Wanted
rows.cast: Sally Forrest, Keefe Brasselle, Leo Penn
rows.extract: Not Wanted is a 1949 American drama film directed by Elmer Clifton and an un-credited Ida Lupino and starring Sally Forrest, Keefe Brasselle and Leo Penn.

rows.title: Oh, You Beautiful Doll
rows.cast: Mark Stevens, June Haver, Gale Robbins
rows.extract: Oh, You Beautiful Doll is a 1949 musical film directed by John M. Stahl, starring the musical queen June Haver and Mark Stevens. Co-stars included S.Z. Sakall, Charlotte Greenwood, and Gale Robbins.

rows.title: Once More, My Darling
rows.cast: Robert Montgomery, Ann Blyth
rows.extract: Once More, My Darling is a 1949 American comedy film directed by and starring Robert Montgomery and Ann Blyth. The film was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Sound Recording.

rows.title: One Last Fling
rows.cast: Alexis Smith, Zachary Scott
rows.extract: One Last Fling is a 1949 American comedy film directed by Peter Godfrey and written by Richard Flournoy and William Sackheim. The film stars Alexis Smith, Zachary Scott, Douglas Kennedy, Ann Doran, Ransom M. Sherman and Veda Ann Borg. The film was released by Warner Bros. on June 30, 1949.

rows.cast: Gene Kelly, Frank Sinatra, Ann Miller, Betty Garrett
rows.extract: On the Town is a 1949 American Technicolor musical film with music by Leonard Bernstein and Roger Edens and book and lyrics by Betty Comden and Adolph Green. It is an adaptation of the Broadway stage musical of the same name produced in 1944, although many changes in script and score were made from

rows.title: Outcasts of the Trail
rows.cast: Monte Hale, Jeff Donnell
rows.extract: Outcasts of the Trail is a 1949 American Western film directed by Philip Ford and written by Olive Cooper. The film stars Monte Hale, Paul Hurst, Jeff Donnell, Roy Barcroft, John Gallaudet and Milton Parsons. The film was released on June 8, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Outpost in Morocco
rows.cast: George Raft, Marie Windsor
rows.extract: Outpost in Morocco is a 1949 American action adventure film directed by Robert Florey, starring George Raft and Marie Windsor. rows.title: Pinky
rows.cast: Jeanne Crain, Ethel Barrymore, Ethel Waters
rows.extract: Pinky is a 1949 American drama film directed by Elia Kazan and produced by Darryl F. Zanuck. The screenplay was adapted by Philip Dunne and Dudley Nichols based on Cid Ricketts Sumner's 1946 novel Quality. rows.title: Pioneer Marshal
rows.cast: Monte Hale, Paul Hurst, Nan Leslie
rows.extract: Pioneer Marshal is a 1949 American Western film directed by Philip Ford and written by Robert Creighton Williams. rows.title: The Pirates of Capri
rows.cast: Louis Hayward, Binnie Barnes, Mariella Lotti
rows.extract: The Pirates of Capri, released in the United Kingdom as The Masked Pirate, is a 1949 Italian/American international co-production swashbuckler film directed by Edgar G. Ulmer starring Louis Hayward. It was filmed on location in Italy.

rows.title: Post Office Investigator
rows.cast: Audrey Long, Warren Douglas
rows.extract: Post Office Investigator is a 1949 black and white American crime film about the theft of postage stamps, directed by George Blair, and starring Audrey Long, Warren Douglas and Jeff Donnell. Allmovie called it a "diligent Republic programmer."

rows.title: Port of New York
rows.cast: Scott Brady, K. T. Stevens, Yul Brynner
rows.extract: Port of New York is a 1949 American film noir/crime film directed by László Benedek with cinematography by George E. Diskant and shot in semidocumentary style. The film is notable for being Yul Brynner's first film appearance. The film, which is very similar to T-Men (1947), was shot on location in

rows.title: Powder River Rustlers
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Eddy Waller
rows.extract: Powder River Rustlers is a 1949 American Western film directed by Philip Ford and written by Richard Wormser. The film stars Allan Lane, Eddy Waller, Gerry Ganzer, Roy Barcroft, Francis McDonald and Cliff Clark. The film was November 25, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Prince of Foxes
rows.cast: Tyrone Power, Orson Welles
rows.extract: Prince of Foxes is a 1949 film adapted from Samuel Shellabarger's novel Prince of Foxes. The movie starred Tyrone Power as Orsini and Orson Welles as Cesare Borgia. It was nominated for two Oscars during the 22nd Academy Awards: Best Black and White Cinematography and Best Costume Design, Black and

rows.title: Prince of the Plains
rows.cast: Monte Hale, Paul Hurst
rows.extract: Prince of the Plains is a 1949 American Western film directed by Philip Ford and written by Louise Rousseau and Albert DeMond. The film stars Monte Hale, Paul Hurst, Shirley Davis, Roy Barcroft, Rory Mallinson and Harry Lauter. The film was released on April 8, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Prison Warden
rows.cast: Warner Baxter, Anna Lee
rows.extract: Prison Warden is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by Seymour Friedman and starring Warner Baxter, Anna Lee and Harlan Warde.

rows.title: Range Justice
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Max Terhune
rows.extract: Range Justice is a 1949 American Western film directed by Ray Taylor and written by Ronald Davidson. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Max Terhune, Tris Coffin, Riley Hill, Sarah Padden and Eddie Parker. The film was released on July 16, 1949, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Ranger of Cherokee Strip
rows.cast: Monte Hale, Paul Hurst
rows.extract: Ranger of Cherokee Strip is a 1949 American Western film directed by Philip Ford and written by Robert Creighton Williams. The film stars Monte Hale, Paul Hurst, Alix Talton, Roy Barcroft, Douglas Kennedy and George Meeker. The film was released on November 4, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Reckless Moment
rows.cast: James Mason, Joan Bennett, Geraldine Brooks
rows.extract: The Reckless Moment is a 1949 American film noir melodrama directed by Max Ophüls, produced by Walter Wanger, and released by Columbia Pictures with Burnett Guffey as cinematographer. It starred James Mason and Joan Bennett. The film is based on The Blank Wall (1947), a novel written by Elisabeth Sa

rows.title: Red Canyon
rows.cast: Ann Blyth, Howard Duff, George Brent
rows.extract: Red Canyon is a 1949 American Western film directed by George Sherman and starring Ann Blyth, Howard Duff and George Brent. It was based on the novel Wildfire by Zane Grey.

rows.title: The Red Danube
rows.cast: Peter Lawford, Janet Leigh, Angela Lansbury
rows.extract: The Red Danube is a 1949 American drama film directed by George Sidney and starring Walter Pidgeon. The film is set during Operation Keelhaul and was based on the 1947 novel Vespers in Vienna by Bruce Marshall.

rows.title: Red, Hot and Blue
rows.cast: Betty Hutton, Victor Mature, William Demarest
rows.extract: Red, Hot and Blue is a 1949 American musical comedy film starring Betty Hutton as an actress who gets mixed up with gangsters and murder. Frank Loesser wrote the songs and plays a key role.

rows.title: Red Light
rows.cast: George Raft, Virginia Mayo, Raymond Burr
rows.extract: Red Light is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed and produced by Roy Del Ruth, starring George Raft and Virginia Mayo, and based on the story "This Guy Gideon" by Don "Red" Barry, featuring strong religious overtones.

rows.title: The Red Menace
rows.cast: Robert Rockwell, Betty Lou Gerson
rows.extract: The Red Menace is a 1949 anti-communist film noir drama film directed by R. G. Springsteen starring Robert Rockwell and Hannelore Axman.

rows.title: The Red Pony
rows.cast: Myrna Loy, Robert Mitchum
rows.extract: The Red Pony is a 1949 American rural drama film in Technicolor based on John Steinbeck's 1937 novella of the same name. Steinbeck also wrote the screenplay for this film.

rows.title: Red Rock Outlaw
rows.cast: Lee "Lasses" White, Reno Browne
rows.extract: Red Rock Outlaw is a 1949 American musical Western film directed by Elmer Clifton.

rows.title: Red Stallion in the Rockies
rows.cast: Jean Heather, Arthur Franz
rows.extract: Red Stallion in the Rockies is a 1949 American Cinecolor Western film directed by Ralph Murphy and starring Arthur Franz

rows.title: Reign of Terror
rows.cast: Robert Cummings, Arlene Dahl
rows.extract: Reign of Terror is a 1949 American spy thriller film directed by Anthony Mann and starring Robert Cummings, Richard Basehart and Arlene Dahl. The film is set during the French Revolution. Plotters seek to bring down Maximilien Robespierre and end his bloodthirsty Reign of Terror.

rows.title: Renegades of the Sage
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette
rows.extract: Renegades of the Sage is a 1949 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Earle Snell. The film stars Charles Starrett, Smiley Burnette, Leslie Banning, Trevor Bardette, Douglas Fowley and Jock Mahoney. The film was released on November 24, 1949, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Ride, Ryder, Ride!
rows.cast: Jim Bannon, Don Reynolds, Emmett Lynn
rows.extract: Ride, Ryder, Ride! is a 1949 American Cinecolor Western film directed by Lewis D. Collins and starring Jim Bannon, Don Reynolds and Emmett Lynn. It is based on the Red Ryder series by Fred Harman, one of four films made by Eagle-Lion Films featuring the character.

rows.title: Riders in the Sky
rows.cast: Gene Autry, Gloria Henry
rows.extract: Riders in the Sky is a 1949 American Western film directed by John English and starring and co-produced by Gene Autry; featuring Gloria Henry, and Pat Buttram. Based on the song by Stan Jones, the film is about a murder, of which rancher Ralph Lawson is accused, and Gene Autry attempting to clear hi

rows.title: Riders of the Range
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Richard Martin, Jacqueline White
rows.extract: Riders of the Range is a 1949 American Western film directed by Lesley Selander.

rows.title: Riders of the Whistling Pines
rows.cast: Gene Autry, Patricia Barry
rows.extract: Riders of the Whistling Pines is a 1949 American Western film directed by John English and starring Gene Autry, Patricia Barry, and Jimmy Lloyd. Written by Jack Townley, the film is about a gang of outlaws who are destroying the timberland and who frame a singing cowboy on a cattle-poisoning charge,

rows.title: Rimfire
rows.cast: Mary Beth Hughes, James Millican
rows.extract: Rimfire is a 1949 American Western film directed by B. Reeves Eason. It is a noir Western.

rows.title: Rim of the Canyon
rows.cast: Gene Autry, Thurston Hall
rows.extract: Rim of the Canyon is a 1949 American Western film directed by John English and starring and co-produced by Gene Autry; featuring Nan Leslie, and Thurston Hall. Based on the short story Phantom .45's Talk Loud by Joseph Chadwick, the film is about a horse stolen by escaped convicts and the cowboy who

rows.title: Ringside
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Tom Brown, Sheila Ryan
rows.extract: Ringside is a 1949 American film noir drama sport film directed by Frank McDonald for Lippert Pictures from a story by Daniel B. Ullman, adapted by Ron Ormond.

rows.title: Roaring Westward
rows.cast: Jimmy Wakely, Lois Hall
rows.extract: Roaring Westward is a 1949 American Western film directed by Oliver Drake and written by Ronald Davidson. The film stars Jimmy Wakely, Dub Taylor, Dennis Moore, Lois Hall, Jack Ingram and Claire Whitney. The film was released on September 15, 1949, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Roll, Thunder, Roll!
rows.cast: Jim Bannon, Don Reynolds, Emmett Lynn
rows.extract: Roll, Thunder, Roll! is a 1949 American Western film directed by Lewis D. Collins and starring Jim Bannon, Don Reynolds and Emmett Lynn. It was shot in Cinecolor. It is based on the Red Ryder series by Fred Harman, one of four films made by Eagle-Lion Films featuring the character.

rows.title: Rope of Sand
rows.cast: Burt Lancaster, Paul Henreid, Claude Rains
rows.extract: Rope of Sand is a 1949 adventure-suspense film noir directed by William Dieterle, produced by Hal Wallis, and starring Burt Lancaster and three stars from Wallis's Casablanca - Paul Henreid, Claude Rains and Peter Lorre. The film introduces Corinne Calvet and features Sam Jaffe, John Bromfield, and

rows.title: Roseanna McCoy
rows.cast: Farley Granger, Joan Evans
rows.extract: Roseanna McCoy is a 1949 American drama film directed by Irving Reis. The screenplay by John Collier, based on the 1947 novel of the same title by Alberta Hannum, is a romanticized and semi-fictionalized account of the Hatfield–McCoy feud. The film stars Farley Granger and Joan Evans.

rows.title: Rose of the Yukon
rows.cast: Myrna Dell, Steve Brodie
rows.extract: Rose of the Yukon is a 1949 American adventure film directed by George Blair and written by Norman S. Hall. The film stars Steve Brodie, Myrna Dell, William Wright, Emory Parnell, Jonathan Hale and Benny Baker. The film was released on January 5, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Roughshod
rows.cast: Gloria Grahame, Robert Sterling
rows.extract: Roughshod is a 1949 black-and-white Western film starring Gloria Grahame and Robert Sterling and directed by Mark Robson.

rows.title: Rustlers
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Richard Martin, Martha Hyer
rows.extract: Rustlers is a 1949 American Western directed by Lesley Selander. The film is a Tim Holt B Western about a group of Arizona ranchers intent on stopping a gang of cattle rustlers.

rows.title: Rusty's Birthday
rows.cast: John Litel, Ann Doran
rows.extract: Rusty's Birthday is a black-and-white American juvenile drama, released by Columbia Pictures in November 1949. rows.title: Rusty Saves a Life
rows.cast: John Litel, Ann Doran
rows.extract: Rusty Saves a Life is a 1949 American drama film directed by Seymour Friedman and starring Ted Donaldson, Gloria Henry and Ann Doran. It was part of the Rusty series of films produced by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Samson and Delilah
rows.cast: Hedy Lamarr, Victor Mature, Angela Lansbury
rows.extract: Samson and Delilah is a 1949 American romantic biblical drama film produced and directed by Cecil B. DeMille and released by Paramount Pictures. rows.title: San Antone Ambush
rows.cast: Monte Hale, Paul Hurst
rows.extract: San Antone Ambush is a 1949 American Western film directed by Philip Ford and written by Norman S. Hall. The film stars Monte Hale, Bette Daniels, Paul Hurst, Roy Barcroft, James Cardwell, and Trevor Bardette. The film was released on October 7, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Sand
rows.cast: Coleen Gray, Mark Stevens
rows.extract: Sand is a 1949 American Western film directed by Louis King and starring Mark Stevens and Coleen Gray. It was nominated at the 22nd Academy Awards for Best Cinematography (color)-which Charles G. Clarke was nominated for.

rows.title: Sands of Iwo Jima
rows.cast: John Wayne, John Agar, Forrest Tucker
rows.extract: Sands of Iwo Jima is a 1949 war film starring John Wayne that follows a group of United States Marines from training to the Battle of Iwo Jima during World War II. rows.title: Satan's Cradle
rows.cast: Duncan Renaldo, Ann Savage
rows.extract: Satan's Cradle is a 1949 American Western film directed by Ford Beebe and written by J. Benton Cheney, and starring Duncan Renaldo, Leo Carrillo, Ann Savage, Douglas Fowley and Byron Foulger. It was released on October 7, 1949, by United Artists.

rows.title: Scene of the Crime
rows.cast: Van Johnson, Arlene Dahl
rows.extract: Scene of the Crime is a 1949 film noir directed by Roy Rowland, starring Van Johnson, and featuring Gloria DeHaven, Arlene Dahl, and Tom Drake. rows.title: Search for Danger
rows.cast: John Calvert, Albert Dekker
rows.extract: Search for Danger is a 1949 American crime film directed by Jack Bernhard and starring John Calvert, Albert Dekker and Myrna Dell. rows.title: The Secret Garden
rows.cast: Margaret O'Brien, Dean Stockwell
rows.extract: The Secret Garden is a 1949 American drama film. It is the second screen adaptation of the classic 1911 novel by Frances Hodgson Burnett. rows.cast: Richard Ney, Vanessa Brown
rows.extract: The Secret of St. Ives is a 1949 American historical adventure film directed by Phil Rosen and starring Richard Ney, Vanessa Brown and Henry Daniell. rows.title: The Set-Up
rows.cast: Robert Ryan, Audrey Totter
rows.extract: The Set-Up is a 1949 American film noir boxing drama directed by Robert Wise and starring Robert Ryan and Audrey Totter. rows.title: Shamrock Hill
rows.cast: Peggy Ryan, Trudy Marshall
rows.extract: Shamrock Hill is a 1949 American musical comedy film directed by Arthur Dreifuss, starring Peggy Ryan, Ray McDonald and Trudy Marshall.

rows.title: She Shoulda Said No!
rows.cast: Lila Leeds, Lyle Talbot
rows.extract: She Shoulda Said No! is a 1949 exploitation film that follows in the spirit of morality tales such as the 1936 films Reefer Madness and Marihuana. rows.title: She Wore a Yellow Ribbon
rows.cast: John Wayne, Joanne Dru, Ben Johnson
rows.extract: She Wore a Yellow Ribbon is a 1949 American Technicolor Western film directed by John Ford and starring John Wayne. rows.title: Sheriff of Wichita
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Lyn Wilde
rows.extract: Sheriff of Wichita is a 1949 American Western film directed by R. G. Springsteen and written by Robert Creighton Williams. The film stars Allan Lane, Eddy Waller, Roy Barcroft, Lyn Wilde, Clayton Moore and Gene Roth. The film was released on January 22, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Shockproof
rows.cast: Cornel Wilde, Patricia Knight
rows.extract: Shockproof is a 1949 American crime film noir directed by Douglas Sirk and starring Patricia Knight and Cornel Wilde. Wilde and Knight were husband and wife during filming. They divorced in 1951.

rows.title: Siren of Atlantis
rows.cast: Maria Montez, Jean-Pierre Aumont
rows.extract: Siren of Atlantis, also known as Atlantis the Lost Continent, is a 1949 American black-and-white fantasy-adventure film, distributed by United Artists, that stars Maria Montez and her husband Jean Pierre Aumont. It was the first feature she made after leaving Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Sky Dragon
rows.cast: Roland Winters, Noel Neill
rows.extract: Sky Dragon is a 1949 American mystery film, the sixth in which Roland Winters portrayed Charlie Chan. Directed by Lesley Selander, it is the last Chan film in the long-running series that originated in 1930 with Fox Film Corporation production of Charlie Chan Carries On, starring Warner Oland.

rows.title: Slattery's Hurricane
rows.cast: Richard Widmark, Linda Darnell, Veronica Lake
rows.extract: Slattery's Hurricane is a 1949 American drama film directed by Andre DeToth and starring Richard Widmark, Linda Darnell and Veronica Lake. It is based on a story submitted by Herman Wouk, who also coauthored the screenplay and published a novel of the film in 1956.

rows.title: Slightly French
rows.cast: Dorothy Lamour, Don Ameche
rows.extract: Slightly French is a 1949 American musical comedy film directed by Douglas Sirk and starring Dorothy Lamour, Don Ameche and Janis Carter. The screenplay concerns a Hollywood director who recruits an American singer.

rows.cast: Burl Ives, Beulah Bondi, Harry Carey

rows.title: Sorrowful Jones
rows.cast: Bob Hope, Lucille Ball
rows.extract: Sorrowful Jones, also known as Damon Runyon's Sorrowful Jones, is a 1949 American comedy-drama film directed by Sidney Lanfield. The film stars Lucille Ball and Bob Hope.

rows.title: South of Death Valley
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Gail Davis
rows.extract: South of Death Valley is a 1949 American Western film directed by Ray Nazarro and written by Earle Snell. The film stars Charles Starrett, Gail Davis, Fred F. rows.title: South of Rio
rows.cast: Monte Hale, Kay Christopher
rows.extract: South of Rio is a 1949 American Western film directed by Philip Ford, written by Norman S. Hall, and starring Monte Hale, Kay Christopher, Paul Hurst, Roy Barcroft, Douglas Kennedy and Don Haggerty. It was released on July 27, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: South of St. Louis
rows.cast: Joel McCrea, Zachary Scott, Victor Jory
rows.extract: South of St Louis is a 1949 American Technicolor Western film directed by Ray Enright and starring Joel McCrea, Alexis Smith, Zachary Scott and Dorothy Malone. rows.title: Special Agent
rows.cast: William Eythe, Kasey Rogers, Carole Mathews
rows.extract: Special Agent is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by William C. Thomas and starring William Eythe. The storyline is loosely based on the DeAutremont Brothers' 1923 train robbery.

rows.title: Square Dance Jubilee
rows.cast: Don "Red" Barry, Mary Beth Hughes, Wally Vernon
rows.extract: Square Dance Jubilee is a 1949 American Western musical film directed by Paul Landres starring Don "Red" Barry, Mary Beth Hughes and Wally Vernon.

rows.title: Stagecoach Kid
rows.cast: Tim Holt, Richard Martin, Jeff Donnell
rows.extract: Stagecoach Kid is a 1949 American Western film directed by Lew Landers and starring Tim Holt, Jeff Donnell and Richard Martin. It was one of a number of B-Westerns Holt made for RKO.

rows.title: Stampede
rows.cast: Rod Cameron, Gale Storm, Johnny Mack Brown, Don Castle
rows.extract: Stampede is a 1949 American Western film directed by Lesley Selander and starring Rod Cameron, Gale Storm, Johnny Mack Brown and Don Castle.

rows.title: State Department: File 649
rows.cast: Virginia Bruce, William Lundigan
rows.extract: State Department: File 649 is a 1949 film noir Cinecolor American film directed by Sam Newfield.

rows.title: Strange Bargain
rows.cast: Martha Scott, Jeffrey Lynn
rows.extract: Strange Bargain is a 1949 American crime film noir directed by Will Price and starring Martha Scott, Jeffrey Lynn and Harry Morgan.

rows.title: The Stratton Story
rows.cast: James Stewart, June Allyson
rows.extract: The Stratton Story is a 1949 American biographical film directed by Sam Wood that tells the true story of Monty Stratton, a Major League Baseball pitcher who pitched for the Chicago White Sox from 1934 to 1938. rows.title: Streets of Laredo
rows.cast: William Holden, William Bendix, Macdonald Carey, Mona Freeman

rows.title: Streets of San Francisco
rows.cast: Robert Armstrong, Mae Clarke
rows.extract: Streets of San Francisco is a 1949 American crime film directed by George Blair, written by John K. Butler and starring Robert Armstrong, Mae Clarke, Gary Gray, Wally Cassell, Richard Benedict and John Harmon. It was released on April 15, 1949 by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: The Story of Molly X
rows.cast: June Havoc, John Russell, Dorothy Hart
rows.extract: The Story of Molly X is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by Crane Wilbur and starring June Havoc, John Russell and Dorothy Hart. The screenplay concerns a woman who tries to reform after being sent to prison, but faces obstacles.

rows.title: The Story of Seabiscuit
rows.cast: Shirley Temple, Barry Fitzgerald
rows.extract: The Story of Seabiscuit is a 1949 American drama film directed by David Butler and starring Shirley Temple and Barry Fitzgerald in a semi-fictionalized account of racehorse Seabiscuit, the top money winner up to the 1940s. The screenplay was written by John Taintor Foote, uses the actual racehorse n

rows.title: The Sun Comes Up
rows.cast: Jeanette MacDonald, Claude Jarman Jr.
rows.extract: The Sun Comes Up is a 1949 Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Technicolor picture with Lassie. Jeanette MacDonald had been off the screen for five years until her return in Three Daring Daughters (1948), but The Sun Comes Up was to be her last. rows.title: Susanna Pass
rows.cast: Roy Rogers, Dale Evans
rows.extract: Susanna Pass  is a 1949 Republic Pictures Trucolor American Western film directed by William Witney and starring Roy Rogers.

rows.title: Sword in the Desert
rows.cast: Dana Andrews, Märta Torén
rows.extract: Sword in the Desert is a 1949 American war film directed by George Sherman. It was the first American film to deal with the 1947–1948 Civil War in Mandatory Palestine and marked the first significant feature film role for Jeff Chandler.

rows.title: Take One False Step
rows.cast: Shelley Winters, William Powell
rows.extract: Take One False Step is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by Chester Erskine and starring William Powell and Shelley Winters.

rows.title: Tarzan's Magic Fountain
rows.cast: Lex Barker, Brenda Joyce, Evelyn Ankers
rows.extract: Tarzan's Magic Fountain is a 1949 Tarzan film directed by Lee Sholem and starring Lex Barker as Tarzan and Brenda Joyce as his companion Jane. The film also features Albert Dekker and Evelyn Ankers. It was co-written by Curt Siodmak.

rows.title: Task Force
rows.cast: Gary Cooper, Jane Wyatt, Walter Brennan

rows.title: Tell It to the Judge
rows.cast: Rosalind Russell, Robert Cummings
rows.extract: Tell It to the Judge is a 1949 American romantic comedy film directed by Norman Foster and starring Rosalind Russell as a divorcee who tries to get back her ex-husband, played by Robert Cummings.

rows.title: Tension
rows.cast: Richard Basehart, Audrey Totter, Barry Sullivan, Cyd Charisse
rows.extract: Tension is a 1949 American crime film noir directed by John Berry, and written by Allen Rivkin, based on a story written by John D. Klorer. It stars Richard Basehart, Audrey Totter, Cyd Charisse and Barry Sullivan.

rows.title: That Forsyte Woman

rows.extract: That Midnight Kiss is a 1949 Technicolor American musical romance film also starring Mario Lanza and Kathryn Grayson. rows.extract: There's a Girl in My Heart is a 1949 American musical comedy film directed by Arthur Dreifuss, starring Lee Bowman, Elyse Knox, and Gloria Jean. It was made by Allied Artists with many former contract stars from Universal.

rows.title: They Live by Night

rows.extract: They Live by Night is a 1948 American film noir directed by Nicholas Ray, in his directorial debut, and starring Cathy O'Donnell and Farley Granger. rows.title: Thieves' Highway
rows.cast: Richard Conte, Valentina Cortese, Lee J. Cobb
rows.extract: Thieves' Highway is a 1949 film noir directed by Jules Dassin. The screenplay was written by A. I. Bezzerides, based on his novel Thieves' Market. The film was released on DVD as part of the Criterion Collection in 2005.

rows.title: The Threat
rows.cast: Michael O'Shea, Virginia Grey
rows.extract: The Threat is a 1949 American film noir starring Michael O'Shea, Virginia Grey and Charles McGraw, and directed by Felix E. Feist.

rows.title: Tokyo Joe

rows.extract: Tokyo Joe is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by Stuart Heisler and starring Humphrey Bogart. This was Heisler's first of two features starring Bogart, the other was Chain Lightning that also wrapped in 1949 but was held up in release until 1950.

rows.title: Too Late for Tears
rows.cast: Lizabeth Scott, Dan Duryea, Don DeFore
rows.extract: Too Late for Tears is a 1949 film noir directed by Byron Haskin and starring Lizabeth Scott, Arthur Kennedy, Dan Duryea, and Don DeFore. rows.title: Tough Assignment

rows.extract: Tough Assignment is a 1949 American crime film directed by William Beaudine and starring Don Barry, Marjorie Steele and Steve Brodie. It is regarded as a film noir.

rows.title: Trail of the Yukon
rows.cast: Kirby Grant, Suzanne Dalbert
rows.extract: Trail of the Yukon is a 1949 American Northern film directed by William Beaudine and starring Kirby Grant, Suzanne Dalbert and Bill Edwards. rows.title: Trails End
