rows.extract: Trapped is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by Richard Fleischer and starring Lloyd Bridges, Barbara Payton, and John Hoyt. It was written by George Zuckerman and Earl Felton.

rows.title: Treasure of Monte Cristo
rows.cast: Glenn Langan, Adele Jergens
rows.extract: Treasure of Monte Cristo is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by William Berke and starring Glenn Langan, Adele Jergens and Steve Brodie.

rows.title: Tucson
rows.cast: Jimmy Lydon, Penny Edwards
rows.extract: Tucson is a 1949 American drama film directed by William F. Claxton, written by Arnold Belgard and starring Jimmy Lydon, Penny Edwards, Deanna Wayne, Charles Russell, Joe Sawyer and Walter Sande. It was released on April 27, 1949 by 20th Century-Fox.

rows.title: Tulsa
rows.cast: Susan Hayward, Robert Preston
rows.extract: Tulsa is a 1949 American Western action film directed by Stuart Heisler and starring Susan Hayward and Robert Preston, and featured Lloyd Gough, Chill Wills, and Ed Begley in one of his earliest film roles, billed as Edward Begley.

rows.title: Tuna Clipper
rows.cast: Roddy McDowall, Elena Verdugo
rows.extract: Tuna Clipper is a 1949 American drama film directed by William Beaudine and starring Roddy McDowall, Elena Verdugo and Roland Winters. It was one of a series of films McDowall made for Monogram.

rows.title: Twelve O'Clock High
rows.cast: Gregory Peck, Gary Merrill, Dean Jagger
rows.extract: Twelve O'Clock High is a 1949 American war film about aircrews in the United States Army's Eighth Air Force, who flew daylight bombing missions against Germany and Occupied France during the early days of American involvement in World War II. rows.title: The Undercover Man
rows.cast: Glenn Ford, Nina Foch, James Whitmore
rows.extract: The Undercover Man is a 1949 American crime film noir directed by Joseph H. Lewis and starring Glenn Ford, Nina Foch and James Whitmore.

rows.title: Undertow
rows.cast: Scott Brady, John Russell, Dorothy Hart, Peggy Dow
rows.extract: Undertow is a 1949 American film noir crime film directed by William Castle and starring Scott Brady, John Russell, Dorothy Hart and Peggy Dow. rows.cast: Randolph Scott, Ella Raines
rows.extract: The Walking Hills is a 1949 American Western film directed by John Sturges and starring Randolph Scott and Ella Raines. rows.cast: Jennifer Jones, John Garfield, Pedro Armendáriz
rows.extract: We Were Strangers is a 1949 American adventure drama film directed by John Huston and starring Jennifer Jones and John Garfield. rows.title: West of El Dorado
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Max Terhune, Reno Browne
rows.extract: West of El Dorado is a 1949 American Western film directed by Ray Taylor and written by Adele Buffington. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Max Terhune, Reno Browne, Teddy Infuhr, Milburn Morante and Terry Frost. The film was released on June 5, 1949, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Western Renegades
rows.cast: Johnny Mack Brown, Max Terhune
rows.extract: Western Renegades is a 1949 American Western film directed by Wallace Fox and written by Adele Buffington. The film stars Johnny Mack Brown, Max Terhune, Poni Adams, Hugh Prosser, Riley Hill and Marshall Reed. The film was released on October 9, 1949, by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: White Heat
rows.cast: James Cagney, Virginia Mayo, Edmond O'Brien, Steve Cochran
rows.extract: White Heat is a 1949 American film noir directed by Raoul Walsh and starring James Cagney, Virginia Mayo, Edmond O'Brien, Margaret Wycherly and Steve Cochran.

rows.title: Wicked City
rows.cast: Maria Montez, Jean-Pierre Aumont, Lilli Palmer
rows.extract: Wicked City is a 1949 French-American drama film directed by François Villiers and starring the husband-and-wife team of Jean-Pierre Aumont and Maria Montez. It was Montez's first film in Europe.

rows.title: The Window
rows.cast: Bobby Driscoll, Barbara Hale
rows.extract: The Window is a 1949 American black-and-white film noir, based on the short story "The Boy Cried Murder" by Cornell Woolrich, about a lying boy who suspects that his neighbors are killers. rows.cast: Laraine Day, Dane Clark, Franchot Tone
rows.extract: Without Honor is a 1949 film noir directed by Irving Pichel and starring Bruce Bennett, Laraine Day, Dane Clark, Agnes Moorehead, and Franchot Tone.

rows.title: The Wolf Hunters
rows.cast: Kirby Grant, Jan Clayton
rows.extract: The Wolf Hunters is a 1949 American Northern film directed by Budd Boetticher and starring Kirby Grant, Jan Clayton and Edward Norris. rows.title: A Woman's Secret
rows.cast: Maureen O'Hara, Melvyn Douglas, Gloria Grahame
rows.extract: A Woman's Secret is a 1949 film noir directed by Nicholas Ray and starring Maureen O'Hara, Gloria Grahame and Melvyn Douglas. The film was based on the novel Mortgage on Life by Vicki Baum.

rows.title: The Wyoming Bandit
rows.cast: Allan Lane, Eddy Waller
rows.extract: The Wyoming Bandit is a 1949 American Western film directed by Philip Ford and written by M. Coates Webster. The film stars Allan Lane, Eddy Waller, Trevor Bardette, Victor Kilian, Rand Brooks and William Haade. The film was released on July 15, 1949, by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Yes Sir, That's My Baby
rows.cast: Donald O'Connor, Gloria DeHaven
rows.extract: Yes Sir, That's My Baby is a 1949 American musical comedy film directed by George Sherman and starring Donald O'Connor and Gloria DeHaven.

rows.title: The Younger Brothers
rows.cast: Wayne Morris, Bruce Bennett, Janis Paige
rows.extract: The Younger Brothers is a 1949 American Western film directed by Edwin L. Marin and starring Wayne Morris, Bruce Bennett, Janis Paige.

rows.title: You're My Everything
rows.cast: Dan Dailey, Anne Baxter, Anne Revere
rows.extract: You're My Everything is a 1949 American comedy musical film directed by Walter Lang and starring Dan Dailey and Anne Baxter.

rows.cast: George Reeves, Lois Hall
rows.extract: Adventures of Sir Galahad is the 41st serial released in 1949 by Columbia Pictures. rows.extract: New Adventures of Batman and Robin, the Boy Wonder, also known as simply Batman and Robin, is a 15-chapter serial released in 1949 by Columbia Pictures. rows.cast: Tom Neal, Judy Clark
rows.extract: Bruce Gentry – Daredevil of the Skies (1949) is a 15-episode Columbia Pictures movie serial based on the Bruce Gentry comic strip created by Ray Bailey. It features the first cinematic appearance of a flying saucer, as the secret weapon of the villainous Recorder.

rows.title: Ghost of Zorro
rows.cast: Clayton Moore, Pamela Blake
rows.extract: Ghost of Zorro is a 1949 Republic Movie serial. It uses substantial stock footage from earlier serials, including Son of Zorro and Daredevils of the West. This film was shot in Chatsworth, Los Angeles.

rows.title: King of the Rocket Men
rows.cast: Tris Coffin, Mae Clarke
rows.extract: King of the Rocket Men is a 1949 12-chapter movie serial from Republic Pictures, produced by Franklin Adreon, directed Fred C. Brannon, that stars Tristram Coffin, Mae Clarke, Don Haggerty, House Peters, Jr., James Craven, and I. Stanford Jolley.

rows.title: Radar Patrol vs. Spy King
rows.cast: Kirk Alyn
rows.extract: Radar Patrol vs. Spy King is a 1949 12-chapter black-and-white spy film serial produced and distributed by Republic Pictures from an original, commissioned screenplay collaboratively written by Royal K. Cole, William Lively and Sol Shor. Kirk Alyn played the lead.

rows.title: Awful Orphan
rows.extract: Awful Orphan is a 1949 Warner Bros. Merrie Melodies cartoon, directed by Chuck Jones and written by Michael Maltese. It is a sequel to the 1947 Looney Tunes short Little Orphan Airedale.

rows.title: Dunked in the Deep
rows.cast: The Three Stooges
rows.extract: Dunked in the Deep is a 1949 short subject directed by Jules White starring American slapstick comedy team The Three Stooges. It is the 119th entry in the series released by Columbia Pictures starring the comedians, who released 190 shorts for the studio between 1934 and 1959.

rows.title: For Scent-imental Reasons
rows.extract: For Scent-imental Reasons is a 1949 Warner Bros. Looney Tunes short directed by Chuck Jones and written by Michael Maltese. The short was released on November 12, 1949, and stars Pepé Le Pew and Penelope Pussycat.

rows.title: Frigid Hare
rows.cast: Bugs Bunny
rows.extract: Frigid Hare is a Warner Bros. Merrie Melodies short, released on October 8, 1949. It is directed by Chuck Jones and written by Michael Maltese, and features Bugs Bunny. The title can be seen as a simple play on "frigid air" and/or on the refrigerator brand called "Frigidaire".

rows.cast: Bugs Bunny

rows.extract: Malice in the Palace is a 1949 short subject directed by Jules White starring American slapstick comedy team The Three Stooges. It is the 117th entry in the series released by Columbia Pictures starring the comedians, who released 190 shorts for the studio between 1934 and 1959.

rows.cast: Porky Pig
rows.extract: Porky in Wackyland is a 1938 Warner Bros. Looney Tunes animated short film, directed by Bob Clampett. The short was released on September 24, 1938, and stars Porky Pig venturing out to find the last do-do bird, which he finds in Wackyland, a land that makes no sense located in Darkest Africa.

rows.cast: Bugs Bunny
rows.extract: Rebel Rabbit is a 1949 Warner Bros. Merrie Melodies animated short. The cartoon was released on April 9, 1949, and features Bugs Bunny.
